column6: Packing the features in a limited budget.
column7:
I have written this comprehensive review keeping in mind that I have bought a phone which is within the Rs. 10K limit. So, there will be no grousing on Corning Gorilla Glass, NFC or Qualcomm Snapdragon processor in this review.
  
  There are a bunch of unexpected Pros and Cons in the device. I will elaborate each striking feature so that it will help my fellow buyers in deciding if the product will suit them or not.
  

  Pros:
  

  1. 2.5D Glass: This is exemplary for a phone in this budget. Together with its metal body design and embedded camera (similar to 5th Gen G-series), this phone gives an undoubted premium look.
  

  2. Dolby Atmos: The Moto E4 Plus is an audible delight. It outperforms Moto G5 and Moto X1 with its speakers as well as audio jack delivering one of the best sounds you can expect from a smartphone.
  

  3. Android 7.1.1 with 3GB RAM: There a quite a few Android Nougat phones in the market and owning the latest Android is something to brag. But it is essential to have sufficient RAM to utilize your smartphones to the fullest. My average RAM usage for 24 hours is 1.7 GB. Having a 2 GB RAM would be dreadful for both the product as well as the user.
  

  4. 32 GB ROM: The internal memory is sure to fulfil every user's needs. With enough and more space for apps and multimedia, Moto has given a really good deal within 10K. It is commendable that Moto maintained a dedicated slot for expansion rather than a hybrid slot.
  

  5. 5000 mAH Battery: This striking feature at the product launch is efficacious. With rough usage, the battery ended the day at 33% which is indeed remarkable! Under fair usage, the battery may last 2-3 days.
  

  Cons:
  

  1. Camera: Although the camera specifications look promising, it doesn't perform as expected. The quality is average but not bad. If someone is looking for a great camera smartphone, this is not the one.
  

  2. Non-removable battery: For most users, the whole purpose of a removable battery is to shut down the mobile if it gets hanged. In case of a non-removable battery, you will have to wait till the charge drains completely. Considering a 5000 mAH battery, it would inconveniently take days till you run out of charge. Hopefully, Moto has designed a counter feature to prevent this occurrence.
  

  3. Moto gestures: Moto did a pretty good job by providing gesture operations for camera, flashlight, etc in higher models. Moto E4 plus is an incomplete smartphone without these features.
  

  Notable mentions:
  

  1. LED notification light: Many customers these days search for this feature. A cute little fancy dual colour notification light exists in this device to content the users.
  

  2. Performance: The MediaTek Quad Core isn't really that big a disappointment! It runs Asphalt 8 and NFS No Limits without any lag though a certain lag is experienced while launching such games.
  

  3. Turbocharger: One must not be too keen on this feature as Moto E4 Plus is not equipped with USB type-C. The 10W charger just ensures that the mammoth battery charges quicker than conventional 4-6W chargers.
  

  I know this might be one of the longest reviews on Flipkart, but if you liked it please give a thumbs up.

I read so many reviews b4 buying the product and was not sure whether to go with it or not, finally decided to buy it instead of Redmi 4. And what I come to know after using the product for a week of use:
  
  1.	Battery: The tag of the phone (5000mAh)! I'm a very heavy user, & for me it last for more than 20 hours. Hope it will be 40 hrs> for light user. Massive battery takes only 2.5 hrs to complete charge with rapid charger.(10/10)
  
  2.	Display: 5.5  HD (not full hd) display with 267ppi  gives a good look but not so vivid & vibrant. U won't be disappointed. Though little glossy in very bright sunlight, still comfortable. (7.5/10)
  
  3.	Camera: Rear 13MP, f 2.0 very good in daylight( for both still image & video). A bit focuses issue though. In low light still image is good but video is sufficiently poor( flash for video ain't up to the mark).  Front 5 MP, f 2.4(flash is also good) also works fine, image is good but video poor. (8/10)
  
  4.	Performance: With MTK6737 & 3GB RAM deliver a good performance, good gaming(Asphalt 8, Mortal Combat X, in medium quality). Almost 1.5 Gb RAM free. Can handle more than 20 window with ease. And heating issue is minimal.(8/10)
  
  5.	 Look: Brilliant, as a metal finish is there, though back panel is removable still it seems unibody design. And 2.5D curved glass add up one more step. (9/10)
  
  6.	Network & Call: With no hybrid slot u can use 2 sim both 4G. Clear sufficiently loud audio during call. VoLTE works fine on both SIM slot.(10/10)
  
  7.	Sensor: Here a little disappointment, only 3(accelero, light & proxy) along with fingerprint. Fingerprint works absolutely fine(less than 1 sec).(7/10)
  
  8.	Gesture: 1 button navigation, swipe to shrink screen(for single hand operation) and moto display is just perfect.(8/10)
  
  9.	 Speaker: Single speaker with Dolby Atmos is very audible. And headset is also nice.(8.5/10)
  
  10.	 OS: Stock Android 7.1.1, some customization and simple UI makes it very user friendly. Though no good app for gallery & music(default from google) but u can get it later.(9/10)
  
  ## For notification a cute dual led light is also there. Pretty cool.
  
  Verdict- Overall(8.5/10) it's a good phone under 10k. A smart budget smartphone.  A long review but I give every detail, hope it's useful for all.

This phone is a blessing for me (as far as battery is concerned).
  
  2. Price: In 7k you get and very decent phone.
  
  3. OS: You get the latest android OS.
  
  4. Decent specs: You get 2 GB RAM, 16 GB ROM (can be extended to 32 GB), Quad core 1.3 GHz processor and HD display.
  

  Not so good things:
  
  1. Proximity sensor: It does not have a proximity sensor, which is hard to believe for a smartphone in 2017. Its display does not go off when you bring it close to your ear while on a call which is inconvenient.
  
  2. Touch response: Its touch response is not so great.
  
  3. Overall design: Not so great.
  

  Neutral: I am neutral on following.
  
  1. Camera: I am not a photo/selfie enthusiast. I own a DSLR camera for my photo needs. But I took some photos and they looked OK to me.
  
  2. Gaming performance: I do not have any games installed on the phone and therefore cannot comment on the phone's performance in this aspect also.

column6: Review of Moto G5 Plus (after 2 days of usage)
column7:
Well,without wasting any time..I'll write the Pros and cons (What I feel after 2 days of usage).
  

  Pros:-
  
  1.Nice display..Not the best 1080p display,but lives up to expectation.
  
  2.Lag-Free experience with near stock android and handy moto experiences.
  
  3.A great 12 MP camera that focuses very fast and can do well in low lit conditions.
  
  3.Nice design with aluminum back which has a good amount of grip and is sure to grab some attention.
  
  4.Turbo charger charges the 3000 mAh battery very fast which can easily last for a whole day.
  
  5.The fingerprint sensor is also very fast and this phone also comes with NFC which is going to be handy if android pay is launched in India
  
  6.One thing in which moto G5 really shines is that it provides a separate micro sd and SIM card
  
  Slot...no need to compromise.And yes,This phone supports voLTE
  

  Enough Pros,Now lets Check the Cons:-
  
  1.No led..You have to pick up your phone to check the notifications.
  
  2.We also don't get 64 Gb of storage with the highest version...There is expandable storage but come on internal storage is the one on which most people rely on..Also when future updates come..The storage will reduce even more.
  
  3.The headphones provided with this phone are shit..Seriously,even Micromax provide headphones which are better than moto's.
  
  4.For me a 5.2 Inch screen is OK..But for many people It is not as per as their requirement.
  
  5.No Google assistant guys..Yes,This phone doesn't come with google assistant preinstalled don't be in the wrong notion that you're gonna get Siri like assistant on your phone..That doesn't mean that assistant won't come..It will,but not anytime soon.

Graphics is surprisingly great with a stable 30fps even with intense gaming. The screen is punchy and adequately bright. But sunlight legibility could have been further improved. For me, the battery lasted for a good 30 hours with mixed usage. In my opinion, the 3400mAh battery that does duty in Moto Z play would have returned a fantastic endurance result. Still no complaints with the battery.  Coming to the show-stopper the amazing camera coupled with dual pixel 1.7 aperture. It gives stellar images and excellent low light performance. With a host of professional mode features one can take exceptional snaps with a single tap. Only complaint here is the lack of optical image stabilization. The front camera is a mediocre unit, though still, it gives you good selfies and the screen flash helps to some extent. One more excellent thing about the phone is it's audio output via headphone jack. The sound quality is terrific. I use a pair of JBL T150A ear buds and it just adds up to the amazing experience. But the external speaker is very harsh to listen and the call volume at times seem very low even when cranked to the fullest.To sum it up, the Moto G5 plus is truly an all rounder. It gives you adequate performance, great user experience, a stellar camera, assured fast updates, premium build, while all this without compromising on battery life.
  
  Build - 9/10
  
  Performance - 8/10 (One cannot expect anything more from SD625)
  
  UI experience - 9/10 (Stock Android Nougat with assured updates)
  
  Display - 8/10 (AMOLED would have done great)
  
  Battery - 8/10 (The competition has a 4100mAh unit)
  
  Primary Camera - 9/10 (Just because OIS is missing)
  
  Secondary Camera - 5/10 (Either a better sensor or a front flash was sorely missed)
  
  Call Quality - 7/10 (Speaker volume is a little unpredictable)

  3. Fingerprint sensor is terrific. You will find it very sensitive and it works really good. The extra feature associated with Moto gestures ale it to be used as Android navigation and home button. This is something smart!
  

  4. Well with a powerful processor and a great amount of RAM, it never lags or freezes or presents any annoying haptic feedbacks. There is no heating. Well the Summers are on, so while running heavy applications you may feel the heat due to its metallic back.
  

  5. Camera is above average. Due to the new aperture length and tech it really captures more light. This helps you shoot some really good images. I used the camera in daylight and they were nice. Low light shootings is obviously affected. I personally feel the mediocrity of camera is due to poor Moto camera app. Video shoots are good. Focussing is faster than normal phones. I bet it captures better images than Note 4. Front camera is good. Video call quality doesn't bother me as far as camera is concerned. For me camera works good in this phone. Refer to Geekyranjith guy for camera review. He presents an accurate experience.
  

  6. You will really feel that the speaker could have been louder. It is just an earpiece speaker. It is average. However the sound output is excellent especially with the headphones. I love it. Music lovers will appreciate this.
  

  7. It supports VoLTE. One SIM runs 4g and the other can be in 3G mode.
  

  8. Turbo Charge took 1 hour to charge from 0-100% when ambient temperature was around 18deg Celsius. It depends on the ambient room temperature.
  

  9. Holding the phone will give you a premium feel. The metallic cover adds to its beautiful design. I like the ergonomics of this phone. The phone is lighter too.
  

  10. Running Android N, the phone presents a terrific UI experience.
  

  11. Battery works great until now. It easily lasts for more than 13 hours even after heavy data usage and moderate UI interactions. For anyone living in a city a phone with a battery that lasts more than 10 hours is good. I charged it too 100% 8 hours ago. It currently shows 61% and I have been continuously using Data in the meantime. I must point out that the battery saver that comes with Android N works really great.
  

  12. Call quality is great. The UI presents an easy SIM management.
  

  13. I especially loved the idea which allows you to have two SIM cards along with SD card. It paves way out for those hybrid Sim slots.
  

  14. For moderate users, this phone is a great choice. Although I think this phone is overpriced, the feeling goes away once you handle the phone.(especially because at 8k I couldn't have wished more)
  

  15. Although it lacks a compass, you won't have any problems in navigation using maps.
  

  I will give it a 4/5. I just wanted a louder speaker and a better complementing Camera application.

After 24+ hours of usage here is my viewpoint,
  
  Build quality is very firm and looks very premium. One will love the detailing on the back panel and the chrome garnish around the bezel looks upmarket. The overall form factor is compact and easy to use, thanks to 5.2-inch profile and extreme light-weightedness. Though there is a slight bump for housing the back camera, one needs to be extra careful while putting it on flat surfaces. The IPS LCD when not lit shows strange horizontal lines when seen very minutely. The Lunar Grey color closely resembles gunmetal hue which is again a very good thing. From the exterior point of view, the phone is a beauty to behold and a personality statement to flaunt.
  
  Now coming to day-to-day usage, the phone simply surprises. It gives you a flawless buttery smooth experience with the stock Nougat. There is absolutely no lag and believe me SD625 does wonders here. And thanks to 4GB of RAM  multitasking and multi-window operation becomes so easy. Graphics is surprisingly great with a stable 30fps even with intense gaming. The screen is punchy and adequately bright. But sunlight legibility could have been further improved. For me, the battery lasted for a good 30 hours with mixed usage. In my opinion, the 3400mAh battery that does duty in Moto Z play would have returned a fantastic endurance result. Still no complaints with the battery.  Coming to the show-stopper the amazing camera coupled with dual pixel 1.7 aperture. It gives stellar images and excellent low light performance. With a host of professional mode features one can take exceptional snaps with a single tap. Only complaint here is the lack of optical image stabilization. The front camera is a mediocre unit, though still, it gives you good selfies and the screen flash helps to some extent. One more excellent thing about the phone is it's audio output via headphone jack. The sound quality is terrific. I use a pair of JBL T150A ear buds and it just adds up to the amazing experience. But the external speaker is very harsh to listen and the call volume at times seem very low even when cranked to the fullest.To sum it up, the Moto G5 plus is truly an all rounder. It gives you adequate performance, great user experience, a stellar camera, assured fast updates, premium build, while all this without compromising on battery life.
  
  Build - 9/10
  
  Performance - 8/10 (One cannot expect anything more from SD625)
  
  UI experience - 9/10 (Stock Android Nougat with assured updates)
  
  Display - 8/10 (AMOLED would have done great)
  
  Battery - 8/10 (The competition has a 4100mAh unit)
  
  Primary Camera - 9/10 (Just because OIS is missing)
  
  Secondary Camera - 5/10 (Either a better sensor or a front flash was sorely missed)
  
  Call Quality - 7/10 (Speaker volume is a little unpredictable)
  

  One thing should be kept in mind, with that price tag, you cannot get everything. While still this phone is a complete package and offers exceptional value.

So finally after 1 week of heavy usage, I am gonna write my review about this mid range budget smartphone from Motorola. First of all, I have always been a Motorola fan and so might be little biased. Please hit like if you find the review helpful. I am gonna divide it into sub-sections starting with design.
  

  Design: This is not a metal unibody device as claimed by Motorola. Only the back cover is made from metal and rest all plastic with a metal like finish. The bezel looks quite thicker in comparison to the modern standard. However, overall the device looks quite premium and the best part is that it does not copy the iPhone design as done by the majority of the Chinese companies. I would say the design is unique although bezels could have been made much thinner.
  

  Camera: The most discussed feature of this smartphone is its camera which uses the same specs of galaxy s7. Although in reality, S7 does a much better job, I would say this is the camera you would get under 30k. Some people has complained regarding the low light images but with a little bit tweak in the settings (professional mode) you can get awesome snaps with this device.
  

  Battery: On paper, it's 3000mAh which some people may feel not enough, but from my experience for the last 1 week I found it doing surprisingly well. With even heavy usage it easily lasts for a complete day and gives SOT of around 4-6 hrs on average. So somehow Motorola has done a very good work on this.
  
  Processor: It uses Snapdragon 625 with 4Gb of ram. This is one of the best processors in terms of performance and energy efficiency.
  

  User experience: simply the best. You can compare against any of the flagships available in the market. SD625 chipset coupled with 4gb ram and stock android does a fantastic job in providing a very smooth user experience with zero lag and manageable heating. I would say this is what makes Moto G5 plus stand away from the crowd. One must understand it's not about the specs but the performance and Moto G5 plus won't disappoint you.
  

  Fast Charging: Although it comes with a fast charger, it's certainly not the best. It takes around 2 hrs to charge the phone from 0 to 100% whereas my moto g4 plus with same capacity used to take around 1 hr 15 mins. When I checked the charger specs, found that the current rating is much lower than the one that was provided with g4 plus. I am not sure why Motorola has degraded the charger, it might be related to the processor, but still it charges the phone from 0 to 45-50% in around 55 mins which I believe is quite fast.
  
  Overall, the only thing that I feel could have been improved is the design, else everything is just perfect with this beast. If you are looking for something below 20k just go for it without any second thought !!!

  4) Battery back up is one full day with moderate usage (1 hr video, 1 hr watsapp, 45 min call, ~2 hrs net etc). Here, redmi scores high with backup of ~2 days with similar usage. However, this is compensated by turbo charging available in moto (1.5 hrs to fully charge from 0 to 100%, with first 80% in 40 min only vs ~4 hrs for redmi for full charge). So its a matter of preference here, charging once for long and using it for 2 days vs very short charging time and 1 day use
  
  5) I read some people writing about heating issues in moto, but luckiliy my device is not heating up. Also, redmi doesnt heat up too. Both phones similar here.
  
  6) Higher android version (nougat), which is class in itself, in Moto vs marshmallow in redmi
  
  7) Both sims and sd card active in moto g5 at the same time vs either 2 sims or one sim and sdcard in redmi

This review is after 3 days of usage. Build quality of this phone is awesome. It feels like a premium smartphone. With metal body and gold look, this smartphone scores full marks in looks department. This being said...a lot of things are wrong with the software and optimization. Why I say this..you'll come to know as you read along. First of all camera....despite being 16MP camera, it doesn't feel like one. Photos are grainy and it's performance in low light is not up to the mark. Front facing 8MP camera is also of same quality as it rear counterpart. Battery life is another disappointing feature of this phone. This phone boasts battery power of 3050mah. 2600mah of moto g3 turbo gives more screen on time than this one. With phone charged to 100 % at 7 in the morning, it doesn't lasts for even 12 hrs, that too after "careful" usage(mind the words not moderate not light but careful usage). This device is powered by Mediatek choose with MaliT860. Though this soc cannot be termed as weak per se, still graphics performance of this device is not what I expected . Frame drops , lags and jitters in heavy and graphic intensive games is quite evident . Fingerprint sensor is fast but not as fast as other devices like moto g4 plus or even 10k range lenovo phones. All these issues do not appear to be hardware related and can be fixed by a comprehensive software update from Motorola. Right now, as is...this phone is not bang for the buck...but can become one after a good software update. Last but not the least...this phone comes with Android M out of the box which right now is least of our concerns but this was unexpected. I hope upgrade to Android N is in Motorola 's agenda.

Was using Moto X Play before buying Moto M, so there will be few comparisons which I know are not fair but still using as a reference point at few places.
  

  Nice build quality, feels good in hand. The back cover supplied with phone is not very high quality. Suggest you order a new one from flipkart for better protection from falls. Also go for a tempered glass. Didn't use one for my X play and had to pay price for that.
  

  Performance is good. Apps load quickly, finger print scanner responds in a snap. Overall much better performance than X Play bcoz of better processor.
  
  It is almost stock Android.
  

  Dolby atoms sound is good. It is better than any of the Moto phones till date. But as usual, the earphones provided are average at best. Suggest you order JBL earphones for a truly dolby experience.
  

  Camera is above average. Great results in day light, average in low light conditions. Enhanced camera app provides additional options. But overall X Play camera (21 MP) will any day score over Moto M camera (16 MP).
  
  Battery again is smaller that X Play but the quick charging option makes for it.
  

  One refreshing change is toggling of cellular data in one click.
  

  Unlike X Play which can house 2 sims and SD card at once, Moto M can either hold 2 sims or 1 sim and SD card. I chose to go with my Jio sim card instead of SD card. Speaking of which, the 4G reception is much better than X Play and getting much faster data rates.
  

  It is priced slightly higher than G4 plus but there are lot of things better in M (Faster processor, dolby atoms, much better looks).
  

  Iv'e been a Moto loyalist and this one is a great offering in its price range.

  Battery performance :

column7:
Verdict:
  
  Consider the Moto X style if you are looking for a big screen smartphone with a sharp display, stock Android UI and rugged build quality.
  

  Highlights:
  
  Large Quad HD display is a joy to look at
  
  Rugged build and ergonomic design
  
  Stock Android interface
  
  Good camera quality
  
  Average battery life
  

  The Experience:
  
  The first thing that strikes you is the way in which Motorola has managed to keep the overall device size in check despite the huge 5.7-inch display. The slim bezels and curved back design play a major role in keeping the overall size in check. What's even better is the build quality and finish on the device. The Moto X Style is built like a tank and it offers a reassuring grip. Thanks to the high quality rubberized back, you need not worry about scratches or be in a hurry to put a cover on it. The almost stock Android interface will appeal to Android purists and Moto fans alike. With no signs of bloatware or custom UI, the phone feels zippy in daily usage. Apart from the design and high quality display, the 21MP camera on the Moto X is a highlight feature. The camera captures good quality photos and is super-fast in response. We wish Motorola had offered a higher capacity battery on the device. With a 3000 mAh battery pack, the device offers an average battery life. That being said, Quick Charge support acts like a saving grace allowing you to quickly juice up 40% of the battery in 15 minutes flat. On the performance front, the Snapdragon 808 combined with 3GB RAM keeps things fluid and fast on most occasions. We did notice the occasional lag on heavy gaming, most of which can be attributed to the Quad HD screen that needs extra performance to fill up the pixel dense screen. We didn't face any heating issues on the Moto X Style, even after prolonged gaming during our review period. All in all, the Moto X Style should be on your consideration list if you are looking for a well-built big screen smartphone with stock Android interface.

column6: Honest Opinion - One of the Best Devices of 2015
column7:
If you've been thinking about buying this phone but are still unsure - if this review won't convince you, nothing will! The Moto X Style has pretty much all you can ask for compared to any other phone from a major, reliable brand (excluding Indian/smaller Chinese companies, because they don't last more than 6 months - and I have a lot of experience with this) at this price point. I'm writing this after about 2-3 weeks of usage, so I have a fair idea about the performance.
  

  I won't be talking about the specs here, cause you can easily look that up. First and foremost, I'd like to clear some myths about the phone:
  
  1) People saying there is a 'Heating Problem'
  
  There is no such problem. The phone is pretty cool on everyday usage, and yes, it does get warm on heavy usage (for example if you're doing intensive gaming), but that's perfectly FINE! The processors in phones nowadays do get a little warm, but those temperatures are completely SAFE for your device. This is a huge myth among Indian consumers for some reason and really needs to be cleared out. The only problem that comes with heating is that your performance might slow down, but as the Snapdragon 808 doesn't heat as much as the faster (and infamous) Snapdragon 810 at warm temperatures, its performance is actually better.
  
  2) People saying Battery Backup is bad
  
  The battery backup is definitely not bad, in actuality it is average. I'm not claiming that the Moto X Style has the best battery backup around, because it doesn't. But for a QuadHD (1440p) 5.7" display, you have to make sure you're comparing the battery with devices with similar specs, not with your old phone with an HD 720p or Full HD 1080p display. In that case, the battery backup is just fine. TurboCharging is by no means a replacement for good battery backup, but it does help a lot.
  
  3) People saying phone is too big
  
  If you can handle a 5" phone like the Moto G2, then you will have absolutely NO PROBLEM using this device. I personally used the Moto G2 and find the X Style easier to handle. The curved back really does help with handling.
  

  A few facts I'd like to mention that I haven't seen in other reviews:
  
  - OTG support is definitely there in the Moto X Style, I've tested it - works fine.
  
  - Also, there is no notification LED but the phone has Moto Display, which might sound like a gimmick but is actually VERY useful, as I've realized over the few weeks. I actually prefer Moto Display because I don't have a bright light at night when I'm trying to sleep because of the notification LED.
  
  - You might see 2 red dots where the back and menu buttons are on other phones - those are motion sensors for Moto Display.
  
  - There is no fingerprint scanner, but, to be honest, it is more of a gimmick right now and is far from being a major feature for everyday usage even in the west, forget in India. But I'm mentioning it as it might be a deal breaker for some people.
  
  - Has normal microUSB charging cable, not USB-C, which is, again, effectively a gimmick right now because USB-C chargers and converting cables are so rare and really just a hassle.
  
  - The device is IP52 certified with a water repellent nano-coating, which basically means if you spill water on your Moto X Style or use it in the rain, it is completely safe. But don't go and dip it in a bucket!
  

  So, you're getting:
  
  - QuadHD (1440p, better than FullHD which is 1080p) 5.7" display,
  
  - Snapdragon 808 - one of the best processors/ SoCs out there right now,
  
  - A 21MP camera finally good enough to compete with flagships,
  
  - A decent front camera with flash,
  
  - Almost stock android with Moto's improvements (which I actually prefer over the android on Nexus devices, thanks to Moto Actions and display mainly),
  
  - You'll get android updates as fast as Nexus devices,
  
  - LTE (4G) support with dual SIM
  
  - One of the best stereo dual front facing speakers out there (as good as HTC BoomSound),
  
  - TurboCharging with an okayish battery backup,
  
  - An IP52 certified water repellent device,
  
  - AND most importantly expandable storage up to 128GB (first in a Moto X!),
  
  ALL AT 30-32k.
  
  Compare that to the performance of comparable devices, say the Nexus 5X (no expandable storage, screen with lower resolution of 1080p, higher price, lower battery size) or the OnePlus 2 (average camera, slow updates, unreliable after-sales service) you'll see that this is clearly the better deal. I honestly don't understand how this phone has a 3.9 rating on Flipkart right now? Look up anywhere on the internet on trusted global mobile reviewing sites, and you'll see the acclaim this phone has been getting for a good reason.
  

  Very satisfied with my purchase as of now, and I might edit this review later on if I have anything else to add about my experience with the Moto X Style.

column6: Best phone in the market right now, irrespective of price
column7:
There is no perfect smartphone... period. But MXS ticks most number of boxes...
  

  I will summarize the pros and cons of this awesome device
  

  1. One of the very few flagships with both dual sim and microSD card.
  
  2. 0.5 inches bigger than last years MX(2014), yet just as wide, excellent for one hand use. It's even easier on the fingers than the iPhone6+ though the screen size is larger
  
  3. 4K display, as good as most other flagships, AMOLED would have sounded better, but Moto has optimized the display such that it actually looks like AMOLED, can't tell the difference from the MX2014
  
  4. Front stereo speakers. Takes anything on the screen or playing games to the next level.  No more cupping the palm behind or below the phone.
  
  5. Moto display and moto assist, the most addictive features of MXS. Use it for couple of weeks, you will hate all other phones out there.
  
  6. Turbo charger. I am a pretty heavy user and charge my phone twice daily. 15-20 mins in the morning (7am) and 30 mins in the evening (8pm). Never felt that the battery will die on me. I recommend the app "DOZE" till the marshmallow hits this phone. This app is a bit like Sony's battery management. Stops all the data and background activities when you are not using the phone
  
  7. Camera. Don't listen to what the reviewers are saying. This camera is one of the best in the market, especially the video is awesome... no jerks at all... and that selfie camera is just wao...
  
  8. Call quality. With Nokia out of the picture, Motorola is the best when it comes to voice and call quality. Period. No reviews really focus on this most important aspect. We use phones primarily for calling, right?
  
  9. Ergonomics. MXS is known for the feel of the phone. The phone feels solid in the hand and the curved back with silicone finish gives that confidence (that you will not drop it) which you will never get from the all-metal body phones... the moto dimple at the back will also grow on you. Again kudos to Moto designers who hit a very high screen to body ratio...
  
  10. Finally, the software. As smooth as any nexus, brilliantly optimized for android, wayyyy smoother than any non-Nexus phones (and that includes the likes of S6 or OP2, which I have used). Hopefully Marshmallow will always exist.
  

  Time for the negatives, focusing on the real ones and not the perceived ones)
  
  1. The top speaker is slightly weaker than bottom speaker, it shows up a bit when you see good quality videos without earphones. You will only notice if you are an audiophile. But I guess it's better that the last years MX where the top speaker was kept mute during video plays
  
  2. The pocket to ear gesture to activate moto assist do not always work
  
  3. The 2.5D glass is curved at the edges, chances of breaking a bit high. The bumper provided (or any case which covers the sides) tend to touch the tempered glass protectors and break the edges. Better to use plastic screen guards than tempered glass if you are using a bumper case type of protection
  
  4. The earphones are good but I would still recommend investing on a good set of earbuds.
  
  5. The camera app is somewhat less friendly for serious shooters. I miss the Sony app... Trying out other third party apps...
  


  If you are looking to buy a good phone, buy this no questions asked, if your budget is 25k, borrow 5-6k and buy this... if your budget is 70k, buy this phone, go to Goa for the weekend and take me out for a dinner treat after you return ;)

  One of the biggest disappointment with this phone. Though motorola has given 3000mah battery it doesn't give proper back up. Max 8 hrsI got from it and I feel a software update may fix this issue. Turbo charging as claimed by Motorola is really upto the Mark.

column6: Simply the best smartphone - A Smartphone in every sense.

I was waiting for this phone since last 3-4 months when it was announced by Motorola. I am a resident of Middle East and this phone being not yet launched here, I was awaiting for the availability of 32GB version on Flipkart.
  

  Before that, I have gone through all relevant videos (reviews & comparison) of this phone on YouTube and I must say I took the correct decision to buy it as this phones beats all other Flagship phones in almost all departments.
  

  I was about to buy Samsung Galaxy Note 4 as Moto X Style was not available in Middle east. But somehow I waited, went to India in Diwali and ordered it.
  

  Hats of to Flipkart for a faster delivery. I ordered this phone on 2nd November 2015, but somehow it was cancelled by Flipkart on 4th November 2015. I reordered it on 4th Nov and Flipkart delivered on 6th Nov. Superb courier service Flipkart - The packaging was as usual great!
  

  Coming to the PROS and CONS of this phone.
  

  PROS:
  

  1) First impressions - 10/10. Its feel is simply premium and eye-catching. I have used iPhone and have seen Note 4 too, but trust me,  there is no comparison at all. This phone has its own charisma. The back cover is so soft and grippy that there are no chances of slipping over from your hand. The metal frame around the edges extrudes a premium feel. The phone is the smallest in the market to fit a 5.7 inch screen - Best Screen to Body ratio ever. Its really pocketable but sometimes difficult to use it with one hand - unless you have bigger hands.
  

  2) One of the thinnest bezels I have ever came across in smartphones - 10/10
  

  3) The curved back and dimple on the back is fantastic from ergonomic point of view - 10/10
  

  4) The Quad HD 5.7 inch display is a winner of this phone. Watching videos, browsing and playing games gives you a beautiful feeling to your eyes - 10/10
  

  5) Camera of this phone takes stunningly beautiful photographs in outdoors in natural light and indoors that are brightly lit. That doesn't mean that low light photos are bad either - But I would say u need stable hands for better pics in low light  - 9/10
  

  6) Pure Android experience is simply the best UI I have ever used. I was frustrated with iOS using on my iphone. 10/10

column3: Moto X Style (White and Champagne, 16 GB)
column6: A Flagship Device worth Half the Price...!! Go for it..!!
column7:
I am a gadget freak and am in a constant search of the perfect smartphone. Alas, I have not found it yet. Though the Moto X Style comes quite close. Hence the rating of 5 Star cause any device which can be even compared to the perfect phone of my dreams is worth the 5 Star Rating.
  

  First the Cons.
  

  1. Battery Life is just about average. Even after the Android Marshmallow Update.
  

  2. It will be very hard, if not impossible, to find a decent Tempered Glass Screen Protector.
  

  3. Camera is just about above average in low light condition. Another thing, the camera interface sucks and Motorola needs to update it.
  

  4. No Fingerprint Scanner. I mean is it a necessity, not at all. I mean not for me. I have a smart watch and all my devices are configured to keep it unlocked when they detect my smartwatch nearby so I have no need to unlock it. Also I am not a RAW Agent or a Spy who needs to secure highly classified national security documents with a fingerprint.
  

  Now the Pros.
  

  1. Amazing Screen Quality. Its 2K or QHD and blah blah blah, none of it matters. This is one amazing screen which is quite color accurate and very bright. Black are deep but not Samsung AMOLED Deep. Also the side bezels, which is the black or white area around the screen, is very thin, almost the thinnest in a smartphone.
  

  2. Front facing, Stereo Speakers which are very very loud. This is probably the loudest speakers you can get on a phone, with amazing sound quality. This is one of the very few phones which I do not have to keep at maximum volume.
  

  3. Amazing camera quality, in day time or with good to average lighting. Comparable to any other flagship camera. The focus is fast and accurate. With ultra fast shutter speed.
  

  4. Micro SD Card support and with the Android Marshmallow Update, this become an even amazing feature. After update you can merge the Internal Memory and External SD Card Memory into one single block. For example in other devices you get a 32 GB Internal Memory and you can get a 32 GB Micro SD Card, but all the apps (like Whatsapp, Large Games, etc.), will always use the internal storage for storing Data. The Micro SD Card will only be used for storing media files such as Photos, Videos and/or Music. But after update in Moto X Style, it become 1 single Storage. For example, I have a 32 GB Moto X Style with 128 GB Samsung Micro SD XC Card UHS-1 so after everything I have a single 150 GB of Storage which will be available for all apps. No Internal/External Storage. 1 Single Storage.
  

  5. Turbo Charging. Do not get fooled by Fast Charging of other phones. This is Qualcomm Quickcharge 2.0 and "the fastest charging phone in the world". Normal fast chargers use a 9W charger, other with faster charging use, 15W Charger while Moto uses a whopping 25W Charger. The whole battery charges from 0-100 in about 70-80 mins and in about 20-25 mins, you can get about 50% battery.
  

  6. Finally Performance. Any device above 25000 Rs would get your job done. Most of the time. I am currently using a Oneplus One with Snapdragon 801 - 3GB RAM, a Samsung Galaxy Note 4 with Snapdragon 805 - 3 GB RAM, a Moto X Style with Snapdragon 808 - 3 GB RAM and a ZTE Nubia Z9 with Snapdragon 810 - 3 GB RAM and all of these devices have almost similar performance, most of the time. Only in a very high end game like the Asphalt 8 of Modern Combat 5 or NOVA 3 with Graphics set to extreme or highest, can you see a minor difference. The Snapdragon 810 heats up the fastest, then performance gets throttled and the device still performs well. FOR HEATING ISSUES - READ THIS CAREFULLY. ALL ABOVE DEVICES HEAT UP WITH EXTREME GAMING OF ABOUT 15-20 MINS. NONE BECOMES UNABLE TO USE.
  

  Meanwhile for Moto X Style, there is no lag in anything, performance is buttery smooth. 3 GB RAM is plenty for hardcore multitasking.
  

  7. One of the first devices to get Android Marshmallow Update. All others will have to wait till next year unless you buy a Nexus.
  

  To sum it up, Moto X Style is a great device. A Must buy for this price. I understand that this is cheaper to buy all over the world and it is overpriced in India but 32000 is a price you would be happy to pay for t. I mean, considering most flagship phones, the minimum you have to pay for a top end phone is almost 40000 and even then you would have to compromise in certain areas.

column3: Moto X Style (White and Champagne, 16 GB)
column7:
I bought Moto X Style as a replacement to my Moto G1(as I was running out of storage) and after comparing the features of Redmi Note 3, Moto X Play, Moto G4, One Plus 3, Samsung.
  
  After using this mobile for 5 months, I write this.
  

  Processor (5/5):
  
  Snapdragon 808 provides a smooth and lag free performance for 4k videos and games with high end graphics.
  

  Display (5/5):
  
  QHD display with such a high pixel density has really enabled a crystal clear view of pictures. Though, it won't be as good as an AMOLED.
  

  Camera(4/5):
  
  Macro images are fantastic! Could have been a better performer under low light. Video recording is brilliant. However, mobile gets heated when recording 4K videos.
  
  Front flash is an added advantage, though I'm not using it much.
  

  Battery(5/5):
  
  I observed the following, keeping the display brightness at about 10% of the maximum brightness.
  
  1. Routine Life: I charge my battery to 100% everyday morning. Connected to WiFi / Data all the day. Browse and chat. And still would be left with 40-50% of life by EoD. So, it is more than enough.
  
  2. For special occasions like traveling, where mobile network connectivity will not be stable all the time and camera is heavily used: Good enough for capturing 250+ photos under daylight. But almost dead by the EoD. With a power bank backup, we are on a safer side.
  

  Audio (5/5):
  
  The dual speakers in the front provides an enhanced sound quality. Unlike other Moto phones, X Style has good quality ear phone which makes us feel the equalizer in a better way. Also, it sits in the ear cartilages perfectly.
  

  Storage (5/5):
  
  I bought the 16GB variant. Usable memory is 9GB and I use a 32GB memory card. Unlike other mobiles in the market, this supports a dual sim and micro SD card support together. Also, with Android M, the external memory card could also be configured as an internal memory. So more space for apps.
  
  I'm wondering why Flipkart has a note mentioning that it has a hybrid sim/microSD card slot!
  

  Notifications (4/5):
  
  The screen flashes to provide us the notification. I miss the notification LED which was in Moto G1. I was surprised that this mobile has an invisible notification LED which turns on only when you connect the charger after the battery is dead. Strange, isn't it?
  

  Android (5/5):
  
  Launched with Android L.. Upgraded to M. Update to Android N is on the cards. Excited!
  

  Turbo Charging (5/5):
  
  This is a great technology which almost every mobile has. Don't panic when the mobile heats up while charging. Which such a high charging rate, heating is a normal phenomenon.
  

  Customer Support (5/5):
  
  I had a problem which i found after 2 weeks of buying. While watching videos on YouTube in full screen mode, the display turns off randomly. A worried I, had a chat with the Moto customer support. I was asked to do some tests in safe mode. At the end realized that a 3rd party app, which I installed for monitoring the outputs of different sensors in this mobile was causing this problem. After uninstalling this, the problem got resolved.
  

  Price (4/5):
  
  I bought this for an offer price of 20,999 INR in Flipkart, which I feel is the right price for this mobile. Otherwise the mobile is overpriced.
  

  Overall (5/5):
  
  I'm a happy customer with yet another Moto device.

column3: Moto X Style (White and Champagne, 16 GB)
column7:
Hi guys,
  

  I bought my moto X style 16gb black colour on 3rd october during the Flipkart big billion days for a price of 15.3K. I would firstly like to thank Flipkart for delivering the product in the given timeframe and also for a discount of nearly 50% on this amazing phone. 5/5 to Flipkart in this regard. My phone is hardly 10 days old and I am certainly very happy with it. Please read below my review:
  

  1. In box accessories: a) Handset
  
  b)Turbo charger
  
  c) 3 manuals out of which one is the warranty booklet
  
  d) Sim pin as it has a sim tray
  
  e) Earphones
  
  f) Bumper case (useless)
  
  I was going to buy a moto g4 plus 32 gb. But when I got to know about this offer, I weighed the pros and cons of both the phones and I finally decided to buy this phone.
  

  2. Display: This is the thing that really stood out for this phone. It has a 5.7 inch display with the resolution of 2560x1440 and 520ppi. Let me clarify that it is not an AMOLED or SUPER AMOLED  display that we find on Samsung phones but it is at par with some of the best in the market. If you put it on maximum brightness you will see those vibrant colours of the display but I would suggest not to do this as it can be harmful to your eyes. Adaptive brightness works like a charm, when you are out there in the sun the brightness shoots up and when you are in the dark, it dims and is soothing to the eyes. I would like to say that moto has done a wonderful job in this aspect and I would like to grade this part 5/5.
  

  3. Design: The phone is curved allowing a 5.7 inch display to fit in. Although it is a 5.7 inch it does not feel cumbersome and fits nicely in one's hand. The sides of the phone have a metallic frames with antenna lines at the bottom and at the top. The back of the phone is plastic. It is not one of those cheap looking plastic backs but works like an anti-skid surface and really looks nice. It is upto you if you want a back cover or not but looks classy even without one. So, I rate this area 5/5.
  

  4. Camera: The phone boasts of a 21 Mp primary camera and a 5MP front camera. The photos that I have clicked till now are of good quality and the zoomed in pictures are also not blurred. The auto focus is fast and captures bright and sharp pictures. The selfie camera also takes decent selfies. Haven't tried the phone for low light photography but once I do, I will update the observation. I request people to not compare this phone with S7 edge and iPhone 6s or 7 because it would be unfair to compare a 30k phone's camera with a 60k phone's camera. Save that money and buy a DSLR :D. I rate this part 4.5/5
  

  Storage: I bought the 16GB version but the phone also has a 32GB version. Although, memory should not be problem as it is expandable upto 128GB. When you open the phone and go to storage and usb, the memory is close to 9.6GB out of which 6Gb was taken by android OS. But after you install marshmallow update, you can  pair your SD card with your phone's internal storage. I had a 8 GB SD card and after pairing it with my internal storage memory rose to 24GB. 5/5 in this area to Google for making this update.
  

  OS: The phone came pre-installed with lollipop but as soon as I opened up the phone I got the marshmallow update and 2 Android security update's. This phone can at max take 2 more versions of android updates. There was no pre-installed apps in the phone just stock android UI and it works fluidly. 5/5 in this regard.
  

  Performance: The phone has a 1.8 GHz Hexa core Qualcomm Snapdragon 808 processor and a 3GB RAM. Till now the phone has not shown any kind of lag and multi tasking is very smooth with the 3GB Ram. I play a lot of games like clash of clans, Boom beach, FIFA 15, Asphalt 8 and everything works perfectly fine and the gaming experience is too good. With marshmallow update, you can now monitor your RAM management and it never exceeds 2GB out of the available 2.5GB RAM. I would suggest that you download some RAM cleaning apps. It has really helped me keep my RAM down to 1.8GB. I would give a 5/5 to this aspect also.
  

  Battery: One of the main concerns of the phone. Turbo charger charges your phone from 10%-90% in 50 mins. Screen and android Os are main battery suckers. It provides an on screen time of 9 hrs with moderate usage and around 5 hours with heavy usage. I would give 5/5 to turbo charger and 3/5 to the battery life.
  

  Sound: This phone scores in this department as well. Sound output is good, although the earphones are not of an exceptional quality!
  

  All in all the phone is an excellent device with the only drawback being it's battery life.
  

  Thank you for reading this review :D

column3: Moto X Style (White and Champagne, 16 GB)
column6: You just can't go much wrong with it.
column7:
So I received my Moto X Style on 1st Nov and had a couple of days to check it out befor writing this review.
  
  First of all The build  is Sexy and  feels  premium in Hand and the Rubberised textured back makes its super grippy. Its primarily a two handed device but I can get through some casual fuctionalities with one hand.
  
  Display is crisp and awesome (Its not amoled but that's not a deal breaker for me )
  
  Sounds get really loud and clear and it certainly enhances your experience if you are a gamer and also does the same for other multimedia experiences. Decent enough in-ear headphones available in the box (its not great but not bad)
  
  Camera in daylight is awesome but quality takes a bit of a hit with low light shots but that's the case with every smartphone. In daylight its comparable with all other super high-end flagships in the market. The colours are vibrant not too saturated, which is nice and offers lots of details as you would expect from a 21 megapixel shooter. In case of low light, ehh not so much but its certainly not bad either.Front facing camera also does a good enough job. I wish they update the camera software a bit, its way too simple for my liking. You can certailnly use third party apps in this case.
  
  Performance is snappy as you would expect from motorola. With near stock android and a strong processor multi-tasking is a breeze on this device and seriously there has been no lags till now. Moto features are really useful although its not perfect all the time but still works really well most of the time. There has been no issues with gaming on this device although I am not that big of a gamer on my phone. But It handles heavy games really well from what I experienced.
  
  The phone certainly heats up after extended gaming and while charging with the turbo charger provided in the box. But it never got extremely hot and i did not face any heating issues with regular usage.
  
  Micro-sd card expansion is awesome and so I picked up the 16 gigs and when marshmallow hits the device I can turn my SD card storage in Internal storage of the phone so am waiting for it. Still you get 9.50gb out of the box which is cool if you don't store your media on the phone's memory.
  
  And uhh you get a free bumper. I don't think am ever gona use it but well you can't complain on free stuff. xP
  
  Call quality is great and its gets good signal strength.
  
  No fingerprint scanner, not much of a big deal if you don't use NFC much. And I really don't get the point of having a finger print scanner just to bypass the lock screen. Seems redundant to me for that purpose only. I don't know, its just me. But for NFC users a finger print scanner would have been great but its not a deal breaker.
  
  The battery is pretty average. May be, it can last a full day with low or moderate use but you will need to plug in the charger more often than not if you are a heavy user. I hope It gets better over time. And did I mention how awesome the turbo charger is ?It works like a charm and charges it super fast.
  

  All in all if your looking for a top end phone but don't wanna pay the 40k or 50k or even 60k price of other falgships, then this is it. This is the real deal and you cannot get wrong with this. Priced at 30k its still competes with the top end flagships in the market and stays in the fight !!!

column3: Moto X Style (White and Champagne, 16 GB)
column6: You won't go wrong buying this product
column7:
This is a comprehensive review of moto x style 16 gb variant
  
  I have been using this phone from past few days and here's what i found
  

  Display
  
  Quad hd screen. Its sheer beauty to look at this screen.though its a downgrade from the last year super amoled display but the LCD panel is super crisp and clear. Add to this the 2k resolution you get sharper text and vibrant colors. Watching 2k videos on YouTube is a charm.
  

  Camera
  
  The camera as far I have used is brilliant. My past phone was a lg g2 and comparing it to moto x style it was much better than that. Though the moto x lacks the ois but you will not feel it in real life usage. The focus is fast. The Google camera app is very basic with very less control over camera overall the rear camera produces rich colorful photos in daylight but struggles in a bit in night due to smaller sensor size. The front camera with flash is an added advantage and produces average selfies.
  

  Video
  
  The moto x style has three video modes . full hd, slo mo@720p and 4k video recording. Though you might be feeling that because moto x lacks ois the videos recording may be suffering but no the inbuilt digital stabilisation is great. Slo mo videos are not as smooth as you would expect too. 4k video contains a lot of details and videos are a bit on cooler side with less saturation and contrast. So its all upon your preference
  

  Storage
  
  Moto x style comes in two variants 16gb and 32gb. Initially you should go for 32gb
  
  NOTE with the android marshmallow update you can use your memory card to act as internal storage. So for eg you insert a memory card of 32gb yo can encrypt that card (it will ask for your confirmation) and it will act as internal storage. So if you don't want to shell out extra 2k this feature will come in as handy.
  

  Battery
  
  On marshmallow expect an on screen time of 4 hours to 4 and a half hours with medium usage. About the heating the phone do gets a little warm but I won't say its get hot. The best thing is that the phone comes along with tubro charger so with your switched off the phone will be fully juiced up in about 80 minutes.
  

  Sound
  
  Best speaker in class. Believe me moto x style puts htc boomsound to shame. Moto x style has the best speakers in the market today and it won't let you down. Though the headphones provided are average. Buy the speakers quality isind blowing.
  

  Performance
  
  Motorolla did a good move by not going for the snapdragon 810 due to its heating issues and opted to go with LG policy of opting hexacore 808 processor resulting in fluid performance. Apps open up quickly. Though while typing with the Google keyboard you will notice a bit lagginess but not too much I will say.
  
  Build quality
  
  Being a 5.7inch phone you would think twice before buying this. But Motorola has done a good job here too. The phone has great ergonomics. The back is curved a little bit to give that great solid hold over the phone it never feels slippery. The back is kind of rugged and rubbery.
  

  Note- I would suggest this phone for anyone going for nexus 6p and even 5x because in real life it performs at par with nexus 6p and even better than 5x (though you will have to give up the fingerprint)
  
  Rest its a great phone with a user affordable price tag . though I miss the moto maker as currently its not available in India. Sad.

column6: Ppbly the smartest upgrage you can make in 2015
column7:
If you have plans to buy this phone, hope my review proves helpful.
  
  I set out with a budget of 60k to buy a phone and my requirements were
  
  >Dual Sim >Expandable Storage >Decent Cameras >No locked up o/s that i'll have to jailbreak >5.5"+screen size >Above full hd display >Native 4k video recording >Enough juice for a normal day >Wireless charging or at least fast charging >Lag free performance.
  
  With these requirements the iphone was already out of the scene. And i was left with
  
  G4, S6 edge+ and 1+2 , Knocked out the edge+ because i didn't find any sense in such a good hardware on a 1440p phone and in daily usage i wont have any benefits of it.
  
  But the camera is ppbly the best in the market if you include low light situations . 1+2 was like a jackpot to purchase and at the end of the day its not a brand i'm familiar with was more of an alternative to the XPlay..so skipped it too. G4 vs X Style . G4 has blurring on the sides of the pics captured which is a sign of poor lens built. Rest of the hardware specs were pretty close except for the dual sim 4G. And i believe the moto's cam had the potential to put out very good pics in daylight...at night it will suffer from the aperture which is 2.0 and a tad higher ; but with a well optimized app you can bring out a bright and crisp picture from a down-sampled 21 mp pic to about say 8mp which can throw the competition to dust with the pixel advantage...I'm working on an app...but apparently the latest camera update from moto has dramatically improved focusing issues and low light photography seems to have improved a lil bit. If i succeed in tweaking the best out of the sensor, expect my App on the appstore soon named XMCAM(for Motorola 21/5mp sensors) . So i finally made my decision to buy this. Well on a tighter budget the MotoXPlay is a very good option too. No native 4k and down to 2 gb ram and a 1080p display...but for all practical reasons...still very good.And the battery backup is good enough for two days and you get the same camera.
  
  Back to my review
  
  The phone is sturdy. Has a premium finish. Fits your hand just as well as a 5"phone. Front cam is pretty wide and the front flash really helps. No notification light...but the display will turn on when you are nearby or give it a look or shake it...so no issues. Display is bright and decent...comparable to the G4 but S6 is absolutely brilliant. Also screen might be unevenly lit if you look very carefully...but livable. Battery...will take you through a day after the first couple of charge cycles under normal use. Internal memory is faster than external(sd) stick to 32GB version for all practical reasons. Heating issues is not something to worry, normal with phones with this specifications in this generation.
  
  For me, the camera, dual sim, expandable storage, 1440p diplay at 5.7" and the price were deal breakers . Hope it wins your heart too. If you love photography, get the lens kit for the phone...it works pretty well :)
  

  Oh..the stereo speakers are pretty loud too and front firing is a really big advantage while watching or sharing a video or a song.

column3: Moto X Style (White and Champagne, 16 GB)
column7:
Posting this review after one year of usage. The is one of the few large screen phones with full dual SIM capability and a dedicated memory slot (Not a hybrid SIM). It tends to heat up a bit during charging but nothing major. DO NOT reboot the phone while it is charging or it will go into an endless loop as it happened with me. I had to order a replacement and Flipkart customer service aren't exactly the smartest around. The 2.1A turbo charger is very handy as it charges the phone to 60-70  in approx 15 mins when down to 3-15  charge. The battery life isn't bad with ~5 hrs of continuous use (I mean continuous- YouTube, music, surfing, calls) and you can easily eke out a full days worth if you keep the phone on silent and switch off vibration mode. The ringtones given with the phone are quite nice. The display of the phone is pretty good with quad HD and watching HD videos are a joy. The speakers are also quite decent but this depends on the original recording. Since the speakers are dual front-facing, the sound is clear and stereophonic when recorded that way. The earphones that come with the box are quite good but not as good as those that come from Sony or Apple although, this is hardly a negative. It's advisable to use the phone with a flip cover to protect the screen. Even though I've dropped it on its face a few times the screen wasn't scratched in the least and the raised steel stubs of the two front speakers prevent the glass from touching the surface. Overall, the phone is a delight to handle without a casing due to its curved and sleek design but as mentioned, it's worth getting that cover just to preserve it that way should you ever decide to sell it. The UI is typical of Motorola- free of bloatware and with the latest updates.  Playing games isn't my thing on phones but I've experimented with Asphalt which seemed to run without a glitch but I'd suggest checking reviews on Google for that. The camera is pretty good with video recordings in 4k exceptional. However, pictures taken in low light aren't that good. This is a good phone but at 28k slightly over priced. I got mine at 21k through a sale on flipkart and I'd suggest either waiting or picking up a Samsung 32Gb phone due to its  resale value. I've deducted one star bec the first instrument I recvd hung up and had to be replaced as well as owing to Flipkart's  customer service.

column3: Moto Z Play with Style Mod (Black, 32 GB)
column7:
Okay I have exchanged my moto g3 with moto z play with a good discount of 5900 and I have got this phone on 20th of Oct (writing review on 21th, Oct)
  

  Built quality
  
  Am an old moto customer and built quality of moto is always good, I did had some problem with moto e but moto z play is awesome with built quality keys at right are nicely designed and the body look heavy and smart too.
  

  Software
  
  Qctacore as you all must be kbowing, phone works smooth no lags I have found yet, it starts up good, only thing I hate I lenevo which comes to display when you start the phone but you have to live with it so can't help that.
  

  Camera
  
  Camera quality is little better than moto g4+ if you or your friends have that not too much difference HDR is always good. Selfies cam has a flash which works okay. Overall both the rear and front camera are not that awesome but are okay you can take good clicks. Maybe moto mod cam can help you for a pro shot.
  

  Battery
  
  Now it's has a good battery trust me. Just turn your phone off and exactly in 80 min to 85 min (as I have recorded) your phone will be 98-100% if it was 5% initially. A morning recharge will run your phone all through the day with continuous internet on, games, music, camera in between and will end up with 10-15% battery while you go to bed.
  

  Sensor
  
  Sensor works awesomely well, just touch and it locks and unlocks very smartly it's same with moto g4+ too.
  
  Touch is as usual fantastic like other Motos.
  

  Few negatives
  
  Sim card and SD tray is smart but if have you have change your  sim in some problem then can't really help it as it opens with a moto needle tool. This might hurt you
  

  If you're expecting a exceptionally good camera than think twice
  

  Again you can't see your battery like other Motos ( few people hate this )
  

  Charging slot is different as that of common charging slot so now you can compare it with iPhone chargers actually. ( But I don't think you will need charging that soon) Plus point is that moto gives a USB chord separately from turbo charger which can help you.
  

  Size is little big small hands should think twice.
  

  You will not get any tempered glass or any sought of screen guard, however it's gorilla glass but still Indian environs are too dusty. What I have done is that I have used a nail paint remover over the screen guard which comes with the phone and will wait for screen guards to come in the market. So you can also use this hack for sometime and trust me it works good.
  


  So this was my review don't trust me blindly and check for negatives reviews too.
  
  Thank-you

column6: Great Smartphone! A Bit Heavy, But Dashing! My Full Review ~
column7:
Its a Beast! Love it in White! The moment I started using it, I immediately felt that its a great buy in terms on Performance, Looks, Sound, Camera and Battery. I applied the screen protector front and back the moment I got the phone and a Shockproof clear case which also takes care of the back camera bump. My full honest review is as follows :
  

  1) Performance :
  
  The main small and big points people should know about performance is that the apps install so quickly! Motorola has balanced/tweaked this phone's hardware and software so well that I have not noticed a single lag! There were 1 or 2 apps where the app crashed but worked normal after opening them again... let me tell you "this happens in all the android phones no matter what the price range". I noticed just one time frame drop in asphalt 8 when I played it for the first time after install, apart from this no lag in other heavy games that I played. The speed by which it opens the apps, keyboard open n type, fingerprint unlocking (100% accurate for me), phone dialer and after call if you have 3rd party app call recorder to show summary of the recording pop-up to open, app drawer, Camera, Gestures, etc all is just BLAZING fast and super smooth! Love to keep the animations on .5x , .5x and 1x (in developer options).
  

  2) Looks :
  
  Its big, not a compact 5.5 inch Beast. It has killer looks and style! The feel is also great in the hand... Just a bit heavy as its understandable due to the bigger battery. Display is great but not the best i have seen. Few icons like snapchat, airtel, etc looks cartoonish, like too much color and shine... like popin out 3d . Though music videos, clarity, viewing angles & experience and colors are awesome . I don't feel anything being washed out or anything at all.
  

  3) Sound :
  
  Loud Speaker of the Z PLAY is somewhat I feel like iphone 5s's speaker . Not exactly the same.... but better having more bass and clarity in it and the good part is that it is loud. Good while watching YouTube videos too.
  
  A little dislike about the software while on a call with the in-call speaker volume is, if i reduce the volume while on call of course or while its ringing and complete the talk, and then dial any other number and check the in-call speaker volume level, the volume is back again up to full itself! This never happened in Htc M8 or other phones which i was previously using. It remained to where i had reduced or increased it. On this phone i will need to always reduce the volume manually if required. A software fix should come asap to fix this small issue, so that where i kept the in-call speaker volume to be, it should stay there throughout . Shockingly when I adjust the volume level of the loud speaker on call, that remains to where I had set it even on all next calls I make. Maybe its glitch Motorola/Lenovo missed or I need to reset my phone.
  

  4) Camera :
  
  Camera takes better than decent photos. Laser autofocus is really great! Clear and crisp images. Front camera is nice too Haven't tested the video recording yet. Love the selfie photo mirror option!
  

  5) Battery :
  
  Wow! Battery of this phone is amazing. I have charged it only once from 9% to a 100% full and right now live its been 14 hours and 17 mins since last charge. I have used it to click photos, play 2-3 games (5-5 mins), Install 2-3 heavy games, Made Calls, 45 to 1 hour in total of youtube videos and playing audio songs. 40% Brightness level. Still battery level is 51% remaining. Its fantabulous! Turbo charging is amazing!! Many quick chargers/dash charge just charge quickly to a level of 60 to 70%, but this keeps turbo charging till full 100%.
  

  In the end I give it a 9 out of 10.... I love it! 1 point taken as it doesn't supports miracast/mirroring even if your smart tv has it. You need to have google chromecast to mirror phone's display on your led,smart tv, etc(if your smart tv does not have inbuilt chromecast). I have bought jbl soundboost mod and they are on their way, have not used them yet..... I'm sure the audio and video experience will be on the whole another level and I might change it to a 10 then :P . Being a lover of music and balance, I say its better than 3 or 3t as I would hate bluetooth speakers, low battery back-up efficiency(that's why gimmick dash charge, keep charging is there) and too much power is trouble ;). Hope this honest review helps a lot of you guys out there! Go for it!

column3: Moto Z Play with Style Mod (Black, 32 GB)
column7:
I've been using this product for the past 3 days. I took my time before writing a review here as I wanted to assess this device in a better way. So, as other reviewers do, I too want to sum up things by mentioning the Pros and Cons of this device.
  

  Pros:
  

  Battery Backup
  
  Crisp Display
  
  Highly responsive Fingerprint Sensor
  
  Turbo Charge
  
  NFC
  
  Rear Camera
  
  Moto Display
  
  Near-stock Android Experience
  
  Dual SIM (Not Hybrid) with dedicated SD card slot
  

  Cons:
  

  A little heavy device (3510 mAh battery is the reason)
  
  Large bezels
  
  Not-so-good front camera
  

  As some reviewers are complaining about heating while charging the device, for their information, it's pretty common. The device, when connected to TurboCharger, draws more power than conventional chargers in order to charge the battery faster. This excessive power draw results in heating of the device. For others, who are looking for Restart option while holding down the power button, it is not there. Motorola provides a stock Android experience and no stock Android comes with a Restart option (Check Nexus devices).
  

  The device literally stays cool while playing games for a longer time. For graphics-intensive games, any device is bound to get warm, so that's not an issue here. I, personally, haven't felt heat on this device if the device is not connected to TurboCharger. Moto Display is good, saves your time if you want to check notifications on your device without unlocking it. Moto Voice works flawlessly and the fingerprint scanner is pretty fast.
  

  Bezels could have been made shorter and the device would have been not-so-huge then, but we had to sacrifice the battery. The battery lasts long, in a true sense. I charged the battery at 11.30 PM the day before yesterday to 100% and even after being always connected to the WiFi, playing games (for more than 2 hours), messaging, downloading several apps and watching video clips online, the level is now at 38% ( today at 5.30 PM). I believe the SD 625 is the reason here, no excessive power draw and unnecessary overheating. The processor clocked at 2.0 GHz (max) does it's job in multitasking, though I think 4GB of RAM should have been there (memory management is not good if you suspend heavy games in the background).
  

  The rear camera takes photos really quick and clear both in daylight and artificial lights. The colour of the flash is natural warm (a bit yellowish) and I don't know if others too experience this. But both the cameras take photos without much yellow tint (with flash). A 8MP front camera could have been a better choice, though. The front-facing speaker is not so loud, but I can't say it's not good.
  

  Till now, it's a good choice to buy this device. People who are looking for OnePlus 3 over this Moto Unit, please keep in mind, you may not get a good servicing for your product, if, at all, your device needs to visit it's respective service center.
  

  I will update this review if the experience changes or if there's something important that is needed to be shared.

column3: Moto Z Play with Style Mod (Black, 32 GB)
column7:
Really I was waiting for this device for quite some time and it's a beast. Got this phone on exchange and other offers combined at 17k which is a stellar deal! Ordered on 17th and got it in a day delivery. Flipkart always does a great job in delivery and exchange offers. It does included a diagnostic function to check your old phone condition! Flipkart app service is wonderful.
  

  I love Moto for its close to pure Android experience and quick updates. I was comparing many phones which are flagship on paper but one or the other lack SD card slot, hybrid SIM slot, custom UI (which i don't like after used to pure android experience) and full of bloatwares, which impacts the performance.
  

  It handles multi tasking in ease and to surprise, no heating issues. App installation is very fast and performance is a real beast. Never felt a lag...very smooth. I have installed close to 50apps and it did completed download and installation real quick. I think users won't be able to notice the difference of SD 820 or SD 625! I am not a hard core gamer but watch lots and lots of videos and listen music and heavy browsing. It works perfect for my usage.
  

  It heats up a bit while charging but not real hot. The quick charger does wonders in charging the phone from 60 to 100  in 20mins! Noticed that it gets bit warm in non-AC conditions with heavy usage but still performing like a breeze!
  

  Moto display and other gestures to open torch and camera are quite useful. I was bit skeptical about using finger print scanner but it supports 5 finger print options. That's really a good add on.
  

  16mp camera works fine in outdoor light conditions but lacks in low light conditions. For selfie lovers it does have front flash too.
  

  I used dual sim and noticed only either one of the SIM slot supports 4G, not both. When you use single sim then irrespective of the sim slot it does supports 4G. The SIM and SD card tray is bit tricky when you try to insert it...it gets stuck sometimes and you need to push a bit hard.
  

  Another oversight by Moto is, it doesn't have a Gallery app and no FM too. Users can download gallery apps from playstore but i like the default one provided in other Moto phones.
  

  Super AMOLED FHD screen looks cool... colors are vibrant and vivid even under the sun. I am not sure it does have a gorilla glass protection as Moto site or Flipkart specs didn't mention about it.
  

  Call quality and data reception is really good. The speaker on the front does a good job when you turn on the loudspeaker. Sound enough but i don't personally like listening over loud speaker. Listening through headset is awesome and sound is crystal clear and pleasing. I use Sennheiser CX 180 Street II which further enhances the listening experience. For this price, Moto should have provided a better headset as the one provided in the box is cheap.
  

  The box also has a USB cable and the charging adapter is a fixed one. So users can't switch the adapter if any fault.
  

  The another weird thing is, Moto has organised volume rocker and power button awkwardly, especially the split of volume rocker and placing power button below the volume rocker. Users will get confused with the power button and volume rocker till they get use to it.
  

  By default the phone has a Moto ringtone but no choices of default ringtones except this one. The default one is longer for a SMS/Whatsapp notification. User has to download notification ringtones if they need a short and crisp tones.
  

  The package includes a mod style shell which fits perfectly and gives a good grip to the phone. But I felt bit bulky and heavy as I am used to a 5inch phone for quite sometime. Moto should have launched a Z play Mini with 5inch size...that would be great for me.
  

  Further exploring the phone and will update my review soon. Overall it's a beautiful beast and does its job perfectly. Really worth the wait!

column3: Moto Z Play with Style Mod (Black, 32 GB)
column7:
The Moto Z series is here to stay.
  

  I'll try to be as objective as possible and there will be a few comparisons drawn out with the Moto X Style because that was my previous phone.
  

  Right off the box, the looks are stunning, I bought the white variant and it just blew me away. Premium looks made much more premium with the camera bump.
  

  The volume and power buttons are placed awkwardly. The placement in the Moto X was good but with time you get adjusted easily. USB C and 3.5mm jack at the bottom make for a deadly combo. You can never be left out!
  

  Whoever is calling this phone 'thicker' is messing with your head. It is much lighter and slimmer than the moto x. The style mod though makes it bulky but it is good looking.
  

  If you're stepping down from a QHD IPS display like me, the display on Moto Z is very likely to confuse you. It is a sAMOLED full HD display with an awkward DPI at 480. The icons are large and eat up a lot of space. Native settings in Nougat allow you to change the DPI but they go either too small at 408 or too big at 540. A few ADB commands can alter this and I would advise a DPI between 432 and 440. You can look it up in XDA forums. Do that and you will not want to take your eyes away from the screen.
  

  Deep blacks are appealing but it fails to hit the whitest of whites unless you turn off adaptive brightness. Adaptive brightness somehow keeps the brightness very low and that is coming from someone who prefers low brightness.
  

  Objectively, the sound is decent but nowhere near the Moto X dual front facing speakers.
  

  The cameras in bright lights and daylight are excellent. In low light they are just above ordinary.
  

  The processor makes this an absolute beast. Snapdragon 625 is supposedly the little brother of SD 820 and it has (after a month's use) never ever lagged or stuttered even with heavy multitasking. It was fast and smooth and it was a pleasure to use my phone.
  

  The snappy processor, super AMOLED display and 3GB RAM together make the 3510mAH battery the best in class. Trust me, with light usage you can nick in 3 days. You can walk through a day with extremely heavy usage!
  

  A few other things - the glass can withstand enormous stress so no worries here, The fingerprint sensor is so pragmatically at the right place. Modularity is good but mods (those in the market now) are very expensive. The support for new mods is extremely good so hoping for the best here. Yes, it has VoLTE support and is dual 4G with a separate SD card slot. Oh and Moto has revamped it's apps and they are much much better and Moto voice is much more responsive now. You'll also get Nougat right off the bat!
  

  Final thoughts - In no walk of life I'd ever put this as a midranger, rather a toned down flagship. For the price, modularity, battery and it's surprising ability to compete with other flagships, you will be getting an absolute beast here.
