  1.Its a modular phone . Agreed ! However will u spend another 7K-19K on buying those modules ? If yes, then go for it. If no, then please look into some other phones in this price segment which offers same if not better specs (OP3 , Le 2)
  
  Now even if you don't want to buy the Moto Mods, you can still go for this phone because this is the only phone in this Price Segment which has a separate memory card slot , which for me is a must.
  
  Another major pro in this phone is the Stock Android that this phone has.
  
  Going to other pro's:
  
  The battery back up is fantastic. I almost got 13-14 hrs of screen on time with a single charge and with extensive usage.
  
  Coming to camera: I wouldn't say it's the best in this Price Segment but it takes good pictures  in exterior locations and would do a decent job in low lighting areas as well and the front cam has a flash and you wouldn't have any issues with selfies as well.Overall it has a decent camera that you can't complain much about.
  
  Coming to display : Excellent display .It has an AMOLED screen and the viewing angles are great. Nothing much to say/complain here.
  
  Now the Cons:
  
  It gets a little warm when you charge the phone, especially around the volume and the power button area but that has been intermittent. However haven't experienced any heating issues with extended gaming (Asphalt etc)
  
  The cellular call quality is good but at times I saw my network connection being lost at places where I never had network issues. So I'm not sure if that's an issue with the phone or the network.
  
  The phone doesn't have a dedicated speaker.The speaker at the top for calls act as  an external speaker Hence the Output through the speaker's are not that loud. However the sound through headset is very good.
  
  The modules being sold by the phone are too expensive . Hopefully we get cheaper modules in future.
  
  So in case you need a phone which gives you a decent camera, Excellent battery and an overall good performance in addition to the uniqueness of Modular Phone, you can definetly go for MotoZ Play .
  
  I Hope you find this review helpful.

column3: Moto Z Play with Style Mod (Black, 32 GB)
column7:
It's been more than a week since I got the phone handy.. So, within this period of time and with my way of usage, certainly it's fair enough to review unbiased.. Mainly, I used this mobile for browsing, gaming, apps performance test and to watch live streamed videos on YouTube.
  

  At least, I have been using my mobile for more than 6 hours of on screen time a day to do all my stuffs online. Battery performance is really outstanding with 3510 mAH power and Qualcomm 625 snapdragon processor which is very power efficient. I happened to charge only after 35 hours to 40 hours of my usage once the battery was charged to 95%.. The best part of charging is that it juices the pack for nearly 70% in less than an hour and it completely charges in less than or equally 2 hours.. I charged for precisely 20minutes and got the battery packed from 8% to 35%.. Thanks for Turbo Charging, though I have a con about it which I'm discussing down..
  

  Gaming performance is really stunning for games like Asphalt 8, Modern Combat and Nova3.. I am an extensive gamer and spend at least an hour or two regularly.. No graphics frame drop did I notice with these games.. Almost No or minimal heating issues even after continuous play for an hour..
  

  Screen resolution is good with AMOLED display.. Not very bright though.. Camera performance is good with rear camera in outdoor conditions.. But, fairly average in internal or dull lighting.. Dual LED is an added advantage, though it adds more light to the image..
  

  Touch quality is really good with Corning Gorilla 4 glass with high temperament.. Without any screen guard, you can enjoy the real touch..
  

  With almost 50 apps installed, memory still shows 1.2 GB free out of 3GB.. Sound quality for music and videos is good.. Comparatively, I found its up to par, but Lenovo Vibe K5 Note with Dolby Atmos effect is better than this..
  

  Dual sim slot with dedicated memory slot is a major advantage.. Never had a chance to test Reliance Jio in this week..
  

  Coming to the challenges and talking about cons, major glitch I found is, device heating issue while charging.. The temperature was really above 48 to 50 C.. I'm not sure if it is normal in Turbo charging devices or not. Please confirm if anyone has same issues.. If none has this issue, I ll check with Moto..
  

  Second major issue is, the handset is really slippery with glass finish and it slipped off my hands at least 4 times in last one week.. Luckily on bed.. Hopefully, a solid back cover may help.. Good feel factor is a stock Android experience without any theme..
  

  Certainly a good bet mobile under 25K.. Please share your feedback of this review..

column3: Moto Z Play with Style Mod (Black, 32 GB)
column7:
Brilliant phone in just about every aspect... Display, Battery life, Sound quality ..... Except for the camera. There's something fundamentally wrong with the autofocus system in this model. Its like a hit and miss affair really - 70 percent of the time it will lock focus and you'll end up getting a clear, sharp image .... 30 percent of the time your subject will be completely out of focus and you'll get an unexpectedly blurry photo. The AF behaves erratically when you least expect it. All things considered - during the day you can get some great images... that will easily rival any dedicated point and shoot camera. Low light images are okay... not entirely horrible... but definitely nothing to write home about either - Problem is that since there's no OIS , the camera resorts to drastically increasing the ISO speed - often selecting ISO 2000 - 2500 - And this is precisely where the excess noise is generated from.
  

  The Selfie cam is not bad... does a decent job under good lightling... and becomes a smuge fest in low light.
  

  My main point of concern is the quality control aspect. the first phone I received had a few minor scratches on the screen and pannel covering the camera - signal connectivity issues - and a battery that refused to charge... So got it replaced. Flipkart's customer care and service is outstanding in these matters - Got the second phone a few days later - Thoroughly inspected it to make sure everything was in order - Once again noticed scratches, This time on the back pannel - Plus very fine scratches on the glass housing the camera - and last but not least a small amount of some kind of sticky gel like substance on the back... Nevertheless I decided to keep the phone because I've heard similar complaints from other users of this particular model... and didn't want to wait some days again for another replacement. But it raises doubt over Lenovo / Motorola's quality control especially for Indian manufactured devices.

  -No -VoLTE Video Call and No 3G Video Call support supports only audio calls.

  Could have been better:
  
  -The build design its good but the camera is poped out which is likely to get scratched while placing the phone older Moto's had dipped camera sensor.
  
  -Finger print sensor has eaten a lot of space instead of finger it should have been dual speakers.
  
  -Home Menu Back key n Recent key should have been placed in finger sensor area they have wasted space of the display n left extra empty space on Right n Left of the sensor.
  
  - The reading mode should have been there.

column6: The good, the bad and the bottom line...

The GOOD: No phone offers you the swap-able options as this does. Front camera is 5-megapixel unit and also has a wide-angle lens, its own flash.
  

  The Bad: The SIM slot is hybrid which means you have to give way to one SIM card for extra memory card. :I,  The finger print sensor takes too much space and just makes the phone unnecessarily big. Without the mods the phone is feels quite slippery and wants you to hold it tighter. Screen when compared to S7 is no match, not the quality but the looks. The S7 just looks premium against Z. Some of the mods are really costly, the Hasselblad, the projector is more than the cost of a Moto X play 16 GB. :| ....
  

  The bottom line: Good phone at this price. has everything and more which you would expect from similar ranged phones. Mods are cool and will make you 'the talk of the town' but some are just too expensive to try on. Looks are not that great but performance compensates for it. Unless you are quick changer of phones, this phone with the mods options are great, but if you often change phones, this is not for you.

It has been a month since I am using this phone. Received it on the 16th of April. I am absolutely glad of my purchase but not only wannabe owners of this phone but if Motorola's taking note of feedback take note of a few pointers:
  

  1. Yes, it does overheat. Not complaining about when its charging (its turbo charging a huge battery in under 2 hours! C'mon) but even when sometimes the screen time crosses 30 minutes with constant data usage (that shouldn't happen and that's concerning!) I complained too but my request for replacement got rejected by flipkart (Go Figure!)
  

  2. Volume is moderate for watching content on mobile and playing music in a room. Would have hit the sweet spot if there was a dual speaker at the bottom like on the top. (you listening Moto?)
  

  3. The 2MP front facing camera just seems like a chipped tooth to your snarling 'Beast' 5 MP was a NO BRAINER! Oh and no complaints about the 21MP camera except it would be great to get the 1st click right and not the 3rd or 4th since there is no Optical image stabilizer! (Don't people at Motorola party and click images how does one keep a steady hand then?)
  

  4. Moto - Do provide a factory seal screen on the display atleast! It just makes you look shabby during the end game!
  

  5. Potential buyers listen up - here's something that came to my attention more recently after purchase, Moto Turbo comes with 4G support only on 1800 MHz I do not think it supports 2300Mhz which means your 4G eligibility is device & carrier dependent together. Please do your own research before buying else you ll be missing the 4G train despite getting a ticket, a very expensive ticket
  

  6. Only the above drawbacks makes it seem that the device may have overshot its deserving ceiling price by just about 5-6k. I mean, i wish i had an AM EX credit card but i don't and hence feel overpaid for it slightly
  

  7. This one may be a stretch to complain about but may for the next version - Water Resistant instead of Water Repellent would have been AWESOME!!!!!!
  

  8. Another stretch - The bevel at the bottom looks like a double chin. Could save the half inch there if possible.
  

  OK I ve belted you enough Moto now for a few pats on the back
  

  1. Good Job. To be the pioneers of the next gen specs at a relatively affordable price
  

  2. The colours seem to be protruding from the phone screen. No complaints whatsoever about the display. Its like nothing I ve seen till now.
  

  3. Moto assist is a brilliant piece of tech. Hope it just evolves with user adaption and updates from your end unlike Siri which was just a fad this one could actually be here to stay and is more functional
  

  4. Battery performance is great. Lasts me anywhere between 24-36 hours depending on my use (which is moderate) but never been 48 hours. Still not complaining about that.
  

  5.Look and feel is awesome. Feels like a real masculine phone with the rugged look not like those other metrosexual M8's and Galaxies and even Xperia for that matter
  

  6. Performance -Yet to subject it to something it can't handle or even stutter on for that matter..
  

  Gtg now.. hit overtime! Overall phone is definite BUY!!

column6: A Turbo Beast for Next 2-3 Years.
column7:
First of all, Thanks FK fr wonderful 1 day delivery.Ordered on Fri(29th May) & got device on Sat noon.Now My review: The packaging was good & on delivery the guy shrd details fr replacement in case of any defect.
  

  Coming directly to main points: what the buyers & Turbo seeker wud look for: Cons & FAQ:
  
  1. Camera: Camera images r Sharp & clear.But without OIS you need to click 2-3 pics to get that perfect pic. Front cam 2 MP, Good fr groupies & selfies.(I often get remarks frm people "Why not 5 MP at least" Well ask Moto, why wud they do this?) Records 4K videos and 720p slow-mo videos.
  
  2. Heating issue: I wont Say it has "Heating ISSUE". It gets slightly hot after surfing & playing games fr more than 45 minutes & while Turbo charging. But its expected Bcoz of: 3G Network  ,QuadHD AMOLED Display & constant processing. Upgrading frm Samsung S2(using fr 3.5+ yrs) it used to get a lot hotter(80+ C no joke) while doing the same activities.
  
  3. Speaker: Only 1 speaker (Top bar ,left Half) not even a dual speaker, OK fr normal indoor use. Youtube & surfing you may need to use headphones to get the sound more clearly(depends on videos sound too.) I think a Dual front speaker wud've been gr8,or 2 Front speakers  of current quality cud've done too.
  
  4. 4G: I dont have 4G connection so i cant update anything @ it. No issues or complaints with 3G speed on my TATA Docomo(Which didn't identify my device :P fr Internet setting, but set it correctly anyways.)
  
  5. U R going to thank me fr this one ;) A LOT. Many people complained about no factory screen guard & not able to get a proper screen guard. So heres a trick, take some cotton & your (/Mom/ Wife/ Sister/GF's) nail paint remover.Put 2-3 drops on it & gently wipe the screen & Thank Me fr free screen guard. Its not scratch resistant but a good temporary one.
  

  These were the major topics that i felt like sharing/addressing fr now. will update if i find anything new.
  

  Now lets move to Turbo review- bound to last for 2-3 yrs:
  

  1. Packaging : Wonderful packaging; beautiful texture & color of ballistic nylon backing.Its better than wht u expect. The box contains Device, Data cable, earphones(Not earplugs,normal bass & treble), Manual & TURBO charger.
  

  2. Charging: Turbo Charger :2 to 2.5hours 0% -100% with warm mobile & Normal charger: @ 4hrs & no heating.
  

  3. Battery Backup: Great backup; Lasts fr 2 days normal usage & 15 Hrs Heavy Usage [Gaming, Downloading & updating apps on 3G network, music,streaming]. CONTINUOUS use (Gaming & streaming) on medium brightness will drain the battery frm100 to 0 in 6 hrs Max with hot device.
  
  Irritating things :  [i] Google App and play services(26%) r big battery suckers. Display(5% fr 4hrs of ON time) shows less battery consumption as comprd to these. [ii]In Battery graph Wifi is shown always on even when its off: resolved by updating all apps & disabling wifi search in background even when wifi is off (in Settings>wifi>menu> Advanced)
  

  4. Perfrmance: Installed few games & apps fr testing the perfrmnce: Asphalt 8(1.6GB), Hungry Shark Evolution, Vector,Shadow Fight 2. No Lag or perfrmance issue. Woks perfectly smooth & crisp on display. Multitasking between Chrome ,Musixmatch & normal phone usage along with debugging didnt get any issue or lag. Has OTG support (try Kbd & mouse too :D)
  

  5. Display: Brighter, vibrant colors & superb viewing angle. Active & Attentive display r 2 Great features. The screen is very bright ,sharp & crystal clear even when viewed directly under the sun. No trouble reading the texts & notifications. The Proximity sensory r great. Moto Action does its magic accurately, though i wondering whats the use of bottom 2 sensors as they don't seem to be the trigger fr wake screen on wave gesture, Checked many frums too but cudn't get the exact answer (No impact on use)
  

  6. Voice cmd(even when screen is OFF) r working good with 85-90% accuracy in comm& detection. Can do many simple task using voice only comm&s.Eg., messaging, chatting, launching apps, setting reminders, googling stuff. (Try & set some funny launch phrase fr activation , my comm& is "ry aye Moto", like "ry oh Samba" frmSHOLAY ;) :D it will definitely bring a smile on everyone's face)
  

  7. Sound Quality is good fr indoor use. Earphones r gud too, i already had earplugs & Headphones so this adds to the collection. Different (good) sound quality on 3 different types of accessories. Try out & use  which ever appeals you most, the setting frm sounds> audio effects,Moto has a few decent options to choose frm.
  

  8. Economical?: Considering the design, build(almost as big as Moto G 2nd Gen), Config/Specs &  price (everything same as Nexus6 but in more portable version with more battery backup but non OIS camera) is not a bad choice. Its June 2015 & Moto Turbo is Second best Phone to own and best at this price.
  

  Hope this helps U make your decision.

column6: Hits way below the mark, a few issues, fails to impress
column7:
At the time of writing the review, I have requested for a replacement unit for this phone. I have used and tested it for about a week now, and I have to say, it fails to impress because of a lot of bugging issues, which were not the least expected from this device. During this review, I will draw comparisons with my Xperia SP, which I used for about 2.5 years prior to this.
  

  1. Battery: This phone has a massive 3900 MaH battery. My Xperia SP had a 2370 MaH battery, which lasted the whole day even after 2.5 years of medium - moderately heavy usage. The Moto Turbo I had to charge, on average, every 7 hours. Take off charge in the morning, it'll be sub 15% by the evening when I put it on charge again, and by midnight, it was back down to the lower battery levels. I was aghast. Location services off, auto sync off, NO widgets on the screen, and still this phone lasted less than my 2.5 year old phone with 2/3rd the battery size. The turbocharger was quick. no issues there. I really hope this is a defect in my particular set.
  

  2. WiFi: The signal just keeps dropping. My other phone gets a strong signal in the same area, and holds it well. With this phone, if I move, hold the phone in another way, the signal drops. This doesn't happen always, but it still is a persistent issue.
  

  3. Performance: 2.7 GHz Qualcomm 805 Processor, Adreno 420 Graphics. Performance is below the mark. Within two days itself, I started noticing stutters and lags while operating the phone. Again, not expected with the specs this device has.
  

  4. Overheating: Not a major issue, heats up while charging, while playing games, and also while using light applications like Evernote, sometimes.
  

  5. Camera: It has a good camera, nothing to write home about.
  

  I bought this phone thinking I am buying a future proof flagship device. The battery was one of the important things for me. Keeping my expectations in check, I tested this phone for a week, but though pretty good, it fails to impress as it should have. I hope the issue is with this particular device, and things change with the replacement...

I love the fell of the phone. IT DOES NOT COME WITH A SCREEN GUARD. So thats the first thing one has to get as soon as you get the phone in your hands.
  

  Screen: Fantastic Sensitive QHD screen. Pictures Videos everything look amazing and I cannot complain at all.
  

  Software: Comes with the updated 5.0.2. Makes the phone feel smooth as butter. It has to experienced to actually appreciate it. Its been a week since I have had this phone and I have not had any problems ex glitch etc. The only time there were problem were with specific apps and that has to do with the real time update of the apps. As I used social media to share a lot of the stuff i read on the phone.As far as the software is concerned absolutely no lags and runs perfectly fine.
  

  Camera: It is as it is advertised. Excellent. Now  must confess I have not tried the HD version Slo Mo or the 4k recording nor did I try the various options of the kind of pics req simply because I am not big on them. For me  normal pic does the job but I just came from red bull show run and took some videos and they came out absolutely amazing!! Now I believe this does not have the Image Optimisation Software but I have not used one that has so I cannot judge the difference but from the pics and videos I have taken I have no complains whatsoever. They are sharp and crisp and thats what I need.
  

  Battery: By far the BEST THING about the phone. Now I must confess that while doing my research I found a Lot of reviews here on Flipkart about how unsatisfactory the battery performance was. Fortunately I had the opposite experience. I use my phones for apart from Calls ,heavy usage of Social media and streaming of videos and all the while on wi fi. Till date I have not charged the phone again less than 12 hrs. i.e If i remove the charge at 6 am in the morning my next charge is at close to 10 or 11 pm. YES you read it right. Easy more than 12 hours. EASY. I even did the "charge the new phone for 12hrs test and see results". On the day I did the charge came for good 14 hr. But i did that after 5 days., The first day  I charged it for 2 hours cause that what it takes to charge from 0 to 100 because of turbo charging and it is impressive and the results were same close to 14 hrs battery life. for ex. Yest i.e 4th april my phone lasted from 6 am to 2 am the next day i.e Today 5th april at which point it had 9 percent charging. pretty impressive. It does get a little hot while charging but nothing exaggerated at all. I believe its common for a phone that packs the kind of specs that this one does. A lot is packed in a small area.Heating of the phone is absolutely nothing to worry about. I can honestly say you will hardly notice it unless you have a faulty device and it gets really hot under the hood.
  

  Moto Fuctionality : I really like the gesture recognition ability that this phone has. Fun to play around with. V cool.
  

  Cons;
  

  The speakers : Disappointing. Not as loud as you require but when talking on the phone you can hear the person other end of the line loud and clear the issue is playing videos or listening to music. U cant.  Have to do it with ear phones and that performance is impressive. But without the earphones there is lot left to desire.
  

  wifi: There was a lot of chatter about the phone dropping wi fi regularly on the net. I experience it once in awhile and takes about 30 sec to come back onto it in the first 2 to 3 days but have not after that. I expect it to happen again. But I am not really sure If i am too bothered about it. I mean I wouldnt even put it in cons unless I am nitpicking. Which I am right now :p.
  

  So, in short I would recommend ANYONE to buy the phone. The only kind I would not recommend the phone to is for someone who is completely dependent on their phone to watch and stream videos and music on their phone throughout the day without headphones.I am not sure on the manufacturing reliability as this is the first moto phone I am using.

column6: This beast is Bolder than you think!
column7:
This review is coming after a week of ownership of a Moto Turbo and I'd try to cover as much concerns as possible which haven't been covered yet in the reviews.
  
  Performance: With Snapdragon 805,3 gigs of RAM and Adreno 420,whichever app or game you throw,it handles them like a breeze.There might be some rare awkward lag or bugs but that has nothing to do with the hardware.The 5.1 update should get rid of those tiny pebbles too.Nevertheless, It's a beast on and off the paper.Period.
  
  Battery: Okay,washing away the myths, this one here won't give you a 48hr or even a 40 hr of playtime but hey, with good 30-32 hrs(with moderate use) it still leaves the Galaxies and the Xperias by a long enough margin.Worth the mention is the Krait 400 here, which is known to adapt your usage habits to get most juice of that battery.The Special turbo charger works as just the way it is named and can charge up the battery to 100% within 2hours,now that's something!
  
  Camera: At 21MP it shoot at 4:3 while it shoots at 16:9 when 15.5MP is chosen.Theres no Image stabilizer present here so it might take you more than a couple of clicks to get that perfect shot but you'll get use to with time or a steadier hand will get the job right the first time.Also,the phone supports mostly all the manual settings for camera,so serious photographers will find find joy using the apps which gives you manual control over the settings(DSLR Camera is the one I'm using).
  
  Screen: There's a small complain I have here, as you'll shift the screen to it's minimum brightness you'll gradually see a strange pink hue which is all over the screen.It's not a problem with the screen it just gets the hue in lower brightness and you just can't help but get use to it specially when using the phone at night on bed.But it when you move that slider to eastern most corner you'll get to see the true magnificence of the screen.It's bright,have great colour replication,have 565ppi density and since its a Gorilla Glass 3 I can still keep the phone without a screen guard and not be worried about it.
  
  Looks: With that bold ballistic nylon back it ain't here to charm anyone but it's here to make a statement.When was the last time you saw a phone with a fabric-mesh nylon back?Not only it gives the phone the uber cool look but also adds up to give the immense grip for the palm.Plus, since it's a kind of a nylon you don't have to worry if you drop a oil stain or even ink for that matter you just need to wipe it with a damp cloth and you'll have the grin back onto your face.
  

  Gestures: The Infrared sensor at each end of the phone are a great and even a unique addition.Now you can wake up the screen by just approaching your hand near the screen.Cool,right?
  

  Heat: Well the only time it heats up a bit is when it's charging which again is not an issue to be worried of.
  
  All in all, It's definitely a great phone to buy especially if you like to stand different in the crowd. Ofcourse that difference creator comes at a price but it's truly worth that extra.I got my Turbo at 39,899 which was during an offer with 5% discount.As of my experience I'm utterly satisfied rather have got more than I expected with the Moto Turbo.

column6: Great phone, albeit, a little expensive
column7:
The first time I charged the battery completely, it lasted me about 10 hours. I was devastated. But then, playing around in the settings, I realized that the default network was set to 4G. I switched to 3G and my battery life jumped by almost 40%. But then again, this wasn't as long as I'd expected a 3900 mAh phone to last. I checked my battery usage stat for about two days and noticed that even though I using it fairly heavily, the apps which I was using accounted for only about 4-5% of the battery usage. Google Services were eating up a huge chunk. So again I fiddled around in the settings and noticed that all Google services were autosyncing. Not just mails, but your Chrome searches, all the stupid questions you inevitably ask Google Now, your location and a few others I don't recall now. Turned them all off and my battery easily lasts more than 24 hours on a single charge with data/Wi-Fi switched on.
  

  The primary camera is kind of a let down without OIS. But it still does take very sharp images in daylight if you have a steady hand. But I'm not a shutter bug, so the camera doesn't bother me.
  

  Turbocharging is great, but I'm not sure if using it on a daily basis is recommended.
  

  All in all, I love this phone. It is sleek, very responsive and the overall experience has been very positive.
  

  Note: If the only reason you want to buy this phone is because the manufacturers claim that the battery lasts 4 days, then don't buy it. Even the "15 minutes of turbo charging gives an 8 hour usage" claim comes with fine line where you probably shouldn't be using data/Wi-Fi.

column6: Battery is awesome but TOO COSTLY purchase
column7:
It's been 15 days since i started using this phone. it was delivered to me on 16th April 2015.
  

  Previously i was using Nexus 4, which was good phone, it has few opportunities which Moto Turbo was able to grab.
  
  For me Nexus 4 has issue of heating up while charging, talking on phone, using applications, playing games. Battery drains out very quickly without even location services and Bluetooth, etc switched ON. Had to carry power banks OR phone charger along with me, which were heavy and it was Heavy for its size. Rest everything was very good with Nexus 4.
  
  So i wanted a phone which will free me from previous constraints of carrying power banks OR charger.
  
  Moto Turbo has 3900 mAH battery, and it lasts for complete 2 days. I've my location services switched ON 24X7 and i use Facebook chat, whats app, email, and listening to music and taking pictures apart from talking over phone for longs hours. These are my primary usage areas.
  

  If i tend to play games like NFS, call of duty, modern combat for hour or so then battery consumption increases and i get battery for about 1 day(24 hrs).
  
  though the phone has all the latest hardware and 64 GB of internal memory, but i have no use for such big space. my primary focus was battery and freedom from power banks and charger.
  
  Going by Specs, purchasing a Moto E was sufficient for me, but i needed freedom from power banks as i need location services for my specific purpose and emails and Chat applications.
  
  Though its very costly affair for me. the costliest phone I've every purchased, almost double the cost of Nexus 4, but it addressed my needs. hence i'm content and happy with the phone.

  1. Good Display ( Black's are stunning )
  
  2. Good Camera ( You can't expect it to perform like a D-SLR )
  
  3. Good Performance ( So far no glitches on anything )
  
  4. Good Call Quality ( After a workaround described below, it's great )
  
  5. Good Battery ( For my usage of occasional calls, occasional whatsapp and like 20 shots camera per day and browsing often it comes nearly 2 days - I use low brightness like 25-40%)
  


  Cons:
  

  1. Low (Terrible) speaker output ( it's quite low, phone ringing in crowd or quite noisy environment may not be audible )
  

  2. Many has quoted that during low brightness setting, the screen tends to go pink shade. But the workaround is that you have to 'Disable Adaptive Screen Brightness' in Display settings to remove the pink shade. It WORKS perfectly after disabling it (OR) Upgrade to Marshmallow it solves it automatically.
  

  3. The call volume during calls is too low and you have to put your phone inside the ear to hear people talk. It's TRUE. But the workaround is that when you call, the call volume is set to 20% .. That's weird.. So increase the call volume by pressing the + button on the right side of the phone. Try disabling audio effects as suggested by tons of article in internet as a work around.
  

  Now my phone is crystal clear, my culprit was that the call volume was low, after increasing it to 80% and a phone reboot solved it. Now call volume like a mini speaker.. LOL..
  

  4. 2MP Front camera is very poor, they could have provided a 5MP camera.
  

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  
  Features which could have been included to make it AWESOME
  
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  

  ** Fingerprint Unlock would have been useful.
  
  ** 5 MP Front Camera.
  
  ** VOLTE Support
  

  Almost all snapdragon chipset phones supports VoLTE in hardware perspective, it's only the software provisioning from Google or Cyanogen or OxygenOS or ColorOS etc.. who has to collaborate with JIO to enable VoLTE.. FINGERS CROSSED..
  

  As of now this is a great phone,
  
  - It's hard to find a perfect screen guard and back cover.
  
  - The ballistic nylon looks great, but I find it too slippery, i love the rubberised side frame grip.
  
  - This phone has good resale value.
  

  I got this in Big Billion Day sale for 12599 /- Cheers!!!
  

  NOTE:
  
  4G support is there, but this phone supports only 4G LTE-FDD band 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 17.
  
  JIO Mobile Data (Internet) Works and Voice call can be made through JIO4G Voice App ... :)

I am a happy Moto Turbo user since the last one week !
  

  Before this, I was using the iPhone 5S and before that the Nokia Lumia 925 - having come back to Android after almost 2 years was a refreshing change for me (before Lumia I had the Samsung S3).
  

  My primary reason for change was the battery - this 3900 mAH battery is awesome. It easily gives me over 24 hours of phone life in a single charge (from 100% to about 20%). And this is with wifi/3G on almost non-stop (except at nights when sleeping). The other reason for my change was the dismal 16gb on the iPhone 5S - this 64gb is more than enough for me (at least for a year or so if not more). Having said that, users get about 53-54gb of space in this phone which is still enough (even though it's not exactly 64gb as advertised).
  

  The phone does heat during charging and using it then is not recommended. However during normal usage I did not face heating issues (when playing Temple Run 2 for about 20 minutes it does get warm).
  

  The 5.2inch QHD screen is absolutely crisp and clear - even under the afternoon sun. The processor and 3gb RAM are efficient and I have not faced any lag whatsoever. Phone functions are buttery smooth and super quick.
  

  Cameras (front and back) seem to be OK - not as great as the iPhone 6 camera but just alright for my purposes (I use my dedicated Nikon D750 when I need proper photographs).
  

  The headset that comes in the box is bare - I would suggest an earphone/headphone upgrade for serious music listeners.
  

  One final point - most phone shops don't have the screen guard/case for this phone yet (probably because - I think - Flipkart sells this exclusively in India so far). Hence my recommendation is to get a screen-guard along with this purchase. Box - I don't think it is needed. The back is a premium looking/feeling blast nylon and I personally wouldn't choose to cover it.
  

  Flipkart delivery as usual was great - they delivered this 2 days before the promised date!

column6: Don't be fooled by Dual core processor complaints of others, Here's what you need to know.
column7:
The moto X was not designed like others. It was all about a decent phone with excellent performance over countless meaningless sub standard features.
  

  Coming to the processor. Yes it has a Dual core processor but that's not where the story ends.
  
  1 It has a 2 core Snapdragon S4 CPU for general usage of the phone
  
  2 It has a 4 core Adreno 320 GPU for performance gaming etc
  
  3 It has 1 core For dedicated contextual computing and gesture recognition making it more fluid
  
  4 It has 1 core especially for natural language processing making it more likely to understand any form of speech input
  

  That's a total of 8 cores all managed by Motorola X8 computing system. A dedicated core for each of the specific function means an enhanced battery life and optimization of usage. So in reality it's Octa-Core but since you don't need all of them running together at all times their functions have been segregated.
  

  Another complaint made by people is about Active display. Yes you can grab an app for that but here's what you should know. Moto X uses AMOLED display which unlike IPS display does not use the entire screen while using active display. So if you use active display on IPS LCD it will drain your battery. On Moto X it only uses the part that's enough for showing notifications and thus you won't be running to charge it every few hours.
  
  In my opinion Motorola is giving a phone that boasts of performance and near Vanilla Android experience instead of adding stuff that doesn't matter. Also 720p was deliberate to further enhance performance and improve battery life and you'll hardly notice any difference

column6: Moto X vs Moto G : Perfect Mid-Ranger at decent price?
column7:
This review is to explain the performance comparison between Moto X and Moto G and Return on Investment if you buy them.
  

  I am an owner of Sony Xperia SP which has same processor as Moto X : Qualcomm Snapdragon S4 Pro (1.7 GHz Dual Core Krait with Adreno 320 GPU). The fact is that this processor is very fast. If you go by benchmarks my Xperia SP scores around 8200 in Quadrant and 21000 in Antutu which will be almost same in Moto X too if not better. Moto X has more RAM (2 GB) than Xperia SP which has 1 GB, so definitely it will perform better.
  

  But if you want to compare it's performance with Moto G, the Quad Cortex A7 CPU in Moto G from Qualcomm will give almost same CPU performance (little bit less) which means each Cortex A7 is half as powerful as a Krait at 1.7GHz. But if you compare GPU with Moto G which has Adreno 305, Moto X will have a decent win with Adreno 320.
  

  So if performance in games is not a big factor, then Moto G isn't a bad option, given that it costs 10k less. If you are going to use Whatsapp, normal games, calling, definitely Moto G is the best option out there.
  

  Next comes screen. Both have 720p screens. 4.5 inch in Moto G and 4.7 inch in Moto X. Moto X's screen will be little better definitely. The size doesn't makes a big difference. Both are decent sized. My Xperia SP is 4.6 inch 720p and it is very comfortable to hold and very sharp. (~320 ppi, as good as iPhone 5s).
  

  The main differentiating point would be a camera and some voice awake features. The Camera on Moto X will be definitely better than Moto G, but is it worth the extra 10k?, you decide. I don't think so. You can buy a decent point-and-shoot in that price.
  

  I really like the wooden texture Moto X devices, but they increase the price by another 2k,  it is a personal choice if you want to go for it.
  

  So if you are a complete geek user and performance matters a lot to you, be aware Moto X is not the best performing device out there. Then you should better look at Nexus 5, Xperia Z1, etc which are actually top-of the line.
  

  If you are a mid-range user who will use normal apps, normal games, then deciding between Moto G and Moto X can be a big problem for you. Moto X will definitely give you a better feeling as owner, but it comes wit a price (10k more than Moto G).
  

  To help you out, think this way: If you think better Camera and some extra features like Voice Awake, Active Display and a little more snappier CPU performance are not worth the extra 10k than Moto G's price, then definitely go with Moto G. It will save you a lot of money and give decent performance. If you want a decent Camera phone, much better GPU performance and the high end status associated with Moto X, go with Moto X by paying the money.
  

  Some other features: Moto G is dual SIM, Moto X is single sim. It shouldn't matter much.
  

  I hope it helps.

Firstly, Addressing the dual core processor. This has been emphasized upon enough already. DON'T go on the number of cores. The phone is super snappy, handles anything thrown at it.   The screen is super amoled. Means you get superb contrast ratios. And saves battery! (The amoled screens don't use power for displaying blacks. So the display is basically switched off in all black areas)
  

  The touch less control and the active display have the whole android community going gaga over it. Read the online reviews. It actually does understand things pretty accurately and trust me guys I've stopped dialling people, setting alarms, setting memos, searching on the web manually. All you need is to ask google now!
  

  The camera is not bad but isn't that great either but as mentioned few posts before it will get you through everyday clicks, if you want something more, buying a camera would be more prudent.
  

  It packs 2 gigs of ram, enough to handle anything thrown at it. Multitasking is a breeze.
  

  The GPU is a quad core Adreno 320 chip. It handles every game I've tried on it, completely lag free, and I consider myself as a heavy gamer.
  

  The phone supports 4G LTE for all those looking for that.
  

  The design of the phone is such that it's very easy and comfortable to hold in your hand. I know this hardly sounds like something you'd care about but once you hold the device you'll know what I'm talking about.
  

  The charger is 1150mA and charges the phone from 0 to 100 in a little less than 2 hrs. Pretty quick.
  

  The speaker is loud! And has really good sound. While using earphones you can't keep the volume at full. Yes, it's that loud! Superb sound quality. The built in audio effects are great.

  The phone heats up occasionally with heavy usage while it's on charge. This had happened twice. I had 3G on too. But this is true for any mobile nowadays because of so many things packed into such a small device with no actual cooling mechanism. My advice, don't put a back cover. P.S- I have one :P
  

  There's no SD card expansion slot. You get 16 gigs out of which 12 is usable.
  
  The silver lining? The phone supports OTG meaning you can connect pen drives to the phone!
  

  Now coming to the battery life, the company claims 24 hrs, I haven't been able to get that. With normal usage, I get around 18 hrs, not bad. With heavy usage, includes gaming, excessive texting, browsing, 3G always on, it's more of 8 hrs. So that's for you to decide.

column6: Confused between MOTO G and MOTO X..... Go for MOTO X
column7:
Friends this review is not regarding how overwhelming MOTO X is but I have done a first hand comparison between G and X.
  
  Obviously MOTO G is a great phone at its price range but if you are confused between both...I would say go for X.
  
  I bought this phone on the first day considering the popularity of G but certainly made a good decision.
  

  1. The first prominent diff is the Touchless control. X has it and G doesn't. And mind it, its not any other feature which you can overlook. Its the future of Mobile.
  

  2. One of the most important difference is the processor. X has a 1.7GHz Snapdragon S4 processor. Also It has what the company calls the Motorola X8 Mobile processor, which is essentially a low power consuming co-processor that stays awake while the phone is in sleep mode. This not only enables the always-on voice command and active display features but also ensures that the Moto X has a longer battery life as the main processor is not activated unless required for processor intensive tasks.
  

  3. There is no Active Display in MOTO G, which I must tell you is very awesome feature. I after using this feature for about a month can't think of a phone without this feature. The moment I pick my cell up or take it out from my pocket, everything shows up on the screen in a very battery efficient way.
  

  4. G has a corning Gorilla glass but no Amoled screen. Also the size of both the phones are same but the screen size of G is smaller making the edges bigger. Even the Weight of X is 130 gms whearas G is 140 gms.
  

  5. The battery of G is 2070 mAh whearas of X its 2200 but as explained in pt no 2, X saves a lot of battery. Also you have a unique charger having two usb slots. Thus you can charge two phones from a single adapter at a time which is great.  G comes with a standalone charger and not the charger with usb cable. It neither gives a data cable in the box.
  

  6. Other visible features are the camera. X has 10 and 2 whearas G has 5 and 1.2 primary and secondary camera resp.
  

  7. X has 2 GB RAM which is great. G only boasts 1 GB.
  

  So my verdict "The Moto X is not the fastest phone in the world. It's also not the most cutting-edge, it doesn't feature the biggest display, and it isn't the thinnest Android phone. However, there is absolutely no doubt that the Moto X is the most amazing Android phone I have ever used, and I think most people will agree."

  Phone came with a multipurpose charger, which can be converted into data cable, an earphone (not the one with buds) quite useless to me, and other user manuals and stuff.
  

  Now talking about the highlighted features.
  

  1) Touchless control: Needs alot of updating yet. So do not go GAGA over this one. Although that shouldn't stop you from buying this phone. Note that this is not a negative point for the phone. But the thing is I had to turn off this feature because it always keeps listening and like an over enthusiastic helper it pops up even if I don't say 'ok google now..'. Also for an average indian user this feature would be useless as we hardly use reminders or frequently set alarms or send text message in complete English.
  

  But if you do, go for it without thinking because it understands indian accent very nicely. It responds quite fast and it is quite robust. What are the things it can do ... well just youtube '50 tips and tricks with moto x' and you will know. Its awesome. (note that listening to music and telling you the song name doesn't work in India as of now)
  

  2) Active display: You can customize which notifications should come or stay hidden on your active display screen. I think (not sure) it uses some combination of proximity and gyro sensors so the display isn't always ON (thus doesn't consume alot of power) also only A PART of display is active not the whole screen thus saving battery again.
  

  3) Moto assist: Also available on moto G and E and super helpful. Will detect if you're driving (or say moving fast) and if you're not driving then you can tell the phone so, so that it doesn't turn ON the feature.
  

  --------------------------

  Yes, it is true sadly. Gorilla glass 3 or not, this phone is delicate up to some extent. I have habit of keeping my phone in back pocket and saddest thing happened when i sat on the ground with phone in my back pocket and heard the crack sound. I completely take responsibility it was my mistake and stupidity. And yes another rumor is true as well that the replacement of screen costs you 13000/- I mean what the hell right? 23000 phone has 13000 worth display.
  

  Anyways, its your mistake if you break your phone and company can't give you replacement of that. So be advised while buying. Get a bumper case or whatever to protect your phone.

  Coming to cons:
  

  - Fast ... very fast. Open 10 tabs in chrome, and simultaneously run another 10 apps but you will still be able to play any game without lag.
  
  - I cant boast enough about the display of this phone.
  
  - Camera is average. Its not a con and yes there are better cameras out in market but whatever, its a long debate.
  
  - Crystal clear sound from both ends during call.
  
  - Loud speakers are loud. Ringtones can be heard from another room clearly without the noise or any sort of sound blasting or crackling.
  
  - Again this one is not a CON but if you're not a regular 3g user or your phone isn't connected with internet at all times then most of the features are just useless for you. So if your touchless control isn't responding very fast that's because of your net speed. Stop cribbing seriously. If you can use a 24000/- phone then you can definitely spare 198/- monthly for a 3G recharge. duh.
  
  - This is for gamers: Dead trigger 2, Injustice: gods among us, Shadow fighter 2, Asphalt 7 and 8. All tested with crystal graphics and zero lag. Enjoy.

  Final verdict: Only serious android users buy this phone. You will be the second one to get updates after nexus. This has best display arguably. Internal storage is sufficient for me. column7:
Myth-"A quad-core is powerful than a dual-core."
  

  Truth- This statement is false. Those fools who said that Moto g has a quad-core and moto-x is a Dual-core need some enlightenment.
  

  The phone has a dual-core krait which is clocked at 1.7Ghz which is 50% more powerful than the snapdragon 400 quad-core cortex A7 in real applications used in moto g and 100% powerful than grand quattro. Despite the higher frequency it is lower on power-consumption. It beats them in benchmarks as well!
  
  Moto g cannot even play a 4K video despite the fact it has a quad-core (I own a moto g) but it can.It is even better than a nexus 4. Even Apple is stuck on dual-core only architecture is being improved.
  

  The performance is actually dependent on the architecture of the CPU (whether krait or Cortex A-5, A-7 or A-17 based)  which affects per-core performance rather than number of cores. Being dual-core adds an advantage of being power efficient and gives better battery life in situations of higher CPU loads.
  
  A quad-core might not give you performance benefits but for sure more cores are going to suck your battery.
  

  Second, the GPU is Adreno 320 which is better than what is found on other quad-core counterparts.
  

  The 720p display will actually perform better than 1080p one both load-wise and performance-wise.
  

  You will get around 12.5 GB of space which allows you to install all pre-installed app updates, 250 songs (7mb avg.), 400 pics(10 mp) , 10 Full HD videos, 30 apps/games(60 mb avg.) leaving  about 5 GB space. What else?
  
  Plus, you get OTG functionality through which you can connect your pen-drive and store whatever you want.
  

  Go for it!!

I spent nearly a month comparing different models, and the top contenders for my new phone were the Nexus 5, Alcatel Idol X+ and the Mi3. Let's face it, given the chance we'd all go running for the Mi3, but it's way too much trouble to wait for Flipkart's Tatkal system.
  

  My previous phone (which I gave to my mom in exchange for giving away her Ace Duos) was a Nexus 4, which honestly is a brilliant phone in both feel and performance despite its technological age. So it takes more than a bit of spec-worthiness to beat it.
  

  Moto X first caught my eye when I looked at CPUBoss and saw it's measly dual-core keeping up with the likes of 2 Ghz quadcores and sometimes beating them (especially in certain java benchmarks). Then I saw reviews on the Active Display and Voiceless Control . I was wowed, but not so much. Given the way things are going, most phones will have this by next year. Also a simple fact is that the Voiceless Control feature is basically Google Now without the hassle of having to drag your home button up. So the faults of Google Now will all be there. And it doesn't answer funny inane questions like Siri, apart from whatever Easter Eggs google has put in.
  

  Okay, simply put, here's why the Moto X is value for money -
  
  1. Good build quality (still feels somewhat inferior to my Nexus)
  
  2. Sharp screen (text clarity is crisp and amazing)
  
  3. Decent battery life (this is harder to get these days than it might seem, but the built-in smartness of the Moto X ensures I get around 30-40% more juice out of it than my nexus)
  
  4. You can exchange old crappy smartphones for 4k thanks to flipkart (which is exactly what I did)
  
  5. Moto phones will always be second in line to get android updates after the Nexuses (or is it Nexii?)
  
  6. It's slightly better than stock android but keeps all the flexibility.
  
  7. Active Display is damn cool.
  

  If you're thinking, "hey, other phones give me higher pixel density and Full HD and other things that show up on geekaphone", also remember that all of these things - A) Need more of your processing power, B) Suck more battery and C) Are not really noticeable when it's down to brass tacks. The dual core is fairly zippy and I would prefer sturdiness and a lower SAR rating over fragile plasticky things with superheated octa-cores.

  My observations after using this for a month:
  




  Design & Construction:
  
  ---------------------------------
  
  - It's slimmer at the bottom and gets thicker as u go to the top, making it a really well-balanced phone. The dimple at the back makes for a natural place to rest ur index finger on & is well placed in relation to the weight.
  
  - The back is rubberized and is easy to grip.
  
  - It's solid in overall construction, though there's a creaking sound if pressed near the volume rocker, but that may differ from piece to piece.
  




  Accessories:
  
  -------------------
  
  - The earphones provided are not in-ear and look cheap(sound quality is decent though), so does the usb charger.
  
  - Both Apple earphones(with mic) and Samsung can be used, but calls can only be accepted and not ended.
  



  Hardware:
  
  --------------
  
  - Performance is very good with no lag at all. Dual core is more than enough, unless ur into video encoding and heavy games.
  
  - Supports 4G band of 1800 MHz, but in India, Airtel has launched 4G on 2300 MHz, though the Govt. has allowed 4G to be used on any of these 2 bands.
  
  - Speaker(rear and front) quality is good. Rear speaker is very loud.
  
  - Mic performance is probably not as good as Samsung. Voice is not that loud at the receiving end(comparatively).
  
  - Battery life - 1 day of moderate use. If used on 2G, it's about 1.5 days. Charging time - 2.5 - 3 hrs. Battery saver mode only disables data if it's less than 15%.
  



  Software:
  
  -------------
  
  - Active notifications:
  
  - Shows your last notification when the screen is locked. Downloaded apps can also be configured.
  
  - Activated at any kind of movement like picking-up the phone, braking while driving etc.
  
  - An unadvertised feature to activate: Waving ur hand above the screen(similar to Galaxy S4).
  
  - If lying unattended with screen facing up & with unread notifications, it keeps on popping-up every 6-7 secs. If it's in the pocket, or lying face-down, notifications r not displayed as it uses the proximity sensor.
  
  - If there are no notifications, a "lock" icon is displayed instead, and you practically never need to use the unlock button for unlocking.
  

  - Touchless control - Very useful. Requires data for most commands(some like "Find my Phone", "What's up?" work w/o data as well). Doesn't read the entire notification for 3rd party apps like Times of India/other email clients etc. Mentions the no. of notifications instead.
  
  - 5 fixed homescreens(can't be changed), all have google search bar which can't be removed.
  
  - Dialer - Always displays recent contacts on launch. An extra tap is required to open the dial-pad. Individual entries from Call Log can't be deleted. No option of "Edit No. b4 Call".
  
  - Camera settings are much easier to operate than stock android.
  
  - No kill all processes option in recent apps as Samsung
  


  Overall rating - 4.5/5. Almost all the negatives can be overcome by apps. Highly recommended!

column6: Good Smartphone,but lacks in battery life and camera!
column7:
I bought this phone for a bargain on flipkart through the Exchange offer.I exchanged my 5 year old HTC Wildfire for a cool 4000/- when nobody in the market was even ready to consider it for an exchange/resell.
  


  The Moto X offers true android experience which to is to my liking.The phone works butter smooth.A couple of features separates this phone from the rest of them available in the market.The display is crisp and clear and unlike its other Amoled siblings,the colours represented on this phone seem to be true in nature.
  
  Touchless control and the Active Control works like a gem.A really useful tool specially while driving. Answering a call while driving is real easy and also to mention,the speakers on the phone are loud and clear.
  


  I use the phone mainly for call(20mins),texting,reading,facebook and occasionally to watch videos.The active display feature is quite a handy one if you want to go through the content of the message in a glance.
  


  The "Twist the Wrist" feature to enable the camera works all the time.It does enable the camera in less than 2 secs but alas thats where the good part comes to an end.The auto focus on the camera is a pain, so taking a quick snap is out of the question.The photos captured in a haste come out blurred .The photos taken from the Primary camera(10mp) are average in quality.Pictures taken during the night come out grainy.The Secondary camera(2mp) takes surprisingly good photos when the conditions are bright,good enough for "selfies" in a well lit environment.When the pictures do not come out well it does not make sense to talk about any of its camera features.
  


  The battery on this phone is something that I am very disappointed with.It takes forever(more than 2hrs) for a full charge and drains out pretty soon.Even with light usage, it doesn't last for more than 12 hours i.e. with the battery saver mode switched on. I plan to monitor the situation with the battery for a few more days.if the problem persists then i will get back to motorola on this issue.
  


  Also provided in the box is charger with dual charging slots.Charging two phones simultaneously with this charger is a bad idea.The headset provided is of poor quality with bad output.
  
  I bought this phone for 19999/- and considering the fact that I have to buy a power bank and a decent pair of earphones/headphones, I am glad that I got it for that price.
  


  All said and done .. I like this phone !.A very handy smartphone with loads of "Usable" features but lacks where it matters the most..i.e. its battery and camera performance.

The Moto X is one of the best mobile phones available in the market and the makers have lived up to their name. The specifications of this phone are great not only on paper, but also when it comes to performance.
  

  Do not be misled by the "Dual Core" you see on the specifications. It has 8 Working Cores which optimize battery usage and thus provide a better smartphone experience.
  

  1 & 2 :
  
  It has 1.7Ghz Dual Core Krait CPU from the Qualcomm Snapdragon S4Pro family, which powers your basic interactions and more.
  
  3,4,5 & 6:
  
  It has a Quad - Core Adreno 320 Graphics Processing Unit for great viewing, astounding deep colour displays and great gaming.
  
  The last two processors are the ones which make Moto X stand out:
  

  7:
  
  The natural language processor, which is on standby and is always ready to listen to your voice (Since this phone is a Google product, it is one of the phones offering the best "Google Now" experiences").
  
  8:
  
  The Contextual Computing Processor uses all the sensors on the phone to detect movement, and it comes in so handy that with just two flicks of your wrist while holding the mobile, you can whip up your camera. It uses the proximity sensor and ambient light to detect whether your phone is in your hand or in your pocket or your bag. ( The use of this will be explained later on).
  

  So this X8 computing system really optimizes battery usage and never leaves you wanting for more power. It was a good decision that I bought this phone since the performance is the best i've seen.
  

  Once you train it to listen to your voice, it brings in the noise cancellation technique to filter your voice only and cancels ambient noise. You can ask the phone anything or set your alarm, reminders and tons of stuff by just saying the command phrase "Ok Google Now", when you have your net connection. It is better if you have a WiFi connection.
  

  As metioned earlier, it detects whether your phone is in your hand or pocket and uses this to display "Active Notifications Display".When the screen is locked (sleeping), The AMOLED screen gives the advantage to partially light up only the pixels needed on the screen to display notifications, thus saving you a lot of battery life. You can swipe these away or view them on the locked screen itself, since it stays on the screen till you view or dismiss it. When your phone is inside your pocket, it doesnt do so. Also, you can choose the option to not display these notifications during night (11:00pm to 6am). Or you could just turn off the whole 'Active Display' in Settings but who would refuse such a great feature?
  

  The camera quality is good, and it has Auto Focus as well as Manual settings where you can control the Focus and Exposure by dragging the shutter icon on the screen. The pictures taken using Auto Focus weren't that good, but if you manually control the Focus and Exposure, the camera on this phone can do wonders.
  

  The sound clarity was also good, though sometimes I would rate the call clarity to be just above average. You can get along with the headphones, since I would rate them as just 7 on a scale of 1 to 10.
  

  The phone comes with an Internal Storage of 16GB and around 11 to 12 GB is user available. This was a letdown since you cannot have too much mass storage data like movies,videos and songs.
  


  Display        :  9/10
  
  Performance: 10/10
  
  Camera       :   8/10
  
  Sound         :   8/10
  

  I experienced no lag in the day to  day operations and even during games. The multitasking is especially great.
  
  Overall, this phone is definitely worth the money you pay for it.

column6: Moto X is priced right with the right set of features.
column7:
After a long time, we have a phone which is priced right with the right feature set and design. If you are looking for a phone with top of the line specs, this isn't the phone for you. However, what Moto X offers is simple practicality. Let me explain.
  

  Design
  

  The phone fits perfectly into your hand. the slight curve of back gives you good grip and feels good in your hard. The size isn't too big either. the soft touch back gives a nice premium feel to the phone. The bevel is pretty thin, giving you more screen space is a small size.
  

  Performance
  

  The phone is fast and smooth. Playing games is no problem, the dual core notwithstanding. In fact the phone performs brilliantly. The battery last me for a day an da half. That includes a few hours of phone calls, browsing apart from have counituous background checking of 3 email accounts, facebook, whatsapp, magicjack, and news. I have touchless control on along with active display, wifi, auto backup of photos, 3G on 24/7 with the occasional bluetooth. he camera takes pretty good pictures as well. Still have to fully explore that aspect of it.
  

  Moto X might not have the best specs and crazy features of the flagship phones, but what it does have is good feature set with some really useful and practical features. The touchless control is really good and very useful which driving. I dont need to to unlock my phone and dial numbers. the active display is something I really missed since the Sony Ericsson K700/K750 days. Thanks to those phones, I stopped using a watch because I kept checking the time on my phones display more than my watch. With smart phones, that was a feature I sorely missed. Now thanks to Motorola's unique implementation of the solution, I can also check a few limes of the notifications you get without actually switching on your phone. Surprisingly, neither of these two features seem to drain the battery much.
  

  As I said earlier, Moto X does a good in all departments (camera, battery, screen,...) but I think where it excels is in its usability features.

column6: Hello Moto - A different kind of smartphone, the last one from Google!
column7:
Moto X is not about raw hardware specification. It is about balance and optimization. The Moto X is terrific to hold and use, too. It's a meaty device, thin enough to compete with its contemporaries, yet dense. Fully packed. The size is just about perfect for my hands, and I was able to reach across the 4.7-inch display to the upper-left corner with little difficulty. The curved back feels right on. The button placement is not only sensible, but the buttons seem built to last: clicky, punctual, tough.
  

  As far as resolution is concerned, text and graphics look plenty smooth on a 4.7-inch 720p display. As with most Motorola phones, the speakers on the Moto X are excellent. They're loud enough to use in the car hands-free and generally clear for speakerphone use and even a little YouTube or music playback. The first thing that you should know about the software on this phone is that it is thankfully, mercifully, for all intents and purposes "stock" Android Kit-kat 4.4.2.
  

  There is no perceivable difference between a full HD and HD resolution in this screen size, except for the battery life compromise. The deal with other brands is that the battery life & some hardware features start to falter within 6-9 months. By the same token, devices made by Motorola and perhaps Nokia have by far the most reliable hardware including quality of battery. The additions to the software that Motorola has made are legitimately useful and really quite impressive. They add to the experience of Android without removing what is most vital in Google's software, unlike the competition, which seems intent on obscuring what's already a sophisticated and beautiful operating system. And the phone is nice. I mean, really nice to use. It's a reminder that the way something is built can be as important as what it's made of.
  

  The voice control, active display and camera quick-start features are excellent additions to the standard Android experience, and Motorola's commitment to optimization and speed is evident as the device is lag-free.
  

  The Moto X is not a perfect phone, but neither is any other phone on the market right now. What it is, however, is a pretty damn good phone and one I can recommend. User-friendly, satisfying experience, a great mix of personalization & convenience. Worth buying!

column6: Moto X. The best Android "phone" in sub 30k range. Period
column7:
Well I got this phone just one week ago from Flipkart, as usual their delivery time was exceptional, 36 hours from the order and the phone was delivered!
  

  Display : Nice, coming from S4 though nothing can impress me, maybe the S5, well. It's still a very good Samsung made OLED panel, I can compare this with the Note 2 I had, it's really good. And yeah it's 720p, but NO, you are not gonna notice it coming from 1080p, yet I have very sharp eyes, besides I am obsessed with display quality too, still.
  

  Call quality : Exceptional. I don't remember what was the last phone I used which had as great call quality like this. It's crisp, clear and just great.
  

  Size : The best part of this phone. It's just the perfect size for me, and I believe for other human beings too. While Samsung, LG, Sony and hTC are going with the ridiculous trend of upping the dimension of each and every flagship, and yet our hands are still there of same size since human beings appeared on planet earth, I am really confused where exactly we are headed. I am quite confident that it will stop, and probably those manufacturers have to dial it back, very soon.
  

  The phone looks great by the way, too. Seems like very well built. I got the White one and it looks classy to be honest.
  

  Performance : As I said, it's fantastic. You will not notice any lag (well the occasional micro stutters are still somewhat there, but blame Android and it's ecosystem, not Moto). It's the most fluid Android I have ever used. And I don't really wanna disrespect the performance by comparing it to the S4 I had, which was simply awful.
  

  Camera : Now I see this is a big part of nowadays users, as they depend on a cell phone camera quite a lot. Now let's get this straight, this camera will not replace your cheapest P&S. It's just fine for social stuffs, more than fine actually, but it's just not up to the mark for something more important stuffs. This is the "only" thing I will miss from S4. Still, when I prioritize stuffs, camera comes last, so that's not a big issue for me, at all. Honestly I find it ridiculous when people pay 45+ k for devices like Z2 or S5, only for it's camera, so foolish and idiotic, thinking it takes as good photos as even a cheap P&S does! LOL. Just go and buy those Canon 510HS or something for 8k or something and you will forget about your Z2. Whatever, to each his own I suppose.
  

  Just a tip to get a good photo, just don't shoot as soon as you open the camera, just focus on a subject, then let the camera stay there for at least 4-5 seconds, then take the shot.
  

  Active Display - Well everyone knows this is a trademark feature of X, and yes it's awesome. I won't say that it's far better than normal LED notifications, but yes it's cool, and using a separate chip and OLED display is clever.
  

  Touchless control : To be honest, I haven't played with it at all, and I am not gonna unless it supports offline voice recognition.
  

  Battery life : Another aspect which I suppose is important for most users, and this device has fantastic battery life. You can easily get 4+ hours screen on time with 24 hours or more standy time, keeping WiFi and GPS on all time. You can even hit 4  to 5 hours mark if you can tweak the kernel setting a bit (Faux kernel of course). 720p display is definitely for win here.
  

  Gaming : I don't game on mobile phones, so I won't comment. But yeah, I played a slight bit of Angry Birds, and it runs as smooth as on the S4 I had, maybe a frame or two less, but nothing worth mentioning. Don't see what's the point of having a Snapdragon 805 either, maybe people play GTA V or Crysis 3 on them, whatever.
  

  External Speaker : The speaker is awesome. It will sound as close to the M7 with Beats audio crap I had, yes, it sounds like stereo. A nice touch of bass is even there. Lovely speaker. But again, the placement is nonsense.
  

  Sound : Haven't input the headphones yet, so won't comment. By the way, the stock Motorola in ear which comes with the phone bundled is basically crap. It's one of those flat ones which won't even go inside your ear, cheap Moto. Anyway I wasn't gonna use it anyway.
  

  All other important features like GPS and all works flawlessly as expected. Nothing really worth mentioning here.
  

  So all in all, coming from an S4 i9500 to Moto X is a technical downgrade in every possible section, and some kids might call you crazy, but again, unless and until you have used a device with pure Android you don't know what you were missing, so for me it's a fantastic upgrade. Perfect size, great ergonomics with good build, superb performance, a capable camera for less serious occasions, a very good display, excellent call quality, lovely speaker volume, and all these for which I believe at a great price (price was the last thing I cared about) are just for the win. Once you use this you will feel how awful TouchWiz is, even Sense and Sony's skin might feel heavy. I am not going back to TouchWiz, heck I can NOT.
  

  Thanks for reading,
  
  Saurav (ithehappy)

column6: Why this gem of phone might not do so well in India
column7:
Well, to begin with I am not surprised with so many negative reviews for this phone here on Flipkart!! Most of the people posting negative reviews here have never ever used this phone personally and are happy using their substandard Micromax, Lava and Xolo phones with quad core mediatek processors. We Indians are more into number of processors and other high end specifications without even bothering about the real life performance. On the outset it might appear that MotoX has only a dual core processor but dig deep and you get a real picture. It has different sets of cores for different functionalities that delivers flawless experience, thereby taking off stress from the battery. Each set of processor is only activated when required. Active display and touchless control gotta be the best feature of the mobile apart from Motorola Assist. The UI is almost stock with few minor tweeks here and there whic enhances the user experience. In last few years Android phones have been all about high end specs and less emphasis on performance and Google(Motorola Mobility is now owned by Lenevo) has tried to change that trend and has succeeded in putting user experience above anything else.You might only get a 720P HD display in the time of 1020 FHD display but at 4.7 inches you hardly notice the difference. The Super AMOLED display is crisp and vibrant at around 320 ppi. HD display also helps in improving battery life. I have used my Friend's Moto X for almost 10-15 days (He got it imported from US) and I must say that it was quite a pleasing experience using the phone. The size of the phone makes it pretty easy to use and operate and the battery easy lasted me for around 18 hours with moderate to heavy usage. The only downer for me was the 10 MP camera. While the UI is pretty clean and smooth but the picture quality was just passable. Nothing great about it. But once you start uing this phone for a fair amount of time you start falling in love with it and  it becomes almost hard to put off and not use it anymore. For all those complaining about the price I must say that the pricing by Flipkart is quite fair and aggressive too. Going by the pricing in US and UK I was expecting the 16 GB variant to be priced at around 28-29k but Flipkart surprised many of us.
  

  For those folks crying foul over QUAD CORE and FULL HD DISPLAY I would suggest you to see the review on Phonearena, Techradar, Engadget, Android Authority or YouTube and you can see for yourself how this phone has managed to capture the imagination of some of the best reviewers around. If you are still in doubt I would recommed you to buy Quad Core Micromax, Lava, Karbonn or Xolo and be happy with them and flaunt them with pride. For me Moto X has to be one of the best phones in the market and surely best value for money device. Although I wish 32 GB option was also available.

  The screen is super amoled. Means you get superb contrast ratios. And saves battery! (The amoled screens don't use power for displaying blacks. So the display is basically switched off in all black areas)
  

  The touch less control and the active display have the whole android community going gaga over it. Read the online reviews. It actually does understand things pretty accurately and trust me guys I've stopped dialling people, setting alarms, setting memos, searching on the web manually. All you need is to ask google now!
  

  The camera is not bad but isn't that great either but as mentioned few posts before it will get you through everyday clicks, if you want something more, buying a camera would be more prudent.
  

  It packs 2 gigs of ram, enough to handle anything thrown at it. Multitasking is a breeze.
  

  The GPU is a quad core Adreno 320 chip. It handles every game I've tried on it, completely lag free, and I consider myself as a heavy gamer.
  

  The phone supports 4G LTE for all those looking for that.
  

  The design of the phone is such that it's very easy and comfortable to hold in your hand. I know this hardly sounds like something you'd care about but once you hold the device you'll know what I'm talking about.
  

  The charger is 1150mA and charges the phone from 0 to 100 in a little less than 2 hrs. Pretty quick.
  

  The speaker is loud! And has really good sound. While using earphones you can't keep the volume at full. Yes, it's that loud! Superb sound quality. The built in audio effects are great.
  

  Enough of the praises, now for some cons:
  

  The phone heats up occasionally with heavy usage while it's on charge. This had happened twice. I had 3G on too. But this is true for any mobile nowadays because of so many things packed into such a small device with no actual cooling mechanism. My advice, don't put a back cover. P.S- I have one :P
  

  There's no SD card expansion slot. You get 16 gigs out of which 12 is usable.
  
  The silver lining? The phone supports OTG meaning you can connect pen drives to the phone!
  

  Now coming to the battery life, the company claims 24 hrs, I haven't been able to get that. With normal usage, I get around 18 hrs, not bad. With heavy usage, includes gaming, excessive texting, browsing, 3G always on, it's more of 8 hrs. So that's for you to decide.
  

  I'm really trying really hard to think of more but trust me it's not that easy.
  

  I've tried to be unbiased in this review. And weigh both pros and cons, which I actually did before going for this device. I hope this helps you.

column6: Confused between MOTO G and MOTO X..... Go for MOTO X
column7:
Friends this review is not regarding how overwhelming MOTO X is but I have done a first hand comparison between G and X.
  
  Obviously MOTO G is a great phone at its price range but if you are confused between both...I would say go for X.
  
  I bought this phone on the first day considering the popularity of G but certainly made a good decision.
  

  1. The first prominent diff is the Touchless control. X has it and G doesn't. And mind it, its not any other feature which you can overlook. Its the future of Mobile.
  

  2. One of the most important difference is the processor. X has a 1.7GHz Snapdragon S4 processor. Also It has what the company calls the Motorola X8 Mobile processor, which is essentially a low power consuming co-processor that stays awake while the phone is in sleep mode. This not only enables the always-on voice command and active display features but also ensures that the Moto X has a longer battery life as the main processor is not activated unless required for processor intensive tasks.
  

  3. There is no Active Display in MOTO G, which I must tell you is very awesome feature. I after using this feature for about a month can't think of a phone without this feature. The moment I pick my cell up or take it out from my pocket, everything shows up on the screen in a very battery efficient way.
  

  4. G has a corning Gorilla glass but no Amoled screen. Also the size of both the phones are same but the screen size of G is smaller making the edges bigger. Even the Weight of X is 130 gms whearas G is 140 gms.
  

  5. The battery of G is 2070 mAh whearas of X its 2200 but as explained in pt no 2, X saves a lot of battery. Also you have a unique charger having two usb slots. Thus you can charge two phones from a single adapter at a time which is great.  G comes with a standalone charger and not the charger with usb cable. It neither gives a data cable in the box.
  

  6. Other visible features are the camera. X has 10 and 2 whearas G has 5 and 1.2 primary and secondary camera resp.
  

  7. X has 2 GB RAM which is great. G only boasts 1 GB.
  

  So my verdict "The Moto X is not the fastest phone in the world. It's also not the most cutting-edge, it doesn't feature the biggest display, and it isn't the thinnest Android phone. However, there is absolutely no doubt that the Moto X is the most amazing Android phone I have ever used, and I think most people will agree."
