column6: Never thought it would be an awesome phone. (Honest Review)
column7:
Let's start with the Impressive Stuffs:
  

  1. Performance : Awesome, can't describe better than that. First off, No lagging while multitasking, Which is very important to me. Still very smooth though I opened 30 apps right after one and let it all run in background at the same time. I could still choose any app at any time by going into the recent tasks option to open any specific app that I want and there was no slow performance that I could notice. So I give 9/10 (Let me explain later why I can't give score 10)
  

  2. Primary Camera : 13 MP.. Seriously?! It looks much more better than 13 MP. That's where Nexus has hidden a wonderful surprise with the 493 PPI gift for us taking beautiful and clear pictures at anywhere anytime. It has more cool features under camera options that you would love. Got no more words to say about it but I JUST LOVE IT! 10/10
  

  3. Display : QUAD HD Display = Beautiful Display. Yes, It looks cool when the brightness stays at the range of around 50%. Believe me, You don't want to use the screen brightness at the lowest unless you want to save power consumption. 10/10
  

  4. Speaker : Crystal clear! It has two speakers. One at the top and another at the bottom. All two in front of the phone. There is none on the back side. Though You might want to reduce the volume while on the phone call. It might hurt a little bit. But still very good clarity. 9/10
  

  5. Battery life : That means...our life. Lol.. I should say that It has a fair battery life. You can just use it around 5 hours roughly with Screen-On-Time. But when you want to play high end games, It might not last much longer. The reason is, it has QUAD HD display which is designed to give better clarity all the time. So it consumes more battery power for that. But Believe me, you can use this for a day without playing games. I text my friends all the time but not continuously, which gives me a day for the next turn for charging my phone. Please remember.. Like I said, it has only 4 - 5 hours of SOT roughly. So it completely depends on how you use your phone. 8/10
  

  6. Turbo Charger : One of the coolest features in this phone. Most of the phones got it. However it is must-have feature in this Nexus phone since it has QUAD HD screen which drains the power more often. But don't worry. You don't have to wait so long for your android phone to be fully charged again. You can do it in just an hour. 10/10
  

  Things that bothers me :
  

  1. Performance and Graphics: I can't just say it is a defect. Because I noticed it was lagging a very little bit while playing high end games. I don't know why, It could be the graphics or the performance. I am sorry, I am no expert to find the reason why. I just thought I should inform this to the phone gamers. I am really ok with this very little issue. But that made me hesitated. This is why I could't give score 10 in the first place.
  

  2. Secondary Camera : It is only 2 MP front camera. Selfie lovers are not going to love this one. It looks better out in the daylight. But You can see the differences when you take shots inside the building. Good but not better.

column6: Two month review of my Nexus 6 - 64 GB
column7:
I bought the nexus 6 in august 2015 after the price drop and this review is after the two months of use.
  

  I'm not really going for the specs, coming to the point..
  
  The phone is big ( reason why google made a 5.7 inch successor the 6p) but for me it is comfortable to use, only problem being hard to slip into pockets.
  

  It came with android lollipop which after the update to marshmallow 6.0 is giving a more than average battery life(after moderate use too 50% remains by evening) which is infact a boon considering the fact that you are using a top of the line device with almost the latest hardware, be it the screen or the processor and other components. The turbo charger helps us keep on going long even with the short duration charging of flat 15 minutes.
  
  Front speakers are excellent comparing all the phones that i have used till date be it my old sony xperia zl, samsung or the older sony w550i walkman phone. All apps run smoothly without any issues. The rear camera is awsome too after the latest update lastweek and is quite good for photos and 4 k videos. The front camera is a big dissapointment, the 2mp cam is not even comparable to my old sony zl's front cam.
  
  I don't use the moto headset that came with the phone as i have been using the sony sbh 20 bluetooth  stereo headset with my sony zl earlier. Should say that the headset gives a better output with nexus 6 and it infact pairs much faster compared to my old handset and thus converting a call from the phone earpiece to the bluetooth headset works like a charm and till date it has been working perfectly fine with the NFC pairing option too. The screen protector that comes with the phone is not that great and I have put a tempered glass by MTT Neo. The touch screen feels too good with the MTT tempered glass and in addition to that I am using the nilkin hard bumper case for the added protection.
  
  I bought the 64 gb variant and now the prices have dropped another 5k. At 30k it is the best deal i would say.
  
  Awsome phone!!!
  
  Thank you google and thank you moto!!

Nexus 6 even though large is very comfortable to hold in hand (i have big hands by the way), because of its ergonomics and its not that heavy as well. It fits perfectly in my jeans as well. Got no complaints on that department. Once get used to the size, my 5" S4 looked like a dwarf and believe me you wont have problems getting used to the phone. :)
  
  6" screen is absolutly a beauty and when we lower the brightness to min in auto mode, slight pink coloring is there which i like by the way because i prefer it like that during night times in my room :D. Its bright @ outdoors in direct sunlight as well and Contents on the screen are readable too. Its good for reading and watching vidoes and movies as well.
  
  As far as Performance is concerned my Nexus handles everything smoothly and fastly. Games and apps open faster and transitions are smooth. While doing task switching you will notice teeny tiny lag because of all the pixels it have to push on the screen. But in no way it will hinder your daily usage and you wont notice that unless you are a geek :P. Also i havent noticed a lag because of the encryption. So 5 stars for performance.
  
  Next will be the Camera, 13Mp rear shooter takes some amazing shots in bright conditions and it handles well in low light conditions as well. Images are sharp and color reproduction is good as well. I am not a photoholic so am not comparing camera to that of iphones or galaxys or DSLR. 2mp front cam is good, but noise is visible and its not that sharp. It will good for posting to your social networking site, thats that. Am pretty happy with the camera of Nexus 6.
  
  Lollipop is great, had the Nexus 6 come with Kitkat. i would not have bought it. UI is clean and animations are great and i am in love with the material design :D. But it needs improvement, its very much buggy. For example in my Nexus 6, if i uncheck the automatic date and time option and then change the time manually, the recent apps button is rendered useless and i have to restart the phone to get it to work. Like this some bugs are there, but am sure bugs will be rectified very quickly and i will be getting updates before i know. Quoting my favourite reviwer MKBHD - "There is nothing that Software updates cant improve and Nexus 6 has one of the best hardware available in market to date".I got the 5.0.1 update as well. If this was sammy (samsung), i had to wait months to get the update. This is another reason i bought Nexus. :D :D
  
  Speakers are aaweesomee guys; I seldom heard music through loudspeakers on my S4, but speakers on Nexus 6 changed my attitude completly. But the headset provided with phone is not at all good and provide no noise insulation as well. So for music fans out there buy a good headset.
  
  Another most important thing as far as am concerned is Battery Life. I go to work at 6am in morning and get back home by 8pm and i will be left with atleast 10% of battery and i dont need to carry charger any more. Am very very happy with that. Am getting 4.30-5.15hrs of screen on time what ever the usage is. If you turn on 2g/3g/LTE/wifi all the time then battery lasts for 18-24hrs, if you turn on the cellular/wifi connectivity occassionly then battery lasts fr more than a day. If you seldom use the data connectivity, then you can sctretch the usage upto 2 days :D. 3220MAH is adequate enough for me. Turbo charging is a good asset too but it kicks in only when the charge is less than 15% or 10% (am not sure if that). Gets from 4% to 30% in 15mins and there after charges normally-gets to 100% in under 1.5hrs.
  
  Call quality is good, its loud and clear unless your in a noisy environment like a travelling bus by the window side :P
  

  1 thing i absolutly loved in Nexus 6/Lollipop is the facial password. If you turn on facial password and when in lockscreen a small circle will be shown at the bottom of screen. if the face is recognized it will unlock or else it will show the lock in the circle, you can then swipe up the screen to type your alternate password and unlock device. facial recognition is very fast and a neat feature which i use all the time.
  
  Google Now works even when the screen is off and its pretty accurate too in recognizing our voice.

column6: An Amazing phablet with some flaws!
column7:
I had my eyes on this device months before it was officially launched by Moto. So, when the price dropped and FK had that Cashback offer, i booked it without a second thought.
  
  Got it in my hands well before the promised date and trust me the first thing you feel as you take this device in your hands is the premium quality and the great feel it has.
  
  I am coming from a 5.5 incher Note 2 and if something like that feels comfortable in your hands, this thing is going to be amazing!
  

  Pros:
  
  1. Very thin and premium looking device.
  
  2. The QHD screen is gorgeous
  
  3. Turbo charger takes around an one and a half hour to charge this device from 0-100.
  
  4. With Snapdragon 80 beast comes, Great processing power. This is almost the same rig that comes with the samsung high end NOTE 4.
  
  5. RAW and pure android 5.1.1 makes this device very very snappy.
  
  6. Fast updates - it's been three days since i booted this device and have already got 3 updates ( 1 major-2 minor)
  
  7. Great inbuilt sound - If you have some good pair of headphones, this phone can make great use of them. I have a Sennheiser PX-200 II and they sound pretty great! The bundled earphones are great as well.
  
  8. AMAZING front firing speakers - This is a beast in this department as well. two speakers on the front of the screen and they are clear, crisp and loud! better than any phone out there. Almost sounds like you are playing over a soundbar.
  
  9. Size - Fits perfect in my hand. Note 2 left me asking for more! This device just filled the gaps! It can be big if you have small hands.
  
  10. Watching movies and playing games on that QHD screen is a great experience.
  


  Cons:
  
  1. Slippery Design. If you don't get a cover for this device, it's gonna slip out of the hand.
  
  2. Two handed usage (Mostly) - The device is big and slippery, i needs two hands * sometimes* to reach to the other end of the screen comfortably.
  
  3. Battery - The battery is almost BAD. with just 3.5 hrs of screen on time, this leaves you dissatisfied and trying to use this beautiful device a bit less just to save some juice on it. looking at this beauty, it's a shame. Most of it can be attributed to the QHD screen.
  
  4. Camera - If you want a good camera on your phone, this is NOT the phone you should get. The camera is really bad. maybe it's just the software tweak that may be required to get the best out of it but i haven't found it yet and it continues to underperform and dissapoint!
  
  5. Back Design - If you keep this phone on the table, it just doesn't sits still. You can almost spin it. Since it has a tapered design and only the centre of the phone's back touches the table. hard to type while this is on a flat surface.
  

  Well, that's all i had. This phone is a beast overall. But like i said, the flaws are big. But mostly smarphones are trading off between these features, aren't they? you just can't have it all in one!
  
  If you're a heavy use like me, this phone packs all the power. But you might have to carry a portable charger with you. I still love this and can see myself using this device for next year and a half before i go back to the note series if they bring out a pure android edition by then. HIghly unlikely though!

column6: This Lollipop is both sweet and sour
column7:
I have been using this phone for the past one month.  Bought it from Flipkart (where else??) and they sweetly delivered the phone the very next day.  As soon as I opened the package, I was blown away by the size of the phone.  And the sweeter thing was that despite the size, the phone is fairly easy to handle because of the curved backside that gives it a good grip in the hand. And I just love the metal outline to the body.  During the ongoing winter months, the metal rim actually chills down and whenever you pick the phone after few minutes of idle time, it gives a nice cold touch.
  

  Look-wise, the phone looks premium and the NEXUS logo looks classy at the back.  It definitely helps make a style statement of sorts when you hold the phone to your ear and the Nexus logo visible to the everyone around you. Subtle but drives the point home. On the front side, you get the full advantage of the almost 6-inches of super AMOLED screen due to very thin bezels.
  

  The phone runs Lollipop as all of you know but I am not a techie to comment upon how good or bad it is.  All I have experienced so far is that it gels well with many good applications which come preloaded and you can use them to make your daily life streamlined and structured.
  

  The processor is definitely sweet and the GPU also does its job well.  I tried basic gaming and have not experienced any lags during game play.
  

  But for all the sweetness there are some basic stuff which leaves a bit of a sour taste in the mouth.
  

  1. To begin with, there is no FM radio (pre-installed) which I believe is a big downer since most of the other phones have this facility.  I know I can stock up music and use Google play but the radio gives you that sense unpredictability about the next song and also the intermittent joviality of the RJ so I definitely miss it
  

  2. I am an amateur photographer and I love to carry around my DSLR but there are those few moments where i would like to rely on my phone camera and thats the second disappointment.  The back camera is of 13MP but lacks versatility. Effects and customization are limited.  I mean very limited.  The only part that wow'd me was the fisheye/panorama effect but other than that, the camera effects are fairly pedestrian.  The previous phone (honor 6) had better camera effects than this. Google photos is just different kind of instagram and its irritating when google tries to encroach your space into the google drive.
  

  3. You can't put the phone in silent mode..!!!!  I might be missing a point here but somehow lollipop does not have a facility to put the phone on mute.  You can organize your preference to allow all incoming calls/alerts (read interruptions) or the priority ones or  none at all.  The issue is when you chose "none", it stops the alarm too.  so definitely, this is proving to be very difficult for me especially when I am sleeping as I prefer to put the phone on silent mode to avoid interruptions. Not sure why you would take away such a basic feature.
  

  4. The front camera, the so-called selfie camera lacks punch with only 2MP lens.  So if you are a selfie-freak then look the other way.  In my previous phone Honor 6, I found this very intuitive feature in the front facing camera.  One, it has a self-timer or 3 seconds and second, the screen highlights the portion where you should see to get the prefect selfie.  Simple, basic but drives the point home. No such feature in this one though..!!
  

  Overall, I am happy about some good features that are new but disappointed with some previous facilities being taken away basis i dont know what analysis Google would have done.

Google Nexus 6 is a supersized version of the new Moto X that has been given a two-handed booster shot and, appropriately, received a Lollipop.
  

  This is the first smartphone to run Android 5.0 Lollipop and, really, there's no better way to experience all of the changes Google has made to its operating system.
  

  It parades the new Material Design interface on a massive 6-inch display, moves seamlessly between apps thanks to the latest Snapdragon processor and 3GB of RAM, and lasts all day with a Qi-chargeable 3220 mAh battery.
  

  Nexus 6 review
  

  Nexus 6 isn't for everyone, especially one-handed texters who think a 5.2-inch Moto X pushes the limit, but Motorola has what may be the best Android phablet yet with few feature misgivings.
  

  Key features
  

  The Nexus 6 has a head-turning 5.96-inch AMOLED display that is not only bigger and brighter than the Moto X, it edges out the 5.5-inch iPhone 6 Plus in every way.
  

  That's because it doubles down on Apple's full HD screen with a more stunning 1440 x 2560 resolution and 493 pixels per inch. It's officially welcomed into the Quad HD club.
  

  Nexus 6 review
  

  Yes, that Quad HD club already includes Android members like the LG G3 and Samsung Galaxy Note 4, but Google Nexus 6 stands out from the pack with its exaggerated display.
  

  There's no 6-inch juggernaut like it and its edge-to-edge display and on-screen soft buttons maximize the screen real estate while minimizing the overall phone's dimensions.
  

  It's bigger without feeling overbearing: 159.3mm (6.27in) tall, 83.0 mm (3.15in) wide and a depth of 3.8mm - 10.1mm (0.15in - 0.39in). It weighs noticeable but acceptable 184g (6.49oz).
  

  Design
  

  Google Nexus 6 also feels better in the hand for its size. Motorola's design, borrowed from the Moto X, gives it a sturdy BendGate-free aluminum metal frame and gently curved back.
  

  Google Nexus 6 review
  

  The curve feels natural against my hand or, in most cases, hands and the plastic back is at least smooth. There are no Moto Maker customizations for wood or leather backs here.
  

  Nexus 6 colors are limited to either Cloud White or Midnight Blue with the advantage of being compatible with Qi wireless chargers, a feature all tricked-out Moto X phones don't support.
  

  Nexus 6 review
  

  Google's new phone also benefits from dual speakers at the top and bottom and comes with a Turbo Charger that juices up the phone with six additional hours of battery in just 15 minutes.
  

  Specs
  

  At the heart of the Nexus 6 is a 2.7Ghz Qualcomm Snapdragon 805 quad-core processor that has an Adreno 420 GPU. It's a top-of-the-line chip for Google's largest Android phone yet.
  

  Backing that up is 3GB of RAM and a reasonable 32GB or 64GB of internal storage. Notice, there's no silly 16GB model to cheapen the value.
  

  Nexus 6 review
  

  All of these Nexus 6 specs aren't overkill. It's important for the lightweight, but feature-filled Android Lollipop update that's pre-installed on the phone.
  

  Android does more things than ever in the background: running multiple apps, receiving notifications that hit the new lockscreen non-stop, making the instantly accessible Google Now available with one swipe to the left and performing voice searches whenever I say the "Okay Google" prompt.
  

  Camera
  

  Around back, there's a 13-megapixel camera that seems to be on par with 13-megapixel Moto X snapper. It's not. It has a better Sony IMX214 sensor with a wider f/2.0 aperture and optical image stabilization.
  

  Nexus 6 review
  

  This trumps the Moto X camera specs that comprise of an older sensor and lacked OIS. It's also far superior to what we got with 8-megapixel Nexus 5 camera last year.
  

  We'll evaluate camera performance with plenty of samples, run conclusive battery life tests and pour over every other feature in-depth throughout the week.
  
  VERDICT
  

  Nexus 6 proves that Google's Nexus program is not only far from dead, it's alive and kicking with a powerful 6-inch phablet that runs its latest Android software.

column6: Well tried Google, but not upto the mark,
column7:
I used Nexus 6 for about a week. All that time I was on wifi and never turned on mobile data. I had turned on mobile data (I have a 2G data plan) only few days back and thereafter, I noticed random shut down of the device. I have to manually turn on the device. To provide more details, I have locked my sim with a pin, if that matters. Since I have a 2g data plan, I changed the preferred data network from lte to 3g and then to 2g, but even after that I noticed random shut down. Since I guess there is some network related issue, I switched on the aeroplane mode (with mobile data on prior to turning on aeroplane mode) and immediately the device powered off by itself. When I switched it on again, it powered off one more time when I was at the sim unlock screen (since I had set up a sim lock pin). After that, I booted my device and disabled sim lock, but even after that, I noticed a random shut down. Then I changed my preferred data type to lte(since it's recommended). I also noticed that when the shut down occurred, the device was relatively hot than the temperature at normal usage. Out of the total 4 to 5 shut downs, 2 to 3 shut downs occurred when I was playing a game (Crazy Taxi). These shut downs occurred after switching on the mobile data.
  

  I did a factory reset and then updated to 5.0.1, then used as it is for about a week with only 2 to 3 third party apps installed. I faced no random shut downs during this period. Thereafter I installed all my apps (around 160) and suddenly the device turned little hot and it turned off. Therefore,the issue has got something to do with RAM management/memory leaks as it can not handle very heavy usage. I can thus say that it is a software bug and maybe google will fix it with a software update. However,I did not expect such issues with such a high end device,therefore, I returned the device and got the refund.
  
  For a highly priced device like nexus 6,we expect a bug-free device. It's not just the specs under the hood that makes a device better. You need your hardware and software in sync to work flawlessly. Moreover, it is just an ordinary android device. With such a huge screen,we at-least expect some multi tasking features. Just one advice to all users - If you are a moderate to heavy user,this device may not be for you unless the bugs are fixed,else it is a great device. Instead,spend few more bucks and get note 4.

Writing this review after using the Nexus 6 for the past 2 weeks....
  

  Was very skeptical about buying this phone at first due to the size (moved from the Moto G). Read many a review which criticized how large the phone actually was. When I received it, it indeed seemed very large, however, have gotten so used to it now that anything smaller just doesn't seem right.
  

  The price seemed fairly high considering that the Nexus 5 was priced almost 14K lower. But the specs made it seem like a sweet deal compared to the flagships of HTC & Samsung. Yes, one can argue that smaller chinese start-ups like One Plus or Oppo manufacture phones with similar specs that are much cheaper, but the fact that its a NEXUS (stock android, priority updates etc.) won me over.
  

  The build quality is exceptional and the phone feels good & comfortable to hold. Contrary to other reviews, the phone has never felt slippery or like it would pop out of my hand at any moment.
  

  The display is nothing short of fantastic & watching a 1080p movie is an incredible experience with the dual front facing speakers.
  

  Unlocked the bootloader & rooted on Day 1 (Its a Nexus afterall :)). Installed Tasker, Double Tap To Wake (through XDA) & enabled the LED under the speaker grill (through Light Flow). 'Ok Google' works great with the screen off (similar to the Active Listening feature on the Moto X) as Google/Motorola have included hardware to support the feature.
  

  Installed a ton of resource heavy games (COD-Heroes, Real Racing, FIFA etc.) and have never felt the phone lag at all. Performance is buttery smooth with Lollipop and it makes it feel like a huge step up from Kitkat (which it is).
  

  Battery backup wasn't excellent and I used to get between 12-15 hours of usage before hitting 20%. Installed a few apps to improve battery life and it worked wonders. Greenify has helped improve battery life to around 18 hours. I know that I would get at least 10% more if I enable DS Battery Saver but 18 hours is more than enough for me. Especially when a 15 -30 min charge using the turbo charger can take me back to 80% (provided you don't use the phone in between).
  

  The camera is really good in normal light conditions. Some shots can rival DSLR's. Use a photo-editor like Snapseed and you're all set. There is definitely a time lag when clicking in HDR mode which may be a bone of contention for some, but its workable for me. The only grouse I have is the twin LED flash. It just seems too powerful & many pictures end up with a strong red-eye.
  

  Finding a case has been extremely difficult, however, recently ordered the Spigen Ultra Hybrid after going through a few reviews on Youtube. Looks promising...
  

  Bottom line - The phone is simply exceptional and looking at the specs ond the fact that its a Nexus, I didn't find it too hard to justify the price to the better half ;) One should go for it if you're looking for a decent flagship at a sub 50K price. DEFINITELY go for it if Stock Android, Priority Updates, Unlocked Bootloaders, Rooting & Flashing Custom ROMS are your thing.
  

  For those that prefer playing it safe, the Moto X 32GB (2nd Gen) is a cheaper alternative with a few compromises.

column6: 6 Inch Lollipop - crafted by Google made by Moto
column7:
Nexus 6 - The best of Android release ever  Lollipop  running on a phone with the top notch specs amongst all the current devices and still way cheaper than closest contenders the Note 4 and iPhone 6Plus
  

  Writing this review after close to a month of usage
  

  Who should not buy?
  

  -Those who need the additional gimmicky features on their phones and willing to compromise on the user experience and with patience to bear the lag even with daily tasks like calls, messaging, taking and viewing photos and who doesn't care about the awesome material design    Can buy Samsung, LG, Sony, HTC etc.
  

  -Those who need even better performance at a very high price and willing to compromise on lots of important features like Bluetooth file transfer, wifi direct, NFC, wireless charging or even use their phone as mass storage device etc. and willing to spend 3k for a charger if they lose one   Can buy iPhone
  

  -Those who need a phone which is a stable performer for daily use with better camera but willing to stay without google services (Gmaps, Drive etc) and compromise on few missing apps or poor quality of the available apps and lack of few features   Can buy Lumia
  

  And all those with tiny hands please think twice even if you want to buy   Consider Moto X
  


  Who should buy?
  

  -Those who need a premium phone with best specs to support all apps and games for at least 2 years from now and willing to deal with the large size of the phone without stylus and fingerprint scanner.
  

  -Those who want to experience how beautiful and impressive the material design of the Lollipop really is in its purest form and who want to get the latest android updates first on their devices even if they might be buggy sometimes at the time of initial release.
  

  -Those who need an android phone with buttery smooth performance at all the times and for all actions, but willing to compromise on some of the less useful features like smart stay, air gestures, pressure, UV, heart rate sensors etc.
  


  Adding some more points for those willing to buy.
  

  Yes, it's a large phone and not very convenient for single handed usage but it will bother you only for the first few days.
  
  The phone feels light and slim. Once you get used to it, trust me you can never go back to a smaller phone and you will never feel it's too large.
  

  #Design - The design is simplistic yet elegant, curved back feels good in hand and the phone feels very thin, the metal frame gives a solid and premium feel.
  
  There is a downside with the curved back, the phone wobbles and rotates when you start typing with the phone lying on the desk.
  

  #Display   It is so amazing that the moment you start using it you will never regret about the large size. You might never need your tablet or even laptop for anything.
  
  There is a pink tint when you turn the brightness to lowest with adaptive brightness turned on, this is nothing major to complain and you can choose to turn off the adaptive brightness.
  
  Ambient display is not well implemented; Double tap to wake is sorely missed.
  

  #Sound - Front firing speakers are really loud and impressive, call quality is good. You will be pleased with the sound quality of the headphone given in the box.
  

  #Camera   13MP camera on the rear is a huge leap from previous nexus devices in terms of image quality. Camera is not fast and the HDR mode is on slower side.
  
  You can take amazing snaps in the day but the low light images might disappoint you. Front camera does very good job thought its 2MP.
  
  Having OIS in it you can definitely expect improvements in low light images in future updates.
  

  #Battery   Battery life is just decent for a device this size with 2k resolution, I am able to get through a day for my usage. However sometimes it's unpredictable. You can expect a maximum of 4-5 hrs of screen on time.
  
  Turbocharger is really handy and the phone charges up really quick. Battery life improvements are expected in upcoming 5.1 update.
  

  #Performance  You will absolutely love the animations and the looks of material design. Everything is superfast except that phone dialer takes slightly longer time to launch.
  
  I did have some apps crashing, reboots and lag before the 5.0.1 update but after the update there are no issues noticed.

column6: Superb phone badly manufactured by Motorola but great service by flipkart
column7:
I got this phone from Flipkart after reading a lot of reviews online. I'll start with the good things first.
  
  1. The phone is superb in terms of the performance. Super smooth response at every level.
  
  2. The sound is the best I have ever experienced in a phone. I was playing a movie in my room and my brother in the adjacent room asked me what channel on the TG was I watching the movie.
  
  3. The android lollipop is very smooth and almost bug free once you upgrade in the beginning during device setup.
  

  Now comes the bad.
  
  1. I got 2 replacements from Flipkart and all three were defective. First one would auto shutdown at battery level of 30% or more after giving a false zero battery indicator. Second phone would show charging indicator even when unplugged and when put on charging it would sometimes not charge and cause the battery level to fall rapidly. The third phone I got had a perfect battery giving me backup of almost 24-28hrs with wifi and data always on and with a screen on time of 5-6.5 hrs which is very good. Unfortunately the screen of this phone had a red tints across the entire lower half of the phone which made its sight unbearable. And considering the fact that you actually pay a premium price for this phone , such defects cannot be tolerated. So I did a lot of reading online and found that these issues are common and mostly due to poor quality battery and screen being used by Motorola.
  
  2. I can understand that electronics can have quality issues and maybe my experience was rare. But the worst thing is that when I called Motorola customer support, they simply told me to take the phone to service centre for repair. I mean, how can they expect us to take a brand new phone for clear manufacturing defects?
  

  But the best part was the service from Flipkart. At every stage they tried to troubleshoot the problem. They knew what needs to be checked and what had to be done to see if the problem goes away. This in my opinion should have been done by Motorola.
  
  Finally I have not been able to get a defect free phone which maybe a rare thing but Flipkart has initiated a refund for me after giving 2 replacements. So kudos to Flipkart. You have just got yourself a loyal customer for life.
  
  Final verdict: if you can afford it, give it a shot. You will get used to the size and fall in love with the phone. If you get a defect free phone, keep it but be prepared to get harassed by Motorola in case anything goes wrong once Flipkart 30 days guarantee gets over.

column6: Moto X Force: May the force be with you
column7:
After using this device for few days I must say this device is a worthy Flagship. All those Buttery hands and performance freaks give it a try.
  

  Design: Sturdy and long lasting. It feels good to hold this device in hand. apart from shatter shield , back of this device is made of ballistic nylon which is used in bullet proof equipments. Screen size might be a drawback for some people like me. Phones above 5 inch screen size are not easy to hold and use with one hand. Still I'm satisfied with the way it is made with narrow bezels and screen to body ratio of 69-70% , making it a bit compact than others. This Device feels good to hold.
  

  Performance: I got it on android 6.0 out of the box. Device runs perfectly fine, there is no lag at all. Play whatever games you want to. Multitasking and everything is butter smooth. Benchmark Rating of this device is slightly better than other snapdragon 810 devices with 3gb ram. Moto exclusive features like voice, display , actions are too good.
  

  Display: Display is something that surprised me. I wanted to to see how display looks like after that much protection and it really excellent. Bright and Natural colours. I was expecting heating issue because of snapdragon 810 but there isn't any such issue at all it remains cool and works smooth.
  

  Camera: Camera is better than expected.. Front camera is too good. CCT flash is plus point. Camera in low light is good. OIS would have been a good addition. It has got dxo rating of 84 which lies in top 4 fr camera.
  

  Sound Quality: Despite Not have stereo speakers at top and bottom it does have good and loud speakers. I compared it to style and it works as good as moto x style. Dedicated 5 mic technology and sound reduction are like gems to this device.
  

  Battery: Battery is one of the biggest advantages of this device. whopping 3760 MAh with turbo charging technology. With one full charge I spend my whole day with 15-25% remaining. It gives charge of around 8 hours of standard use within 15 minutes. It also supports QI wireless charging.
  

  Advantages:
  
  1.Shatter shield and sturdy back( ballistic nylon)
  
  2. Moto x exclusive features like moto voice , display, actions
  
  3. Stock Android ( 6.0 out of the box)
  
  4. Free from malware and extra apps which makes phone a bit slow
  
  5. Camera with dxo rating of 84
  
  6. Smooth Performance
  
  7. 5 mic technology
  
  8. Long Lasting Battery with turbo and wireless charging.
  
  Disadvantages
  
  1. Although I did not find any disadvantage as such but still an addition of certain thing like OIS, Fingerprint sensor would have been better.
  
  2. Price might disappoint most of the people as Motorola generally keeps price slightly lower than other. But Still this device worth its price.
  

  Verdict: Despite price being on Higher side I would suggest everyone to spend a bit exta penny to experience this beast. May the force be with you.

column7:
I hope everybody will find answers of their questions in my review
  
  Bought this phone few days ago for RS 15,599
  
  (Note1 :- I did not purchased this phone for shatterproof technology and fingerprint sensor, only few people 100/10 give priority to shatterproof phone)
  
  (Note2:- This phone is not VOLTE and do not make any hope that you can enable VOLTE with youtube tricks, rooting the phone could be dangerous, wait if motorola gives any official update for VOLTE)
  

  Design :- is very good and pretty premium, specially wide screen (personally i prefer wide screen phones do not like geometry box shape of phone) ballestic nylon feels great (9/10)
  

  Screen:- On the paper its a 2K screen with AMOLED technology, But trust me its not a true AMOLED screen, colors are washed out, SAMSUNG AMOLED screen has no match with this so I just compared  ZTE Nubia side by side with this and found NUBIA Z11 LCD sceen has much better punchy and saturated color with deep black. (6/10)
  

  OS:- This is the part where this phone skills, pure Nougat android experience  , specially  notifications are the best, sensors are excellent and sensitive  feels nice whenever you wave your hand over the phone or pick up the  phone from the pocket it shows time and notifications (9/10)
  

  Camera:- Camera is fine in lighting condition with good auto focus and practically no body takes occasional photos in dark areas weather your have DSLR you will prefer taking photos only in good lighting condition (8/10)
  

  Processing:- There is no problem in speed, its a super sonic (9/10)
  

  Heating:- I found heating while charging with turbo charger (5/10)
  

  Battery :- Battery drains with 4G (and my experience is that none of phone in market do not give full day or two days battery backup weather you have 2500 mah or 3750 mah, you have to charge your phone twice )
  

  Sound:- Phone speaker sound is pretty loud , and hands free included with the phone is awesome i have not experienced this excellent sound in this price range phone ( did not tested other hands free with this phone)
  

  Conclusion :- This phone is value for money with price 14k to 15k, after all you are getting motorola technology with 21mp camera, ok screen, shatterproof technology. Giving this phone only 3/5 stars because of heating issue and  i did not like screen quality as i prefer AMOLED screens.
  

  Main points
  
  Not true AMOLED screen (If you have previously used SAMSUNG Amoled phones)
  
  Heating problem (Specially with trubo charger)
  
  Battery drains with 4G
  
  No VOLTE support yet
  

  Final:- You can definitely buy this phone if you want good looking, simple sober,strong, long lasting phone packed with practical and realistic features  like notification, as i have experienced that motorola phones can last upto 3 to 4 years.

I had the option of converting my microSD card as internal memory, but since I am a proponent of flexibility, I didn't go for that option.
  

  The audio sound quality is amazingly good...20 times better than my earlier mobile which was a Sony XPeria Z1. The 21 MP camera is extremely good...the images are sharp and the colors are vibrant. You have to be slightly careful while taking snaps because the camera responds immediately. Even the selfies are good because the phone comes with a front-facing flash along with the camera. Low-light shots turn out really well.
  

  The battery has lasted for more than a day even after heavy usage (browsing, installing, playing music, testing camera, talking, etc.). I am not planning to throw my phone down to test the shatterproof screen...so I cannot comment on this feature, which is the main selling point. Processor speed is good and it is able to handle multiple apps at the same time without lag. The Moto app helps you set up voice control commands and the phone responds to your commands quite well after you set it up...and with time, it will understand you better!
  

  Over time, I will know if the performance deteriorates and I might provide more inputs then. For now, I can guarantee this is a good buy.

column6: Every thing is fine,,,but its not true AMOLED screen
column7:
I hope everybody will find answers of their questions in my review
  
  Bought this phone few days ago for RS 15,599
  
  (Note1 :- I did not purchased this phone for shatterproof technology and fingerprint sensor, only few people 100/10 give priority to shatterproof phone)
  
  (Note2:- This phone is not VOLTE and do not make any hope that you can enable VOLTE with youtube tricks, rooting the phone could be dangerous, wait if motorola gives any official update for VOLTE)
  

  Design :- is very good and pretty premium, specially wide screen (personally i prefer wide screen phones do not like geometry box shape of phone) ballestic nylon feels great (9/10)
  

  Screen:- On the paper its a 2K screen with AMOLED technology, But trust me its not a true AMOLED screen, colors are washed out, SAMSUNG AMOLED screen has no match with this so I just compared  ZTE Nubia side by side with this and found NUBIA Z11 LCD sceen has much better punchy and saturated color with deep black. (6/10)
  

  OS:- This is the part where this phone skills, pure Nougat android experience  , specially  notifications are the best, sensors are excellent and sensitive  feels nice whenever you wave your hand over the phone or pick up the  phone from the pocket it shows time and notifications (9/10)
  

  Camera:- Camera is fine in lighting condition with good auto focus and practically no body takes occasional photos in dark areas weather your have DSLR you will prefer taking photos only in good lighting condition (8/10)
  

  Processing:- There is no problem in speed, its a super sonic (9/10)
  

  Heating:- I found heating while charging with turbo charger (5/10)
  

  Battery :- Battery drains with 4G (and my experience is that none of phone in market do not give full day or two days battery backup weather you have 2500 mah or 3750 mah, you have to charge your phone twice )
  

  Sound:- Phone speaker sound is pretty loud , and hands free included with the phone is awesome i have not experienced this excellent sound in this price range phone ( did not tested other hands free with this phone)
  

  Conclusion :- This phone is value for money with price 14k to 15k, after all you are getting motorola technology with 21mp camera, ok screen, shatterproof technology. Giving this phone only 3/5 stars because of heating issue and  i did not like screen quality as i prefer AMOLED screens.
  

  Main points
  
  Not true AMOLED screen (If you have previously used SAMSUNG Amoled phones)
  
  Heating problem (Specially with trubo charger)
  
  Battery drains with 4G
  
  No VOLTE support yet

I bought this mobile yesterday and I must say I am very impressed with the whole package of features that comes with it. I went for the 64GB variant and the mobile is shipped with the Marshmallow version of the Android OS. Installation and setup is a piece of cake. I had the option of converting my microSD card as internal memory, but since I am a proponent of flexibility, I didn't go for that option.
  

  The audio sound quality is amazingly good...20 times better than my earlier mobile which was a Sony XPeria Z1. The 21 MP camera is extremely good...the images are sharp and the colors are vibrant. You have to be slightly careful while taking snaps because the camera responds immediately. Even the selfies are good because the phone comes with a front-facing flash along with the camera. Low-light shots turn out really well.
  

  The battery has lasted for more than a day even after heavy usage (browsing, installing, playing music, testing camera, talking, etc.). I am not planning to throw my phone down to test the shatterproof screen...so I cannot comment on this feature, which is the main selling point. Processor speed is good and it is able to handle multiple apps at the same time without lag. The Moto app helps you set up voice control commands and the phone responds to your commands quite well after you set it up...and with time, it will understand you better!
  

  Over time, I will know if the performance deteriorates and I might provide more inputs then. For now, I can guarantee this is a good buy.

Dear all, after staying on BB OS 10 with Z 10 and Z 30 for more than 3 year I wanted to move on to Android. After a thorough research and going and various reviews on youtube, flipkart, amazon, techrader, gsmarena etc, I finally zeroed on two products Honor 7 and Moto X Force. And out of two I finally made it to Moto X Force. Following are few Pros and Cons that I found after 3 days of usage:
  

  Pros:
  
  1- Pretty good and fast camera (Front and back both, you can take 3 pictures in one sec)
  
  2- Exceptional brightness and display
  
  3- Fast browsing and data transfer
  
  4- Comfortable to hold ( though I don't have big hands)
  
  5- Amazing battery life (3760 MAH, expect close to 35 Hrs)
  
  6- Fast charging (40-100 in 40 Mins)
  
  7- Ergonomic design though it is 9.2 mm thick but in hand it feels 5-6 mm due to curved back
  
  8- Smart lock feature: Till it is in your hand or case it remains unlock, so no need to unlock it every time (so faster that any finger print sensor usage
  
  9- Stock android so you can use your own preferred launcher, I found Microsoft's Arrow launcher pretty cool
  

  Cons:
  
  1- Found volume rocker little sharp
  
  2- Speaker is just OK ( coming from BB Z30 which has marvelous speakers)
  
  3- Earphone is OK
  

  Infamous Heating Isssue:
  

  So far I have found it to be some gimmick, phone is all fine, handles all task pretty well, no heating during charging, video streaming, browsing etc ( used it continuously for more than 2 hours)  I don't know why lots of people are reporting heating issue.
  

  Internet is full of heating issues with S6, S7, HTC 10, iphone 6-7 etc.
  

  Final: Go ahead and buy it

Excellent product at 12999. Between 32GB(12999) and 64GB(15599) , the only difference being internal storage and for just around 25GB increment made no sense to pay 2600 INR. With that price you can buy a 128GB micro sd card and increase your storage space by a huge margin. Now coming to the pros and cons:
  

  1. Quad HD screen
  
  2. Shatter proof display
  
  3. Excellent photo quality and video quality at day time
  
  4. Wireless charging
  
  5. Fast charging
  
  6. Good Battery backup
  
  7. Android Nougat now available
  
  8. No overheating or network or screen issues faced as reported by other reviewers
  
  9. 2016 flagship at a lower mid range price in 2017. Sweet! Unless you require a dual sim this is the one to go for as compared to the likes of lenovo z2 plus, redmi note 4 etc
  
  10. Stock UI
  
  11. Moto gestures
  

  Cons:
  

  1. No Jio VOLTE support (not a con for me) even after Nougat update
  
  2. No dual sim even though the sim tray is that of a hybrid variety
  
  3. Stock camera app sucks big time. You cannot default video recording to 4k. The moment you restart the camera app, the default video setting is back to 1080p. No 1080p 60 frames option although the hardware is capable.
  
  4. Available total RAM is only 2.5 GB, although it hardly matters for this device. Overall RAM management is good.
  

  I would highly recommend this device if you are getting it at 12999 (32GB). column6: Every thing is fine,,,but its not true AMOLED screen
column7:
I hope everybody will find answers of their questions in my review
  
  Bought this phone few days ago for RS 15,599
  
  (Note1 :- I did not purchased this phone for shatterproof technology and fingerprint sensor, only few people 100/10 give priority to shatterproof phone)
  
  (Note2:- This phone is not VOLTE and do not make any hope that you can enable VOLTE with youtube tricks, rooting the phone could be dangerous, wait if motorola gives any official update for VOLTE)
  

  Design :- is very good and pretty premium, specially wide screen (personally i prefer wide screen phones do not like geometry box shape of phone) ballestic nylon feels great (9/10)
  

  Screen:- On the paper its a 2K screen with AMOLED technology, But trust me its not a true AMOLED screen, colors are washed out, SAMSUNG AMOLED screen has no match with this so I just compared  ZTE Nubia side by side with this and found NUBIA Z11 LCD sceen has much better punchy and saturated color with deep black. (6/10)
  

  OS:- This is the part where this phone skills, pure Nougat android experience  , specially  notifications are the best, sensors are excellent and sensitive  feels nice whenever you wave your hand over the phone or pick up the  phone from the pocket it shows time and notifications (9/10)
  

  Camera:- Camera is fine in lighting condition with good auto focus and practically no body takes occasional photos in dark areas weather your have DSLR you will prefer taking photos only in good lighting condition (8/10)
  

  Processing:- There is no problem in speed, its a super sonic (9/10)
  

  Heating:- I found heating while charging with turbo charger (5/10)
  

  Battery :- Battery drains with 4G (and my experience is that none of phone in market do not give full day or two days battery backup weather you have 2500 mah or 3750 mah, you have to charge your phone twice )
  

  Sound:- Phone speaker sound is pretty loud , and hands free included with the phone is awesome i have not experienced this excellent sound in this price range phone ( did not tested other hands free with this phone)
  

  Conclusion :- This phone is value for money with price 14k to 15k, after all you are getting motorola technology with 21mp camera, ok screen, shatterproof technology. Giving this phone only 3/5 stars because of heating issue and  i did not like screen quality as i prefer AMOLED screens.
  

  Main points
  
  Not true AMOLED screen (If you have previously used SAMSUNG Amoled phones)
  
  Heating problem (Specially with trubo charger)
  
  Battery drains with 4G
  
  No VOLTE support yet
  

  Final:- You can definitely buy this phone if you want good looking, simple sober,strong, long lasting phone packed with practical and realistic features  like notification, as i have experienced that motorola phones can last upto 3 to 4 years.

column6: A mobile worth every paise/penny spent!
column7:
I bought this mobile yesterday and I must say I am very impressed with the whole package of features that comes with it. I went for the 64GB variant and the mobile is shipped with the Marshmallow version of the Android OS. Installation and setup is a piece of cake. I had the option of converting my microSD card as internal memory, but since I am a proponent of flexibility, I didn't go for that option.
  

  The audio sound quality is amazingly good...20 times better than my earlier mobile which was a Sony XPeria Z1. The 21 MP camera is extremely good...the images are sharp and the colors are vibrant. You have to be slightly careful while taking snaps because the camera responds immediately. Even the selfies are good because the phone comes with a front-facing flash along with the camera. Low-light shots turn out really well.
  

  The battery has lasted for more than a day even after heavy usage (browsing, installing, playing music, testing camera, talking, etc.). I am not planning to throw my phone down to test the shatterproof screen...so I cannot comment on this feature, which is the main selling point. Processor speed is good and it is able to handle multiple apps at the same time without lag. The Moto app helps you set up voice control commands and the phone responds to your commands quite well after you set it up...and with time, it will understand you better!
  

  Over time, I will know if the performance deteriorates and I might provide more inputs then. For now, I can guarantee this is a good buy.

column6: Best Phone I have used until now!!!!!!
column7:
Pre-ordered my Nexus on 18th Nov and Flipkart delivery was very fast as usual, got it the 2nd day the phone started selling in india. Kudos to flipkart on that.
  
  As far as the phone is concerned, its a beast. I owned a galaxy S4 before this one, so i was tired of the laggy, bloated sammy and its touchwiz UI. Galaxy Note4 even though crammed with same specs and better utilities and camera, meant nothing to me because i never used the gimmicks S4 offerd.
  
  Nexus 6 even though large is very comfortable to hold in hand (i have big hands by the way), because of its ergonomics and its not that heavy as well. It fits perfectly in my jeans as well. Got no complaints on that department. Once get used to the size, my 5" S4 looked like a dwarf and believe me you wont have problems getting used to the phone. :)
  
  6" screen is absolutly a beauty and when we lower the brightness to min in auto mode, slight pink coloring is there which i like by the way because i prefer it like that during night times in my room :D. Its bright @ outdoors in direct sunlight as well and Contents on the screen are readable too. Its good for reading and watching vidoes and movies as well.
  
  As far as Performance is concerned my Nexus handles everything smoothly and fastly. Games and apps open faster and transitions are smooth. While doing task switching you will notice teeny tiny lag because of all the pixels it have to push on the screen. But in no way it will hinder your daily usage and you wont notice that unless you are a geek :P. Also i havent noticed a lag because of the encryption. So 5 stars for performance.
  
  Next will be the Camera, 13Mp rear shooter takes some amazing shots in bright conditions and it handles well in low light conditions as well. Images are sharp and color reproduction is good as well. I am not a photoholic so am not comparing camera to that of iphones or galaxys or DSLR.  2mp front cam is good, but noise is visible and its not that sharp. It will good for posting to your social networking site, thats that. Am pretty happy with the camera of Nexus 6.
  
  Lollipop is great, had the Nexus 6 come with Kitkat. i would not have bought it. UI is clean and animations are great and i am in love with the material design :D. But it needs improvement, its very much buggy. For example in my Nexus 6, if i uncheck the automatic date and time option and then change the time manually, the recent apps button is rendered useless and i have to restart the phone to get it to work. Like this some bugs are there, but am sure bugs will be rectified very quickly and i will be getting updates before i know. Quoting my favourite reviwer MKBHD - "There is nothing that Software updates cant improve and Nexus 6 has one of the best hardware available in market to date".I got the 5.0.1 update as well. If this was sammy (samsung), i had to wait months to get the update. This is another reason i bought Nexus. :D :D
  
  Speakers are aaweesomee guys; I seldom heard music through loudspeakers on my S4, but speakers on Nexus 6 changed my attitude completly. But the headset provided with phone is not at all good and provide no noise insulation as well. So for music fans out there buy a good headset.
  
  Another most important thing as far as am concerned is Battery Life. I go to work at 6am in morning and get back home by 8pm and i will be left with atleast 10% of battery  and i dont need to carry charger any more. Am very very happy with that. Am getting 4.30-5.15hrs of screen on time what ever the usage is. If you turn on 2g/3g/LTE/wifi all the time then battery lasts for 18-24hrs, if you turn on the cellular/wifi connectivity occassionly then battery lasts fr more than a day. If you seldom use the data connectivity, then you can sctretch the usage upto 2 days :D. 3220MAH is adequate enough for me. Turbo charging is a good asset too but it kicks in only when the charge is less than 15% or 10% (am not sure if that). Gets from 4% to 30% in 15mins and there after charges normally-gets to 100% in under 1.5hrs.
  
  Call quality is good, its loud and clear unless your in a noisy environment like a travelling bus by the window side :P
  

  1 thing i absolutly loved in Nexus 6/Lollipop is the facial password. If you turn on facial password and when in lockscreen a small circle will be shown at the bottom of screen. if the face is recognized it will unlock or else it will show the lock in the circle, you can then swipe up the screen to type your alternate password and unlock device. facial recognition is very fast and a neat feature which i use all the time.
  
  Google Now works even when the screen is off and its pretty accurate too in recognizing our voice.
  

  Cons :
  

  Lollipop is buggy but it will improve eventually.
  
  No need of messenger app when you have hangouts.
  

  Am completely satisfied with the 44k i spent on my Nexus 6 unlike the 40Kk spent on S4 and i will recommend it to any1 looking for a decent phone and not some fancy gimmicks.

column6: Great all round Phone, this Nexus beast!
column7:
This phone is an absolute beast created by Google & Motorola! It's been around a month & a half since I have been using this phone & I would like to share my initial impressions about the same. I was using an iPhone 6 plus (16gb) before this, but handed the same over to my wife since I needed more storage space, so picked the 64gb Nexus 6. Also the price drop was a major factor in my purchase too!
  
  What's great:
  
  - The display in Quad HD is eye popping & beautiful! Everything looks rich & vivid, including movies & youtube videos
  
  - The processor functions like a beast! Completing tasks is a breeze & multitasking is superb
  
  - Android Lollipop (when purchased) was my best experience using Android (I returned to Android after a long gap after using IOS for almost 3 years). Marshmallow is even better with great battery saving & the same fluid interface as earlier
  
  - In-built Google Apps work seamlessly & take care of almost all my needs of using the phone
  
  - Power charging is top class & is such a convenience. Overall charge time is super quick & makes using the phone easy with no worries even if battery has drained; a quick charge ensures juice enough to use it longer
  
  What's good:
  
  - Battery life is decent & lasts me a little over a day. With minimal usage I can get through 2 days, however with heavy usage, it drains by the end of the day
  
  - The camera is good, I use a DSLR so my phone is used as a casual alternative & it does not disappoint for this kind of use
  
  - The phone design & finish is pretty good, however I do recommend using a back cover since it can be quite slippery even with a curved back
  
  - This phone supports wireless charging, although I haven't tried it (Great feature considering the new Nexus phones don't have this)
  
  - The front dual speakers are pretty decent too, although they do screech a bit at higher volumes
  
  - Audio performance with headphones is good. I use Senheiser CX 300 in-ears & the performance is quite good
  
  What could have been better:
  
  - The screen is curved at the edges & this is a big pain  when it comes to finding a screen guard or a tempered glass. This is more of a personal itch that I have, although the phone comes with a scratch resistant Gorilla glass display which is excellent, I still wanted a tempered glass screen guard. I must have searched the entire city & whatever I found left a big halo around the edges due to the curves. I finally found the best tempered glass online which was a US import; fits the screen only, not on the edges! (Yootech Tempered Glass for Nexus 6)
  
  - Audio quality of the supplied earphones is pretty ordinary, for a phone at this price, the headphones could have been better
  

  Overall:
  
  This is no doubt one of the best phones I have ever used & having used the iPhone 6 plus for a few  months before this, I can vouch for this statement. The 6 plus is a great phone with a super long lasting battery, but I feel the Nexus 6 has a better display & Android Marshmallow comes closest to the smooth IOS performance with the freedom of Android, making it a better alternative in my opinion. Although IOS I feel is still a safer eco system & Google can feel quite intrusive at times. Would recommend that you go through Google's privacy settings carefully to disable anything you feel can invade your privacy beyond your comfort zone! I don't find the Nexus 6 big, since I used the 6 plus before this & funnily the 6 plus feels smaller after the Nexus 6. I love big screen phones, so I don't mind the lack of one handed use ability.
  
  This phone is highly recommended, although critic reviews were quite mixed, my experience has been great. I think with Motorola build quality & a 5.96 inch screen with wireless charging feature, this phone contains some features even missing in the newly released 6PP. Phones that people choose are personal choices & IOS & Android are almost at a stage where they seem to be borrowing each other's  features. So I would not say that I recommend this phone over others, but I have listed what has worked well for me with the Nexus 6. If this is what you are looking in your phone too, then go for it, as its still available at a mouth watering price with a mind blowing screen & high end features.

column6: A sweet deal at this price
column7:
Nexus 6 was definitely overpriced when it was released, back in late 2014. Current price of 30k for the 32 GB version, however, is very compelling.
  

  Here's why you should go for this phone:
  

  - Stock Android, fast updates. I'm already running Marshmallow (Preview 3). You get a clean and smooth experience. Sure, Lollipop had many bugs initially, but 5.1.1 smoothed many things out. Also the ability to unlock the bootloader easily and install custom software is a must have for me.
  

  - Awesome performance: 5.1 improved performance and battery life, and it's flying more than ever in Marshmallow. It's a noticeable upgrade from my Nexus 4, which is still reasonably fast. Snapdragon 805 really flexes its muscles powering the QHD display, and 3 GB of RAM is aplenty.
  

  - Decent battery life: 1.5 to 2 days of usage under normal conditions. Doze in Marshmallow should be improving it even further.
  

  - Fast charging: It's a must have in present times.
  

  - Decent camera: Camera is reasonably snappy and takes good pictures. Definitely not the best one around, but still packs a punch. The camera module is the same as that of One Plus One. Dual LED flash. The flash ring is mostly a gimmick though.
  

  - Screen: I love looking at this QHD display. It's HUGE and beautiful. Sure, it's not the most accurate calibration, but looks a little punchy. I didn't find it too warm or too blue. Touchscreen is very responsive as expected. It's AMOLED panel is a generation behind the ones in latest Samsung flagships, so it's probably not as efficient as current generation. But no worries otherwise.
  

  - Front facing speakers: Combined with the screen, it makes an awesome media consumption experience. Loudness and clarity is more than decent.
  

  Now some cons:
  

  - No slow motion video: Though the hardware is more than capable of doing it, 60fps and 120fps video capture is not present. A quick Google/XDA search suggests that this is a limitation with the camera drivers used, so installing 3rd party apps probably won't help.
  

  - Front camera is only 2 MP: Though it takes decent pics, detail is limited due to this. Even in 2014, 5 MP front cameras were becoming a standard.
  

  - A bit on the heavier side: This may not be a problem for most. Also, the huge dimensions of the phone might take a little getting used to. But its totally worth it.
  

  - No finger-print scanner: Now it feels like I'm nit-picking, but Marshmallow is bringing native support for them, and new Nexus devices likely to be unveiled in September 2015 are also likely to have it. It would have been a nice addition to this phone.
  

  - I don't think the lack of removable storage is a problem anymore, with 32GB and 64GB versions available. Battery is also non-removable, which is a non-issue for me, but could be an issue for some. I think LG G4 is the decent choice available for such people.
  

  On the whole, it has been an awesome upgrade for me from my Nexus 4. Hopefully, slow-mo video support will come in the future. #Nexus4Life!

column7:
(Please Take the time to read the review, I'm sure it will help) So, The nexus 6 is a very very good phone and of course it is a fab device on paper (Google flagship.DUH!) but it lags behind in some aspects in day to day life. This review can be broken down into 2 segments. The SO good, The Not so good.
  

  Pro's: 1. The epic screen... Lately with the jump into the QHD world smartphones have been giving us wonderful screens. The nexus 6 with its 5.96 inch QHD screen is no exception. It's gorgeous and perfectly saturated with over 16M hues. But it's not the ABSOLUTE best large screen out there. I would give that to the Note 4 because I personally like that extra saturation.
  

  2. It's a nexus.... It would receive updates faster and give you a great materialistic software experience with Android L and so on.
  

  3.Camera.... It's easily the best camera by motorola so far...On par with the Moto Turbo.... It performs well in all lighting conditions and takes classy shots.
  

  4.Performance(multitasking and stuff....)... It's great with the general animations and scrolling and whatsoever you need to do with your device...
  

  5.Additional features.... Touchless control by motorola... Dual front facing speakers (which is the first time dual front facing speakers by motorola has been introduced( No. The Moto X had only a single driver on the bottom not dual speakers.) and water resistance makes it great for use.
  

  6.Of course.... It's built like a tank. It has a great soft touch feeling and the metal band makes it feel premium. Some people would find this a little big but it's overall a great feeling phone.
  

  Not so good category...
  

  1. Software experience.... It's great but android lollipop does very little to help with the single hand experience.
  

  2. Battery life.... Even though it has a 3220 mAh battery but we're in those 1st gen QHD phone section so it has a very slightly above average battery life in the real world mainly because it has all those extra pixels to push.
  

  3.Camera (sigh!) it has a great performing camera as we discussed earlier but due to its sensor it gives slightly grainy shots in extremely low light to low light conditions and the photo snapping process is a little slow compared to other flagships.
  

  4.Performance... Hello,
  
  For everyone who are looking forward to buy this device, a word of caution, this is a large phone with 5.96 inch. But that said, don't get intimidated with its size, you'll get used to it. Graduating from iPhone 4S after using for nearly 2 1/2 yrs, this was a big leap forward for me. I wanted to buy a premium phone with 1 day battery life, top of the line processor and hi-res display as I'm a pretty heavy user with my phone is loaded with graphic games like asphalt, nova 2 etc, WhatsApp, net browsing of all other things. This left me with very few options namely nexus 6, iPhone 6 plus, Note 4, LG G3.
  
  I tried my hands on G3 and Note 4 at Reliance Digital store, but I was unimpressed with its UI. It was lagging (might have been the issue with that piece). and second problem with these devices is the OS update schedule. Samsung and LG are very slow in updated their phones (Only recently they have upgraded to Android 5.0.1). So these two phones were cancelled from the list. This left me with Nexus 6 and iPhone 6 plus.
  
  iPhone 6 plus is really expensive device retailing at 62.5K for 16 GB model. Hence I decided to go with Nexus 6 which was steal of a buy at 33k for 32gb model with exchange. The main reason for going with nexus 6 was Lollipop out of box, otherwise android was a big no for me.
  
  Nexus 6 came with Lollipop 5.0 out of box. Was soon updated to 5.0.1 which fixed many issues from the initial OS release.
  
  After using it 2-3 weeks (bought it on 2nd January, 2015), I wanted to return the phone as it would frequently restart and would heat up as high as 42 deg with little use such as texting and web browsing. I called up Motorola customer care and they guided me to clear the cache memory and factory reset the phone, which I did and the issue was solved. A piece of advice to all, if you experience issues with restarting, heating or abnormal battery drain, kindly clear the cache memory and factory reset it, which should solve the problem.
  
  Talking about the phone, this is a beast of a device. with Snapdragon 805 processor coupled with 3 GB RAM, it just flies through the tasks thrown at it without breaking any sweat.
  
  The screen is a gem to look at with colour reproduction, crisp to read text and a healthy amount of pixel density (but is battery hogger, the screen on time is 4 hrs to 4 1/2 hrs) and the stereo speaker are loud enough and the output is clear enough.
  
  The quick charging feature is really handy as it charges the phone from 10% to 40% in 15 mins with phone kept on standby mode. The phone really heats up during this time, hence advised not to use the phone while charging. The phone cools down to ambient temp once the battery is fully recharged (which takes about an hr and half), so don't worry about the heating.
  
  The headphones provided are not very good, it gives decent output but I would suggest to use headphones from other brand to get better output.
  
  Coming to camera, I'm a bit disappointed with its low light. Taking photos in broad daylight or good light condition gives excellent detailed , sharp pictures using 13Mp, f 2.0 sensor.

  Phone has nano sim card slot.
  
  So overall this phone is a very good phone if you want to stick with Nexus series. column6: Best Phone I have used until now!!!!!!
column7:
Pre-ordered my Nexus on 18th Nov and Flipkart delivery was very fast as usual, got it the 2nd day the phone started selling in india. Kudos to flipkart on that.
  
  As far as the phone is concerned, its a beast. I owned a galaxy S4 before this one, so i was tired of the laggy, bloated sammy and its touchwiz UI. Galaxy Note4 even though crammed with same specs and better utilities and camera, meant nothing to me because i never used the gimmicks S4 offerd.
  
  Nexus 6 even though large is very comfortable to hold in hand (i have big hands by the way), because of its ergonomics and its not that heavy as well. It fits perfectly in my jeans as well. Got no complaints on that department. Once get used to the size, my 5" S4 looked like a dwarf and believe me you wont have problems getting used to the phone. :)
  
  6" screen is absolutly a beauty and when we lower the brightness to min in auto mode, slight pink coloring is there which i like by the way because i prefer it like that during night times in my room :D. Its bright @ outdoors in direct sunlight as well and Contents on the screen are readable too. Its good for reading and watching vidoes and movies as well.
  
  As far as Performance is concerned my Nexus handles everything smoothly and fastly. Games and apps open faster and transitions are smooth. While doing task switching you will notice teeny tiny lag because of all the pixels it have to push on the screen. But in no way it will hinder your daily usage and you wont notice that unless you are a geek :P. Also i havent noticed a lag because of the encryption. So 5 stars for performance.
  
  Next will be the Camera, 13Mp rear shooter takes some amazing shots in bright conditions and it handles well in low light conditions as well. Images are sharp and color reproduction is good as well. I am not a photoholic so am not comparing camera to that of iphones or galaxys or DSLR.  2mp front cam is good, but noise is visible and its not that sharp. It will good for posting to your social networking site, thats that. Am pretty happy with the camera of Nexus 6.
  
  Lollipop is great, had the Nexus 6 come with Kitkat. i would not have bought it. UI is clean and animations are great and i am in love with the material design :D. But it needs improvement, its very much buggy. For example in my Nexus 6, if i uncheck the automatic date and time option and then change the time manually, the recent apps button is rendered useless and i have to restart the phone to get it to work. Like this some bugs are there, but am sure bugs will be rectified very quickly and i will be getting updates before i know. Quoting my favourite reviwer MKBHD - "There is nothing that Software updates cant improve and Nexus 6 has one of the best hardware available in market to date".I got the 5.0.1 update as well. If this was sammy (samsung), i had to wait months to get the update. This is another reason i bought Nexus. :D :D
  
  Speakers are aaweesomee guys; I seldom heard music through loudspeakers on my S4, but speakers on Nexus 6 changed my attitude completly. But the headset provided with phone is not at all good and provide no noise insulation as well. So for music fans out there buy a good headset.
  
  Another most important thing as far as am concerned is Battery Life. I go to work at 6am in morning and get back home by 8pm and i will be left with atleast 10% of battery  and i dont need to carry charger any more. Am very very happy with that. Am getting 4.30-5.15hrs of screen on time what ever the usage is. If you turn on 2g/3g/LTE/wifi all the time then battery lasts for 18-24hrs, if you turn on the cellular/wifi connectivity occassionly then battery lasts fr more than a day. If you seldom use the data connectivity, then you can sctretch the usage upto 2 days :D. 3220MAH is adequate enough for me. Turbo charging is a good asset too but it kicks in only when the charge is less than 15% or 10% (am not sure if that). Gets from 4% to 30% in 15mins and there after charges normally-gets to 100% in under 1.5hrs.
  
  Call quality is good, its loud and clear unless your in a noisy environment like a travelling bus by the window side :P
  

  1 thing i absolutly loved in Nexus 6/Lollipop is the facial password. If you turn on facial password and when in lockscreen a small circle will be shown at the bottom of screen. if the face is recognized it will unlock or else it will show the lock in the circle, you can then swipe up the screen to type your alternate password and unlock device. facial recognition is very fast and a neat feature which i use all the time.
  
  Google Now works even when the screen is off and its pretty accurate too in recognizing our voice.
  

  Cons :
  

  Lollipop is buggy but it will improve eventually.
  
  No need of messenger app when you have hangouts.
  

  Am completely satisfied with the 44k i spent on my Nexus 6 unlike the 40Kk spent on S4 and i will recommend it to any1 looking for a decent phone and not some fancy gimmicks.
