column6: Great all round Phone, this Nexus beast!
column7:
This phone is an absolute beast created by Google & Motorola! It's been around a month & a half since I have been using this phone & I would like to share my initial impressions about the same. I was using an iPhone 6 plus (16gb) before this, but handed the same over to my wife since I needed more storage space, so picked the 64gb Nexus 6. Also the price drop was a major factor in my purchase too!
  
  What's great:
  
  - The display in Quad HD is eye popping & beautiful! Everything looks rich & vivid, including movies & youtube videos
  
  - The processor functions like a beast! Completing tasks is a breeze & multitasking is superb
  
  - Android Lollipop (when purchased) was my best experience using Android (I returned to Android after a long gap after using IOS for almost 3 years). Marshmallow is even better with great battery saving & the same fluid interface as earlier
  
  - In-built Google Apps work seamlessly & take care of almost all my needs of using the phone
  
  - Power charging is top class & is such a convenience. Overall charge time is super quick & makes using the phone easy with no worries even if battery has drained; a quick charge ensures juice enough to use it longer
  
  What's good:
  
  - Battery life is decent & lasts me a little over a day. With minimal usage I can get through 2 days, however with heavy usage, it drains by the end of the day
  
  - The camera is good, I use a DSLR so my phone is used as a casual alternative & it does not disappoint for this kind of use
  
  - The phone design & finish is pretty good, however I do recommend using a back cover since it can be quite slippery even with a curved back
  
  - This phone supports wireless charging, although I haven't tried it (Great feature considering the new Nexus phones don't have this)
  
  - The front dual speakers are pretty decent too, although they do screech a bit at higher volumes
  
  - Audio performance with headphones is good. I use Senheiser CX 300 in-ears & the performance is quite good
  
  What could have been better:
  
  - The screen is curved at the edges & this is a big pain  when it comes to finding a screen guard or a tempered glass. This is more of a personal itch that I have, although the phone comes with a scratch resistant Gorilla glass display which is excellent, I still wanted a tempered glass screen guard. I must have searched the entire city & whatever I found left a big halo around the edges due to the curves. I finally found the best tempered glass online which was a US import; fits the screen only, not on the edges! (Yootech Tempered Glass for Nexus 6)
  
  - Audio quality of the supplied earphones is pretty ordinary, for a phone at this price, the headphones could have been better
  

  Overall:
  
  This is no doubt one of the best phones I have ever used & having used the iPhone 6 plus for a few  months before this, I can vouch for this statement. The 6 plus is a great phone with a super long lasting battery, but I feel the Nexus 6 has a better display & Android Marshmallow comes closest to the smooth IOS performance with the freedom of Android, making it a better alternative in my opinion. Although IOS I feel is still a safer eco system & Google can feel quite intrusive at times. Would recommend that you go through Google's privacy settings carefully to disable anything you feel can invade your privacy beyond your comfort zone! I don't find the Nexus 6 big, since I used the 6 plus before this & funnily the 6 plus feels smaller after the Nexus 6. I love big screen phones, so I don't mind the lack of one handed use ability.
  
  This phone is highly recommended, although critic reviews were quite mixed, my experience has been great. I think with Motorola build quality & a 5.96 inch screen with wireless charging feature, this phone contains some features even missing in the newly released 6PP. Phones that people choose are personal choices & IOS & Android are almost at a stage where they seem to be borrowing each other's  features. So I would not say that I recommend this phone over others, but I have listed what has worked well for me with the Nexus 6. If this is what you are looking in your phone too, then go for it, as its still available at a mouth watering price with a mind blowing screen & high end features.

column6: A sweet deal at this price
column7:
Nexus 6 was definitely overpriced when it was released, back in late 2014. Current price of 30k for the 32 GB version, however, is very compelling.
  

  Here's why you should go for this phone:
  

  - Stock Android, fast updates. I'm already running Marshmallow (Preview 3). You get a clean and smooth experience. Sure, Lollipop had many bugs initially, but 5.1.1 smoothed many things out. Also the ability to unlock the bootloader easily and install custom software is a must have for me.
  

  - Awesome performance: 5.1 improved performance and battery life, and it's flying more than ever in Marshmallow. It's a noticeable upgrade from my Nexus 4, which is still reasonably fast. Snapdragon 805 really flexes its muscles powering the QHD display, and 3 GB of RAM is aplenty.
  

  - Decent battery life: 1.5 to 2 days of usage under normal conditions. Doze in Marshmallow should be improving it even further.
  

  - Fast charging: It's a must have in present times.
  

  - Decent camera: Camera is reasonably snappy and takes good pictures. Definitely not the best one around, but still packs a punch. The camera module is the same as that of One Plus One. Dual LED flash. The flash ring is mostly a gimmick though.
  

  - Screen: I love looking at this QHD display. It's HUGE and beautiful. Sure, it's not the most accurate calibration, but looks a little punchy. I didn't find it too warm or too blue. Touchscreen is very responsive as expected. It's AMOLED panel is a generation behind the ones in latest Samsung flagships, so it's probably not as efficient as current generation. But no worries otherwise.
  

  - Front facing speakers: Combined with the screen, it makes an awesome media consumption experience. Loudness and clarity is more than decent.
  

  Now some cons:
  

  - No slow motion video: Though the hardware is more than capable of doing it, 60fps and 120fps video capture is not present. A quick Google/XDA search suggests that this is a limitation with the camera drivers used, so installing 3rd party apps probably won't help.
  

  - Front camera is only 2 MP: Though it takes decent pics, detail is limited due to this. Even in 2014, 5 MP front cameras were becoming a standard.
  

  - A bit on the heavier side: This may not be a problem for most. Also, the huge dimensions of the phone might take a little getting used to. But its totally worth it.
  

  - No finger-print scanner: Now it feels like I'm nit-picking, but Marshmallow is bringing native support for them, and new Nexus devices likely to be unveiled in September 2015 are also likely to have it. It would have been a nice addition to this phone.
  

  - I don't think the lack of removable storage is a problem anymore, with 32GB and 64GB versions available. Battery is also non-removable, which is a non-issue for me, but could be an issue for some. I think LG G4 is the decent choice available for such people.
  

  On the whole, it has been an awesome upgrade for me from my Nexus 4. Hopefully, slow-mo video support will come in the future. #Nexus4Life!

column6: Nexus 6: A stellar device with a few drawbacks....
column7:
(Please Take the time to read the review, I'm sure it will help) So, The nexus 6 is a very very good phone and of course it is a fab device on paper (Google flagship.DUH!) but it lags behind in some aspects in day to day life. This review can be broken down into 2 segments. The SO good, The Not so good.
  

  Pro's: 1. The epic screen... Lately with the jump into the QHD world smartphones have been giving us wonderful screens. The nexus 6 with its 5.96 inch QHD screen is no exception. It's gorgeous and perfectly saturated with over 16M hues. But it's not the ABSOLUTE best large screen out there. I would give that to the Note 4 because I personally like that extra saturation.
  

  2. It's a nexus.... It would receive updates faster and give you a great materialistic software experience with Android L and so on.
  

  3.Camera.... It's easily the best camera by motorola so far...On par with the Moto Turbo.... It performs well in all lighting conditions and takes classy shots.
  

  4.Performance(multitasking and stuff....)... It's great with the general animations and scrolling and whatsoever you need to do with your device...
  

  5.Additional features.... Touchless control by motorola... Dual front facing speakers (which is the first time dual front facing speakers by motorola has been introduced( No. The Moto X had only a single driver on the bottom not dual speakers.) and water resistance makes it great for use.
  

  6.Of course.... It's built like a tank. It has a great soft touch feeling and the metal band makes it feel premium. Some people would find this a little big but it's overall a great feeling phone.
  

  Not so good category...
  

  1. Software experience.... It's great but android lollipop does very little to help with the single hand experience.
  

  2. Battery life.... Even though it has a 3220 mAh battery but we're in those 1st gen QHD phone section so it has a very slightly above average battery life in the real world mainly because it has all those extra pixels to push.
  

  3.Camera (sigh!) it has a great performing camera as we discussed earlier but due to its sensor it gives slightly grainy shots in extremely low light to low light conditions and the photo snapping process is a little slow compared to other flagships.
  

  4.Performance... As discussed earlier this device will perform great for day to day use and run all games like buttery smooth but the fact that it has all those extra pixels to push it very rarely to "less than often"ly drops frames in general animations in daily activities. But it may be fixed with more software update....
  

  Verdict: Great phone with a few general drawbacks but a must buy for a nexus lover.

I wanted to buy a premium phone with 1 day battery life, top of the line processor and hi-res display as I'm a pretty heavy user with my phone is loaded with graphic games like asphalt, nova 2 etc, WhatsApp, net browsing of all other things. This left me with very few options namely nexus 6, iPhone 6 plus, Note 4, LG G3.
  
  I tried my hands on G3 and Note 4 at Reliance Digital store, but I was unimpressed with its UI. It was lagging (might have been the issue with that piece). and second problem with these devices is the OS update schedule. Samsung and LG are very slow in updated their phones (Only recently they have upgraded to Android 5.0.1). So these two phones were cancelled from the list. This left me with Nexus 6 and iPhone 6 plus.
  
  iPhone 6 plus is really expensive device retailing at 62.5K for 16 GB model. Hence I decided to go with Nexus 6 which was steal of a buy at 33k for 32gb model with exchange. The main reason for going with nexus 6 was Lollipop out of box, otherwise android was a big no for me.
  
  Nexus 6 came with Lollipop 5.0 out of box. Was soon updated to 5.0.1 which fixed many issues from the initial OS release.
  
  After using it 2-3 weeks (bought it on 2nd January, 2015), I wanted to return the phone as it would frequently restart and would heat up as high as 42 deg with little use such as texting and web browsing. I called up Motorola customer care and they guided me to clear the cache memory and factory reset the phone, which I did and the issue was solved. A piece of advice to all, if you experience issues with restarting, heating or abnormal battery drain, kindly clear the cache memory and factory reset it, which should solve the problem.
  
  Talking about the phone, this is a beast of a device. with Snapdragon 805 processor coupled with 3 GB RAM, it just flies through the tasks thrown at it without breaking any sweat.
  
  The screen is a gem to look at with colour reproduction, crisp to read text and a healthy amount of pixel density (but is battery hogger, the screen on time is 4 hrs to 4 1/2 hrs) and the stereo speaker are loud enough and the output is clear enough.
  
  The quick charging feature is really handy as it charges the phone from 10% to 40% in 15 mins with phone kept on standby mode. The phone really heats up during this time, hence advised not to use the phone while charging. The phone cools down to ambient temp once the battery is fully recharged (which takes about an hr and half), so don't worry about the heating.
  
  The headphones provided are not very good, it gives decent output but I would suggest to use headphones from other brand to get better output.
  
  Coming to camera, I'm a bit disappointed with its low light. Taking photos in broad daylight or good light condition gives excellent detailed , sharp pictures using 13Mp, f 2.0 sensor.
  
  The latest flavour of android is really very eye pleasing and brings in a whole new lot of improvement and features compared to previous versions of android. This being the nexus device, you'll be the first to receive the latest OS from the Google and being a vanilla version this is free of any bloat-ware or OEM customisation, which is in a way good and bad depending on your personal preference.
  
  Coming from iOS, I still feel android lagging in few areas as the OS is not optimised for the big screen of Nexus 6 mainly easy of use. Though android allows customisation but lacks in ease of use.
  
  If you are comfortable with manually updating the OS using the factory image then the new version of lollipop i.e.. 5.1 (build LMY47I) is available on the android developer website. I would suggest go ahead and flash this new build as this brings a host of bug fixes and improvement. The battery life has significantly improved and the restart problem has been totally resolved. If you are a beginner or new to android like me search YouTube for detailed walk-through on installing the factory image.
  
  I would recommend this phone to everyone looking out for buying a premium android device which comparable performance with comparison of iPhone 6 plus at nearly 60% of its price.

  Phone has nano sim card slot.

column6: Good phone but only dissatisfaction is the pale screen!
column7:
Before writing this let me you, my trust and loyalty lies with Motorola 100%...I have been using this brand since the days of Motorola Atrix 2 and have used the Moto G, G (2nd generation) and now Nexus (a Moto make). All the phones were exchanged in very good condition with an average ownership of 1.5 to 2 years which is a testament to the fact that Moto produces the most durable phones in the smartphone arena. I gifted my wife (then fiancee) a Samsung Galaxy and later on a Xpera L (coz she somehow didn't like the Moto design) and mind you none of the phone even lasted a year (all technical issues which the service centres could do nothing about). Hey! before judging any further, my wife is quite meticulous with her gadgets and on the contrary I am the one who is more frisky. Enuf of the Moto story...
  

  Now coming down to Nexus, although launched in 2014, this device would still give many other high end smartphones a run for their money in terms of performance. So no questions there...games run slick, apps never hang no matter how many you install, apps open in a blink and the list goes on...
  

  I read many articles on heating issue particularly while charging and most them suggests either a software upgrade or the use of a normal charger (non turbo one). Although haven't done any software upgrade of the phone yet but definitely the normal charger does the trick.  All of the professional reviewers confirm that heating of phones (particularly near the battery) is not a big deal owing to the use of turbo chargers.....
  

  The only downside which I am wondering how Moto could let go is the paleness of the screen. And believe me its considerably pale when compared to its predecessors or any other branded phone for that matter. Most suggests to download screen adjuster and adjust the bluish hue to about 15-17 points which actually solves issue to at least about 90%! But still this is something which didn't allow me to give this phone a full 5 rating...
  

  Videos are awesome, earphone is just okay (felt unnecessary bass and surround fx), call quality is great and speakers are definitely loud and external look & feel is premium.
  

  Overall, a very good buy for people who are looking for phones within sub Rs.20k bracket.

column6: Never thought it would be an awesome phone. (Honest Review)
column7:
Let's start with the Impressive Stuffs:
  

  1. Performance : Awesome, can't describe better than that. First off, No lagging while multitasking, Which is very important to me. Still very smooth though I opened 30 apps right after one and let it all run in background at the same time. I could still choose any app at any time by going into the recent tasks option to open any specific app that I want and there was no slow performance that I could notice. So I give 9/10 (Let me explain later why I can't give score 10)
  

  2. Primary Camera : 13 MP.. Seriously?! It looks much more better than 13 MP. That's where Nexus has hidden a wonderful surprise with the 493 PPI gift for us taking beautiful and clear pictures at anywhere anytime. It has more cool features under camera options that you would love. Got no more words to say about it but I JUST LOVE IT! 10/10
  

  3. Display : QUAD HD Display = Beautiful Display. Yes, It looks cool when the brightness stays at the range of around 50%. Believe me, You don't want to use the screen brightness at the lowest unless you want to save power consumption. 10/10
  

  4. Speaker : Crystal clear! It has two speakers. One at the top and another at the bottom. All two in front of the phone. There is none on the back side. Though You might want to reduce the volume while on the phone call. It might hurt a little bit. But still very good clarity. 9/10
  

  5. Battery life : That means...our life. Lol.. I should say that It has a fair battery life. You can just use it around 5 hours roughly with Screen-On-Time. But when you want to play high end games, It might not last much longer. The reason is, it has QUAD HD display which is designed to give better clarity all the time. So it consumes more battery power for that. But Believe me, you can use this for a day without playing games. I text my friends all the time but not continuously, which gives me a day for the next turn for charging my phone. Please remember.. Like I said, it has only 4 - 5 hours of SOT roughly. So it completely depends on how you use your phone. 8/10
  

  6. Turbo Charger : One of the coolest features in this phone. Most of the phones got it. However it is must-have feature in this Nexus phone since it has QUAD HD screen which drains the power more often. But don't worry. You don't have to wait so long for your android phone to be fully charged again. You can do it in just an hour. 10/10
  

  Things that bothers me :
  

  1. Performance and Graphics: I can't just say it is a defect. Because I noticed it was lagging a very little bit while playing high end games. I don't know why, It could be the graphics or the performance. I am sorry, I am no expert to find the reason why. I just thought I should inform this to the phone gamers. I am really ok with this very little issue. But that made me hesitated. This is why I could't give score 10 in the first place.
  

  2. Secondary Camera : It is only 2 MP front camera. Selfie lovers are not going to love this one. It looks better out in the daylight. But You can see the differences when you take shots inside the building. Good but not better.
  

  3. Screen Size : Very huge. But this is Phablet. Can't say this really bothers me as a defect. But It's not really comfortable to carry around in our pant pockets though.
  

  4. Weight : You don't want to risk your phone falling down on the floor. Yes, We need to use two hands while messaging. Otherwise, it is not too heavy to carry around.
  

  Verdict : This is a very good, beautiful phone. I have been using this about a month and I haven't noticed any issues yet. Sometimes you might feel a little heat on your hand while multitasking. It happens when a device runs with 3GB ram or so on. It is not an issue. It happens with most of the high end models. But this one creates a normal heat and that's alright with me though.
  

  I would highly advice to take this phone only if you wanted a big screen mobile with beautiful clarity and for multitasking purpose. then this is it. I personally would not recommend this to any gamers. Overall the score I could give is 8/10.
  

  (Extra Note : Keep updated the stock android OS to use the phone more stable. or if you want to take the best out of your android phone, you need root the phone, try installing the custom ROM, it might give better stable performance and battery life. If you do this, you will lose your mobile warranty. So check with the XDA developers site for more details. Don't brick your phone.)

column6: Two month review of my Nexus 6 - 64 GB
column7:
I bought the nexus 6 in august 2015 after the price drop and this review is after the two months of use.
  

  I'm not really going for the specs, coming to the point..
  
  The phone is big ( reason why google made a 5.7 inch successor the 6p) but for me it is comfortable to use, only problem being hard to slip into pockets.
  

  It came with android lollipop which after the update to marshmallow 6.0 is giving a more than average battery life(after moderate use too 50% remains by evening) which is infact a boon considering the fact that you are using a top of the line device with almost the latest hardware, be it the screen or the processor and other components. The turbo charger helps us keep on going long even with the short duration charging of flat 15 minutes.
  
  Front speakers are excellent comparing all the phones that i have used till date be it my old sony xperia zl, samsung or the older sony w550i walkman phone. All apps run smoothly without any issues. The rear camera is awsome too after the latest update lastweek and is quite good for photos and 4 k videos. The front camera is a big dissapointment, the 2mp cam is not even comparable to my old sony zl's front cam.
  
  I don't use the moto headset that came with the phone as i have been using the sony sbh 20 bluetooth  stereo headset with my sony zl earlier. Should say that the headset gives a better output with nexus 6 and it infact pairs much faster compared to my old handset and thus converting a call from the phone earpiece to the bluetooth headset works like a charm and till date it has been working perfectly fine with the NFC pairing option too. The screen protector that comes with the phone is not that great and I have put a tempered glass by MTT Neo. The touch screen feels too good with the MTT tempered glass and in addition to that I am using the nilkin hard bumper case for the added protection.
  
  I bought the 64 gb variant and now the prices have dropped another 5k. At 30k it is the best deal i would say.
  
  Awsome phone!!!
  
  Thank you google and thank you moto!!
  
  Ofcourse thank you flipkart for bringing me the same in no time!!!

Nexus 6 even though large is very comfortable to hold in hand (i have big hands by the way), because of its ergonomics and its not that heavy as well. It fits perfectly in my jeans as well. Got no complaints on that department. Once get used to the size, my 5" S4 looked like a dwarf and believe me you wont have problems getting used to the phone. :)
  
  6" screen is absolutly a beauty and when we lower the brightness to min in auto mode, slight pink coloring is there which i like by the way because i prefer it like that during night times in my room :D. Its bright @ outdoors in direct sunlight as well and Contents on the screen are readable too. Its good for reading and watching vidoes and movies as well.
  
  As far as Performance is concerned my Nexus handles everything smoothly and fastly. Games and apps open faster and transitions are smooth. While doing task switching you will notice teeny tiny lag because of all the pixels it have to push on the screen. But in no way it will hinder your daily usage and you wont notice that unless you are a geek :P. Also i havent noticed a lag because of the encryption. So 5 stars for performance.
  
  Next will be the Camera, 13Mp rear shooter takes some amazing shots in bright conditions and it handles well in low light conditions as well. Images are sharp and color reproduction is good as well. I am not a photoholic so am not comparing camera to that of iphones or galaxys or DSLR. 2mp front cam is good, but noise is visible and its not that sharp. It will good for posting to your social networking site, thats that. Am pretty happy with the camera of Nexus 6.
  
  Lollipop is great, had the Nexus 6 come with Kitkat. i would not have bought it. UI is clean and animations are great and i am in love with the material design :D. But it needs improvement, its very much buggy. For example in my Nexus 6, if i uncheck the automatic date and time option and then change the time manually, the recent apps button is rendered useless and i have to restart the phone to get it to work. Like this some bugs are there, but am sure bugs will be rectified very quickly and i will be getting updates before i know. Quoting my favourite reviwer MKBHD - "There is nothing that Software updates cant improve and Nexus 6 has one of the best hardware available in market to date".I got the 5.0.1 update as well. If this was sammy (samsung), i had to wait months to get the update. This is another reason i bought Nexus. :D :D
  
  Speakers are aaweesomee guys; I seldom heard music through loudspeakers on my S4, but speakers on Nexus 6 changed my attitude completly. But the headset provided with phone is not at all good and provide no noise insulation as well. So for music fans out there buy a good headset.
  
  Another most important thing as far as am concerned is Battery Life. I go to work at 6am in morning and get back home by 8pm and i will be left with atleast 10% of battery and i dont need to carry charger any more. Am very very happy with that. Am getting 4.30-5.15hrs of screen on time what ever the usage is. If you turn on 2g/3g/LTE/wifi all the time then battery lasts for 18-24hrs, if you turn on the cellular/wifi connectivity occassionly then battery lasts fr more than a day. If you seldom use the data connectivity, then you can sctretch the usage upto 2 days :D. 3220MAH is adequate enough for me. Turbo charging is a good asset too but it kicks in only when the charge is less than 15% or 10% (am not sure if that). Gets from 4% to 30% in 15mins and there after charges normally-gets to 100% in under 1.5hrs.
  
  Call quality is good, its loud and clear unless your in a noisy environment like a travelling bus by the window side :P
  

  1 thing i absolutly loved in Nexus 6/Lollipop is the facial password. If you turn on facial password and when in lockscreen a small circle will be shown at the bottom of screen. if the face is recognized it will unlock or else it will show the lock in the circle, you can then swipe up the screen to type your alternate password and unlock device. facial recognition is very fast and a neat feature which i use all the time.
  
  Google Now works even when the screen is off and its pretty accurate too in recognizing our voice.

  6. Fast updates - it's been three days since i booted this device and have already got 3 updates ( 1 major-2 minor)
  
  7. Great inbuilt sound - If you have some good pair of headphones, this phone can make great use of them. I have a Sennheiser PX-200 II and they sound pretty great! The bundled earphones are great as well.
  
  8. AMAZING front firing speakers - This is a beast in this department as well. two speakers on the front of the screen and they are clear, crisp and loud! better than any phone out there. Almost sounds like you are playing over a soundbar.
  
  9. Size - Fits perfect in my hand. Note 2 left me asking for more! This device just filled the gaps! It can be big if you have small hands.
  
  10. Watching movies and playing games on that QHD screen is a great experience.
  


  Cons:
  
  1. Slippery Design. If you don't get a cover for this device, it's gonna slip out of the hand.
  
  2. Two handed usage (Mostly) - The device is big and slippery, i needs two hands * sometimes* to reach to the other end of the screen comfortably.
  
  3. Battery - The battery is almost BAD. with just 3.5 hrs of screen on time, this leaves you dissatisfied and trying to use this beautiful device a bit less just to save some juice on it. looking at this beauty, it's a shame. Most of it can be attributed to the QHD screen.
  
  4. Camera - If you want a good camera on your phone, this is NOT the phone you should get. The camera is really bad. maybe it's just the software tweak that may be required to get the best out of it but i haven't found it yet and it continues to underperform and dissapoint!
  
  5. Back Design - If you keep this phone on the table, it just doesn't sits still. You can almost spin it. Since it has a tapered design and only the centre of the phone's back touches the table. hard to type while this is on a flat surface.
  

  Well, that's all i had. This phone is a beast overall. But like i said, the flaws are big. But mostly smarphones are trading off between these features, aren't they? you just can't have it all in one!
  
  If you're a heavy use like me, this phone packs all the power. But you might have to carry a portable charger with you. I hope everybody will find answers of their questions in my review
  
  Bought this phone few days ago for RS 15,599
  
  (Note1 :- I did not purchased this phone for shatterproof technology and fingerprint sensor, only few people 100/10 give priority to shatterproof phone)
  
  (Note2:- This phone is not VOLTE and do not make any hope that you can enable VOLTE with youtube tricks, rooting the phone could be dangerous, wait if motorola gives any official update for VOLTE)
  

  Design :- is very good and pretty premium, specially wide screen (personally i prefer wide screen phones do not like geometry box shape of phone) ballestic nylon feels great (9/10)
  

  Screen:- On the paper its a 2K screen with AMOLED technology, But trust me its not a true AMOLED screen, colors are washed out, SAMSUNG AMOLED screen has no match with this so I just compared  ZTE Nubia side by side with this and found NUBIA Z11 LCD sceen has much better punchy and saturated color with deep black. (6/10)
  

  OS:- This is the part where this phone skills, pure Nougat android experience  , specially  notifications are the best, sensors are excellent and sensitive  feels nice whenever you wave your hand over the phone or pick up the  phone from the pocket it shows time and notifications (9/10)
  

  Camera:- Camera is fine in lighting condition with good auto focus and practically no body takes occasional photos in dark areas weather your have DSLR you will prefer taking photos only in good lighting condition (8/10)
  

  Processing:- There is no problem in speed, its a super sonic (9/10)
  

  Heating:- I found heating while charging with turbo charger (5/10)
  

  Battery :- Battery drains with 4G (and my experience is that none of phone in market do not give full day or two days battery backup weather you have 2500 mah or 3750 mah, you have to charge your phone twice )
  

  Sound:- Phone speaker sound is pretty loud , and hands free included with the phone is awesome i have not experienced this excellent sound in this price range phone ( did not tested other hands free with this phone)
  

  Conclusion :- This phone is value for money with price 14k to 15k, after all you are getting motorola technology with 21mp camera, ok screen, shatterproof technology. Giving this phone only 3/5 stars because of heating issue and  i did not like screen quality as i prefer AMOLED screens.
  

  Main points
  
  Not true AMOLED screen (If you have previously used SAMSUNG Amoled phones)
  
  Heating problem (Specially with trubo charger)
  
  Battery drains with 4G
  
  No VOLTE support yet
  

  Final:- You can definitely buy this phone if you want good looking, simple sober,strong, long lasting phone packed with practical and realistic features  like notification, as i have experienced that motorola phones can last upto 3 to 4 years.

column6: A mobile worth every paise/penny spent!
column7:
I bought this mobile yesterday and I must say I am very impressed with the whole package of features that comes with it. I went for the 64GB variant and the mobile is shipped with the Marshmallow version of the Android OS. Installation and setup is a piece of cake. I had the option of converting my microSD card as internal memory, but since I am a proponent of flexibility, I didn't go for that option.
  

  The audio sound quality is amazingly good...20 times better than my earlier mobile which was a Sony XPeria Z1. The 21 MP camera is extremely good...the images are sharp and the colors are vibrant. You have to be slightly careful while taking snaps because the camera responds immediately. Even the selfies are good because the phone comes with a front-facing flash along with the camera. Low-light shots turn out really well.
  

  The battery has lasted for more than a day even after heavy usage (browsing, installing, playing music, testing camera, talking, etc.). I am not planning to throw my phone down to test the shatterproof screen...so I cannot comment on this feature, which is the main selling point. Processor speed is good and it is able to handle multiple apps at the same time without lag. The Moto app helps you set up voice control commands and the phone responds to your commands quite well after you set it up...and with time, it will understand you better!
  

  Over time, I will know if the performance deteriorates and I might provide more inputs then. For now, I can guarantee this is a good buy.

This is a very good phone. If you are buying after the Flipkart promotional discount of rs. 20000 then this is an excellent choice to go with.. the screen of the phone is what they are advertising it to be. It does not break, but scratches nonetheless. So have a tempered on the screen.
  

  And the screen is not as bright as other Moto phones if you chose to believe some reviewers. I do not!! The screen is very bright.. I do not believe those who say otherwise.
  

  Further the phone is eye-catching as the dimensions of this phone are not common. The screen is wider than most of the phones which I find appealing. Plus the back material is ballistic nylon. It has a very nice feel to it. Plus no other phone has a such a body. It feels very premium.
  

  The one thing that I really would like to mention is that at least my phone does not overheat. I have played a lot of games(even some heavy games like asphalt). The phone gets hot but at no point it becomes uncomfortable to hold.. also the battery life is superb.. with phone on 4G and with moderate usage I still get 40-50% remaining everyday.. this is with net on for 24 hours... So I don't think an average user would have battery issues.
  

  This has been a very satisfying purchase for me BUT KEEP IN MIND THAT I HAD TO REPLACE MY PHONE THRICE.. first two had severe hanging issue and the third one was suffering from a speaker issue.. though replacement procedure was very easy. Flipkart gave me no trouble at all.. so if you get a good piece to begin with then consider yourself lucky. But you will enjoy the phone.
  

  Also if you are someone who is clumsy with his/her phone and breaks the device often then this should prove to be a good product for you.. with a tempered glass and a cover this phone is unbreakable..

I bought this phone against the several warnings given by many of my friends since the processor used here is of MediaTek (MT) and not Snapdragon. I had to raise another request again even after doing complete factory reset because vibration still didn't work. Then again, I raised another return request, again spent time explaining the issues to another customer executive, then a technical visit was arranged. I had to make myself free from workplace to make myself available for the technical person to visit and then after several tests carried out in my phone, they agreed to replace with a new handset. After the new handset arrived, the phone now has problems with the gyroscope and magnetometer features as I am not able to view any 360 degree videos in YouTube. When I downloaded the app from Android Play store to test my Gyroscope and Magnetometer, it says that my phone is 100% compatible for VR Experience but the videos are rotating constantly on their own for no reason ruining my VR video watching experience. The parts are probably assembled in a hurry or the processor is not up to the mark or as good as snapdragon processor, I don't know. The phone's price tag is not at all justifiable. The android version is not updated to Nougat yet either. Overall, worst experience with this Moto M 64 GB model (MediaTek Processor). column6: Honest Review After 6 months of use
column7:
I bought this phone on the  launch date of the phone December 2016
  

  PROS:
  
  1) Super fast fingerprint sensor - it works during the stand by mode also
  
  2) 4 GB ram - you will easily get around 1.5gb of Free RAM even if you install 40-50 apps.
  
  3) Gorilla glass 4 - my phone fell down on highway from ceiling many a times still intact display and hardly any noticeable scratch on the phone
  
  4) Spill proof - Phone is spill proof so it doesnt have any problem  if you hold it with wet hand or while shower.
  
  5) 64 GB of huge  ROM - total usable memory is around 55 GB
  
  6) Selfie camera is awesome - but it has slow shutter speed.
  
  7) Looks - gold color looks awesome to hold
  

  Cons
  
  1) Battery - if you are using continuously on 4G network , it wont last a day
  
  2) Heating problem - if you are continuously playing games or videos with Internet on it heats up a lot
  
  3) Back Camera is good for the day light some pictures are awesome but in the night mode it has very high noise. Also No slow motion video recording is there.
  
  4) It has google cast so it does not support most of the latest technology TVs which supports MIRACAST
  
  5) GPS consumes too much battery
  
  6) Price is too high compared to rivals like Redmi not 4
  
  7) Still no update for Android N ( i hope it will increase the battery life)
  

  My suggestion if you want to go for Pure android go for this phone it works really well . If you love some customization like IR blaster , Miracast this phone is not for you.
  

  Final verdict if you dont spend much time using 4G data or GPS go for this phone battery will last 1.5 days.  Till date this phone never hanged not having any problem with the stock android .

The parts are probably assembled in a hurry or the processor is not up to the mark or as good as snapdragon processor, I don't know. The phone's price tag is not at all justifiable. The android version is not updated to Nougat yet either. Overall, worst experience with this Moto M 64 GB model (MediaTek Processor). I bought this phone against the several warnings given by many of my friends since the processor used here is of MediaTek (MT) and not Snapdragon. I had to raise another request again even after doing complete factory reset because vibration still didn't work. Then again, I raised another return request, again spent time explaining the issues to another customer executive, then a technical visit was arranged. I had to make myself free from workplace to make myself available for the technical person to visit and then after several tests carried out in my phone, they agreed to replace with a new handset. After the new handset arrived, the phone now has problems with the gyroscope and magnetometer features as I am not able to view any 360 degree videos in YouTube. When I downloaded the app from Android Play store to test my Gyroscope and Magnetometer, it says that my phone is 100% compatible for VR Experience but the videos are rotating constantly on their own for no reason ruining my VR video watching experience. The parts are probably assembled in a hurry or the processor is not up to the mark or as good as snapdragon processor, I don't know. The phone's price tag is not at all justifiable. The android version is not updated to Nougat yet either. Overall, worst experience with this Moto M 64 GB model (MediaTek Processor). This review is after 3 days of usage. Build quality of this phone is awesome. It feels like a premium smartphone. With metal body and gold look, this smartphone scores full marks in looks department. This being said...a lot of things are wrong with the software and optimization. Why I say this..you'll come to know as you read along. First of all camera....despite being 16MP camera, it doesn't feel like one. Photos are grainy and it's performance in low light is not up to the mark. Front facing 8MP camera is also of same quality as it rear counterpart. Battery life is another disappointing feature of this phone. This phone boasts battery power of 3050mah. 2600mah of moto g3 turbo gives more screen on time than this one. With phone charged to 100 % at 7 in the morning, it doesn't lasts for even 12 hrs, that too after "careful" usage(mind the words not moderate not light but careful usage). This device is powered by Mediatek choose with MaliT860. Though this soc cannot be termed as weak per se, still graphics performance of this device is not what I expected . Frame drops , lags and jitters in heavy and graphic intensive games is quite evident . Fingerprint sensor is fast but not as fast as other devices like moto g4 plus or even 10k range lenovo phones. All these issues do not appear to be hardware related and can be fixed by a comprehensive software update from Motorola. Right now, as is...this phone is not bang for the buck...but can become one after a good software update. Last but not the least...this phone comes with Android M out of the box which right now is least of our concerns but this was unexpected. I hope upgrade to Android N is in Motorola 's agenda.

column6: Moto M review after 1 month of usuage
column7:
I was looking for a good exchange offer for my Samsung ACE phone after 5 years of use, with durable phone with latest android & decent performance. I got a 2500 exchange off for my old phone (3GB version for 13,500). So i will highly recommend to utilize the exchange offer.
  
  Full metal body build & look of the phone is impressive, especially golden color with curvy edges. Moto M has confirmed that there will be Nougat upgrade by first half of 2017. So can expect latest version stock android. I did a software update before using the phone. So far 2 update rolled out by Moto.
  

  Pros
  
  - Build quality - Full metal body design and looks is impressive.
  
  - Audio with Dolby turned on is very crisp and clear. In some reviews there is concern raised on number of speaker, but in Moto website its clearly mentioned its 1 speaker phone and other slot is for mike.
  
  - Delivery was done one day before the proposed date and packaging was good.
  
  - Fingerprint sensor response is very good and placing it in back side improved the accessibility
  
  - User interface is neat and pretty fast. No lag felt so far and really loved stock android.
  
  - Phone come with Microsoft Word, Excel, Power point, Note and Outlook installed which will help to configure your office email faster
  
  - No heating issues found so far. Easily giving more than 1 day of battery with Normal usage.
  
  - Screen guard & transparent back cover provided along with the package is really helpful. Transparent back cover will not spoil the look of phone.
  
  - Photo quality is good. But expectation were high for a 16 Mega pixel camera. I hope after Moto M provide a fix for this in next updates.
  
  - Initially phone charges very fast 10% -> 50% in 20 minutes. But the rate of charging slows drops after one point.
  
  - Display clarity is very good and even in sunlight its very clear. Gorilla glass with curved edges looks good.
  
  Cons
  
  - Option to take selfie by using fingerprint sensor is not available. This would be a good to have feature.
  
  - Gallery is available in file manager only
  
  - USB charger is not compatible. USB Type C is provided due to which other USB cable cannot be used.
  
  - Ring tone setting might require you to copy the required song to the specified folder.
  
  - Video recording provides limited options. Slow motion recording is not available
  
  - Even though dual sim we cannot utilize the second slot if memory card is added
  
  Phone is slightly overpriced, but if you are getting a good exchange it will a good bet. Compared to available mid budget phone from Lenova , I felt the build quality and looks is better with Moto M.

column6: Goods and bads of Moto M...a step by step review
column7:
I have switched over from Samsung Galaxy Note 4 to this phone. And I will try to be as clear as possible.
  

  1. LOOKS: Trendy stylish look. Not very thick or heavy. Would have preferred bezels to be smaller.
  
  2. SPEED: Good but there is a lag in gaming. Otherwise can handle multiple apps easily.
  
  3. SOUND: One of the big positives. Nice clear sound. Reasonably loud.
  
  4. CAMERA: Possibly one of the biggest drawbacks of this phone. I wouldn't exactly expect a very nice camera in this price range. But I would definitely expect the company to be true to their specifications. These are not 16 and 8 mp cameras at all.
  
  5. BATTERY LIFE:- Decent. I am a reasonably heavy user and the battery has enough juice to last from morning till late evening.
  
  6. FINGERPRINT SENSOR: Reasonably responsive.
  

  Overall reasonably priced phone and reasonable features according to the money you pay.
  

  Edit:
  
  After 4 months of use, this is my updated review:-
  
  1. Problem in bluetooth - Every time I need to connect my bluetooth handsfree or any other paired device, I have to go to app settings and clear all data and reconnect
  
  2. Problem in ringer and vibration - The ring and vibration for message/notification stops midway.
  
  3. Problem with proximity sensor - Has become moody. Frequently stops working on its own and then starts working again.
  
  4. Problem with speaker - I am using flip cover. Every time I am on a call and I open the flip cover, call goes to handsfree speaker on its own.
  
  This was my first Motorola phone... and very surely, this ia my last one as well. DISAPPOINTED....

column3: Moto Z Play with Style Mod (White, 32 GB)
column7:
Very happy with the phone and the delivery.
  
  What I like:
  
  Looks:
  
  - Aluminium Bezel
  
  - Glassy backside
  
  - Free style mod (although not classy I did not expect this to be out of the box)
  
  Performance:
  
  - Made in India !!
  
  - Fingerprint sensor is butter smooth
  
  - No Gallery app. Google Photos and Gallery were redundant anyway. So one less bloatware I guess
  
  - Awesome battery life. Lost only 20% since 6 hours with moderate usage (basic app downloads and updates and a bit playing around)
  
  - Phone reception seems good (particularly because the signal is weak in my area)
  
  - Layout and Navigation is the same as Moto X play on Android M 6.0.1
  
  - Camera gives good resolution pic in good lighting. Very grainy if shot in low light
  
  - Front camera is slightly better than Moto X play. Also has a front flash
  
  - Without a software like Ultrapixel for HTC, photos are overall plain in quality
  
  - Ofcourse yet to try out the USP of this product viz. the moto mods. I will probably buy the Incipio PowerGrid and JBL speakers
  
  - Also not tried any load testing to see if it fumbles with any graphic / processor intensive tasks but I heard the Snapdragon (625?) is quite a step from their problematic 620.
  

  What I did not like:
  
  - Heavy to carry due to the bigass battery
  
  - Very thick, though the Aluminium bezel makes it visually good, it's still medieval to have this thickness
  
  - 5.5 inch screen wastes a lot of real estate for the fingerprint sensor (barren land on either side of the sensor)
  
  - Out of the box headphones are as cheap as they come
  
  - Startup language is Hindi by default. As a southie, I had to struggle a bit to navigate until I could change the language.
  
  - Still a lot of bloatware although moto has gotten rid of their own moto assist/emergency etc. etc.

Its a Beast! Love it in White! The moment I started using it, I immediately felt that its a great buy in terms on Performance, Looks, Sound, Camera and Battery. I applied the screen protector front and back the moment I got the phone and a Shockproof clear case which also takes care of the back camera bump. My full honest review is as follows :
  

  1) Performance :
  
  The main small and big points people should know about performance is that the apps install so quickly! Motorola has balanced/tweaked this phone's hardware and software so well that I have not noticed a single lag! There were 1 or 2 apps where the app crashed but worked normal after opening them again... let me tell you "this happens in all the android phones no matter what the price range". I noticed just one time frame drop in asphalt 8 when I played it for the first time after install, apart from this no lag in other heavy games that I played. The speed by which it opens the apps, keyboard open n type, fingerprint unlocking (100% accurate for me), phone dialer and after call if you have 3rd party app call recorder to show summary of the recording pop-up to open, app drawer, Camera, Gestures, etc all is just BLAZING fast and super smooth! Love to keep the animations on .5x , .5x and 1x (in developer options).
  

  2) Looks :
  
  Its big, not a compact 5.5 inch Beast. It has killer looks and style! The feel is also great in the hand... Just a bit heavy as its understandable due to the bigger battery. Display is great but not the best i have seen. Few icons like snapchat, airtel, etc looks cartoonish, like too much color and shine... like popin out 3d . Though music videos, clarity, viewing angles & experience and colors are awesome . I don't feel anything being washed out or anything at all.
  

  3) Sound :
  
  Loud Speaker of the Z PLAY is somewhat I feel like iphone 5s's speaker . Not exactly the same.... but better having more bass and clarity in it and the good part is that it is loud. Good while watching YouTube videos too.
  
  A little dislike about the software while on a call with the in-call speaker volume is, if i reduce the volume while on call of course or while its ringing and complete the talk, and then dial any other number and check the in-call speaker volume level, the volume is back again up to full itself! This never happened in Htc M8 or other phones which i was previously using. It remained to where i had reduced or increased it. On this phone i will need to always reduce the volume manually if required. A software fix should come asap to fix this small issue, so that where i kept the in-call speaker volume to be, it should stay there throughout . Shockingly when I adjust the volume level of the loud speaker on call, that remains to where I had set it even on all next calls I make. Maybe its glitch Motorola/Lenovo missed or I need to reset my phone.
  

  4) Camera :
  
  Camera takes better than decent photos. Laser autofocus is really great! Clear and crisp images. Front camera is nice too Haven't tested the video recording yet. Love the selfie photo mirror option!
  

  5) Battery :
  
  Wow! Battery of this phone is amazing. I have charged it only once from 9% to a 100% full and right now live its been 14 hours and 17 mins since last charge. I have used it to click photos, play 2-3 games (5-5 mins), Install 2-3 heavy games, Made Calls, 45 to 1 hour in total of youtube videos and playing audio songs. 40% Brightness level. Still battery level is 51% remaining. Its fantabulous! Turbo charging is amazing!! Many quick chargers/dash charge just charge quickly to a level of 60 to 70%, but this keeps turbo charging till full 100%.
  

  In the end I give it a 9 out of 10.... I love it! 1 point taken as it doesn't supports miracast/mirroring even if your smart tv has it. You need to have google chromecast to mirror phone's display on your led,smart tv, etc(if your smart tv does not have inbuilt chromecast). I have bought jbl soundboost mod and they are on their way, have not used them yet..... I'm sure the audio and video experience will be on the whole another level and I might change it to a 10 then :P . Being a lover of music and balance, I say its better than 3 or 3t as I would hate bluetooth speakers, low battery back-up efficiency(that's why gimmick dash charge, keep charging is there) and too much power is trouble ;). Hope this honest review helps a lot of you guys out there! Go for it!

column3: Moto Z Play with Style Mod (White, 32 GB)
column7:
I've been using this product for the past 3 days. I took my time before writing a review here as I wanted to assess this device in a better way. So, as other reviewers do, I too want to sum up things by mentioning the Pros and Cons of this device.
  

  Pros:
  

  Battery Backup
  
  Crisp Display
  
  Highly responsive Fingerprint Sensor
  
  Turbo Charge
  
  NFC
  
  Rear Camera
  
  Moto Display
  
  Near-stock Android Experience
  
  Dual SIM (Not Hybrid) with dedicated SD card slot
  

  Cons:
  

  A little heavy device (3510 mAh battery is the reason)
  
  Large bezels
  
  Not-so-good front camera
  

  As some reviewers are complaining about heating while charging the device, for their information, it's pretty common. The device, when connected to TurboCharger, draws more power than conventional chargers in order to charge the battery faster. This excessive power draw results in heating of the device. For others, who are looking for Restart option while holding down the power button, it is not there. Motorola provides a stock Android experience and no stock Android comes with a Restart option (Check Nexus devices).
  

  The device literally stays cool while playing games for a longer time. For graphics-intensive games, any device is bound to get warm, so that's not an issue here. I, personally, haven't felt heat on this device if the device is not connected to TurboCharger. Moto Display is good, saves your time if you want to check notifications on your device without unlocking it. Moto Voice works flawlessly and the fingerprint scanner is pretty fast.
  

  Bezels could have been made shorter and the device would have been not-so-huge then, but we had to sacrifice the battery. The battery lasts long, in a true sense. I charged the battery at 11.30 PM the day before yesterday to 100% and even after being always connected to the WiFi, playing games (for more than 2 hours), messaging, downloading several apps and watching video clips online, the level is now at 38% ( today at 5.30 PM). I believe the SD 625 is the reason here, no excessive power draw and unnecessary overheating. The processor clocked at 2.0 GHz (max) does it's job in multitasking, though I think 4GB of RAM should have been there (memory management is not good if you suspend heavy games in the background).
  

  The rear camera takes photos really quick and clear both in daylight and artificial lights. The colour of the flash is natural warm (a bit yellowish) and I don't know if others too experience this. But both the cameras take photos without much yellow tint (with flash). A 8MP front camera could have been a better choice, though. The front-facing speaker is not so loud, but I can't say it's not good.
  

  Till now, it's a good choice to buy this device. People who are looking for OnePlus 3 over this Moto Unit, please keep in mind, you may not get a good servicing for your product, if, at all, your device needs to visit it's respective service center.
  

  I will update this review if the experience changes or if there's something important that is needed to be shared.

column3: Moto Z Play with Style Mod (White, 32 GB)
column7:
Really I was waiting for this device for quite some time and it's a beast. Got this phone on exchange and other offers combined at 17k which is a stellar deal! Ordered on 17th and got it in a day delivery. Flipkart always does a great job in delivery and exchange offers. It does included a diagnostic function to check your old phone condition! Flipkart app service is wonderful.
  

  I love Moto for its close to pure Android experience and quick updates. I was comparing many phones which are flagship on paper but one or the other lack SD card slot, hybrid SIM slot, custom UI (which i don't like after used to pure android experience) and full of bloatwares, which impacts the performance.
  

  It handles multi tasking in ease and to surprise, no heating issues. App installation is very fast and performance is a real beast. Never felt a lag...very smooth. I have installed close to 50apps and it did completed download and installation real quick. I think users won't be able to notice the difference of SD 820 or SD 625! I am not a hard core gamer but watch lots and lots of videos and listen music and heavy browsing. It works perfect for my usage.
  

  It heats up a bit while charging but not real hot. The quick charger does wonders in charging the phone from 60 to 100  in 20mins! Noticed that it gets bit warm in non-AC conditions with heavy usage but still performing like a breeze!
  

  Moto display and other gestures to open torch and camera are quite useful. I was bit skeptical about using finger print scanner but it supports 5 finger print options. That's really a good add on.
  

  16mp camera works fine in outdoor light conditions but lacks in low light conditions. For selfie lovers it does have front flash too.
  

  I used dual sim and noticed only either one of the SIM slot supports 4G, not both. When you use single sim then irrespective of the sim slot it does supports 4G. The SIM and SD card tray is bit tricky when you try to insert it...it gets stuck sometimes and you need to push a bit hard.
  

  Another oversight by Moto is, it doesn't have a Gallery app and no FM too. Users can download gallery apps from playstore but i like the default one provided in other Moto phones.
  

  Super AMOLED FHD screen looks cool... colors are vibrant and vivid even under the sun. I am not sure it does have a gorilla glass protection as Moto site or Flipkart specs didn't mention about it.
  

  Call quality and data reception is really good. The speaker on the front does a good job when you turn on the loudspeaker. Sound enough but i don't personally like listening over loud speaker. Listening through headset is awesome and sound is crystal clear and pleasing. I use Sennheiser CX 180 Street II which further enhances the listening experience. For this price, Moto should have provided a better headset as the one provided in the box is cheap.
  

  The box also has a USB cable and the charging adapter is a fixed one. So users can't switch the adapter if any fault.
  

  The another weird thing is, Moto has organised volume rocker and power button awkwardly, especially the split of volume rocker and placing power button below the volume rocker. Users will get confused with the power button and volume rocker till they get use to it.
  

  By default the phone has a Moto ringtone but no choices of default ringtones except this one. The default one is longer for a SMS/Whatsapp notification. User has to download notification ringtones if they need a short and crisp tones.
  

  The package includes a mod style shell which fits perfectly and gives a good grip to the phone. But I felt bit bulky and heavy as I am used to a 5inch phone for quite sometime. Moto should have launched a Z play Mini with 5inch size...that would be great for me.
  

  Further exploring the phone and will update my review soon. Overall it's a beautiful beast and does its job perfectly. Really worth the wait!

column3: Moto Z Play with Style Mod (White, 32 GB)
column7:
The Moto Z series is here to stay.
  

  I'll try to be as objective as possible and there will be a few comparisons drawn out with the Moto X Style because that was my previous phone.
  

  Right off the box, the looks are stunning, I bought the white variant and it just blew me away. Premium looks made much more premium with the camera bump.
  

  The volume and power buttons are placed awkwardly. The placement in the Moto X was good but with time you get adjusted easily. USB C and 3.5mm jack at the bottom make for a deadly combo. You can never be left out!
  

  Whoever is calling this phone 'thicker' is messing with your head. It is much lighter and slimmer than the moto x. The style mod though makes it bulky but it is good looking.
  

  If you're stepping down from a QHD IPS display like me, the display on Moto Z is very likely to confuse you. It is a sAMOLED full HD display with an awkward DPI at 480. The icons are large and eat up a lot of space. Native settings in Nougat allow you to change the DPI but they go either too small at 408 or too big at 540. A few ADB commands can alter this and I would advise a DPI between 432 and 440. You can look it up in XDA forums. Do that and you will not want to take your eyes away from the screen.
  

  Deep blacks are appealing but it fails to hit the whitest of whites unless you turn off adaptive brightness. Adaptive brightness somehow keeps the brightness very low and that is coming from someone who prefers low brightness.
  

  Objectively, the sound is decent but nowhere near the Moto X dual front facing speakers.
  

  The cameras in bright lights and daylight are excellent. In low light they are just above ordinary.
  

  The processor makes this an absolute beast. Snapdragon 625 is supposedly the little brother of SD 820 and it has (after a month's use) never ever lagged or stuttered even with heavy multitasking. It was fast and smooth and it was a pleasure to use my phone.
  

  The snappy processor, super AMOLED display and 3GB RAM together make the 3510mAH battery the best in class. Trust me, with light usage you can nick in 3 days. You can walk through a day with extremely heavy usage!
  

  A few other things - the glass can withstand enormous stress so no worries here, The fingerprint sensor is so pragmatically at the right place. Modularity is good but mods (those in the market now) are very expensive. The support for new mods is extremely good so hoping for the best here. Yes, it has VoLTE support and is dual 4G with a separate SD card slot. Oh and Moto has revamped it's apps and they are much much better and Moto voice is much more responsive now. You'll also get Nougat right off the bat!
  

  Final thoughts - In no walk of life I'd ever put this as a midranger, rather a toned down flagship. For the price, modularity, battery and it's surprising ability to compete with other flagships, you will be getting an absolute beast here.

This is my second Moto phone, the earlier being Moto G3. I got it at a very good price of 19000 ( I got 6000 for my old HTC 816 on exchange ).Now about the phone, let me mention some common elements that you need to know before you buy this phone.
  
  1.Its a modular phone . Agreed ! However will u spend another 7K-19K on buying those modules ? If yes, then go for it. If no, then please look into some other phones in this price segment which offers same if not better specs (OP3 , Le 2)
  
  Now even if you don't want to buy the Moto Mods, you can still go for this phone because this is the only phone in this Price Segment which has a separate memory card slot , which for me is a must.
  
  Another major pro in this phone is the Stock Android that this phone has.
  
  Going to other pro's:
  
  The battery back up is fantastic. I almost got 13-14 hrs of screen on time with a single charge and with extensive usage.
  
  Coming to camera: I wouldn't say it's the best in this Price Segment but it takes good pictures  in exterior locations and would do a decent job in low lighting areas as well and the front cam has a flash and you wouldn't have any issues with selfies as well.Overall it has a decent camera that you can't complain much about.
  
  Coming to display : Excellent display .It has an AMOLED screen and the viewing angles are great. Nothing much to say/complain here.
  
  Now the Cons:
  
  It gets a little warm when you charge the phone, especially around the volume and the power button area but that has been intermittent. However haven't experienced any heating issues with extended gaming (Asphalt etc)
  
  The cellular call quality is good but at times I saw my network connection being lost at places where I never had network issues. So I'm not sure if that's an issue with the phone or the network.
  
  The phone doesn't have a dedicated speaker.The speaker at the top for calls act as  an external speaker Hence the Output through the speaker's are not that loud. However the sound through headset is very good.
  
  The modules being sold by the phone are too expensive . Hopefully we get cheaper modules in future.
  
  So in case you need a phone which gives you a decent camera, Excellent battery and an overall good performance in addition to the uniqueness of Modular Phone, you can definetly go for MotoZ Play .
  
  I Hope you find this review helpful.

column3: Moto Z Play with Style Mod (White, 32 GB)
column7:
It's been more than a week since I got the phone handy.. So, within this period of time and with my way of usage, certainly it's fair enough to review unbiased.. Mainly, I used this mobile for browsing, gaming, apps performance test and to watch live streamed videos on YouTube.
  

  At least, I have been using my mobile for more than 6 hours of on screen time a day to do all my stuffs online. Battery performance is really outstanding with 3510 mAH power and Qualcomm 625 snapdragon processor which is very power efficient. I happened to charge only after 35 hours to 40 hours of my usage once the battery was charged to 95%.. The best part of charging is that it juices the pack for nearly 70% in less than an hour and it completely charges in less than or equally 2 hours.. I charged for precisely 20minutes and got the battery packed from 8% to 35%.. Thanks for Turbo Charging, though I have a con about it which I'm discussing down..
  

  Gaming performance is really stunning for games like Asphalt 8, Modern Combat and Nova3.. I am an extensive gamer and spend at least an hour or two regularly.. No graphics frame drop did I notice with these games.. Almost No or minimal heating issues even after continuous play for an hour..
  

  Screen resolution is good with AMOLED display.. Not very bright though.. Camera performance is good with rear camera in outdoor conditions.. But, fairly average in internal or dull lighting.. Dual LED is an added advantage, though it adds more light to the image..
  

  Touch quality is really good with Corning Gorilla 4 glass with high temperament.. Without any screen guard, you can enjoy the real touch..
  

  With almost 50 apps installed, memory still shows 1.2 GB free out of 3GB.. Sound quality for music and videos is good.. Comparatively, I found its up to par, but Lenovo Vibe K5 Note with Dolby Atmos effect is better than this..
  

  Dual sim slot with dedicated memory slot is a major advantage.. Never had a chance to test Reliance Jio in this week..
  

  Coming to the challenges and talking about cons, major glitch I found is, device heating issue while charging.. The temperature was really above 48 to 50 C.. I'm not sure if it is normal in Turbo charging devices or not. Please confirm if anyone has same issues.. If none has this issue, I ll check with Moto..
  

  Second major issue is, the handset is really slippery with glass finish and it slipped off my hands at least 4 times in last one week.. Luckily on bed.. Hopefully, a solid back cover may help.. Good feel factor is a stock Android experience without any theme..
  

  Certainly a good bet mobile under 25K.. Please share your feedback of this review..

  1. Big phone (though it is 5.5 inch phone the size is big) with very good build quality and it looks premium as well.
  
  2. Simple neat and plain android os.
  
  3. Dual sim option with 4g LTE working seamlessly
  
  4. Processor speed is fast without much of gaming. While gaming not any lag and it handles heavy games easily.
  
  5. Battery is perfect. You can't get better than this. For my use battery stays more than 1.5 days without charging.
  
  6. Moto gestures for camera on and flash night will be handy.
  
  7. Turbo charger comes with the mobile charges within an hour
  
  Cons
  
  1. Camera is less than average and with zero optical stabilisation there are halo effects and face overlapping when pictures are taken.
  
  2. No use of moto mods as it is expensive and there are alternatives like Bluetooth speakers.
  
  3. The connectors for mods are open where it will attract dust.
  
  4.As there is type c connector you cannot connect OTG directly as in samsung and you need connectors
  
  5. Headset is cheap average and low quality.
  

  That's it but overall the phone is good and worth buying if you are not very keen on photography.

Its a cheap,cheerful and reliable phone.With such low price one wonders there must be something wrong with it but there isn't. Now every phone has some pros and cons but in this case the cons are very few.
  
  First i will talk about the enormous pros.
  

  Design
  
  The design of moto g is the replica of moto x.Its a tough phone with a good handy size and the back of the phone is a rubber like plastic with a dimple of motorola logo which makes it very comfortable to hold it.It also has a water repellent nano-coating .This doesn't make it water proof, but at least makes it more resistant to the odd spill/splash.
  

  Screen
  
  One of the biggest highlights of the Moto G is its 4.5-inch 720p HD IPS LCD, which works out to a density of 329 pixels per inch i.e sharper than Apple's iPhone 5s, which offers 326ppi.
  
  It has also used Corning Gorilla Glass 3 on the Moto G to protect it from scratches which is usually found on premium devices priced at Rs. 30,000 and above.
  

  Camera
  
  It delivers pretty decent clicks with a 5 mp rear and 1.3 mp front camera with led flash and HD recording.It has a unique feature of slow motion video recording also with other features HDR and panorama.
  

  Processor & Performance
  
  The Moto G is powered by 1.2GHz quad-core Qualcomm Snapdragon 400 processor with Adreno 305 graphics and 1GB of RAM onboard.The performance is great.It doesn't slows down even with 4-5 background applications running.Even when playing a heavy graphics game like Asphalt-8:Airborne it runs very smoothly.And when i performed a benchmark test by AnTuTu it recorded a score of 11,874 which is pretty close to big phones nexus 4 and Galaxy S III.
  

  Software
  
  One of the best features of moto g is that it has the lastest android version i.e 4.4 KitKat and that too with a stock android,stock edition users get the latest versions of Android OS immediately they are out, while customized users have to wait months   and sometimes a year (Ahem! Sony.. cough!) to get updates to their device.
  

  Battery Life
  
  The 2070 mAh seems low but actually it isn't in the case of moto g.The battery life of moto g is pretty decent.With a normal usage it lasted about a day and with heavy usage like playing games,movies with wifi/3g enabled the whole time and calling for 2-3 hours it lasted for about 12-13 hours,which was not bad.
  

  Cons
  
  The only downside of moto g is that there is no NFC.Although NFC is a pretty cool tech but think about it even if it had would you use it.
  

  Verdict
  
  At this price point, no other phones offer an experience that is as good, so in that sense the Moto G is a game changer.I bought it and i definetly recommend you to get it.

column6: Awesome phone with an awesome user experience! Go for it!
column7:
This phone feels like you are holding a very premium phone in your hand. Awesome feel. After using it for last 8 months, I can say this is the best you can get below Rs. 20000/-. I bought the 16 gb version.
  
  So, here are some useful points for new buyers:
  
  1) Display: Awesome, crisp, clear, vivid and beautiful.
  
  2) Speed and performance: Zero lag, lightening fast. Pure Android experience as expected from & by Google. After the kitkat update, the performance is much better as kitkat is optimized for 512MB RAM phones. So, 1GB is more than enough here! Battery performs really well, goes for 1.5-2 days on one full charge with nominal usage. With heavy 3G usage, it goes for 1 day+.
  
  3) Call quality: No issues! Clean and clear!
  
  4) Build quality: just great, design is awesome. Its a joy holding this phone in your hand. Corning Gorilla glass 3 and water repellent coating makes the phone life proof.
  
  5) Camera: In this department, the phone is behind other phones which have 8MP cameras. But still, for a 5MP camera, it takes good photos in day light. But, its bad in dark. Flash is powerful. (Use droidlight by motorola app for using it as a torch)
  
  6)Storage: 16GB version gives you 12.xx GB for use, I feel its good enough for me. Also you may connect an USB/pen drive using the micro usb cable and watch movies/listen to songs. It works on kitkat also without any paid software, you just need a file manager (free).
  

  So, overall it's a thumbs up for this phone!
  

  PLEASE NOTE (For those who have queries):
  
  1)The service center names which flipkart is sending with the product are old ones, the latest ones can be viewed on in.motorola.com > moto g > customer service > authorized service centers.
  
  2) Those who are complaining that the phone is not genuine : Motorola has officially launched the phone exclusively via flipkart (can be read on their fb, twitter pages), so you will surely get a genuine product. Also, on the moto g box it is written : Imported in India by Flipkart India.
  
  3) Regarding ringtones : Just install a file manager (FX) or use your pc and move the song (which u want to set as ringtone) in ringtones folder.
  
  4) Unable to share mp3 files: this is another rumor spread by anti- moto g reviewers. I have shared audio files a lot of times using moto g. Just use a file manager (FX).
  

  So, be care free and order it! It's the best phone ever under 20k. You will surely get a replacement from flipkart if the piece is faulty (which is very rare).
  

  Edit: Now as 2nd gen is available, I would suggest to go for 2nd gen unless you want a smaller phone. Also, If this one (16gb Gen 1) is available for less than 10.5k, go for it, best vfm at that price), else spend a few thousand more to get the 2nd gen.

Ok so, I am sure you would have read how good this phone is and the awesome value for money proposition it provides. No debating that - the phone is awesome. But how good is a phone if you cannot make a call from it?
  

  To cut long story short, the network drops regularly and the phone automatically switches to airplane mode. The SIM cards are not recognised and there is no apparent reason for this. The only way to fix this is to remove the SIM cards and put it back on and you have to keep checking your phone every 10 minutes to see if it is registered on the network or not.
  

  This has happened post the 4.4.2 update and I guess Motorola is actively working on a fix but no official communication yet (or at least I haven't come across). You can read multiple threads online on this issue.
