I was one of the first few people who ordered the Moto G. Ordered it at midnight 7 minutes after launch and also opted for the 1day guarantee. Flipkart really stood true to their word. My phone was delivered by noon on 7th Feb! So brownie points to Flipkart for their quick and awesome service.
  
  The phone itself is a lot better than I expected it to be. The black shell looks simply stunning. I also took advantage of the launch day offer and ordered a turquoise shell at 70% off!
  
  I have to tell you I was rather skeptic about the delivery as I had never ordered anything from Flipkart before and never bought anything costing over a 1000 bucks online. But Flipkart has earned my trust with their prompt service.
  
  So upon opening the package and unboxing, the first thing that'll hit you is the gleaming beauty of the screen. Also the build and the finish quality of the body is simply superb. Top notch work from Motorola. Quickly power it on and you'll notice its bright and clear HD display. That's the first thing you'll observe and the thing you'll love the most about this phone. The in-box accessories include a pair of headphones and a standard 0.5A wall charger (with attached cable as opposed to USB chargers we see these days). A USB data cable is NOT included in the box but you'll hardly need it. Also inside the box are a couple of manuals and a warranty book sorta thing.
  
  So far in my 3 days of usage, I have not even had slight glimpse of lag. So far i have installed around 15 apps. The device comes with Android 4.3 JellyBean out of the box and runs butter smooth. The update to KitKat is not yet available but once that's rolled out the performance will be further enhanced. The Motorola Migrate app came in very handy. With just a couple of taps, all the contacts, texts, call logs and all the media on the sd card of my old phone were quickly transferred on to the Moto G. The 16 GB device has around 12GB (12.32 GB to be precise) of user available memory out of the box.
  
  For all the entertainment purposes, the quad core processor coupled with the 1GB of RAM (882 MB actually) and the excellent display, gives a very satisfying experience. The speaker also gives out a rather loud output. It may not match neck to neck against the top tier phones available right now, but considering the price point, it isn't supposed to be compared with them. While the smaller games such as subway surfers run perfectly with no issues, I was amazed to note that a much more demanding game such as Riptide GP2 also runs with full graphic settings by default. Viewing angles are also great thanks to the IPS panel. I could not observe any change in colour even when looking at the screen from very wide angles. The music playback through the headphones is  loud and clear but it left me wanting a little more.
  
  The camera as it was observed in several other reviews, is rather slow and I could not capture anything worthwhile in the first few clicks. The lens take more than usual time to focus on any subject and the whole camera feels very slow. But this quickly changed when i changed the tap to focus setting. The cam app gives you an on screen bracket that can be dragged around to control focus and exposure. Once you get a hang of this, the pictures you can capture improve drastically. This is by no means a great camera. The focus rate is still rather slow and low light pics tend to be a bit grainy but neither can it be written off as a very bad camera. Again considering the price and the remaining specs, the camera isn't as bad as it could've been. You won't really be cursing it once you get a hang of how it works. (Y)
  
  The front cam is good enough for video calling and selfies in good light.
  
  So far I have not noticed any signal drops and all the radios on the device seem to be doing their job just the way they are supposed to.
  
  I cannot comment on the battery life just yet but so far it has been holding up pretty well. I went on a clicking spree with the camera and kept it running for around 5 hours non-stop, clicking around 300 pics and a couple of videos, not to mention data usage and whatsapp at the same time. At the end of that the phone still had around 30% of charge left, so under average use, I'm sure it'll easily last over a whole day!
  
  All in all, the Moto G is a complete package that is offered, as Moto says, at an exception price. It is an incredible bargain and a joy to use. What Moto G really offers is a premium feel at a fraction of the price.
  
  So anyone who's thinking of picking this up, think no further my friend. Moto G is the answer to all your electronic needs ;)
  
  Thanks a ton Motorola - This phone was totally worth the wait (:
  
  And Flipkart - thanks again for the lightning fast delivery. I wouldn't have been able to wait any longer :D

I was one of the lucky few who were able to successfully order the 16GB model. I haven't seen a product on Flipkart getting sold out so quickly ( in half an hour!), especially on the day of the launch.
  

  Flipkart's delivery was exceptional as always and the product was delivered to me at noon today (7th February 2014, ie in 1 Day!) even though I opted for standard shipping. The box contains quick start guides (in Hindi and English), warranty card, wall charger, wired headset and of course, the stunning Moto G. An interesting observation is that the phone available in the US comes without the headset and the wall charger but instead, only has a USB cable. +1 to Motorola on giving extra stuff to Indian customers.
  

  Coming to the phone, not only does it have amazing hardware specs (kindly refer to the description on Flipkart, no point in repeating the same here) but it is very well designed too. The detailed observations are listed below -
  

  Design -
  
  The Moto G has a great design and the button placement is really good, with the lock/unlock button being easily accessible, irrespective of the hand in which it is being held. The rounded edges make it feel slimmer and at around 140 grams, it is certainly not the heaviest phone around. The most striking design feature is that it is difficult to to differentiate between the display and the bezel, making the front appear like it is 'monolithic', similar to the design of Nexus devices.
  

  Screen -
  
  The 720p IPS LCD display at 329 ppi is spectacular and the colours produced are vivid and the saturation levels are very good. The viewing angles are great and the unit I received did not contain any dead pixels, as reported by a few people. The presence of Gorilla Glass 3 serves as an icing on the cake, making the Moto have the best display in its class by far.
  

  Processor -
  
  Powered by a 1.2 Ghz quad core Qualcomm Snapdragon 400 chipset with Adreno 305, there is no compromise felt in performance. Opening and switching between apps is very fast and swiping across and pinching in and out on the screen is very responsive and no lag is felt whatsoever, thanks to the 1GB of RAM. Again, no phone in this price range stands a chance against the Moto.
  

  Operating System -
  
  The OS is almost stock Android in terms of the UI and Motorola has added a few of its applications like -
  
  1. Moto Assist (schedules tasks such as silencing the phone during a meeting or while sleeping),
  
  2. Moto Migrate (to transfer stuff from your old phone),
  
  3. Moto Device ID (to track the phone if it gets lost) etc.
  
  These apps are very useful and consume minimal resources and hence it is highly unfair to classify them as bloatware (as some people claim).
  
  The device runs Android Jelly Bean 4.3 and an upgrade to Kitkat (ie 4.4) is around the corner, which should improve performance further, adding more features at the same time.
  

  Camera -
  
  One of the most criticised features of this phone is undoubtedly the camera, which takes 5MP photos. However, when compared to my friend's Nexus 4 (which has an 8MP camera), the results were a pleasant surprise.
  
  We took photos of the same object at 1X zoom and on comparison, we agreed on the fact that the pics taken by the Moto G were on par with the Nexus 4, if not better, despite having the lower megapixel count.
  
  I also compared the camera with another friend's HTC Desire SV (8 MP). The Moto takes much better and sharper photos and makes the comparison feel unfair!
  
  This not only confirms claims that the Nexus 4 has a relatively poor camera but also proves that a higher megapixel count does not necessarily mean better photos.
  

  Battery life is supposed to be good although it is too early to reach a judgement. I will be subsequently updating this review with more information.
  

  I would recommend the 16GB model even though it is not in stock now since the phone storage cannot be expanded due to the absence of a micro sd card slot. Waiting for some time for the same would prove to be advantageous in the longer run.
  

  Overall, the device is the best phone in this price range by far, and is in fact better than many which cost more. If you are on the lookout for a phone in the sub 15K price range, look no further because it does not get better than this ...

In the box:
  
  Moto G
  
  Wall charger
  
  Wired headset
  
  Quick start guides in Hindi and English
  
  Warranty card
  

  The Phone:
  
  It's a vibrant HD screen that's just the right size and has a clean, stock Android interface. Viewing angles are limited but I don't mind this because it means people can't peek around your shoulder.
  

  The phone feels premium to hold and processing power is good, so's the RAM and the phone barely lags (though it does occasionally slow down when changing apps). The matte back panel of the phone has an extremely pleasing texture but is also a smudge magnet. Also, no screen guard was provided in the box and none can be found on flipkart.
  

  Both these problems, however, are solved by the flip cover I purchased with the phone, which is even more premium. The thoughtfully located Moto logo has a depression perfect for my index finger, and the magnetic felt-lined cover will autolock or unlock and clean fingerprints on your phone when you flip it.
  

  The Cameras:
  
  No amount of smooth scrolling will make up for the halfpenny back camera and the severely inadequate 1.3 MP front camera. Although the camera is capable of shooting slo-mo videos (this is really, really cool), they are grainy and jerky. Movement in the video is not smooth and I can only put this down to low FPS. The camera is unusable in low light and is average at best in normal light. The LED flash is blinding.
  

  The Battery:
  
  Although it's too soon to say anything about battery life, from my estimates it should do 24 hrs on one full charge with moderate wifi and 3G use.
  

  The Accessories:
  
  Apart from the phone, everything in the box was majorly disappointing. The headphones feel cheap, sound substandard and are really not worth reviewing. No data cable was included in the box. Instead I received only a micro-usb wall charger. Hello, moto?
  

  UPDATE: I attempted to transfer files with several data cables on multiple computers and there is a glaring issue here: the phone does not stay connected for more than two minutes at a time. Windows Explorer hangs when i try to transfer multiple albums simultaneously as they take longer than 2 mins to transfer. When I first plug it into the PC it is recognised as device XT1033 but then 2 mins later it just drops off the PC and all transfers hang. Then I have to manually disconnect and reconnect the data cable, and I have another 2 minute window to transfer files before it drops off again. The phone is charging all this while, though.
  

  I am getting in touch with flipkart about this issue.

I bought this phone after much research and have used it for almost 2 months now; needless to say, I love it, it's amazing for the price, etc, etc. Incidentally, right after I bought this, the 2nd gen. Moto G came out. Since I was quite happy with mine, I suggested the new model to my sister and she bought it. Having spent some time with both models now, I'm in a position to do a practical comparison between the two (with my own opinions added):
  

  First of all, the basics- processor power, battery life, connectivity, voice clarity, etc. are the same. Incidentally, the new Moto G is advertised to feature a water-repellant nano-coating, which the old one also has. This doesn't make the phone 'water-proof', as we'd like to believe, but it does mean the phone has a much better chance of recovering from everyday aquatic accidents.
  

  Here are the differences:
  

  1) Screen: The 2nd gen's screen is bigger, but the resolution, ie. no of pixels, is the same. What this means is that on the one hand, it's noticeable less sharp than the 1st gen, but on the other hand, icons are bigger, text is easier to read and it's easier to touch very closely spaced buttons individually.
  
  However, unless you place these two phones side by side, you won't think that the 2nd gen isn't sharp enough. Likewise, it's not particularly hard to type or read fine text on the 1st gen either; unless you specifically like big and easy-to-read, it won't make a difference. There is one major difference that isn't on the specs, which is that the 2nd gen screen lacks in brightness. Putting both phones on auto-brightness in the same lighting, the older one is definitely brighter and the colours more vivid. Again, it might just be more noticeable in a side-by-side comparison, but the auto-brightness on the new phone does seem to err on the dimmer side.
  

  2) Size: Easy choice for me. I prefer the smaller size of the 1st gen. To be fair, 2nd gen is not ridiculously oversized, like those phablets that just seem awkward to hold up to your ear, but if I can get the same processing power and features in a smaller gadget, I find it more convenient.
  

  3) Camera: 8MP vs 5MP (new vs old). Another thing I noticed that isn't mentioned anywhere is that the new Moto G has some kind of an anti-reflection coating on the lens which the older one doesn't. I've yet to see if it actually reduces flare or something. Both phones only excel outdoors in daytime. Low-light shots are, frankly bad. Lots of blur and noise. The 3MP difference makes almost no difference, unless you zoom all the way into a photo. That said, the camera is decent for the price range. The only other phones with significantly better camera and similar price would probably be the Nokia Lumias, but those have other issues.
  

  4) Speakers: Two big, loud, front-facing ones on 2nd gen. Single, respectably sized rear one on 1st gen. If you use loudspeakers all the time, this might matter. For me, the 1st gen's speakers have quite adequate volume. Clarity is good on both.
  

  5) Grip cover: This was a big deal for me. The grip cover available for the 1st gen has been discontinued with the newer model. And it is awesome. Build quality is great. The rubber sides make for a completely non-slip grip on your phone and they're raised above the screen edges, so you can lay the phone face-first on a flat surface without fear of scratches. It adds minimal bulk to the phone since it just replaces the back.
  
  Most importantly, this cover hides all those seams and edges where the body panels of the phone meet, and that is where most gadgets reveal their actual price-range. By covering all those edges with smooth matte-black rubber and plastic, this cover actually projects a better build quality than the phone has. If you buy Moto G 1st gen, definitely get this cover. (I have a white one on a black phone - it looks great and surprisingly, doesn't accumulate dirt/fingerprints at all.)
  

  6) Software: Yes, the 2nd model is guaranteed to be upgraded to the next android version. The 1st gen might just be upgraded (I'm optimistic because Moto G was designed under Google itself for the 'pure android' experience). Currently, differences in the OS are too minor to mention.
  

  7) Memory card slot: 2nd gen has it, 1st gen doesn't. To me this doesn't matter much, but it does to a lot of people, so think about it. Still, being stuck with only 16 GB in-built storage isn't as bad as it sounds.
  

  8) Price: This is the main point. With the 1st gen currently selling at 10k (plus 10% discount on SBI cards, so potentially 9k) against 13k for the 2nd gen, you should consider whether the handful of changes is worth the 3-4k price gap. I think it isn't, but then I'm biased towards the 1st gen.
  

  To sum up, you can't go wrong with either Moto G, just consider the differences and see which ones matter to you.

column6: Moto G 16GB XT-1033, Product Details & Initial Impressions.

Hey Flipkarters!
  

  I received my Moto G on the 8th Feb 2014 afternoon (Instead of  the expected delivery date of 17th Feb as per the mail received) - Kudos to the Flipkart team on achieving this feat.
  

  Box Contents: I will write about the contents at first; due to the fact that many of you guys are impatiently waiting for someone to give you some useful info about the product.
  

  Be Warned: Impatient readers may get frustrated about my over-detailing stuff, but I'm gonna risk it anyways.
  

  The Package contained a relatively small retail box.  On opening the Non-sealed box i found the Handset with a screen protector with the Moto logo etched on it.
  
  - Further i found a white Micro-USB wall charger and a white non in-ear Headphone with built in mic and a call pick&drop button.
  
  - Along with that we also get the standard set of quick start guides.
  
  Guys don't panic at the missing seal. As far as my sources, they confirmed receipt of the retail package sans-the-seal all around the globe.
  
  There is no data sync cable included in the box which is kind of a let-down but who cares? We all have 2-3 of them lying around unused in some corner anyways.
  
  The Headphones are just there i guess due to the manufacturer's belief that the Indian market would be furious without it so do not expect anything fancy and use your current one instead.
  

  First Impressions:
  
  Another warning: I'm not comparing this phone to any other phone in the world. So if any of you are expecting a comparison I suggest you look elsewhere.
  
  - After admiring the above average build quality, I decided leaving the phone to charge up-to 100% while at work. I switched it on and immediately struck a wow factor viz., A stunning display.
  
  - Mind you, the Power Lock button and the Volume rockers may seem wobbly and over-protruding at first but give an excellent click and are easier to access.
  
  - The back cover feels like a super smooth rubberized-finish which is highly flexible and removing it seems to be a bit tricky. Just as I wrote the above sentence I received the Vivid Red Flip Shell which is of premium quality.
  
  - The Processor is quite fast and has handled multitasks without any visible hiccups. The User available RAM on my phone is around 900 MB out of which 250+ of it is free every-time i check under normal use.
  
  - The Speaker on this phone is LOUD when kept on full volume but is marginally low if you just minus it by just one click (This is weird).
  
  - The call quality on this phone is quite good and not as bad as the Global edition GeekyRanjit was reviewing. The Speaker was loud enough and the person at the other end said my voice was very audible.
  
  - The Music experience with stock headphones is bland and therefore again recommend using other headphones. Interestingly i found that Moto has in-built Audio Effects service which keeps running on the background. Good to know that Moto is not just manufacturing and dumping phones on the users rather; they're working on the software too.
  
  - The Camera is of average quality but at the same time is a bit slow at saving the image. To properly capture an image without blur, you need to have steady hands. The LED flash is Ridonkulously bright and has the capacity to temporarily render the subject blind for a few seconds! The secondary camera is good enough for Skype video calls.
  
  - The Battery for the first time lasted me for a good 15 hours out of which 9+ hours have been continuous usage with music, radio, app installs and general usage with WiFi connection and still had around 9% juice left when i finally decided to connect it to the wall charger.
  
  Please note: I haven't used data  connection on either 2G or 3G network simply because i have access to WiFi both at work as well as home, therefore rendering data connection useless & an expense for the sake of expense.
  
  The lack of user replaceable battery does not bug me much.
  

  I Cannot put more info on this page since i have so much to explore and  have run out of the 5000 character mark, therefore will come into an initial conclusion on this device (People who have been patiently reading me will breath a huge sigh of relief :D )
  

  I Rate this Device somewhere between 4.5-4.75 out of 5 considering the price point of this entry level Moto phone. Since neither of the above values can be entered i have given it a 5 Star rating.

column6: Moto G IS the game changer.
column7:
what you need to about this device.I have used MotoG for over a week now and it's simply brilliant. Here is my review.
  
  Pros:
  
  1. Display: At 326ppi its 4.5" IPS HD screen stands as tall as Apple's iphone 5s retina screen. Add Corning Gorilla Glass 3(which has only been seen on phones like Nexus and Xperia z) to that and you have yourself questioning how Motorola managed to offer it all under 15k?
  
  What that means:A crystal clear display with great viewing angles and no loss of colors. even under direct sun, the viewing is just fine. You can keep your car keys in the same pocket with your phone without worrying about the scratches on the screen, thanks to Gorilla Glass 3 which also makes the screen dust resistant and fairly water resistant too.Honestly, the screen IS something to talk about regarding it's price.
  

  2. Processor:\
  
  Moto G is powered by a quad core Snapdragon.
  
  What that means:An ultra responsive smartphone which registers almost every touch and shows no sign of lags under its limits. Multitasking is as easy as it can be and it doesn't hang itself till death like Samsung and Micromax  I won't say that this phone is a powerhouse gaming smartphone but it runs all the popular games very well and for the likes of graphic heavy "Asphalt" and  "FIFA14" the running is smooth after a little bit of tweaking in the game settings.
  

  3. Platform:This Android is a KitKat! well actually it comes as a Jelly Bean out of the box but as soon as you will connect it to internet it will upgrade itself to the latest version of Android i.e KitKat or 4.4.2 which was only limited to Google flagship devices like Nexus 5 till now Moreover MotoG is pure Google as it has no skin/bloatware/sponsored apps installed on it. So Long TouchWiz!
  
  What that means:Better Android experience with latest version in the form of KitKat Google now is more handy and intuitive. there are no lags and the over all look and feel of OS has improved making it a more premium experience and since KitKat was designed with mid-range handsets in mind it works superbly on this device. Now without any flagship skin or bloatware, phone does run faster and feels simpler which is a good thing.
  

  4. Aesthetics:The whole look and feel of MotoG screams about the care Motorola and Google has put in this device to make it look premium and feel sturdy. When I first held it in hand I found it hard to believe that this a "cheap" device because it certainly doesnt feel so. Hats Off to Motorola. at 140gms it is not light but it wont feel heavy either. It will feel solid and maybe a little bit hefty but not at all cheap. Hardware is top notch with a rubberized back panel which isn't wafer like (Samsung Galaxy devices) or creaky like other cheap phones. even the power button and volume rocker are solid, sharp and shiny. There are videos on youtube which show this phone under water for upto 30 minutes and still working fine. All in all it doesn't look like a phone worth 14k but something around 22-25k and feels really nice in hand.
  

  5. Battery and speakers:2070 mAh. Good enough to run this device for a day and maybe a slight bit more than that after a little optimization. Nothing extraordinary going on here but not a downer either. Speakers are something else which impressed me and this might only be a personal opinion but they do sound loud,crisp and clear which was a surprise as I was expecting a dull and murky experience at this price but once again Motorola has delivered with a stunning piece of hardware at low cost.
  

  Cons:All is not well though with this handset and there are a few things which could have been done in a better way but would definitely mean pushing the price tag more towards 20-22K
  
  1. Storage:8GB/16GB And that's it! ouch! MotoG doesnt offer a memory slot for any of above mentioned versions but I think at 16GB it offers ample space for all what is needed in a phone. Not to forget 50 GB cloud storage provided by Google on Google drive for free which is welcoming but far from being a solution. It wasn't a deal-breaker for me and I think 16GB is sufficient for an avg. user. otherwise OTG cable Zindabaad!
  
  2. Camera Rear:5MP Front:1.2 MP HDR and slow motion video recording
  
  at 5MP this phone leaves you wanting for more. it performs just fine in adequate light with an image which has nothing to be talked about. Although features like HD recording and Slow motion video recording adds to the experience but still far from a great camera.
  

  The Biggest PRO is ofcourse pricing and at 14k(16GB) this phone is almost like a revolution, shifting the balance of the market more towards mid range phones which can also deliver.
  
  Conclusion: For those who are looking  for a no fuss, good looking, sturdy device with a great display and hardware offering latest OS available with a reliable chipset under the bonnet at and affordable price (that's pretty much what one needs anyway).

An excellent device. You may buy this without a second thought. I usually research and window-shop for at least a couple of months, but this is the first phone I've purchased on an impulse!
  

  Even when I had absolutely no intention of buying the Moto G, I was disappointed that it went out of stock so soon on the launch day! I happened to notice it back in stock in the afternoon, but was able to get only the 8GB (~5.5GB usable). I was initially not very convinced with the internal storage and thought I'll eventually cancel the order and wait for the 16GB, but I held on, secretly wishing for a 100% cash back amongst other goodies. I however got the other launch day offers for clothing and e-books, and purchased a royal blue back cover for Rs.270.
  

  The pure Android OS is slick and snappy, showing no signs of any lag whatsoever, and is actually addictive to the point where I sometimes switch on the display just to toggle through the homescreens and launcher! The experience is simply superb!
  

  After two weeks of usage, I have all but forgotten that I do not have much internal storage left. This is such a beautifully crafted piece! I am pretty sure I'll move all photos to the 65GB Google Drive, keep ~2GB of mp3s, and small games. I use the phone mostly for browsing, texting, social networking, light gaming, phone calls, YouTube, Skype, Viber etc,. I do not mind the non-expandable internal storage, but it would have been nice to have a micro SD slot.
  

  The Jellybean install had a small bug with the volume control. It would remain low till about 90% and then get very loud in the last 10% or so. This issue is resolved post installing KitKat, and the volume increase is now gradual.
  

  After I upgraded to KitKat, the battery dropped from 62% to 42% after the initial reboot! The backup seems to have stabilised after a factory reset and a few days of usage, and hopefully it will continue to remain an 'all day battery'.
  

  Mounting storage through OTG reportedly works well on the Indian Moto G with 4.4.2, as demonstrated by user 'Geekyranjit' on his YouTube channel. I haven't tried this yet, but I am planning to buy a cable or an OTG pen drive.
  

  The HD display is crisp and stunning. You will want to watch movies on this thing! Watching HD videos from YouTube is mind blowing, but I do this only while on WiFi as the data usage is heavy for such content. Small text is legible and very clear. Corning Gorilla Glass 3 is very thin, so the screen is almost close to the glass, making it all the more beautiful!
  

  The build quality is great and the phone feels very premium! The phone feels slim and sufficiently weighted and it literally slips into the pocket. The volume and power buttons rattle a bit, but provide nice tactile feedback. The back cover is difficult to take off, but there is a one minute video by user 'himesh123456789' on YouTube that demostrates how to do this easily.
  

  The non removable battery is fine. Due to long backup, expect lesser charging cycles and hence longer battery life. Keep the phone charged at 45-90% with regular top-ups to prolong its life. Never deep cycle (0-100%) your smartphone battery often, except when there is a need to calibrate, as doing so will reduce its service life. There is no 'memory effect', so you can charge at random.
  

  The camera isn't the best, but it does the job. The secondary cam is decent. The LED bulb is very bright and lights up a fairly large area.
  

  The loudspeaker is very shrill, and extremely loud! This is important in noisy environments where one can miss hearing a ringtone. Music is surprisingly crisp and the tiniest of details are audible.The treble is extreme, but the bass is low. One should refrain from keeping the volume at 100% while playing media, as the speaker tends to crackle and distort. 95% is the sweet spot for clean maximum volume. Audio quality through headphones is alright.
  

  Call quality is nice. Voice is clear and reception is neat. The earpiece is sufficiently loud. WiFi and 3G connectivity is good and I haven't faced any connection drops till now. The browsing experience is smooth. Kinetic scrolling and zoom work perfectly.
  

  The bundled accessories aren't of the best quality and the headphones just add up to the pile of unused wired hands-free devices lying around since the first Nokia days. The all white charger looks neat but comes with an awkward looking two pin, like it was put together in a hurry for the Indian retail packaging. I would've personally preferred to have the standalone USB cable like the one bundled with the US version, but I already have a tough Sony Ericsson cable and charger that came with the st15i. A micro USB wall charger is however a welcome addition to the collection in some ways, so one can be kept plugged in at home, one in office, one in the travel bag, etc,.
  

  All in all, a nice package! A purchase that would bring you up to date with the flagship smartphone experience, for a fraction of the price.

column6: Forget the other options and just go Moto!
column7:
Most people wanting to buy this phone will have probably heard that it's the best budget handset and while that's true, this phone is more than that. Motorola is one of the few or in fact the only manufacturer that appreciates that tampering with stock Android only spoils the user experience. So you won't find a hyped up, poorly designed UI like TouchWiz on Samsung devices on this phone. This phone runs almost stock Android with a few Motorola improvements that actually add value rather than coming off as gimmicky features.
  

  First and foremost, the typical Indian prospective buyer will have done a lot of research and narrowed down his choices to a handful of phones in this price range and I can say with conviction that the Moto G will be better than everyone of them. Specs don't matter a lot but the Indian smartphone enthusiast is very swayed by numbers and that's what manufacturers like Micromax are notorious for advertising. No wonder they manage to sell phones that don't even run the latest version of Android. Please stay away from Micromax because they use substandard internals from lesser known companies and so the buyer is just left wondering in the end why Android lags so much on his 1.5 GHz Quad Core phone with 2 GB RAM and then blames the OS for it. Such manufacturers make Android look bad and Motorola is out to right that wrong.
  

  I've owned this phone for over a month now and I upgraded to it from my beloved Galaxy Nexus (a Nexus smartphone, mind you). Even at this point I have no regrets that I didn't pick up another Nexus smartphone. This phone is pretty much the complete package. It runs stock Android, has excellent battery life (almost Galaxy Note 2 level battery life) providing over 5 and a half hours of screen on time on a single charge, it is dual SIM, has a very very loud speaker that produces great quality sound and of course has a gorgeous display! The display is IPS LCD and so gets much brighter and produces quite natural colours. It's hands down the best display you'll see on a smartphone in this price range. The camera is the only Achilles' heel of this phone but mind you it's still pretty good and takes some great photos in good lighting conditions. Gaming fans can read other reviews since I personally don't play heavy games on my phone but casual, light games like QuizUp run without a hitch.
  

  Also the dual SIM functionality is crucial to many potential buyers as it was for me because I didn't want to carry two phones around, one personal and another for work. I'm pleased to say that the dual SIM implementation on the Moto G is simply perfect! It feels like it's baked into Android, it's that good! No SIM is ever on standby like many dumb phones and you can see and monitor data usage per SIM. You can also name each SIM card in the settings, assign them colours and so on. On making a call you are prompted to choose a SIM and you can set a particular SIM as default for some contacts. There's also a smart feature that you can enable that learns which SIM you often choose while calling a particular person and it just picks that SIM automatically instead of you having to choose.
  

  Very often it's the little things that make you happy and there are quite a few of those with the Moto G! You get an offer of 50 GB of free Google Drive space for 2 years! Then there's Motorola Migrate which happens to be the feature that made me feel instantly satisfied with the phone. Motorola Migrate is an app that helps you migrate all you contacts, photos, videos and music from your old smartphone (Android or iPhone) to your new Motorola phone. And I just can't express how delighted I was to find that my worries of having to manually migrate all my stuff from my old phone to the new one were pointless! Then if you're a fan of Android looking to have the latest and greatest of the OS i.e. KitKat 4,4,2 but can't shell out the money for a Nexus then the Moto G is you're only option right now and it runs KitKat like a boss! And finally if you, like me, have an OCD for app design then you'll be pleased to know that all of Motorola's apps adhere to the latest Android design guidelines and don't look like they're stuck in the Gingerbread era like all of Samsung's apps.
  

  All in all this has been a great purchase for me and I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone who wants to buy a great phone or a great first Android phone! If you want no regrets after making a smartphone purchase then go Moto!

I was one of the buyers who purchased the Moto G on the first day of it's sale here on Flipkart. I've been using this phone as my primary phone for the past one month. My impressions -
  

  a) Screen - the screen is gorgeous to say the least. It's a 720p display with a ppi which matches the latest iPhone. Do I need to say more? Only the most expensive premium handsets like HTC One have a better display.
  

  b) Battery life - this is one of the most important factors for me. I'm easily able to get about a day's worth of battery life. This is with heavy usage. So light users will easily get around 2 days. There is one issue though - around 1% battery drop per hour has been seen when the phone is on airplane mode. This is a little more than usual. Motorola is aware of this issue.
  

  c) Design aesthetics - this phone is a bit heavy. My last smartphone was Samsung Galaxy S2 which was insanely light. As compared to that, this phone is a bit heavy. If you're going to use this continuously for a long period of time, then you would need to shift it from one hand to another (which was the case with me as I spend an insanely high amount of time on Twitter). The phone itself looks very good and has a premium touch to it. I had purchased a flip cover (red colour) as it was on 80% reduction on the first day of sale. The red back does look very sexy, I must admit!
  

  d) Software - It was running Jelly bean 4.3 initially when I got the phone. Within a week, I got the update to Kitkat 4.4.2 - the Kitkat android O/S is smooth and a pleasure to use. The best android version yet, hands down. Some apps which make use of the transparent navigation bar and notification bars are a treat to the eyes (Example - Action Launcher, Muzei, QuickPic, Talon for Twitter, EvolveSMS)
  

  e) Headphones and Charger - The international version of this phone does not come with headphones or a ccharger. You just get the phone. In the indian version on sale on flipkart, we get a headphone and a charger bundled in with the phone. However, both these are of very cheap quality and I would not recommend them one bit. The headphones are an apology in front of the high quality (noice cancelling) ones provided by Samsung. The charger also often gets heated up pretty quickly and I use another micro usb charger for my daily charging (any micro usb charger will work).
  

  f) Call quality & Speaker - I'm making a special mention for the speakers on the moto g, because I feel it's important to highlight the awesomeness of the speakers. It's pretty neat, loud and will leave you pretty satisfied with the experience. I usually use speakers while watch you tube videos and ocassionally during some calls. Call quality - is very good. No issues there.
  

  All in all, I think I've invested 14k in a world class product, it's an unbelivable price for a product of this premium quality.

column6: Moto G (16 gb) Review after prolonged use
column7:
I read and saw online a lot about Moto G but I wanted to give my opinion after using it exhaustively for some time. So..I have been using Moto G (16 gb model) for more than 3 weeks now and this device delivers and up to the mark performance. I will be talking about the issues later, let me first write what I loved most about this device.
  

  1. DISPLAY: The first thing you notice when you switch on the phone is its brilliant screen. With around 329 ppi it beats the hell out of premium range of smartphones. I tried very hard to notice the pixels which infact you can on a very high brightness and looking very closley, but in normal day to day use there is no chance to distinguish any. The auto brightness works perfectly and even in bright sunlight you can see every detail on your screen. The colour reproduction is amazing and you can feel the stunning graphics while playing HD games and watching HD videos. It gives more than what you pay for in terms of screen so 5/5 for the display of moto g, its the best part of the phone.
  

  2. PERFORMANCE: The second thing you want from your phone is how fast and responsive it is and Moto G again comes out as the sure shot winner. There is absolutely no lag while flipping through apps and games. I played Asphalt 8-airborne on high settings and the performance was amazing. It runs normal applications like butter (that was the aim of project butter offcourse :D ). With android KitKat 4.4.2 the phone runs smoothly after longer use also. The switching on/off is fast and there is nice motorola animation to greet you after time you turn it on :D. This budget phone delivers performance in comparison to above 20K phones.
  

  3. BATTERY: It promises us a day long battery with mixed use but it falls little short of it. I managed to get around 15 hours with mixed use. But if you are cautiously using your phone you can get more than a days power. Even when both sim cards are active there is not much noticeable difference in discharge rate. So I am happy with the battery life as I don't do much gaming and all.
  

  4. BUILD: The build is the 3rd best thing I liked about the phone. It has a very premium and non plastic feel. The weight is perfect enough to give you a sturdy feel and the phone does not twist while applying good amount of force.  The design fits perfectly and makes the one hand use easier, while the back cover assures that its not going to slip out of your hand. Thumbs up moto g :D.
  

  5. GORILLA GLASS 3: Just one thing about the glass. After constant daily (rough) use there is not a single scratch in the glass surface. I am not using any screen guard and I don't think I need any. 5/5 for the glass panel.
  

  Things which I didn't like about Moto G
  
  1. The call quality was not upto the mark. There is treble in the sound (may be problem with my device only). The problem happens normally at the high volume.
  

  2. I lost the phone sound once in 2 weeks. I could not hear what the other person was talking. I restarted the phone and problem was solved.
  

  3. Camera was not responding once. Restart solved the issue.
  

  4. There is a warm hue in the screen, this is noticeable only when there is a white background. Overall it does not affect the screen quality.
  

  5. There is thin gap between the edge of the glass and the frame, so with constant use, dust accumulates in that gap which is hard to clean.
  

  6. Low light pictures are not good, but in good lighting condition it takes very pretty pictures.
  

  Overall Moto G is the best device out there in terms of performance and price. Its an amazing phone and I am sure that you will not be disappointed once you start using it. If you are planning to buy anything within 25K our 14K Moto G is the BEST. Go for it Android Lovers :D

column6: Great product, Highly recommended, Quick delivery - in just 2 days
column7:
Hi, my company just shifted from CDMA to GSM, and I placed my order for the Moto-G 16GB variant on 22nd by credit card and received the product on 24th morning in a sturdy packaging.
  

  A slight disappointment when i opened the case and couldn't find a data cable inside. Later realized that i may not need it in the first place, and the existing micro usb cable would suffice. I had to get the sim card 25x15 mm cut into micro sim 15x12 mm at a local vendor for Rs.20, and inserted in the sim-1 slot. The phone picked up all 3G settings automatically.
  

  The Moto-G has a software called Motorola Migrate. I downloaded this on my old CDMA android 2.2 as well from play store. On playing the software on both phones it generated a QR code on MG(Moto-G) and asked the old phone camera to scan this code. The old phone did a somersault and worked overtime to scan the basic code. Once the code was read, the software asked me to keep the two phones aside for some time. After 15 minutes there was a message on the phones scolding why the software was still open. I realized that all my phone contacts, text sms, audio files, video files, photographs, pdf files, epubs, whatsapp media files, and all that can be were transferred to MG. Half the battle was already won. Just this much was enough for another colleague to immediately order a 16GB variant from flipkart.
  

  Next came the camera. The primary takes decent snaps. My main usage of the camera is to take random snaps, capture visiting card details and store in phonebook, save scribbled notes and whiteboard notes into pdf and email. Just try out camcard & camscanner softwares on the MG, it'll just blow your mind. The secondary camera is great as well. My priority was to transmit a decent picture over skype, not send my photograph for a modelling assignment.
  

  Do you really feel the user available 13GB is insufficient for mobile use? I admit that additional space is good, for instance I once consumed the entire 16GB internal as well as 32GB external on my galaxy tab, but that was a different story altogether. I will not like to read books for hours or watch 3 hour movies on a 4.5 inch screen. All I would do is load the memory with a hundred apps and games. So I did just that and after loading whatsapp, camcard, facebook, mxplayer, flashlight, indianrail, adobe, bookmyshow, twitter, skype, messenger, qrdroid, utorrent, camscanner, filemanager, timesofindia, templerun2, subwaysurfer, carrom3d, minionrush, hillclimb, 360security and racingmoto I got a little tired. Still waiting for the phone to start bugging me with lags, hangs and jerks, but no luck. So I downloaded the Kitkat update, but didn't install it as yet(who knows? I still fear the reviews I read earlier). Finally I downloaded  ASPHALT 8 . This is the mother of all memory eaters, consumed 1.61 GB space on the phone, took 6 hours to download over an EVDO internet connection, and was my last shot at rejecting the MG. I've been using the 16 GB Moto G for around 15 days now and my review is based on the same. It's slightly lengthy but it'll help clear a lot of doubts regarding the phone.
  

  Before I detail the pros and cons, I'm writing a few tips to help people-
  

  Tips-
  

  1)In case you allow the phone's battery to completely drain and then the phone does not come on after charging, it does not mean your phone is faulty!
  
  It's a failsafe built in by Motorola.
  
  Solution-
  
  Leave the phone in a cool, dry place-like Oregano ;-)- for a few hours and then try to power on by holding the power button for 20+ seconds.
  
  Refer to xdadevelopers.com for more.
  

  2)To improve the camera, do consider apps like PicsArt, Instagram, Camera FX.
  
  Of course these add effects more than anything but the photos look better.
  

  3)To further extend the battery life, download an app called Greenify and greenify the apps you don't use regularly. No need for other battery saving software.
  

  4) To play every format of video and audio, download MX Player.
  

  Now coming to the pros.
  
  Pros-
  

  1) Build Quality- Brilliant.
  
  The matte rubberised back really helps grip and the phone feels premium at this price, not cheap and plasticky.
  
  You might find the volume rocker and power buttons to be a bit loose but that's perfectly normal.
  

  2)Screen- A 720p screen at this price is unheard of.
  
  Most of the new offerings in mwc 2014 viz. xperia m2, lg l90, lg f70 all have similar specs as the Moto g but with qHD screens i.e. 540x960 resolution. That means much lesser ppi.
  

  3)Speakers- The sound output is really brilliant especially with the bundled equaliser software. Best bass on any phone I've ever used.
  

  4)Speed- The phone is blazing fast thanks to a combination of stock android, a quad core Qualcomm Snapdragon 400 and 1 GB Ram.
  
  You never feel as if the processor is old, even though it is.
  

  5)Battery Life- The battery life is brilliant.
  
  I easily manage to churn out at least 36 hours on moderate use and at least 14 hours on heavy use including gaming, browsing, facebook, whatsapp with screen on continuously.
  

  Cons-
  

  1)Camera- It says 5 megapixel but it performs far worse than my galaxy s advance which also has a 5MP camera.
  
  Download some softwares mentioned in the tips to improve performance here.
  

  2)The volume and power buttons might appear loose. Refer to Tips on how to deal with it.
  

  3)Storage- Always go for the 16 GB model as the 8GB one gives you just 4 GB user available memory.
  

  4)Service Centres- There is a list of service centres available on in.motorola.com-->Moto G-->Customer Support-->Service Centres.
  
  The ones given by Flipkart.com might be old in some cases and have wrong phone numbers.
  

  5) Accessories- I urge you to buy the Moto G Flip shell but only if you have the first day buyer offer.
  
  Rs 1600 is way too much for a flip cover otherwise but it adds brilliant protection to your phone.
  

  Now I'll compare the Moto G with some of the new phones released in Mobile World Congress 2014 yesterday that overcome the shortcomings of the moto G. There is no word on their pricing yet though although they are expected to be more expensive.
  

  Moto G vs Xperia M2 vs LG L90
  

  1) Processor- Same Snapdragon 400 in all cases
  
  Winner- Tie
  

  2) Display- Moto G has a 720 p display on a 4.5 inch screen.
  
  Xperia M2 has a qhd display on a 4.8 inch screen.
  
  Lg L90 has a 4.7 inch display on a qhd screen.
  

  Winner- Moto G for resolution.
  
  Xperia M2 for screen size( if you prefer bigger phones)
  

  3) Storage- Moto G= 8/16 GB non user expandable memory.
  
  Xperia M2- 8GB, upto 32 GB user expandable memory.
  
  Lg L90- 8 Gb, expandable memory upto 32 GB.
  

  Winner= LG L90/ Xperia M2 for giving expandable storage
  

  4) Camera- Moto G has a 5 MP back camera and a 1.3 MP front camera.
  
  Xperia M2- 8MP back camera with Sony Sensor, front camera(MP not known yet)
  
  LG L90- 5MP back camera, 1.3 MP front
  

  Winner- Xperia M2
  

  5) Build quality- Moto G has a rubberised matte back and great build quality.
  
  Xperia M2 has a design very similar to xperia Z2 so you get the flagship design for 2014.
  
  LG L90- Plasticky design with metal strip running around, similar to Samsung phones, but a little better.
  

  Winner- Xperia M2/Moto G (it's personal preference really)
  

  6) Battery- Moto g has a 2070 mAh non user removable battery.
  
  Xperia M2 has a 2440 mAh user removable battery.
  
  Lg L90 has a 2300 mAh battery.
  

  Winner- Xperia M2, especially with Sony's power saving software.
  

  Ultimate verdict- The Moto G is the best phone you can buy.
  
  It has a few flaws which have been overcome by the new phones but both the Xperia M2 and the LG L90 won't launch before April at least in the Indian market.
  
  They are expected to be priced higher but of course you get a better camera, better battery life, user removable battery and expandable storage.
  

  The choice is yours.
  
  Thanks for reading my review.

There are a ton of reviews on this site so i am just going to state a few things i personally observed about this phone.
  

  Pros -
  

  1. The Battery. In general i managed to get an average of around 16 hours of battery life with heavy use. Which is good, considering the 2070 mAh battery on the inside..
  

  2. The Processing Power -  With the combination of the snapdragon 400 and near stock android, it flies through almost all applications, given some games do tend to lag a bit. (GTA: VC, GTA:SA - major lag)
  

  3. The Display - This is by far the best part about this device. It has a really bright and true to life display. Colours seem natural and the 326 ppi density makes watching a movie in 1080p really an enjoyable experience. (Its a matter of personal opinion on the size for watching a movie though. Personally, I prefer the 4.5 inch display as a on the go device for multimedia.)
  
  Ps. 1080p works at 30fps only with mp4 format, Other formats do play but tend to have lag.
  

  4. Speakers - The speakers are really quite amazing on this phone. They are really loud and clear. (Slight distortion at maximum volume though)
  

  5. Overall Build - This does not feel like a device that you would get for 14k. It definitely feels like its worth a lot more the way that it is designed and the materials used.
  


  Cons -
  

  1. Bugs with KitKat build
  

  2. Camera - The camera is quite decent with good amount of detail in well lit areas but horrible low light shots. Flash does help but the flash saturation in the photos is way beyond a decent level.
  

  3. Storage - I was really hoping for a bigger storage option. The 16 gb version that i had picked up is already filled up. Most of it though due to the sheer number of applications that are installed and the data files that they generate.
  


  Lastly, I have to mention this for the sake of anyone who is buying this phone. I like a few others who have purchased this phone (not just flipkart) have run into the same issue. A damaged version of the display panel. A few dead pixels, slight backlit bleeding and a dead backlit led. Make sure that if you do purchase this phone that you do check for these particular defects.

ordered a 16 GB Moto G through flipkart with one day delivery guarantee, got it in 5 days! (Though some of my friends got it the next day with normal delivery option). But, finally it costed me Rs. 13,999 only!
  
  secure packaging (thanks to WS Retail) with bubble packed carton!
  

  was pre upgraded to Android 4.4.2 Kitkat! pre loaded with almost no bloatwares. The only two inbuilt apps from the Motorola were Motorola Migrate and Moto Assist (Assist being very useful instead)
  

  The power and volume rockers feel slightly cheap: the only disappointing thing about the built, but it will not make a issue with normal use. Its much better than boring identical Samsung phones design though!
  

  The best feature about the phone is its brilliant high density 4.5 inch IPS Display with a resolution of 720 x 1280 pixels (329 ppi pixel density). It has awesome color reproduction and enough brightness even with the least brightness set. Notably, the Moto G's screen is a bit sharper than Apple's iPhone 5s, which offers 326 ppi. The phone uses the default boring stock UI which I overridden with Google Now Kitkat Launcher which is featured in Nexus Phones. This made the phone UI interesting with Google now cards on the left most home screen and the awesome "OK Google" hot word detection!
  
  My friend ordered a Moto G recently and his display was slightly yellowish as compared to my clear white display. I searched for this issue on internet and lots of posts were flooded with the problem. I guess it might be due to different different components assembly from different OEMs. But his display was also looking brilliant and he is using it without an issue as of now!
  

  The phone is buttery smooth with its Quad-core 1.2 GHz Qualcomm MSM8226 Snapdragon 400 on a Cortex-A7 chipset with an Adreno 305 GPU. Big games and tasks are good to go. The 1 GB RAM also makes the phone much used multi tasking capability easier. I had tried almost all the larger games including Asphalt 8, Real Racing and Injustice and the performance was awesome without an issue.
  
  The 16 GB of the device is nearly 12 GB usable with no expandable memory card slot! The biggest drawback of the phone along with the non removable battery! The back cover is open able only for inserting the two micro SIM cards and for customizing the colorful back panels!
  

  I felt an average speech quality during calls through its earpiece with no call drop issues. During the Line video chat to another Moto G the 720p enabled front camera worked well with nice clarity(both ways)! The loud speaker of the phone is much much loud and above average but only gives Mono audio output.
  
  The Wi-Fi and mobile data works average as compared to other devices in this class. It didn't disappoint me yet! My local media streaming was working well. But I felt a slight laginess on my Wi-Fi connection  during Youtube HD streaming as my other devices were buffering quicker simultaneously!
  
  Rest of the cloud features and syncing were normal and performed without and issue.
  

  The phone sports a 5 mega pixel auto focus camera with a new Motorola camera interface. The camera performs well in terms of autofocus and any novice can use camera with an ease but, it is very low on megapixels. Altough, I never felt cheated for the camera. The back and front camera both are capable of shooting 720p videos. The slow movie capture is also present identical to the iPhone 5s SlowMo! With the latest camera update the volume rockers can be used as dedicated camera shutter buttons although a long press didn't set the focus instead took many multiple shutter shots! The flash is very bright and it is placed in-between the camera and Motorola logo dimple. The camera is good for Instagramming and other social outdoor bright light shots!
  
  The phone supports a non removable 2070 mAh battery with Motorola claiming with 24 hours mix usage. I used the phone with all the mixed features and was able to use the phone whole day with average call, Wi-Fi usage, tweeting, Facebooking, Instagramming, Youtube and texting. With heavy usage it can run upto 16 hours on a single charge. Although the charging time is larger as Motorola provided charger is has low  current output. But it can be charged faster with other USB sockets including PC USB ports. But for this, you have to get an extra data syncing wire as the wire was not included in the box! Despite many rumours on 4.4.2 The OTG storage with a 16 GB USB flash drive worked fine without any issue on my device as I used the Cyanogenmod built File manager. Other popular file managers can also be used for an issue less working of OTG cable. So, the folks worrying about expandable storage should not be worried about the 12 GB inbuilt space.

Clearly we need to understand that flipkart is just like a service,which connects sellers and buyers. If the product is delayed,then it must be because of either the delay of seller or other natural circumstances(may be). So flipkart does'n play much role in this. If they get the product then they deliver it very soon. And another important thing is that,this was a product which was in very high demand,so no one is to be blamed for late delivery.
  

  Regarding the product,if you have used high expensive mobiles like iphone,note etc, then you will find some features left out in this mobile. But you should understand that this mobile has covered many features in this price.Some peoples have been reporting issues with their mobile,i too had very little software issues,but it happens when a product is just
  
  released and in my opinion you should also have little luck to get a good one because you are ordering through online and not by checking the product twice or thrice in a shop.Every issues can be fixed,all we need to do is to be calm and to approach right person to solve issues.
  

  Problem i faced with this mobile:
  
  I didn get much hardware problem.Both the slim slots were working fine and only then i used scratch guard.The real problem was, i couldn update the OS with my mobile data network.Since i dont have wifi,my only option was through mobile data.I contacted motorola customer care 2times,and 2answers was given by different persons. One told like we could update system update only with wifi,and other one said we can update by mobile data/wifi but he doesn know the real problem which i was facing and he told me to take my mobile to a service center.But i wish to find the solution on my own.I realised like i got my sim in my native and this sim works as a roaming in the city which i work.I guessed this was a problem,and today i found that i was correct.
  

  Yes, THE SIM WHICH IS IN ROAMING WILL NOT ALLOW YOU TO DO SYSTEM UPDATES.:)
  

  Even though it will take data from your mobile data network,it will ask you to turn on WIFI(dont know why :D).After updating i did'n get any errors like camera errors,sim not detecting etc.I guess i am lucky since most are facing these problems after updating their OS.
  
  If you have a roaming sim and if you need to update,you can use a friends mobile(if he has mobile hotspot option) to be a wifi-hotspot and you can access internet through his mobile.(his device will be acting as a wifi connection,so you can choose his device name in wifi and can access it) :)
  

  Pros:
  
  *Looks great in hand and placed in a table.
  
  *Boot time is very fast.
  
  *Charge stands for 1 1/2 days for me for normal use,if played games and accessing internet it stands from 12-24hours.
  
  *Loud speaker.
  
  *HD Recording.
  
  *Touch screen is very good.(recommend to use matte finish screen guards)
  

  Cons:
  
  *Headset is just OK,but the clarity and sound is very good
  
  *Camera is good not best but unlike other mobiles telling that it has 12mp and only has 8 or 10mp,this mobile stands for its mentioned specs.
  
  *Dont know why i had to turn on wifi even if i am updating through a mobile data network(yet to be inspected).
  
  *Getting ringtone in the phone even if i am connected to a headset(thats also fine).
  
  *Didn get a usb cable and back cover.(came around 700 extra for me to buy those).
  

  Finally,i recommend this product to people who have just started to buy tough phones,and for people who is looking for a classy low budget phones.
  
  Not suitable for people who have already using iphones or high expensive mobiles,you will keep finding something is missing with this mobile :)
  

  Thanks to flipkart and motorola for this nice product.

The phone is pretty much similar to its sibling the moto X!
  

  Design-The design of the phone is not too flamboyant but neither too cheap. Its decent for a phone in this particular price range.
  

  Display- The 4.5' 720p display is stunning when compared to all the other phone available in this price range.

  Battery Life- From the past two weeks use, the battery performance is brilliant. You can easily juice out 1.5-2 days with out mobile data use.(but who does that???)
  
  And with data connection you can get a complete day, which is not bad!!!
  

  Camera- In this department the phone failed to deliver the 'Moto G' magic. The phone has a average 5 MP camera which does okay in day light and poor in low light even with a normal in built flash.But the HDR mode helps improving the image quality by a bit.
  

  Performance - Being a low power quad core with a pure android Os, the performance of this phone is compared tot he next level phones like Nexus 4, Note 2 ans S3, but with an advantage of low power consumption.
  
  The phone is pretty much sooth and fast with almost no lag like the Nexus 4.
  

  Along with this there are certain disadvantages for the phone, which are actually not disadvantages but limitations!
  

  --> No user replaceable battery( Not much of a required thing).
  
  --> Limited storage, No Micro SD slot.
  
  --> Average Camera.
  

  But the Moto G is still a winner. People often compare Moto G with the Nexus 5, which is a better phone any day but the fact is Moto G offer such features which makes it comparable to the Nexus, even though it is half the price of Nexus!!!

  4) Internal memory is the best performing memory of a phone. Even class 10 SD cards are not as fast.

column6: Buying this phone is one of the most prudent choices I have made
column7:
Unlike most people before me who used the reviews to vent their anger on the issues with service, rather than talk about the Phone, I chose to wait till I actually used this product.
  

  I've been using this new phone for 2 days now, and I'm going to tell you about why I feel I made the best choice in opting for it.
  

  Here are features I discovered on this phone that amazed me (I assume that you, like I did, currently use a cheaper phone or a phone without these features) :
  
  1) It's fast and responsive. You can easily notice the phone is like a wand which responds to your gestures with ease.
  
  2) When you first start your phone, you're asked for your Google/gmail id and suddenly the phone automatically integrates all your stuff and usage patterns from any google site or product you have used before
  
  3) You don't need to type in messages. The Swype feature allows you to glide your finger over the letters in a word and "very accurately" guesses the word you wish to type
  
  4) You don't even need the above feature. The phone has an inbuilt option wherein you can type USING YOUR VOICE. Just speak out your message and it accurately types whatever you're saying. I'm impressed by the how well it picks up my "Indian accent"
  
  5) The phone has inbuilt Google Voice Assist. Click the google search box on the homescreen and say a search query such as "Distance Bangalore to Mumbai". The phone "TALKS BACK" to you. It tells you the distance and shows a map result with directions.
  
  5) Even without internet, you can use the voice assist to dial a number in your contacts. For example, I clicked on the Google search box(without net) and said "Call Prashant". It read my command, showed me the contact detail and asked "Mobile or Home" (The contact had 2 numbers). I replied "Mobile" and it made a call. Love this feature
  
  6) The phone multitasks with ease and there are a lot of great Android apps for all your needs.
  
  7) The Indian edition of the phone comes with a wall charger, but misses out on USB cable. But it looks unnecessary as everything you need can be transferred to and from this phone using the net and with Google help. So don't worry about it.
  

  If you already have a more expensive phone with all these features, then don't bother. But if you're like me who's looking for the latest and best features of technology in a Rs12,500 phone then don't think twice. Buy it!
  

  Hope you find my review useful :)

Samsung Galaxy Grand Quattro also has an quad core CPU which is also 1.2GHz but a MediaTek chipset which clearly shows its capabilities. column6: Why this an Exceptional Phone at Exceptional Price...?
column7:
I will give you 10 reasons...
  

  1)  DISPLAY : You won't get a display of this quality for this price. It is simply stunning.
  
  I will say why. This phone has a 4.5 inch display with 720 x 1280 pixels (~326 ppi pixel density). Human eye is not able to differentiate any detailing above 300 ppi. So this the best that you can see with your eyes (even if you look at a phone with 450 ppi) . I have compared this display with a Nexus 5 and to my wonder this 720p display felt more rich and true than the 1080p display of a 33k phone. This is no exaggeration but the truth. The display stood par with the Note 3 display (only the video quality in the screen is discussed here)
  

  2) PROCESSOR : 1.2 Ghz quad core Snapdragon 400 processor is immensely powerful. The device will feel butter smooth at all times and processing power won't bother you at any point of time. Switching between apps, gaming, 1080p video playback everything is handled exceptionally well.
  

  3)GPU : They are giving you a phone at this price with a GPU, that itself is something great. Adreno 305 is the GPU. So far it handled Asphat 8, GT Racing and few high end graphics demanding games very well without any frame skip or lag or delay.  The game play is super smooth. 1080p video playback was way better in this phone than many phones which were priced at 20k.
  

  4) CORNING GORILLA GLASS 3 : No other phone in this price bracket comes with gorilla glass. It is scratch and shatter proof (as claimed). So you can say a premium feature in a premium phone is there in Moto G which gives you peace of mind while using it.
  

  5) NANO COATING : Yes your phone is waterproof though it is told as spill resistant. This is something you can't even see in a 33k Nexus 5. So you get more than what you pay.
  

  6)ANDROID 4.4 : You get a Kitkat version of android for this price bracket. The experience is flawless. But thd Kitkat update i would say is 95% complete , 5% is still jellybean (like icons, apps wiget separation in menu, long press menu in home screen etc)
  

  7) DECENT FRONT CAM : The 1.3 MP front cam is pretty good and it serves your purpose of video calls fairly well. Many phones in this price range to around 20k has 0.3MP front cam, so again here you get more than what you pay. Back cam is also decent and i won't say it is totally bad. Touch focus and HDR mode and good light gives you good results. Low light performance is poor.
  

  8)BATTERY : I don't know how this phone with 4.5 inch display and quad core processor is able to stay the whole day with a 2070 mAh battery,  but it does manage to do that. The battery backup is really a strong point of this phone, when compared with any other phone of this range or any other range. I do remember Samsung S4 mini battery was draining like anything and it can't manage to stay up till noon with extensive usage.
  

  9) OTG : The phone supports usb 2.0 devices with an OTG cable. I tried a pendrive and Playstation joystick and both were supported. And sadly Nexus 5 failed here too.
  

  10) MISCELLANEOUS : The phone feels sturdy in hand, built quality is way beyond exceptional, phone looks really cool and very similar to the flagship phone Moto X, replaceable back covers which suits your taste and looks trendy, decent loudspeaker, 3.5mm headphone out is good, call quality good, Custom ROM for many more Android versions expected as there was for Motorola defy(support from Froyo to KitKat), if so this phone can stay very alive for next 2 years or beyond.
  

  In short this is an MVFM phone (More Value For Money)

column6: Confused between MOTO G and MOTO X..... Go for MOTO X
column7:
Friends this review is not regarding how overwhelming MOTO X is but I have done a first hand comparison between G and X.
  
  Obviously MOTO G is a great phone at its price range but if you are confused between both...I would say go for X.
  
  I bought this phone on the first day considering the popularity of G but certainly made a good decision.
  

  1. The first prominent diff is the Touchless control. X has it and G doesn't. And mind it, its not any other feature which you can overlook. Its the future of Mobile.
  

  2. One of the most important difference is the processor. X has a 1.7GHz Snapdragon S4 processor. Also It has what the company calls the Motorola X8 Mobile processor, which is essentially a low power consuming co-processor that stays awake while the phone is in sleep mode. This not only enables the always-on voice command and active display features but also ensures that the Moto X has a longer battery life as the main processor is not activated unless required for processor intensive tasks.
  

  3. There is no Active Display in MOTO G, which I must tell you is very awesome feature. I after using this feature for about a month can't think of a phone without this feature. The moment I pick my cell up or take it out from my pocket, everything shows up on the screen in a very battery efficient way.
  

  4. G has a corning Gorilla glass but no Amoled screen. Also the size of both the phones are same but the screen size of G is smaller making the edges bigger. Even the Weight of X is 130 gms whearas G is 140 gms.
  

  5. The battery of G is 2070 mAh whearas of X its 2200 but as explained in pt no 2, X saves a lot of battery. Also you have a unique charger having two usb slots. Thus you can charge two phones from a single adapter at a time which is great.  G comes with a standalone charger and not the charger with usb cable. It neither gives a data cable in the box.
  

  6. Other visible features are the camera. X has 10 and 2 whearas G has 5 and 1.2 primary and secondary camera resp.
  

  7. X has 2 GB RAM which is great. G only boasts 1 GB.
  

  So my verdict "The Moto X is not the fastest phone in the world. It's also not the most cutting-edge, it doesn't feature the biggest display, and it isn't the thinnest Android phone. However, there is absolutely no doubt that the Moto X is the most amazing Android phone I have ever used, and I think most people will agree."

  I will start this review with a look at the existing market scenario in the country.
  
  One player (You know which one! ;))has dominated the smartphone market in India (and most of the world) just because of 2 reasons:

  Now, turning my attention to people who say, "Who will pay 24k for a dual-core processor": My friends, here you are not paying for the hardware,
  
  you are paying for the software optimization.
  
  Still if you think its not enough then look at the hardware. It has Motorola X8 Mobile Computing Chip with
  
  1. Snapdragon S4 Pro 1.7GHz dual core CPU
  
  2. Quad Core Adreno GPU
  
  3. Single Core Natural language processing low power DSP
  
  4. Single Core Contextual processing low power processor.
  
  (That makes eight cores! :D)
  

  I bought this phone way back in the US. Lets talk about the phone itself:
  
  Pros:
  
  1. Great form factor: The shape of the phone is such that you will feel extremely comfortable holding it. Fits your hand perfectly.
  
  2. Display: Beautiful 4.7" 720p AMOLED display which is large enough but does not feel large to hold in your hand.

  because it uses Google's voice recognition software.
  
  4. Active Display: The phone does not have a notification LED. The screen itself is the notification LED. Few pixels light up frequently
  
  to show what notification you have got. You can even read the notification without unlocking the screen. (Extremely useful feature)
  
  It even knows when you want the notification screen to be on! (e.g when you take out your mobile from the pocket)

  11. Motorola Connect: Get all messages and calls on your computer without a cable!
  
  12. Made in the USA! Expect great finishing quality!
  

  Cons:
  
  After cracking my head found some:
  
  1. Dont expect the camera to take great quality pics! After all, for that you have your digital camera!
  
  2. Battery lasts for one day with 3G/WiFi mixed usage. Could have been better.

Being dual-core adds an advantage of being power efficient and gives better battery life in situations of higher CPU loads.

After a lot of research into which phone to go for, I zeroed-in on Moto X, and I'm pretty satisfied with it.
  
  I used Samsung Galaxy S for 3.5 yrs, and I finally had to get a new one as it had become excruciatingly slow. Obviously, I did not want to go with Samsung again. The closest competition was Nexus 5, but having read a lot of reviews about the screen being brittle, I went with Moto X.
  

  My observations after using this for a month:
  




  Design & Construction:
  
  ---------------------------------
  
  - It's slimmer at the bottom and gets thicker as u go to the top, making it a really well-balanced phone. The dimple at the back makes for a natural place to rest ur index finger on & is well placed in relation to the weight.
  
  - The back is rubberized and is easy to grip.
  
  - It's solid in overall construction, though there's a creaking sound if pressed near the volume rocker, but that may differ from piece to piece.
  




  Accessories:
  
  -------------------
  
  - The earphones provided are not in-ear and look cheap(sound quality is decent though), so does the usb charger.
  
  - Both Apple earphones(with mic) and Samsung can be used, but calls can only be accepted and not ended.
  



  Hardware:
  
  --------------
  
  - Performance is very good with no lag at all. Dual core is more than enough, unless ur into video encoding and heavy games.
  
  - Supports 4G band of 1800 MHz, but in India, Airtel has launched 4G on 2300 MHz, though the Govt. has allowed 4G to be used on any of these 2 bands.
  
  - Speaker(rear and front) quality is good. Rear speaker is very loud.
  
  - Mic performance is probably not as good as Samsung. Voice is not that loud at the receiving end(comparatively).
  
  - Battery life - 1 day of moderate use. If used on 2G, it's about 1.5 days. Charging time - 2.5 - 3 hrs. Battery saver mode only disables data if it's less than 15%.
  



  Software:
  
  -------------
  
  - Active notifications:
  
  - Shows your last notification when the screen is locked. Downloaded apps can also be configured.
  
  - Activated at any kind of movement like picking-up the phone, braking while driving etc.
  
  - An unadvertised feature to activate: Waving ur hand above the screen(similar to Galaxy S4).
  
  - If lying unattended with screen facing up & with unread notifications, it keeps on popping-up every 6-7 secs. If it's in the pocket, or lying face-down, notifications r not displayed as it uses the proximity sensor.
  
  - If there are no notifications, a "lock" icon is displayed instead, and you practically never need to use the unlock button for unlocking.
  

  - Touchless control - Very useful. Requires data for most commands(some like "Find my Phone", "What's up?" work w/o data as well). Doesn't read the entire notification for 3rd party apps like Times of India/other email clients etc. Mentions the no. of notifications instead.
  
  - 5 fixed homescreens(can't be changed), all have google search bar which can't be removed.
  
  - Dialer - Always displays recent contacts on launch. An extra tap is required to open the dial-pad. Individual entries from Call Log can't be deleted. No option of "Edit No. b4 Call".
  
  - Camera settings are much easier to operate than stock android.
  
  - No kill all processes option in recent apps as Samsung
  


  Overall rating - 4.5/5. Almost all the negatives can be overcome by apps. Highly recommended!
