  Do not be misled by the "Dual Core" you see on the specifications. It has 8 Working Cores which optimize battery usage and thus provide a better smartphone experience.
  

  1 & 2 :
  
  It has 1.7Ghz Dual Core Krait CPU from the Qualcomm Snapdragon S4Pro family, which powers your basic interactions and more.
  
  3,4,5 & 6:
  
  It has a Quad - Core Adreno 320 Graphics Processing Unit for great viewing, astounding deep colour displays and great gaming.
  
  The last two processors are the ones which make Moto X stand out:
  

  7:
  
  The natural language processor, which is on standby and is always ready to listen to your voice (Since this phone is a Google product, it is one of the phones offering the best "Google Now" experiences").
  
  8:
  
  The Contextual Computing Processor uses all the sensors on the phone to detect movement, and it comes in so handy that with just two flicks of your wrist while holding the mobile, you can whip up your camera. It uses the proximity sensor and ambient light to detect whether your phone is in your hand or in your pocket or your bag. ( The use of this will be explained later on).
  

  So this X8 computing system really optimizes battery usage and never leaves you wanting for more power. It was a good decision that I bought this phone since the performance is the best i've seen.
  

  Once you train it to listen to your voice, it brings in the noise cancellation technique to filter your voice only and cancels ambient noise. You can ask the phone anything or set your alarm, reminders and tons of stuff by just saying the command phrase "Ok Google Now", when you have your net connection. It is better if you have a WiFi connection.
  

  As metioned earlier, it detects whether your phone is in your hand or pocket and uses this to display "Active Notifications Display".When the screen is locked (sleeping), The AMOLED screen gives the advantage to partially light up only the pixels needed on the screen to display notifications, thus saving you a lot of battery life. You can swipe these away or view them on the locked screen itself, since it stays on the screen till you view or dismiss it. When your phone is inside your pocket, it doesnt do so. Also, you can choose the option to not display these notifications during night (11:00pm to 6am). Or you could just turn off the whole 'Active Display' in Settings but who would refuse such a great feature?
  

  The camera quality is good, and it has Auto Focus as well as Manual settings where you can control the Focus and Exposure by dragging the shutter icon on the screen. The size is just about perfect for my hands, and I was able to reach across the 4.7-inch display to the upper-left corner with little difficulty. The curved back feels right on. The button placement is not only sensible, but the buttons seem built to last: clicky, punctual, tough.
  

  As far as resolution is concerned, text and graphics look plenty smooth on a 4.7-inch 720p display. As with most Motorola phones, the speakers on the Moto X are excellent. They're loud enough to use in the car hands-free and generally clear for speakerphone use and even a little YouTube or music playback. The first thing that you should know about the software on this phone is that it is thankfully, mercifully, for all intents and purposes "stock" Android Kit-kat 4.4.2.
  

  There is no perceivable difference between a full HD and HD resolution in this screen size, except for the battery life compromise. The deal with other brands is that the battery life & some hardware features start to falter within 6-9 months. By the same token, devices made by Motorola and perhaps Nokia have by far the most reliable hardware including quality of battery. The additions to the software that Motorola has made are legitimately useful and really quite impressive. They add to the experience of Android without removing what is most vital in Google's software, unlike the competition, which seems intent on obscuring what's already a sophisticated and beautiful operating system. And the phone is nice. I mean, really nice to use. It's a reminder that the way something is built can be as important as what it's made of.
  

  The voice control, active display and camera quick-start features are excellent additions to the standard Android experience, and Motorola's commitment to optimization and speed is evident as the device is lag-free.
  

  The Moto X is not a perfect phone, but neither is any other phone on the market right now. What it is, however, is a pretty damn good phone and one I can recommend. User-friendly, satisfying experience, a great mix of personalization & convenience. Worth buying!

column6: Moto X. The best Android "phone" in sub 30k range. Period
column7:
Well I got this phone just one week ago from Flipkart, as usual their delivery time was exceptional, 36 hours from the order and the phone was delivered!
  

  Display : Nice, coming from S4 though nothing can impress me, maybe the S5, well. It's still a very good Samsung made OLED panel, I can compare this with the Note 2 I had, it's really good. And yeah it's 720p, but NO, you are not gonna notice it coming from 1080p, yet I have very sharp eyes, besides I am obsessed with display quality too, still.
  

  Call quality : Exceptional. I don't remember what was the last phone I used which had as great call quality like this. It's crisp, clear and just great.
  

  Size : The best part of this phone. It's just the perfect size for me, and I believe for other human beings too. While Samsung, LG, Sony and hTC are going with the ridiculous trend of upping the dimension of each and every flagship, and yet our hands are still there of same size since human beings appeared on planet earth, I am really confused where exactly we are headed. I am quite confident that it will stop, and probably those manufacturers have to dial it back, very soon.
  

  The phone looks great by the way, too. Seems like very well built. I got the White one and it looks classy to be honest.
  

  Performance : As I said, it's fantastic. You will not notice any lag (well the occasional micro stutters are still somewhat there, but blame Android and it's ecosystem, not Moto). It's the most fluid Android I have ever used. And I don't really wanna disrespect the performance by comparing it to the S4 I had, which was simply awful.
  

  Camera : Now I see this is a big part of nowadays users, as they depend on a cell phone camera quite a lot. Now let's get this straight, this camera will not replace your cheapest P&S. It's just fine for social stuffs, more than fine actually, but it's just not up to the mark for something more important stuffs. This is the "only" thing I will miss from S4. Still, when I prioritize stuffs, camera comes last, so that's not a big issue for me, at all. Honestly I find it ridiculous when people pay 45+ k for devices like Z2 or S5, only for it's camera, so foolish and idiotic, thinking it takes as good photos as even a cheap P&S does! LOL. Just go and buy those Canon 510HS or something for 8k or something and you will forget about your Z2. Whatever, to each his own I suppose.
  

  Just a tip to get a good photo, just don't shoot as soon as you open the camera, just focus on a subject, then let the camera stay there for at least 4-5 seconds, then take the shot.
  

  Active Display - Well everyone knows this is a trademark feature of X, and yes it's awesome. I won't say that it's far better than normal LED notifications, but yes it's cool, and using a separate chip and OLED display is clever.
  

  Touchless control : To be honest, I haven't played with it at all, and I am not gonna unless it supports offline voice recognition.
  

  Battery life : Another aspect which I suppose is important for most users, and this device has fantastic battery life. You can easily get 4+ hours screen on time with 24 hours or more standy time, keeping WiFi and GPS on all time. You can even hit 4  to 5 hours mark if you can tweak the kernel setting a bit (Faux kernel of course). 720p display is definitely for win here.
  

  Gaming : I don't game on mobile phones, so I won't comment. But yeah, I played a slight bit of Angry Birds, and it runs as smooth as on the S4 I had, maybe a frame or two less, but nothing worth mentioning. Don't see what's the point of having a Snapdragon 805 either, maybe people play GTA V or Crysis 3 on them, whatever.
  

  External Speaker : The speaker is awesome. It will sound as close to the M7 with Beats audio crap I had, yes, it sounds like stereo. A nice touch of bass is even there. Lovely speaker. But again, the placement is nonsense.
  

  Sound : Haven't input the headphones yet, so won't comment. By the way, the stock Motorola in ear which comes with the phone bundled is basically crap. It's one of those flat ones which won't even go inside your ear, cheap Moto. Anyway I wasn't gonna use it anyway.
  

  All other important features like GPS and all works flawlessly as expected. Nothing really worth mentioning here.
  

  So all in all, coming from an S4 i9500 to Moto X is a technical downgrade in every possible section, and some kids might call you crazy, but again, unless and until you have used a device with pure Android you don't know what you were missing, so for me it's a fantastic upgrade. Perfect size, great ergonomics with good build, superb performance, a capable camera for less serious occasions, a very good display, excellent call quality, lovely speaker volume, and all these for which I believe at a great price (price was the last thing I cared about) are just for the win. Once you use this you will feel how awful TouchWiz is, even Sense and Sony's skin might feel heavy. I am not going back to TouchWiz, heck I can NOT.
  

  Thanks for reading,
  
  Saurav (ithehappy)

column6: No phone is perfect neither this one
column7:
I have used Sony Xperia ZR and after that I was using Moto X for the last one month. From my point of view the smartphones available now with in 25000 are not perfect in everything. All of them have some pros and cons.
  

  Moto X pros:-
  
  1. Nice, smooth user interface; no lag at all. The Motorola X8 Mobile Computing System done a quite good job.
  
  2. 2GB RAM never runs out of memory.
  
  3. Performance of Adreno 320, Quad Core Processor is really good while gaming. It allows to play almost every high end graphics games like FIFA 14, Asphalt 8, Nova 3, Real Racing 3 etc.
  
  4. The most impressive thing in this mobile is the battery life. 12-14 hours of normal use, 8-10 hours with heavy gaming and wifi use, approx. 18-22 hours with minimum uses.
  
  5. Stock android which is very simple to use and running with minimum utility apps, i.e. less RAM consumption, less battery consumption.
  
  6. Built quality is pretty good.
  
  7. Noise cancellation (4 microphones) is excellent on this device.
  
  8. Active display which is really help full for notifications and time.
  
  9. Touch less control and Moto assist feature is unique in Moto X.
  
  10. It has a 720p , 4.7 inch display which is good enough for any kind of video or gaming.
  

  Cons:-
  
  1. Although Moto X has a 10 MP camera with HDR mode, but camera quality is not up to the mark. Daylight photography is pretty decent, but low light or in night it captures worst pictures.
  
  Even in the fluorescent light there are some dark linings in the camera screen and its remain there in photo also.
  
  2. As the display is AMOLED display some light black linings both vertically and horizontally may be visible while the screen brightness is low.
  
  3. Although the Moto X has the Corning Gorilla Glass that makes it scratch less but that does not means the glass is unbreakable even after falling from chest height, ironically the glass is very fragile.
  
  4. Heating problem is also a big issue. Although it supports most of the latest high graphics games but it gets very hot even after 5-10 min of playing of normal games like subway surfers.
  
  5. Also Motorola service in India is not quite satisfactory.

column6: MOTO X- A NEW BREED OF TECHNOLOGY THAT HAS REDEFINED SMARTPHONE
column7:
My review for Moto X after using it for more than 2 weeks.
  

  Touchless Control:- Just to begin with, this feature is NOT available in any other smartphone. Be it Samsung, Sony, LG, Nokia,.. Not even Apple!!
  
  I would call the strongest USP of Moto X.
  
  Firstly, you need to train your voice in order to activate this feature. Speak in unique way that no other person could imitate you.
  
  What makes it so special ??!! Just 3 Magical Words.. "O.K. GOOGLE NOW" and...
  
  Without even touching the phone or even holding it, you can get to call anyone from your contacts, get the notifications, open any app, put an alarm, get the info on your favorite topic (by which I mean.. anything & everything !!!).
  
  Note:- It needs internet to perform.
  
  * Don't be disheartened if you will not be able to use it with much ease when in a noisy place like bus, market, etc. But that's just Moto X's hyper-sensitive sensors.
  

  Active Display:- Generally, in order to see the notifications like any message/mail/missed call etc. you have to slide/swipe or unlock the phone first. But not with Active Display!!
  
  The moment you touch the phone it flashes the time along with all your notifications. You can drag to either open or dismiss them. Although, it does not have any kind of LED Notification light but, with this intuitive feature, I am not missing it at all !!
  

  Moto Assist:- Another pack of intuitive features which lets you choose the following types of profile..
  
  Home- Once activated, it will ask you, when you receive a call, either to accept or ignore it. Read out the messages you receive and ask if you wish to reply. You do everything without even touching the phone !!
  
  Driving:- Will do the same as Home. I tried to activate it sitting in the room but it gets activated only when you are driving as it, very intelligently, senses your environment.
  

  Moto Migrate- You can easily transfer data from your old phone without connecting any wire, provided it is an Android/iPhone only. You can transfer from Blackberry as well but that won't be wireless.
  

  Camera:- An impressive 10 M.P. rear and 2 M.P. front camera has made me go on Snapshot Spree!! Love the quality of Pics. It has lot of in-built features like Multiple shots, HDR, Panorama, Slow-Motion, etc. which adds a lot to the quality. HD recording is great.
  
  A Picture-Perfect moment...??!! Just twist your wrinkle twice while holding the phone and TAA-DAA.. your Camera is at your service!!
  

  Processor & OS:- It has Qualcomm Snapdragon S4 Pro processor with a 1.7GHz Dual-Core Krait CPU. Now, being a Heavy-Gamer, this Dual-Core "Hauwaa" (Fee-Faw-Fum) had got me pretty good & left me apprehensive about its gaming performance. While doing some surfing I came to know that it is GPU & RAM that matters. This beast has a Quad-Core Adreno 320 GPU and 2 GB RAM which makes heavy games run Smooth As Silk !! It's been more than 2 weeks, I have been playing heavy games like Asphalt 8, FIFA '14, Modern Combat 4, and guess what...??!!! Not even a SINGLE Lag/Frame Miss.
  
  Now that's what I call.. A STURDY PERFORMANCE !!
  
  It has the latest Android OS i.e. 4.4.2 Kitkat which is means Sure-Shot upgrade to the next & latest OS.
  

  Battery:- Moto X has a 2200 mAh battery and that's decent. If charged 100% in the morning and using it heavily like playing games, internet surfing, music, calling etc., it lasts till evening.
  
  Candidly speaking which smartphone's battery goes beyond that ??
  

  Display & Size:- Moto X come with a 4.7 inch AMOLED Display (720p HD). Though, an old technology but gained popularity these days. It stand for better battery life, greater contrast, darker blacks (Looks great if you use dark themes), and better response time.... Exactly what I was looking for, in my smartphone.
  
  Moto X has Corning Gorilla Glass but it is always wise to play safe !! Get a good screen protector.
  

  Storage:- Moto X has only internal storage i.e. 16 GB ONLY. Being brutally honest, it is less for me and being a heavy gamer, I am experiencing storage constraints. But that's fine since I got an OTG drive for movies, videos & stuff.
  
  It also offer 50 GB free storage data on Google Drive for 2 years.
  

  What really makes Moto X stand out in the market is because of its exclusive features that's not available in any other Smartphones like Touchless Control, Active Display, Motorola Assist, Moto-Functions (Migrate, Connect). That is why I do not own this phone.. I TREASURE IT!!
  

  Flipkart:- This is not the first time I have ordered through Flipkart. And like every time, their Services have been simply OUTSTANDING!!!
  
  I went for In-A-Day-Guarantee for Moto X which had certain amount attached to it. That was supposed to reach me the very next day and IT DID !! The best part was, I had also ordered an OTG & Back Cover (that should have reached me by next week) which got delivered the very next day along with my Moto X.
  

  KUDOS to Moto X !!
  
  KUDOS to Flipkart !!
  
  Regards
  
  Rikshit
  
  (A Proud Moto X Owner)

Motorola seems to be targeting the price-conscious smartphone market with a vengeance. We already know that the budget Moto G has set cash registers ringing around the world, but Motorola hasn't taken its eyes off the mid-range smartphone market either.
  
  Less than two months after the release of the Moto G, comes the company's flagship, the Moto X. The newest member of the Motorola family is squarely aimed at delivering more in terms software, camera, and design without compromising on performance.
  

  When Motorola first announced the Moto X in August last year following its acquisition by Google, it seemed as though the company wanted to position this mid-range device as a premium offering, relying more on design than hardware specifications.
  

  The Moto X has only now made its way to the Indian market, while people overseas are talking of its successor. Thankfully, Motorola has priced it quite reasonably. If it wants to win back any of the market share it has lost in recent years, this is a good way to begin.
  

  Motorola was once known for its ability to churn out solidly built handsets that performed and did not cost the Earth. The Moto X is a blast from that glorious past, with some neat OS features thrown in as well. Will the Moto X be able to revive the mid-range segment? We try to find out.
  

  Look and feel
  
  There's clearly a family resemblance between the Moto X and Moto G. The Moto X isn't a successor or variant, however, and was actually the first new device launched by Motorola under its new leadership; months before the Moto G. In our case, the G came first, so we inevitably wind up comparing the X to it.
  

  The Moto X certainly has a premium look, when compared to the Moto G which has a thicker profile.The Moto X features a body made out of PET composite, a durable plastic; although feels rugged and is surprisingly lightweight.

Moto X is a lovely phone. Flipkart delivery is always on time, kudos to that. But as soon as I open my Moto X and put in a SIM, a dialog box opens and it asks for a "SIM network unlock PIN". So I did some digging, and as it turns out, this is a problem people face who buy phones from abroad, get them to India, and get them unlocked because the phone's generally on contract. Why am I being asked to provide a SIM network unlock PIN? I've bought the bloody phone from a legit source and I demand it be replaced, or repaired as soon as possible. I never expected this.
  

  EDIT:
  
  Earlier rating: 1
  
  New rating: 4
  

  I've got to commend the technical team of Flipkart for providing me with a speedy replacement. I made the complaint on 07 July and the replacement delivery came after 18 hours. They tend to take replacements on priority, but placing such faith in your customers is heartwarming. But all of that does not take away the bitterness left because of a malfunctioning handset. I've got a perfectly working Moto X now, but knowing Moto faultered takes away the shine. Having followed Motorola's progress in 2014, especially in India, the emergence in the market and taking other brands head on, you cannot complement Motorola enough for their amazing quality standards.
  

  I would still like an explanation, or a routine exhaustive/detailed report on why a locked handset was dispatched for delivery. It does pose a lot of questions on Moto's and the retailers reliability.
  

  To summmarize,
  

  Flipkart - 5/5
  
  Moto Service Centre Assistance - 1/5
  
  Moto X - 4/5
  
  Money's worth - 4/5
  

  My suggestions -
  

  With an increasing share in the Indian market, Motorola Mobility LLC must tread carefully and consolidate this trust shown in them in the earlier stages. column6: Motorola Moto X In depth Review
column7:
I will specifically tell my opinion about the phone in various aspects
  

  Design : 4/5
  
  The phone looks almost like a candy bar design but have significant curves around the edges and back which makes it unique from samsung devices. The phone size is very much similar to moto g when you place both the phones near. But the things change when you switch on the device. Moto X has more wide and lengthy display than moto g within that size
  

  The display specs are almost same in both the devices and both have gorilla glass 3 and water repellent coating for added protection
  

  Speaker : 4/5
  
  The Moto X loudspeaker  is loud, but not loud as lumia 720 or xperia zr (phones i compared with). But will satisfy you in every way.
  

  But things change when you connect wired Headset (I use Sony MDR ZX100A -800Rs) and output produced by this phone is awesome. Moto X sound setting provides 4 options as 1) 3D Sound 2) Home Theater 3) Live and 4) Custom (we can adjust the equalizer)
  

  I listen to songs with Home Theater settings and its sweet to my ears...
  

  Camera :3/5
  
  10MP Clear Pixel Camera allows maximum light to enter during night shots but the colors are not natural and lacks sharpness. Also we cannot tune the settings. The day shots are average and also lacks sharpness and looks washed away.
  

  For a real photo person,this phone's camera will let you down
  

  Processor : 5/5
  
  Moto X has done something magical with tuning of the processor. Its 1.7ghz Dual core (when quad core rocks the market nowadays). But the combo of 2gb ram and 1.7ghz dual core snapdragon processor is just awesome. This is my second handset (first was micromax a110) and for the first time i never felt any lag in an android device.
  

  before purchasing this device I had 4 options to chose from
  

  1) HTC Desire 816
  
  2) Sony Xperia ZR
  
  3) Moto X
  
  4) And my least Favorite Galaxy Grand 2
  

  HTC had all the top reviews but it lacked gorilla glass 3 and water repellent coating (My micromax screen got cracked when fell from my head height :) ) so was afraid to buy HTC
  

  Xperia ZR - price was around 19999, but when the day came to buy a phone and I was about to buy, flipkart changed the price to 23000. It was like a slap on my face
  

  Then started researching on Moto X for 3 days and finally i had to sacrifice my camera need and go on with this device
  

  But am happy now.
  

  Active Display :4/5
  
  It shows all the notification in the lock screen . I like my msgs and whatsapp to be private hence turned off. But its a good feature for some people.

column6: Great phone that really brings something new to the smartphone market
column7:
First off let me say that I was never really fond of android until I came across the moto x. The idea of being able to talk to your phone without pushing any buttons seemed really cool and even futuristic. After much research about the moto x I realized it had so much more to offer than just touch less controls. Motorolla has done a really good job by introducing some very useful software here like moto assist and moto migrate. Moto assist automatically picks up when your driving and offers to read your texts and plays the calls you receive on speakerphone. Moto assist also has modes for meeting, sleeping and home. You can chose to activate these as well based on your usage. Another clever idea incorporated is the gesture based control to bring up the phone camera, which is great especially if you need to capture that special moment that just wont last long enough for you to unlock your phone and open up your camera app. After using the phone for a few days now I can say that the gesture control feature is really helpful and works really well all the time. The camera itself is not the best but it does get the job done. The display is excellent and has rich and vibrant colours and when compared to the display of a 1080p phone there is really not too much difference. One of the very few gripes I have with the moto x is the battery life. Although I have read of many users getting excellent battery life I have yet to see such results on my moto x. With a full charge the phone lasts me about half a day or maybe a little more than that. I also noticed the phone tends to overheat a lot even when not in use. After searching about this issue online I found out that turning off location services solves this issue. Turning off location services also helps improve battery life so I hope to get better results now that I have turned it off. It also helps to set the screen brightness to auto in order to get more out of the battery. Aside from this I really have no problem with the phone and it works like a charm. The touch less control works well most of the time and is very useful. You may not get good results when trying to use it in a noisy environment or when you have music playing in the background. This is definitely one off the best android phones in the market today and I can hardly wait for the Moto X+1 which is rumored to be out in the first week of September.

Prologue
  

  It's been a while since Moto X has been out (on Flipkart ofcourse, not in the market).
  
  And people like me who have been intrigued about this phone have read all they
  
  could find about this phone through user and critics reviews and videos reviews as
  
  well. I, for one, did so and stayed up awake an hour or two extra for almost 5-6 nights
  
  to know more about the phone.
  

  With my previous phone, HTC One V, wearing out and ultimately going dead, I knew I
  
  had to purchase a phone soon. In the beginning I had no clue which one to go for and
  
  I was confused like a hungry baby in a topless bar. Each of the phones had some
  
  good features and lacked certain things. Price was a constraint as well. But I had a thing for Motorola, it being my first phone. Also the most durable by far. Yes it was a modest phone , Motorola C168. The best features were FM radio and polyphonic ringtones :D But, what it did, it did well.
  

  The Story
  

  Back to present. This phone reached to me a tad late by Flipkart standards, although
  
  within Flipkart's designated time for it, which was a week. In retrospect, perhaps I was
  
  too excited to get this phone in my hands which led me to notice the otherwise somewhat delay. When it arrived it was neatly packaged in a bubble wrap in a solid cardboard box in a sturdy plastic cover. The phone looked very genuine and all the points to Flipkart for bringing/arranging the sale of Google-Motorola phones in India and doing it the way it should be.
  

  I ordered for a Royal Blue colored Moto X. I trusted Motorola that the feel of the phone
  
  and specially this variant would be nice and it is 'awesome', in a nice way ;) In India,
  
  people can't personalize their Moto X with the Moto Maker but if that option were
  
  available here I probably would have gone for this color anyway. I might have gone a
  
  bit wilder with the bezels though. In my phone the bezels are of metallic blue color.
  
  Which I like nonethless.
  

  Out of the box you get -
  

  Android Kitkat 4.4.2 (Stock)
  
  11.88 GB free out of designated 16 GB
  
  1.7 GHz Dual core processor (actually Octa-core but the other six are for different
  
  purposes like 4 cores for GPU, 1 core for natural language processing and 1 core for
  
  contextual computing)
  
  2 GB RAM (I like this one most, because my HTC lagged like anything)
  
  4.7 inch 720p HD AMOLED display
  
  and other tech stuff you can read about, elsewhere.
  

  Touchless Control
  
  I like the touchless control of OK Google now which I set up as soon as I got the
  
  phone and works almost all times, to be honest. But it needs to be improved to
  
  understand and perform activities. As of now, its a good idea and nice execution. The way it listens to YOU only is a nice touch.
  

  Active display
  
  This is a nice, discrete and battery friendly way of telling the user of any notifications.
  
  I like it :)
  

  Twist to camera
  
  Another fast feature and a handy one. Takes lesser time than actually unlocking the phone and tapping the camera icon. They could have just put a dedicated camera button ;)
  

  Stock Android
  
  Beautiful OS in itself. Love it for that. Hate those customised bloatwares that
  
  samsung, htc, sony etc put on their devices.
  

  Spotlight Stories
  
  I like the Moto Spotlight Stories a lot. Its such an innovative way to showing
  
  animation making use of the gyro sensors. Two thumbs up for the idea and the
  
  execution.
  

  Voice clarity is very clear on both ends of the call. Speaker and mic are nice.
  

  The phone is buttery smooth and zipping fast. Multitasking is no issue.
  

  The above make it a innovative and practical phone. A lovely one at that.
  

  The Phone is too beautiful for me to want to put a cover on top of it. It would just ruin
  
  the look. Maybe that's a con, but in a good way ;).
  

  I am a bit disappointed with the camera and the google play music player which
  
  comes by default with the phone. Interestingly these were two good things with my
  
  last phone. In HTC one V, the camera was an outperformer given its 5MP sensor and
  
  it had beats audio enhancement. It used to work great with my Skullcandy
  
  headphones. Good thing is this phone also supports my existing headphones but the
  
  sound quality is somewhat lesser. Perhaps if I use different apps for it, then the two
  
  might improve. I am exploring the phone everyday. So if I come across any other
  
  flaws, I'd let you know.
  

  Epilogue
  

  You will love this phone. Once you hold it, you won't 'like' it for the high end specs (it
  
  doesn't have them but runs excellently). But you would like the phone for being
  
  itself. It has an identity to it which you admire. You feel like its made for you!

  1. superb amoled display ( easy on the eyes and pictures look beautiful )
  
  2. Very good camera with the clear pixel technology which gives good photos in low light

  4. The dedicated chip for gestures like flip to open camera, turning on the active display when you take the phone in your hand all without compromising on battery thanks once again to a dedicated chip.
  
  5. Active display which displays alerts lighting up only the pixels which are required ( only possible on amoled displays )
  
  6. Moto assist which helps you listen to and reply to SMS when you are driving. It also blocks calls from non favorite contacts when you sleep. At the same time, it's smart enough to ring if the person calls you more than once within 5 minutes.
  

  All this is done without compromising on the biggest advantage of nexus - fast android updates and stock android experience.
  

  For me, If Moto G is the best value for money smart phone, moto X is the best smart phone that money can buy. I had followed the Moto X right from its inception and always hoped it'd come to India. Thanks to Flipkart for making that happen. I bought this phone for my mom and I'm sure there could haven't been a better choice. The phone itself is a work of art.
  

  Pros:
  
  1) Best of Google (KitKat) with a Moto flourish (Moto Assist and "OK Google Now") right out of the box. Cool features like twist to launch camera, touchless control and active display make it a delight to use.
  
  2) Good build quality, beautiful looks and quite a few color variants. Feels comfortable in the hand.
  
  3) The display is an HD (720p) AMOLED screen. The colors and viewing angles put my Xperia Z to shame. The Gorilla glass is an added advantage.
  
  4) The camera. I don't know why there have been complaints. The Moto X's camera has performed exceptionally well. Again, it put my Xperia Z to shame, especially in the low light area. And the slow motion video is actually splendid. You can launch it even when the phone's locked by twisting the phone and that is a feature that will help convert those "near-miss" moments into good memories.
  
  5) Google has done everyone a favor by not participating in the numbers game. The Moto X is actually a "smart" phone. With dedicated cores for graphics, co-processing and touchless controls, the Moto X does more, and does it better while using less battery.
  

  Cons:
  
  1) The battery drains a tad too fast for my liking, but it's more than enough for my mom.
  
  2) Owing to the speaker's position, you might miss calls and notifications if you place it face up on surfaces like a couch or a bed.
  
  3) No external storage, that's standard with Google phones. But then again, there's enough on board for my mom.
  
  4) No Moto Maker/customization options in India.
  

  The Moto X may not be a spec monster, but it eats up the competition with its features and the value it delivers for money.

Space: You'll get about 11GB+ on this, not 16. (After adding music etc., you will feel the space crunch. Expandable memory would have been a better option, if you like carrying movies/episodes/a lot of music when you travel.)
  

  Looks and Feel: It is very slim, and goes in the pocket comfortably, considering its size (lengthwise). It is very light and doesn't seem to be a bother. At the back there is a dimple/depression at the back, which is well placed as you can put your finger there and it adds to the comfort of holding the phone while on a call.
  

  RAM: You can actually feel the difference. It is fast and doesn't lag.
  

  Screen: The resolution is great, and it is a pleasure reading articles online, as the font no matter how small or bad, appears crisp.
  

  Camera: For the 10MP that is boasts, the camera is infact a let down. Especially in lower light conditions. So if you are a shutterbug, I wouldn't suggest this phone. Try Sony or Samsung for that.
  
  It is HDR capable, and well you can see the difference in that.
  
  An added bonus- which I personally am fond of - adds to the convenience and UI - double twist to access the camera even when the phone is locked. You don't have to unlock the phone and then access the camera, and can save that additional step.
  

  Call Answering/Ending: There is an option to use the power button as the option to end the call. I prefer this feature, which I enabled in my previous phone as well. But, the downside in this is that if you enable it and take a call, the screen switches off, and thereafter if you want to access the homescreen to take down a note/jot down a number, there is no way to get there. Holding the phone away from your ear/holding it horizontally while on the call doesn't make the screen light up and give you access to the homescreen. You can't press the power button because then the call will end. A way around was to double twist, turn on the camera and then access the homescreen, which is basically a highly stupid and redundant way to access it.
  
  Also, there is no inbuilt option for vibrate on call connect. That feature is neat and useful. My previous phone had that inbuilt. But the new Android OS doesn't have it loaded.
  

  Apps: There are a few useless apps that are preloaded. MotoMigrate was not compatible with my phone. Although it is a good app, but it was of no use for me.
  

  Speakers: Not very impressive.
  

  Headphones: It comes with a pair of super lousy Moto headphones, which keep popping out of the ears. I use a pair of Samsung stock in ear headphones. Moto headphones are not in-ear ones.
  

  Charger: The charger comes with two USB ports, which is a blessing. However, within the first month my charger is busted. It doesn't charge the phone beyond 67% even after leaving it overnight. Using the USB cable directly via a USM extension box/computer the phone does get charged to a 100%
  

  Battery: Will last you for the day. My wi-fi is on 24x7, calls are minimal, lot of texting, few games, surfing the internet, and listening to music. Since 0800 hrs to 2100hrs - still have 57% juice left in it - minimal usage.
  

  Hanging: It has happened 2-3 times so far that while getting a call the phone hangs and you can't swipe to receive the call.
  

  Play Music: I added songs in the music folder - but here is the deal. You use the PlayMusic (Google) App, go to the library and select the artist that you want - but it will play all the songs in your library no matter which artist you selected.
  
  Therefore if you want to play songs only by one artist - I think - you need to make separate folders while copying songs. This is an unnecessary hassle. I never had this problem with my earlier devices, not even an issue in the old non-android based phones.
  

  Ringtones: Unlike other devices where you can directly make a song that is in your music library as a ringtone - you need to specifically copy that file in your ringtones folder to make it an option for a ringtone. Pretty idiotic.
  

  File Manager: In dire need of a file managing app. It is quite a pain to transfer files from one place to another - the only way is doing it manually through the computer.
  

  These are just little things that can irritate a person.
  

  The phone for my overall usage is perfect and quite the charm. Emails, text messages, Facebook, Skype, music, reading - these are most of the things that I require the phone for.
  

  Lastly, I have noticed that when you make calls, with some devices, the sound is weird, as though you are in a closed room. The sound is crystal clear, but it only happens with few handsets - Sony Xperia C, iPhone.
  
  Doesn't happen on Nexus, Samsung S2 and Note 2.

  2)Motorola Assist: This is another handy feature. Motorola assist has three modes Namely Driving, Sleep and meeting.
  

  The Driving Mode is automatically activated wen u start driving. In driving mode it can read text messages and also names of caller wen u receive a call or message. You can choose to reply to call or message using voice commands. If you are not able pick up a call it will prompt you to send a message using your voice or it will send a pre-typed message to caller.
  

  It can also play song automatically whe you start driving. But that feature is not working properly. i have notified motorola on this and they said they are working on an update that will solve this problem.
  

  Meeting and Sleeping mode are almost same. they dont allow calls or message during that period. It can scan your calendar for appointments and meetings and automatically go in meeting mode for those timings. You can also alllow calls from your favorite caller or pick up calls from some one who has called more than twice.
  

  3) Amazing Battery: Now this is one of the greatest plus point of thus handset atleast for me. Unlike other high end smart phones, Moto X's Battery lasts an entire day. column6: Wonderful phone! The always on voice detection adds a fantastic level of usability
column7:
I bought this phone on the launch date and received it well in time. Great consistency with delivery timing by flipkart. There has been lots that people have mentioned about this phone so I will just give my ratings based on the criteria that mattered to me the most.
  

  Hardware (Tech specs) - 4/5
  
  The X8 processor does take a hit on synthetic tests but in real world usage I have to yet see it lag on anything. For most people this won't be an issue but for people who must have a "quad core" driven phone. The phone loses a point for not using a mainstream processor and gains half a point because the dedicated cores for context awareness and language processing are awesome. All other hardware is pretty standard for a phone in this price range. Would have liked an expandable slot for microsd though that can be mitigated to an extent with USB OTG.
  

  Display - 4/5
  
  The 720p resolution is good enough for the screen size so the ppi is quite good. Again loses a point for not being full HD but I understand it was done to cut down on battery usage.
  

  Usability - 5/5
  
  Would have given 6/5 for this one. The language recognition is quite spot on even when dictating messages and emails. For people who drive cars for long commutes, this is actually a godsend. The context awareness picks up that you are driving and decides to read out all messages, emails and calls. Also allows you to take calls or read messages using purely voice commands. The context awareness works exactly as advertised and was the main reason I went for this phone. Best of all you can simply dictate your emails while driving without having to take your eyes off the road.
  

  Camera - 4/5
  
  Not the greatest camera out there but fairly good for some basic clicking. I wouldn't use a camera phone for any hardcore photography any way. However, the camera is pretty decent for shots in good light. The shots in low light conditions with the flash were fair but nothing great. The slow motion camera option is a nice touch.
  

  Sound Quality 4/5
  
  I am not exactly an audiophile but I did use a sony ericsson for a few years which has skewed my perception of good sound. The speaker is pretty good and loud. I just found that on melodic music, the speaker seemed a little harsh. All in all not bad sound though. Maybe I should try it with my entire Yanni collection :)
  

  Connectivity - 5/5
  
  I get decent speed on the wireless as well as 3G, however I didn't find too many places in Pune where I got a good 3G connection. That might be due to the service provider (IDEA) though. The places where the connection was good, I was able to download at pretty good speeds.
  

  Conclusion
  
  All in all a very decent phone for the price charged. Would I like it if it were priced lower, well of course I would but even at this price range it is pretty decent. I have colleagues who use the Galaxy S4, Nokia 1320, Nexus 5 as well as the Samsung Note 2 and I have yet to see too much of a difference in performance as a user. If Google Now allowed for full control of a device through voice commands, this phone would meet its true potential. As it is, it is still a very useful phone and a must buy for people who drive 4 wheelers.

column6: A phone you will fall in love with... an unbiased review
column7:
Well, I am not gonna talk about the product specs or features, as I am sure that like me, you would have spent enough time reading the reviews on other websites. Instead am going to tell you things that usually do not come up in forums or reviews, and will share my experience in the past two weeks hoping it will help someone to take an informed decision.
  

  I placed my order for the Moto X on the day of the launch, and in true Flipkart style I received the item the very next day. No complaints there.
  

  Now, before I placed my order, I was in a dilemma to choose between Xperia ZR and Moto X.  Xperia ZR had a slightly bigger replaceable battery, with SD card slot and it claimed to be water resistant as well. However, the sheer number of positive reviews I read about the Moto X, tipped me in its favor and I can proudly say, am not disappointed with my decision.
  

  So, as I was saying, I received my product the next day. The packaging was quite alright and came with the printed invoice. The phone comes with a SIM insert tool, cheap looking charger and an even cheaper looking pair of earphones. The first thing you need to do is throw away these earphones and get a pair of Sennheisers (don't blame Moto, no phones come with a good pair of bundled earphones).
  

  Once you turn on the phone, everything is pure magic. The UI is smooth and beautiful. Connectivity is nice. It hardly takes any time to lock on to a network or WIFI. The phone required a nano SIM for which I had to visit my nearby Vodafone showroom. I got the SIM in 15 mins and the connection in another 30 mins. SIM insertion is also quite simple with the tool that comes with the pack.
  

  PROS
  
  Now what I like about the phone is the active display feature which is quite handy. I have stopped turning on my phone unnecessarily just to check for new messages or alerts. In love.
  

  The next big feature is the Touchless control. At first I was a little apprehensive whether the phone would be able to recognize an Indian accent. But, it works like a charm (if you are clear enough) and I had fun showing off my Tony Stark skills my friends. Feels kind of nice to know that there is someone always listening to you. Falling deeper in love.
  

  Good to watch movies and browsing is real smooth as there is minimal lag in opening web pages.
  

  CONS
  
  The biggest drawback is that, put of the 16GB internal memory, you only gets to use around 11GB. This is not good if you got a lot of music, games and movies on your phone. I however can live with it cos I only got around 5GB of songs and I don't play games on my phone.
  

  Do you remember the Moto X campaign in the US. It used to proudly announce that the Moto X is the only smart phone assembled in USA. However, the phone you get in India is assembled in China (It's clearly state on the back). A real BUMMER
  

  I observed a drastic loss in battery life in the past few days, because of the Android OS. I checked the web, and it seems to be a key problem plaguing all KitKat phones. Hence I had to do a factory reset to sort it out. Sadly, since there is no external memory, I lost all my music and data with the factory reset. Also, I feel that the phone gets slightly heated up during charging.
  


  So, as a verdict I will say it is not the fastest or the biggest phone in the market. It has its downside, but well, what phone hasn't. But if you are willing to ignore the small glitches, then it is a phone which you will fall in love with. Everything from its thin form factor to the smooth finish oozes charm. I just hope it stays that way, cos the service capabilities of the brand in India are not something I am sure of.
  

  AND REMEMBER PEOPLE, NO MATTER WHICH PHONE YOU BUY ALWAYS USE A SCREEN GUARD. THE GLASSES MAY BE SCRATCH RESISTANT BUT NOT SHATTER PROOF.

column6: Moto X - Why, with its pros and cons, its Value for Money!
column7:
PROS: Came with latest Android v4.4.2, 2GB RAM & within 66mm width - my preferred width for one-hand operability which makes it fabulous to hold and operate - Motorola managed to get a 4.7" screen in this frame. Amazing feat!  CALL + SPEAKERPHONE quality is neat. BUILD quality is excellent although I am using Pudini Rose Brown Case Cover to avoid scratches on back cover - chose original device as an all around black for this reason. FUNCTIONING is smooth albeit after some 'inaugural' hiccups - nothing a simple on-n-off couldn't solve. PRICING is satisfactory because this device has outshined or come close to giving a befitting performance when pitted against high-end spec'd devices from Samsung/HTC. So it is wallet-friendly and shouldn't be construed as a costly device IMO. INTERNET: 2G works well.
  

  CONS: TRANSFERRING Contacts from Motorola Defy was a huge task - Motorola Migrate did a bad job wherein all my device nos remained in the device and few SIM Nos that got thru' had lost their defined characteristics. It took me a good ten days to get all my Contacts alphabet-wise from old device to X as I did not want all synched to gmail. Why can't I simply BULK transfer all (Device + SIM) Contacts manually using two Android devices - old to new - without having to suffer so much. C'mon Google you must refine Migrate. It is useless. I started using my device a good 10/12 days after I got delivery for Google's flawed transfer mechanism. BATTERY LIFE i.e., battery-life on one-time charge till it goes below 30% - is not living upto the earlier v4.4.2 standards and is a major let down. Several reviews/forums seem to point to this version being responsible for the downgrade in battery life. There is an update to v4.4.3 that may offset this negative. We just need to wait n watch if and when Moto X would get treated to this update to hopefully curb the battery life problem. I definitely want more from my Moto X's battery. NO GOOGLE TALK WIDGET: I hesitate to join Google + but it seems I have to join G+ to be on Hangouts - as of now shoddy app that is trying to shift users from Google Talk + sms to this. Big Downer. I think Google should rethink on bring back Google Talk Widget - it was very convenient and I did not need to join another social platform for using this. SMS: Since I am not on Hangouts, I use regular SMS service which thankfully is still there. However, when I tried to insert a contact's number, I couldn't get around to doing that which I could easily do on my previous v2.2 device (Moto Defy) and I feel SMS needs to be revamped. The "forward" function does not work on SMS on this device. Keep SMS & TALK outside the purview of Hangouts is what I am trying to get Google technical team to consider. Incidentally, now the Hangouts App doesn't open either which doesn't bother me. Hangouts = Hangups, IMO..lol!
  

  Having said the above, I am going to make time to fully acclimatise myself with the "real" experience of the Moto X = Touchless Control, Motorola Assist & few others which do not even figure within the so-called high-end device costing upwards of 40K.
  

  Google needs to work on the above cons and not make users forcefully comply with caveats like the compulsory signing up for services like G+ just to chat (GoogleTalk) or sms .. seems very fishy and perhaps snoopy and ofcourse immediately focus on fixing the battery life issue thru' next update.
  

  But, overall am very happy with the device (the cons above relate mostly to the operating system and not the device) and definitely recommend buying this middle-tier-priced yet high-end-device competitor of a device. In short, its a device with talent & character and whoever buys this will not regret buying it cuz this device will remain technologically relevant for a good couple of years more. Rate = 7.75/10 (3 & half stars) .. fix 'cons' mentioned above and this device will get a 9.9/10. For the price, however, its unbeatable. Go for it!

I've been using the Moto X for over an year now. This device by specs is not a monster when compared to other flagships. But as an every day average user, it works perfectly for me. I had to make a decision between the Nexus 5 and the Moto X. and because I spend a lot of time outdoors and is connected Mobile data than WiFi, I chose the Moto X because it comes with an amoled display. And Motorola features like Active Display and and Moto voice, once you get used to it no phones can satisfy you later.
  

  The phone has a 4.7 inch 720p amoled display. Its not big but for me it does the job, its small enough for one-hand operation and fits in pocket. You hardly even notice it in pocket.
  

  It comes with a 2200 mah battery. Even though the battery seems so small, with the amoled display you'll get a whole day with it. Not the greatest on battery phones but it gets the job done.
  

  The camera is okay, it wasn't that great. The rear camera gave soft images even though colours were accurate. In low light lots of grain. And the front camera is okay in normal defused lighting. It tends to over expose and wash out everything on very sunny conditions. I wouldn't recommend this camera if you take selfies on a beach.
  

  10 mega pixel rear camera with 1080p HD video recording

  1.7GHz Dual-Core Krait CPU

I purchased this product on day 1 and Flipkart took 4 days to deliver it to Bangalore from Chennai. Not sure what was the reason for this delay especially when competitors are delivering goods within 24 hours.
  

  I have been using this product for almost a week now. This is my third Motorola phone. I have used Motorola photon and Motorola razr max before this. Both were solid phones and I expected the same experience from play when I ordered the phone.
  

  Here are my thoughts about Motorola play -
  

  Build quality: - Superb in one word. While it may not have metal around it, it feels solid in hand. The quality of fiber used feels excellent and the back cover is innovatively designed so that there is a good grip. The phone has the right weight and feels just right to hold.
  

  Display: - The HD display is the best part of the phone. I was wondering whether 400  ppi would feel cheap on a 5.5 screen but I was wrong. I was blown away when I switched on the screen. It is one of the best screen out there in the market (although it is not quad hd) however, it is perfectly wise decision by Motorola to use a HD display and keep the cost down. You would not notice the difference between a quad hd and hd display on a 5.5 inch screen (you will probably not notice it on a 32 inch screen as well). The display has warmth to it and that make the pictures and videos looks natural. I was using a 5.2 display phone before this and 5.5 inch display does not feel very big.
  

  Call quality:- With Motorola, you do not have to worry about call quality and the phone does not disappoint. The calls quality is loud and clear.
  

  Battery:- I have not yet felt the power of 3600 mah battery as I am using the phone most of the time. The HD display and not so power thirsty processor should easily last for two days.
  

  Connectivity:-  No signal lost and internet access works like a charm with airtel 4g.
  

  Earphones:- Nothing here, look elsewhere.
  

  Charger:- The phone takes quite a long time to charge. I am waiting for Motorola to release the turbo charger.
  

  Camera:- The best that Motorola has offered till date however do not compare it with Samsung galaxy S6 or LG G4. The pictures have lots and lots of details and the 21 megapixel helps here. In lowlight the pictures may feel washed out due to lack of contrast and saturation however, I solved the problem by downloading another camera app from Google store. In bright sunlight, the pictures come out very clean and have good contrast punch.
  

  Overall, I give weightage to the overall phone experience over the  specifications and I am extremely happy with my purchase. Hopefully the love will last long.

column6: Good Phone! But missing some features...
column7:
This phone is very strong on specs. Good Full HD screen, good processor, decent RAM, 21 megapixel camera, big battery etc. The dual 4G SIM and 128 GB microSD is really good to have.
  

  Not having IR sensors or OIS can be excused. However, Motorola chose to leave out some important sensors such as gyroscope that is available in Moto G and other lower models. This means that you cannot use it with the Google Cardboard app for Virtual Reality. Hence the one star less.
  

  The camera takes great pictures with excellent colors, especially when there is good light. The details are good when you try to zoom in. Since there is no optical image stabilisation, and due to the fact that you are asked to touch anywhere on the screen to take pictures, you may end up with some shaky pictures. But as you use it, you tend to get better at shooting without the shake. There are not many settings, but in one way it is good that you don't have many controls to worry about. The flash is quite bright and can be distracting to the person being photographed. Though the photo comes out clear in flash light, the white balance is not that great and the skin tones looks a bit washed out. You may need to experiment a little for good low-light photographs.
  

  With the include camera app video is limited to 1080p @ 30fps or 540p slow motion. 1080p would create bigger file sizes. Install an app such as Open Camera to support more sizes and get more control. If you intend to shoot a lot of videos invest in a 64GB (~1.5K) or 128GB microSD. Keeping the screen pressed results in a burst mode of multiple images shot in quick succession.
  

  The sound is surprisingly loud and clear though it is only one speaker (not stereo). It also has an FM Radio option. The headphone socket was too tight even for the basic headphone supplied with the box.
  

  The Lollipop OS has been retained as such and Motorola has not tried to customize or add any bloatware, which is really great. There are only a couple of Non-Google apps - Moto Assist & Flipkart.
  

  The battery is big, but the screen and processor too are big and hence consume more power. It easily lasts more than a day with moderate usage and good phone reception. Here are a few ways to improve battery time - Change the wallpaper to black or dark color; Don't install too many apps, especially those that keep running in the background. Keep the screen brightness lower.
  

  The Moto Assist feature is cool. You can record any term to wake up your phone when it is away and then it will be ready to answer any question you may have.
  
  I have not come across any heating issue, even with many apps open. I don't play heavy games, so I don't know if that causes any heating.
  
  The phone front face looks symmetrical, above and below the screen. So you may pick up the phone upside down.
  

  The Moto Migrate tool makes copying your contacts, call logs and media from your old phone to the new one over WiFi so easy.
  

  There is a shortage of good accessories for this phone. The turbo charger, good flip case etc. are difficult to get or too expensive. I managed to get a pudini case after some hunting. Back covers seem to be redily available though.
  

  Overall it is a great phone for the price but with some key features missing. Whether you will like the phone, depends on what phone you are migrating from and the expectations you have set for the new phone. Ask yourself if you can live without features like OIS, IR, Fingerprint, Gyroscope etc. for now and in future. If you can, go for this phone.

Unlike, perhaps, other reviewers here, I am not wont to get blown away by phone specs and performance: I simply want a stable, good phone which works well and gives me minimum hiccups because I tend to be busy. Android is a stable and easy software; the X Play seemed like a good bet.
  

  About a week after I purchased this phone, my SD Card suddenly stopped being read. Despite frenetic efforts, nothing worked. I assumed it was a corrupt SD Card, so I replaced it. Said Replacement worked for about a month. My SD Card stopped reading again, so I went to the service centre in Delhi at the recommendation of a particularly unhelpful Moto representative. The Service Centre was rude and discourteous, immediately telling me that my phone would be reset and kept for a week without even examining the problem. I am a working professional, so this caused me great inconvenience and they had my phone for 5 days. In the meantime, I had to manage with nothing but a landline and a PC which is clearly NOT ideal for a business professional. I received my phone with the problem 'fixed'. 2 Weeks later the issue came up again, and a truly inept and idiotic service representative told me to 'bhijit nearest sarvis center' and get a job sheet yet again. He paid no heed to my issue that I live far away and am to busy to go visiting a service centre repeatedly. Besides, the service centre is not ready to offer me a replacement despite the phone being in otherwise perfect condition. Like I said above, I want a no- fuss, efficient and fast phone. If I have to keep going to a service centre because of a MEMORY CARD issue, and no Motorola Representative has the courtesy or the skill to offer me any sort of long- lasting solution, I'm not going to keep grovelling.
  

  Horrendous service from Motorola and despite the phone itself being okay, this sort of lazy, rude service which presumes that I have all the time in the world to keep servicing my phone will simply not cut it. Very disappointed. Understandably for many readers Service may not be a criterion for avoiding a phone, but well if the same inconvenience accrues to any further buyers I would feel truly sympathetic for them.

column6: A good phone for business purpose and basic entertainment.
column7:
This is my review about MOTO X PLAY. It has been more than a week of heavy usage. This phone was suggested by my friend so thanks to him and I bought it for a very good deal on flipkart. Please note that I don't play games but I use phone quite frequently in a day for other purposes. So my review is based on that.
  

  The pros are:-
  
  1. The phone has a great 5.5 inch display with very good viewing angles.
  
  2. The body is made of plastic frame with a gloss metal look (don't know how long the gloss look is going to last without a back cover, hope it doesn't!), at the back it has a stylish rugged rubber kind off finish, which gives a new look to the phone and a good grip as well.
  
  3. I have to mention about the music experience in this phone, if right headphone is used this phone gives a beautiful sound with an awesome bass thump (I use sony xb30ex). The default headphone which comes along with the pack is for basic use. Also, it has a mono speaker which is loud and clear.
  
  4. Battery is quite appreciable. After heavy usage, with display on, continuous texting, watching videos etc. the mobile lasted for 12-13 hours and with normal usage the battery back-up stayed more than a day. But, while listening to music and when screen was off the battery drain was minimal.
  
  5. The front and rear camera are good in good lighting and average in low lighting. I am more impressed with the front cam than the rear in this phone; it takes very good selfies.
  
  6. The call clarity is very good and I had no issues with mobile network reception or Wi-fi.
  

  CONS:
  
  1. For few apps the phone lagged frequently for some reason. Could be because of processor or RAM. I thought with 2GB RAM and octa-core processor, the phone shouldn't lag at all, but it does! when I checked for RAM usage, the system was consuming nearly 30-35 percent of RAM, basic apps consumed another 30-35 percent, which left 700-800 MB of free RAM. So, I had to uninstall and disable few apps for better performance. I hope this issue gets resolved in the next update (marshmallow).
  
  2. The phone is quiet heavy, could be because of the battery, but that's not a major problem.
  
  3. Free internal storage memory in the phone is only 8GB, which is only 50 percent of total space. That's quiet disappointing as an external memory has to be used for heavy data storage.

column6: Moto X Play v/s Moto G3 v/s Lenovo K3 Note
column7:
I have both Moto G3 and Moto X Play and explored Lenovo K3 Note with my colleagues. Here is the comparison between all three:
  

  Form Factor and Build Quality:
  
  Build Quality of Moto phones are definitely better than Lenovo K3 Note. However, I found the back cover of Moto G3 does not fit properly around the camera. Lenovo K3 Note back cover looks very delicate.
  
  Moto X Play has the best Form Factor but it's due to absence of any hard/capacitive buttons. Moto X Play is slightly taller in size than Moto G3 due to its good screen to body ratio.  Major concern: Moto X Play Power button wobbles and feels very delicate.
  
  I did not go for Lenovo K3 note is due to poor back cover and absence of Gorilla glass.
  

  Display:
  
  I opted for Moto X Play over Moto G3 for its FHD display. Yes, clarity and brightness are very good. However, I don't even get to see even one additional line of content whereas I get to see at least 5 additional lines of content in Lenovo K3 Note. I understand some space is lost due to it onscreen buttons. But, I really wonder, whether Moto X Play really has FHD display???
  

  Battery:
  
  Battery is better but not great. Quick Charge 2.0 certified Moto charger could have complemented but is neither included nor available. Third party chargers available, if any, are priced over 2K.
  

  Features:
  
  Moto Assist is good but I can't set the driving and meeting modes manually. I understand no software can detect driving in bumper to bumper traffic but this is when I want to set driving mode and get the benefit of voice commands. Same is with unscheduled meetings which will not be in any calendars!  Missing: File Explorer that works offline.
  

  Price:
  
  While Moto G3 and Lenovo K3 Note are priced almost same in other countries, Moto X Play seems to have been priced to much lower in India. However, I feel Moto X Play is overpriced compared to competition, Indian context and could have been priced in the range of 15K to 17K.

column6: A modest phone that lasts the day
column7:
Having used it for almost a week, I can say that its an unremarkable phone with no major pros or cons. Those WOW reviews seem exaggerated.
  

  Its got a decent battery backup, last the whole day. With two SIMs, 30 mins of voice calls and GPRS ON when not on wifi, it last around 16 - 18 hours. The single SIM version, of which there were rave reviews for the battery life, is not the one we got.
  

  Heating, yes it gets hot, won't feel good in the pocket in the summers, until then, can live with it.
  

  GPS, locks on with decent accuracy. 2G data, works fine. Camera, good in good light, bad in low light. Flash is pretty decent at close range. Web browsing, not really as fast as we would want, but thats OK. Voice quality is passable.
  

  The build is deceptive as the sides are not metal but plastic, and until the paint flakes away or the device falls, no one will be the wiser.
  

  Would have loved to have back covers for variety and for when the original gets scratched.
  

  Finally, Moto Voice, it wakes up for no reason, without the programmed phrase, and definitely leads to battery drain. Noise is usually enough to trigger it.
  

  Somehow, 20K for extra 16GB and 7 useless megapixels and a 10% extra battery capacity is starting to feel like a waste. Maybe K3 Note would have sufficed, but whats done is done. Keeping it at least for a year.

I am writing this review after using the Moto X Play for about 3 weeks and carefully treading all the facets of daily use. Bought this after exchanging my Moto X 1st gen from Flipkart and was impressed by their quick delivery. This review is based on the Marshmallow update on the Moto X play
  

  Design : Simple rugged plastic design, a direct consequence of cost cutting. Nothing to complain at this price but the power and volume buttons feels cheap and flimsy. The rounded back with the textured plastic and the weight distribution provides a very good grip and does not feel like the phone will slip through the hands. Clever engineering to have a single slot for SIM(2 SIM card in fact) tray and SD card
  

  Display : 5.5 inch IPS LCD display with a resolution of 1080p is one of the best screens out there at this mid range phone. Motorola strangely decided to move away from the AMOLED screen to LCD which would be more beneficial for their Moto Display feature. But the brightness of the display is spot on and outdoor visibility is not a problem.
  

  Processor and Memory : Snapdragon 615 has always been a notorious chipset for lagging and heating issue. But in this phone it simply flies with Marshmallow. Although RAM is limited to 2GB but havn't seen the phone crossing 1.6 GB with normal heavy use. Heating issue was reported in a couple of reviews but I have not seen anything alarming so far. Maybe the Marshmallow update fixed it.
  

  Software : This is where Motorola excels at least as of now. Marshmallow already on board and its stock android. No bloatware and Motorola additions are the necessary additions.
  
  Touchless Voice control works effortlessly and was one of the best features of this phone.
  
  Moto Display works equally fine but the Amoled display would have helped in conserving a bit more of the battery.
  

  Camera : Always a weak point for Motorola, this time they have outdone themselves. The 21MP shooter is the best they have ever produced. Sharper images, true color and the auto HDR mode works fine. Low light photography still has a lot to be desired but this is simply a phone camera not a DSLR. For casual photography and social media sharing there is nothing to complain about. The camera does not support 4K recording but it doesn't matter to me
  

  Battery : If there was one feature that is the USP of this device then this is it. Massive 3630 mah battery which can easily last 1.5 days with heavy use. Add on top of that Marshmallow's doze mode and what you have is simply impressive battery life. It supports turbo charging but Motorola is not providing the turbocharger. The normal charger takes a long time to charge the battery though. I bought a Aukey Qualcomm 2.0 certified fast charger and its working seamlessly.
  

  So to sum it up it's probably the best phone under 20K . Latest software, good camera, brilliant screen and an ever lasting battery - what else do you need at this price.

column6: Phone display flicker issue, but service centre replaced it
column7:
**EDIT** The service centre delivered the phone in a week's time - display and ear receiver replaced free of cost - obviously the person who was at the CSC misinformed me and gave me a week of anxiety. The service was prompt and good. Phone works well now. The reason I bought Motorola in the first place is that they may provide better service than some of the new entrants in the market - they justified my faith.
  
  PHONE REVIEW:
  
  The phone is very good - nice display - bright enough even in sunlight. Good volume - speaker is in the front of the phone - so no need to keep your phone face down! It is loud enough to be heard even in noisy areas. The ear receiver could be a little louder - but certainly good enough in most places.
  
  Phone feels heavy but can be operated with one hand when the need arises. Good grip with the back cover - does not feel slippery at all. Got updated to Marshmallow a few days back. Good battery life - I am easily able to get two days with moderate use. The trick is: charge your new phone fully and drain it fully. Repeat this charge - drain cycle 3 or 4 times so that the phone charging gets calibrated.
  
  Phone performs well, Smooth scrolling, screen transitions, ample storage space with 32GB version. Appreciate the quick response GPS - my earlier Samsung phone took sometime to find the location! Camera is good in daylight. Nearly stock android with very little bloatware.
  
  Now the cons:
  
  There is no double tap to wake the phone. Have to use the power button - The power button does not feel too sturdy! This is not an amoled display and is also not water proof as in other moto models.
  

  ISSUE FACED AND NOW RECTIFIED!
  
  Phone display started flickering just a month after purchase. Initially it was sporadic but by end of two months it got very bad. Further the ear piece stopped working! Took it to motorola service centre - they said the display has to be imported and may take upto two months! They wont give me a standby phone either. Asked them for a replacement which should be quicker - but the customer care people denied. Another problem - when you are typing all of a sudden it will start inputting a particular character repeatedly even without any screen press. The only way to get out of this problem was by pressing the power button to switch off the display and then back on. Very poor quality control on this piece I guess.
  
  This is the reason for not giving the product 5 stars that it deserves! For the price point this is an awesome phone. Totally value for money.

column6: This is a Brilliant phone. Must Buy.
column7:
I am writing this review after using this phone extensively for 30days..Here are some of my initial impressions of this phone :
  
  Pros:
  

  (i) Looks : I don't bother about the measurements in numerical values as they can be deceptive..Hold this phone for once and feel how ergonomically beautiful and comfortable it is in your hands!! It's textured back panel gives it a classy look..Even after having a 5.5 inch screen and weighing 169 grams it doesn't feel that big nor that bulky..One hand operation is entirely possible with this 5.5 inch phablet..
  

  (ii) Screen : I really find it amusing when people say "Why Moto X doesn't have 2K screen?" I challenge them to show a single pixel on the screen and I would lose my Moto X Play to them..Again, I request don't go by number games, see the quality..Screen is perfect..IPS LCD screen may not be as bright or as vibrant as AMOLED, but it does has it's own merits..Colours look natural..Black is perfectly black and white also appears natural..Readability under direct sunlight is good..
  

  (iii) Call Quality : I won't write much in this regard..With any smartphone in this range you will definitely get good call quality and Moto X Play is not an exception..
  

  (iv) Speaker Volume : It has a single firing speaker on the front..Don't expect it to perform like Home Theaters.. For all practical purposes it's sound is loud and clear..
  

  (v) Performance : Hmmmm...I have seen many "REVIEWS" lambasting Moto X Play for having SD 615 chip set and "just" 2 GB of RAM..I really find it funny when people start giving specifications much more value compared to real world experience..There may be tens of phones providing better specifications at this price range, but the performance which you get from this phone is just awesome..I am not saying that it is the best performing smartphone, but for a smartphone under 25K, it performs more than enough..I have installed as many as 23-24 applications including some high end games, but the phone has yet to show even a slightest hint lag..I played Real Racing 3 with almost 20 applications running in background (I did it purposefully to check the phone's capability) and the experience was buttery smooth..
  
  After prolonged use, it gets warm but heated?? Hell NO!!!
  

  (vi) Camera : Camera interface is simple..It doesn't have a long list of controls..But it is rather helpful for ameture like me who doesn't get confused between hundreds of options while taking a snapshot..
  
  Rear facing 21MP camera doesn't need any review..It is really a very good camera producing very true colours and great details..However OIS would have made it even better..But surely the phone has best camera for below 30K range smartphones..
  
  Front facing 5MP camera also take great snaps..It has a unique technology that screen gets lit up while taking selfie in low light..It makes selfies better than other 5MP front cameras like that on Lumia 730..
  

  (vii) Battery : I won't comment much on this aspect as of now as I am still exploring it..However I found on moderate usage it can easily give 36 Hours backup..
  

  (viii) Software Updates : Being a Motorola phone one can be sure of timely software updates..Android Marshmallow will be there for Moto X Play as early as December this year.Just compare this with any Samsung or Chinese brands like Xiaomi, Asus etc..
  

  (ix) Touch less Control : Unique feature of Moto X series and Moto X Play is no exception..It may seem like a "not so useful" feature, but it really makes smartphone smart..Use it to feel it..
  

  Cons: Not many to say..Just OIS in rear facing camera would have made it even better..
  

  Conclusion : A large, bright beautiful screen, ergonomic design, excellent camera, smooth performance, good battery backup and timely software update makes this phone as a Complete Smartphone..If one is really wishing to have a smart experience of a smartphone under 30K, Moto X Play is certainly the best choice..

  7) Its pure Android by google, which comes without any bloatwares. So it will better the performance of your mobile.

I had ordered this phone on 11th October and received it on 15th October. The packaging was excellent.

  1) This device looks way better in real life than it does online. The phone may look as heavy but is perfect (does not feel very light though). The phone also does feel a bit thinner as the edges are curved. Overall, it is a perfect & grippy device to hold.
  
  2) FHD screen is a good one and adequately reproduces colors. I haven't seen any 2K screen physically, but this one is enough to impress.

  6) The camera does an very excellent job in daylight and well lit interiors.
  
  7) The Migrate application is really helpful. It completely cloned all the data from my old handset to this one with just a couple of clicks! :)
  
  Now, the cons:
  

  1) This phone DOES heat up. With continuous gaming/ video streaming in wifi, this phone gets heated up. But it is manageable and is not 'untouchable' hot. Anyways, nobody would like this when using their new phone for its first time.
  
  2) Though this phone has a huge battery, the performance is not as one would expect. As like other good phones, it lasts one full business day and a little bit more but not more than that. Nothing to complain about except the ad stating the 48 hours usage time.
  
  3) As we are talking about the battery, this phone takes a really long time to charge. For most of the users, fast charger is a necessary upgrade.
  
  4) I would not comment about the indoor camera capabilities of this phone. It is just a con and nothing else.
  
  Looking at the price and the features of this device, it was well known to us that somewhere this phone would lack in order to cope up, but this device does a fair job in removing that fear. A perfect device with a perfect price I would say!!
