column6: A decent phone under Rs 17000 price tag.
column7:
Here is my review after 5 days of experience with Moto X Play:
  

  Cons:
  
  1. The phone has a only 'SINGLE SIM' tray for its dual sim option and that also include memory card in it. So whenever you want to remove any one of three (MMC, SIM1 or SIM2) you will require to remove all three.
  

  2 To top the first CON, the tray created a dependency on the pin that is shipped in  box. So to remove the tray, you will have to carry the pin with you always. Other wise you will not be able to remove any one of it. This was not the case in any of my previous smartphones.
  

  3. The Phone does not have internal phone storage for contacts. So all contacts are stored into your Android (G-Mail) account. Strange!!!! Anyways that's the feature of STOCK android.
  

  4. The phone comes with NON removable battery. This means the old school solution of removing the battery whenever the phone hung or other during other problem won't work here.
  

  5. The Headset supplied inBox is of normal quality. At the price tag of almost 18000, I expect a good quality headphone.
  

  Pros:
  
  1.Battery: The ultimate and awesome feature of MOTO X play: 3630 mAh battery, that is really a beast in the world of smartphone.
  
  In these 5 days I have only charged twice with moderate usage.
  

  Standby: From the day of first charge, I didn't use much and with standby, it gave me more than 42 hrs of battery backup, with low brightness, NO WIFI connected, only one sim inserted and no games.
  

  Normal use: With second charge, it gave me 30-32 hrs of battery backup, where I used to connect Wifi start and end of the day, watched Youtube, played games, surfed internet and some calls etc.
  

  Heavy usage: I have not used heavily but expect it to give atleast 24 hrs of battery backup.
  

  The phone does not heats much, though I feared for octa core processer and with other people giving review that it touches 45 degree cel.
  
  With heavy use, it is obvious, it will heat up and I expect it with further experience, but for moderate user like me, it did not cross 37 deg cel with maximum usage
  

  2.Camera:
  
  The Rear Camera: (21 MP) is awesome with autofocus works perfectly fine. For me the back camera is a Beast. I could read the text that is far away in the pic. For people loving photography, this phone is a go for them, although there is much available in market (Lumia 1020 - 40 MP) :P
  

  The front Camera: (5 MP) is not much good which gives a good images but not as good in dim light as other phone provides.
  
  This is Sorry for the selfie lovers. But in daylight, it works perfectly fine.
  

  The video quality is also good enough with 21 MP camera. The Camera is also user friendly and with pause option and option to switch of/on shutter sound, it beats samsung smartphones
  

  3.Processor and RAM:
  
  The phone sports Octa core processor with 'Quad-core 1.7 GHz Cortex-A53 & quad-core 1.0 GHz Cortex-A53' and with chipset 'Qualcomm MSM8939 Snapdragon 615' and GPU 'Adreno 405' which gives a awesome performance.
  

  4. Memory:
  
  I bought 16 GB version, which give me 10 GB available internal memory. The Apps consumed around 1.96 GB of space.
  
  After installing some apps and tking some pics, I have 8 GB still available.
  
  I installed 'Cam scanner CPU-Z, ES fileexplorer, M-indicator, messenger, MyAirtel, Naukri APPm OneDrive, SKype and whatsapp and Asphalt'.
  

  The RAM part is bit disappointing, but still manageable:
  

  with 2 GB packed RAM, The system consumes 784 MB and apps consume 500 MB making room for only 600 MB of ram available which is just OK.
  

  5.Display:
  
  With Corning gorilla glass 3 and IPS LCD capacitive touch screen, it feels like a premium phone.
  
  The resolution is also great with 1080x1920 pixels. It is great for movie watching.
  


  Verdict:
  
  At price approx 18000 for people having camera and Battery in priority, this phone is great one.
  
  For heavy gamers, this is phone is a BIG NO.
  
  MOTO can improve a lot with its PROS and CONS to make a great phone
  

  IF the MMC option would be inside phone and not in the tray and removable battery, I would have given 5 stars

column6: Ordered two phones, but unfortunately had to return them
column7:
When I received one of these phones, the packaging which i got was very good and it was at normal temperature. But when i opened it and took the phone it hand.. i could feel the warmness of the phone. As expected the phone doesn't boot up as it would have consumed whole battery juice for this warm up. After 5-10 mins of charge it started showing some symptoms of liveliness.
  
  After charging battery till 5% allowed me to boot it up till then no luck.
  
  So let's look at the pros and cons of the phone (I'll be comparing it w.r.t the price at which I got it @16700Rs)
  

  1.	Build Quality 	: 4.5/5
  
  2.	Display		: 3/5	: Disappointed by the color reproduced by this display even after multiple setting changes
  
  3.	Rear Camera 	: 0/5	: Believe me its not at all 21MP.. its 2.1 MP. Pathetic
  
  4.	Front Camera	: 3/5	: Much much better than rear camera, but the reality is visible when you try video call. Other side fellow will could hardly make out to whom he or she is talking with. I tried comparing the camera performance on same network with Moto X 1st gen and Samsung Galaxy S3/S4 and Moto G3. MOTO X PLAY is nowhere.. in terms of camera performance
  
  5.	GPS		: Didn't work on either phone. It could locate you, but the actual troubling game starts when you surprise to know that it are not navigating at all. After starting a car I faced this surprise and was about to throw this phone.. but couldn't as I had spent 16k on it ?
  
  6.	Battery Life	: 5/5	: Yes you read it right.. it lasts much more beyond the expectation. With 2G/3G + WiFi + Average usage for voice call including Office meeting calls for an hours.. it used to last for minimum of 1.5days to 2 days. Really impressed with it.
  
  7.	Heating		: Except the first time when I felt it is bit warm, I never faced any heating issue even with gaming with 3G active.
  
  8.	Cast Screen	: Random behavior. Sometimes used to freeze or was not able to identify the receiver devices
  
  9.	Audio		: Voice call volume was absolutely okay for initial 2-3 days later started seeing low volume. Make a note.. both the phone suffered in the same way
  

  Conclusion : Just for Build Quality and very high and reliable battery life I cannot live this phone. Hence RETURNED to flipkart where it should be.
  
  Bottom Line: Do check all the functionalities as we want to make use of them regularly. DON'T just do sanity check and get happy.

column6: A Great Experience Spoiled by few important things
column7:
Bought this great phone on Flipkart's Diwali Sale on an exchange offer + cash back and the deal was just awesome. Phone came before promised date.
  

  Now below is my experience till now -
  

  Good Things  
  
  1) Design - Awesome is the word. It's not only sleek but unlike any other phone in the market. Feels good in hand because of curve back and matte finish. Overall nice ergonomics.
  
  2) Software - Pure Stock Android v4.4.4 OS with no stupid layers. Some of the add-on features like gesture phone silent and one tap notification read are awesome. If you have used/experienced Nexus 5 before you will know what I am talking about. It's fuss free and clean.
  
  3) Performance   Throw any application or game and it will play smoothly. Combination of 2GB RAM and 2.5 GHz Processor is awesome for power pack performance.
  

  Sadly don't have much good to write about beyond above. Here are the downsides  
  

  1)	Camera   Sadly for such price range, camera is just about okay. Day photos are good but low light photos are nothing to write about. Video quality is also just decent.
  
  2)	Accessories   Since Motorola is not the most popular brand in current scenario, finding accessories (Back cover, Screen Guards etc.) for this phone at local shops is a nightmare. Eventually had to buy the accessories from an online shopping site where you don't know the exact feel until you get the product on your hand. Also not much options are there in terms of customize covers.
  
  3)	Curved screen   Curve screen looks beautiful at first but you soon get to know the down side once you put a screen guard on it. It comes off too soon. It's only one month I have bought the phone and I have already bought my third screen guard (which also started to come off). This is highly irritating.
  
  4)	No storage expansion   though I knew this before buying the phone and I thought that it won't affect me much but I've started to feel that at least 32GB was necessary to last 2 years gadget life.
  
  5)	Battery   Battery just about lasts 13-14 hours on a heavy usage day (call/internet), if I play games and play video than it might die in 10 hours. Wish it had at least 3000 mAh battery.
  
  6)	Earphones   Moto has shipping highly uncomfortable earphones. They are made of hard plastic and your ear starts to hurt in few minutes of use.
  
  7)	Issue with microphone   This is the biggest spoiler. I don't know if this is particular to my handset but strangely in between the calls the person on opposite end complaints that they can't hear me at all. It's happening pretty frequently now and it's getting very irritating. I am willing for forgo all of above negatives but not the call quality. In fact Moto is boasting about how they have improved the call quality in this one. But sadly I am facing the opposite. What is strange that there are lots of users around the globe who are complaining about this call quality in various forums. If this problem persists I might have to take my phone to service center within 1 months of purchase which will be a shame. Rating the product low only because of this issue.
  

  All in all I was happy with the product until the voice problem surfaced. Hope it gets rectified by the service center. Otherwise I am quite satisfied with the phone and its performance.

column6: Reviewing after two weeks of use
column7:
I have bought this phone as soon as it was available on the market. This is my third android phone. My two previous phone were Moto Defy+ and Nexus 5. I have to move out of nexus because of the unusual hardware fault. Defy+ ran 3 years without much of a problem. I am using this phone for more than two weeks now and writing a segment wise review of the phone.
  

  1) Looks :- To me this the best looking one till date. It is classy, slick and elegant. During the durga puja I was clicking pictures with this phone during Pandals visit, many people came to me and asked about the model. Everybody were just blown away with the looks. The metal frame gives the phone more sturdy feeling and also useful for grip. But it adds to the weight of the phone which would not feel the lightest.
  

  2) Display:- 1080 display with 441 ppi will give you the one of the best displays ever in phone. HD movies , Games looks too good on the phone. Touch is superb. Never experienced a single response glitch till date. The screen guard comes with the phone is pretty good and it still working fine with me. Anyway screen guard is not a must with Gorilla Glass 3. I can surely say this phone has a better touch response or video quality than nexus 5.
  
  The glitch with display is that the visibility is low under sunlight. Even with keeping the display settings as auto, I faced difficulties in reading the screen. Nexus 5, even the Moto x gen 1 would  win the race.
  

  3) Battery:- The battery capacity is low compare to the other flagship models. But believe me it easily last a day even with heavy use. I would still think the battery capacity should be at least 20% higher but when android L with better power management is round the corner then you can still dill with it. Do not expect too much with fast charging hype. There is not much significant difference in charging time.
  

  4) Camera:- If you are Nokia/Sony user you can not be totally satisfied with this 13 MP primary camera. Otherwise it is pretty decent camera to me. Comparing to nexus 5 I would say this one has the better camera. Motorola camera app would give you better customization than your Google camera. Daylight pictures are good and low light pictures are decent. the flash is very strong. But still If you are looking to buy a android phone with brilliant camera buy Gionee E7.
  
  The secondary camera is pretty Ok for Skype call. You can take decent Selfy with 2ndary cam but it is not the best Selfy Phone I guess.
  

  5) Performance: -  The performance is great. There is no lag what's so ever. I tested couple of games like Fifa 15 , Real racing etc. which ran very smooth. But I must admid I am really no addicted for mobile gaming. I have loaded many apps. Do use social n/w, office emails etc. from my phone. No issues observed in multitasking. 3g speed is very good. I have used it for tethering long time without much issue. I am not sure if this device is compatible with airtel 4g. Need to check that. Airtel 4g has his own limitation and it works with only a short list of device. I haven't observed any unnatural heating problem till date.
  

  6) Software:- The selling point of this phone is not the hardware but the smooth voice and gesture control which it offers. Dedicated h/w which is used just to respond to your voice and gestures. You can give your phone any pet name and start calling it in this name. You can get necessary updates you need without unlocking the phone. It can even read out message, can send sms, can call people, can take photos, selfy  for you just responding on your voice commands. The voice response is pretty accurate even with my petty Indian accent.
  

  7) Others: - The headphone quality is pretty good. The phone comes with just more than 12 GB of usable storage capacity. If you are not a pro gamer it should be good enough for you. But I still do not understand why Motorola is giving only 16 gb to a 32k phone. The speaker sound is pretty loud. Signal reception is satisfactory.
  

  Verdict:- If you buy this phone you will not regret it.

  As a true technology fan, I think there are still some scope for improvements in this device. Here are those -
  

  > 9.72gb usable space for a device that can record 4k video and play high end games? I know "No sd card slot" is a kind of monopoly business from Google but at least Motorola should have launched 32 gb model in India like nexus 5.
  

  >Ridiculously light weight device that has a plastic back which is slippery, there is chance of slipping out of hand. Textured back would have given more grip.
  

  >Notably warmer display than any other Amoled screen. Not all people like Yellowish display.

  >What is the use of 13 mp sensor when you can not use it in wide screen mode? 10-12 mp should have been fine and sensor quality should have been improved for low light performance.
  

  >Touch less control can not control all the apps. Only few pre-selected apps can be opened. Motorola should update this in future.
  

  > 2300mAh. Well, Motorola missed that extra 300mAh.
  

  Rest of the features and specifications are just perfect.
  
  Just buy this phone, unbox it and hold it in your hand for the first time, you will not forget that feeling for a long time.
  

  Two major issues reported by some users -
  
  Over heating -  use only the charger provided with this phone. Don't use some other charger as they might have separate Amp rating.
  
  Battery Drain - For the first 2-3 charge cycle, let the device be idle for most of the time. Battery will get used to with the device. Then you can use it the way you want.
  

  Nano Sim tips - If you are changing you sim from mini or micro to nano rather than buying a nano sim then you may face problem while inserting the nano sim like I faced.
  
  # Cut the sim using a good quality cutter. Go to any reputed mobile shop, they have that cutter. Now even if you cut the sim to exact size of the sim tray you may see sim will not go all the way into the phone. That is because of the thickness. Take a piece of sand paper. Rub the non metalic side for few seconds. Eventually you will see your sim will be slimmer than before. Now you are ready to go.
  

  Another Issue - In Moto Voice, you will notice that "Good Morning", "Good Night" and "Talk to Me" commands are missing and even device is not accepting these command rather redirecting to google search when you say these commands. Go to play store, search "Moto", update all Moto apps and RESTART your device. After reboot these commands should work flawlessly.
  

  I did follow these steps, didn't face any concern.

column6: The best deal on arguably the best Android phone of 2014.
column7:
First of all addressing all the complaints of screen cracking: If you are buying a 20K phone then please use a tempered glass protector. It goes without saying!
  

  Looks: The perfect balance between form and function. However, the blue soft back looks different in real life from its pictures of Flipkart. So do google some images before buying.
  

  Ergonomics: A 5.2 inch phone that comfortably snuggles in your palm. If you have average sized hands you can just about use it single-handedly. Buyers with smaller hands beware! Also the curve at the back is functional too and allows for a nice comfortable grip.
  

  Screen: Brilliant Full HD AMOLED screen. No complaints at all. However the colours tend to be a bit warm.
  

  Software: Near stock Android means this is the next best thing to buying a Nexus. Also means no bloatware and a smooth running phone.
  

  Internals: The Snapdragon 801 may be last year's flagship but more than enough to ensure everything is zippy with zero lag. 2 GB ram is sufficient for all purposes but not enough to keep unnecessary apps always running in the background.
  

  Gaming: Not much of a gamer but whatever I tried ran at a smooth FPS with all visuals turned on. However, the slim phone can get quite hot in an extended session. This one is not really a heavy duty gaming phone. The smallish battery doesn't help either.
  

  Calls: Loud and clear! That's all that really matters.
  

  Camera: Not extensively tested but great daytime camera but really disappointing night time camera. Really simple & intuitive camera UI. However if you like more manual controls then look elsewhere or get a 3rd party app. Shutter speed is blisteringly quick though.
  

  Features:
  
  Active display that gives you time & notifications the moment you take your phone out of the pocket or approach it is a great touch.
  
  Moto voice means you can bark commands to Google Now without having to turn on the screen and is brilliant.
  
  Twist to launch camera is another great touch.
  

  Niggles:
  
  The screen tapers towards the edges and hence no tempered glass sticks perfectly to the screen and leaves annoying bubbles at the edges
  
  Moto voice can randomly get activated in conversation or while watching a movie. However this should be solved by tweaking the launch phrase.
  
  Battery life doesn't seem great but not really an issue for me personally as I tend to charge very frequently.
  

  Verdict: One hell of a phone that is way more than the sum of its parts. You've really got to own a Moto to know what it's all about!

column6: Probably the best Android experience yet!
column7:
Let me start this HUGE review by saying this - The Moto X 2nd Gen is a masterpiece.
  

  A good phone is not just about the best hardware. It should offer the best "experience". Everything, from how it feels in the hand to how smooth the apps run, matters. This phone manages to get almost every little thing right. It's one step closer to the "perfect" smartphone. Let's look at the individual elements : -
  

  Design : - This deserves to be mentioned first. Out of all the phones I've used or seen, this is one of the best in terms of design and aesthetics. I have the black model with the grey-ish polycarbonate back. There is a very prominent metal "dimple" in the back, just below the camera (which has a "ring flash"). This, added with the aluminium sides, gives this phone an extremely premium feel. The back is curved, which makes it a joy to hold in the hand. The phone is perfectly sized, and you won't have any problems with it being too big or too small. To summarise, you will absolutely not want to "ruin" this phone by putting it in a cheap case. (Please don't!) This is a work of art.
  

  Screen : - A 5.2-inch Full HD AMOLED screen. It's absolutely spectacular. Colours "pop out" and even incredibly tiny text is perfectly readable, The screen takes up most of the front of the device (compared to Apple and Samsung devices, which have big buttons below the screen), so the overall effect looks stunning. The upcoming Android Lollipop update (which focuses heavily on bright colours and pretty animations) is going to look spectacular on this screen for sure.
  

  Camera : - It's good. The 13mp back shooter takes cool photos, esp. in HDR mode (although it sometimes takes a while to focus). The 2mp front camera is good enough for selfies and video chats. Video recording is great, and the 4 noise cancelling microphones help in getting really good audio (I use it to record myself playing guitar). The camera can be accessed by "twisting" the wrist two times, a trick which every user of this phone will be using all the time. ;)
  

  Speaker : - It may look like two front speakers, but it's the bottom one which is the actual speaker. It's much better than Sony or Samsung speakers, but still far behind the unmatchable HTC Boomsound speakers. Still, bass is audible, and it's really loud.
  

  Software/Hardware : - Motorola takes the cake here. The software is smoother than butter. Hell, I found it to be smoother than my friend's Nexus 5, which is quite an achievement, It's stock Android 4.4.4 as of now. Moto hasn't changed anything from Google's version of Android except adding a few apps of it's own (compared to Samsung which changes EVERYTHING, from the UI to the features). Expect this to get the Lollipop update instantly (after the Nexus phones), which will improve the battery life and add many more features.
  

  Moto's own apps are helpful, and (again, unlike Samsung), not mere gimmicks. Moto Voice is always listening to you (Even when the screen is off), and it has a ton of functionality, which, added with Google Now, helps you control the device without even touching it. It's real helpful when you can check your phone notifications and even send Whatsapp messages while lying in bed, with your phone on your table! It doesn't drain the battery, as it runs on a separate low-power processor instead of the main one.
  

  The best feature, however, is the Moto Display. It activates when you hold your phone, or when you bring your hands near it. It shows the time, and your notifications in a beautiful, battery-saving interface, so that you don't have to even unlock your screen. I've gotten so used to this that I often expect other phones to light up as soon as I bring my hand near them!
  

  Performance is obviously outstanding, thanks to the Snapdragon 801 processor. High-end games run perfectly, and multitasking is perfect, with literally NO lag.
  

  Storage is 16GB and non-expandable, which is fine for most people, unless you store a lot of music and/or movies in your phone.
  

  Battery - 2300mah may look low, but it easily lasts the day with moderate to slightly heavy use. Those of you who are coming from devices with large batteries (like the Galaxy Note series) may find the lower battery slightly unsettling at first, but it's not a big deal. In the last few days, it has consistently lasted the entire day with all moto features + GPS staying on.
  

  At 32k, a phone like this is an absolute STEAL. I got it for around 24k thanks to the exchange offer (exchanged an old Galaxy S2), and I couldn't be any happier. The only good competitor that I can see for this price point is the HTC One E8, which is also a really good phone, to be honest. But it doesn't have the amazing build quality and the superb features of this one.
  

  FIVE out of five! And a HUGE thumbs up! Keep it up, Moto. You will rule the Indian market in no time with phones like this and the Moto G.

Its the perfect display size, perfect in the hand and the features like Moto Display and Moto Voice are the best.Given that its currently at a ridiculously low price of 15000 which decreases even further when you exchange your old phone for it, I'll recommend this phone to you in a heartbeat.
  

  I've read many reviews here on Flipkart that have said that the screen replacement cost is ridiculously high. Allow me to explain the reason.
  
  Most of the phones in the market have an LCD display. LCD displays are much cheaper to manufacture and hence cost less when you break your old display. This phone has an AMOLED display which cost much more to manufacture; just look at the TV market and you'll see that only a few OLED TV's are there (DO NOT confuse with LED TV's). THis kind of display uses less battery power, especially for Moto Display. An LCD Screen will hog battery when Moto Display is in use as the whole display lights up and not just the few pixels.
  
  If you still are not convinced, i suggest you avoid buying this phone or learn to take proper care of your devices. If you want protection, buy a good case and slap on a tempered glass protector. But please stop complaining and giving bad reviews to such an awesome phone.

column6: The Amazing Moto X- android done right
column7:
I will keep this exhaustive so you can feel how I feel, fun fact- this is my 100th smartphone and my cure for incessant search for something better. Since last 5 years I have been down this road of mobile devices starting with a now humble blackberry Curve and a reason for my money going into a futile yet uncontrollable pursuit :) . The following review is for the phone entailing the following aspects-
  

  1) In hand feel- it is always better to know how it feels by giving the phone to users of other phones and knowing their reaction. I did the same with an iPhone purist who never acknowledges a rival product and hates Samsung the most. And you must see how delighted he was appreciating the aluminum frame and smooth feeling of the back and the fanatic Moto logo. And then I gave it to Galaxy S5 users and Sony. I even had a few hours with an iPhone 6 and feel really odd holding a behemoth of a device for 4.7 inch screen,  I mean apple sure could do better. So is this all euphoria and lies,  no sir. I am really and truly happy with the purchase and will keep it till iPhone 6s comes to apple's rescue with a far better camera and an updated processor.
  

  2) Performance- Even Virat has off days, not this beast. Give it any task,  give it to change apps as frequently as you can,  give it a slap or a thud, give it games that scream with demanding graphics and processing prowess. Give it some love cause it can. How does it do,  by keeping things simple and when Motorola gets itself out of Google way of Android. It is a sad affair how all other manufacturers just go on piling stuff after stuff and unnecessarily burden the underlying android for their. The main reason being profit and their own competing ecosystem. Users would not mind if things were to improve, alas we suffer the most in the form of frustrating lags and inordinate delays in getting future android.
  

  3) Hello future- You can almost feel like Iron man when your phone wakes up and tells you answers when you take a command (hello Shaktiman,  in my case: ). I demoed it to wife and she asked me to go to sabji purchase which showed how jealous she was   anyway,  on the use front this is a cool addition and is really helpful when you cannot reach your phone and need some information from Google Now. Moto display too is another my favorite when you can just wave your palm over it or just pick it up or just move the phone a little and it shows up the time and notifications. Just amazing. I think in 2014, every phone should have this cool stuff. Downside to this is a cluttered look on the white version of this owing to 4 IR sensors which make the phone unsightly, bad bad...
  

  4) Display,  Camera and battery life- Truth be told, this phone uses AMOLED from Samsung and they will not be giving Motorola their best, so on display front they are one generation behind Samsung. Still on a 1080p screen things are hardly noticed for the obvious lack of screen refinement. Still when you have a platform of 5.2 inch screen, things will always be interesting. Camera is a frustration  and I would urge everyone to install Google Camera, keep HDR on and problem solved. Better life contrary to everyone's quick judgement is as good as any flagship that launched in first half of the year. Don't forget this is 20k cheaper than iPhone 6 and you will learn to live with the one day battery life
  

  5) Lollipop - Guys, guys, guys,  Google  has a masterstroke in the form of Lollipop with the complete visual overhaul with Android L and they are already seen in apps like hangouts, drive, keep, fit etc to name a few and Motorola having kept it's traditional image will seed in the next as early as December and finally android will be as good looking as iOS. And thanks to Samsung's over the top feature list, you won't know if you got a new OS or just leafed out due to compromising overlaying touchwiz.
  

  And another fun fact, typed this entire review on my Moto X with a little help from SwiftKey :)
  

  Cheers,
  
  Jagan

Upgraded from a Micromax Canvas HD, been using the X for 8 days now. Got an armor case too to protect from any physical damage ever.
  

  Pros:
  
  + Great screen. Looks fabulous at 5.2" with beautiful colors and resolution. A delight to look at.
  
  + Pure android works great. Can't wait for Android L update.
  
  + Good speakers. Could've been a tad bit louder (considering its a 32k phone)
  
  + Voice quality and noise cancellation is good (lest we forget these are also important in a phone :p)
  
  + Camera clicks fast. Makes 'stories', a slideshow of pics/videos automatically which is awesome.
  
  + Spotlight stories is some random fun sprinkled.
  
  + Very premium feel. Great looks and ergonomics!
  
  + Strong flash. Makes the best torch ever :)
  

  Cons:
  
  - Battery could've been a bit better. Nothing you can't live with though.
  
  - The Moto features are just gimmicks [[explained below separately]]
  
  - 16GB seems a bit less for the price. 32gigs or expandable shdve been present.
  

  MOTO FEATURES:
  
  Since these are the main USP, they need separate mention.
  

  1. Moto Voice:
  
  - Very fancy and fun for the first few times, but poor on functionality.
  
  - Very linear in behavior. E.g. I can open FB, but can't give it a next command to open a page/profile/gallery on FB. Similarly, cancelling/going back etc doesn't work. Command -> action and that's it.
  
  - If there is any other sound around, it fails. Only place it seems to work is majorly at home.
  
  - Doesn't always get your command right (atleast our Indian accents)
  
  - Too frikkin slow! I could've sent the whatsapp ping 10 times by the time i get the right message to the right person (currently doesn't work. Fails to finally send the ping it heard)
  

  2. Moto Assist
  
  - Driving is detected well and reads out messages/callerIDs
  
  - Sleeping turns screen off and mutes as per defined time span. You can do this urself in less than 30 seconds. And personally, i don't sleep at the exact same time everyday. Even if i sleep just half hour later, i wouldn't want to miss calls in the time, right?
  
  - Home: didn't find it useful, i would rather just pick up the phone and read the message/callerID.
  
  - Meetings: nothing much here either
  

  3. Actions:
  
  - Twist to open camera is nice and useful. You can chuck the camera icon from ur homescreen now.
  
  - Wave to silence may be useful in the odd scenario when ur hands are occupied/dirty and ur phone is in reachable distance for u to silence..and u want to silence it.
  
  - Approach is useless since it keeps lighting up all the time anywy.
  

  4. Display:
  
  - Shows all notifications from the lock screen. However, often shows only part of the notif (half a line of a status update, half a news headline)
  
  - Doesn't let me interact with it there. E.g. Can't delete the e-mail there itself, or reach for 'reply' to a whatsapp. Thus limited utility.
  

  Overall, the Moto features seem like Chapter 0.1. Lots of possible uses and enhancements in the future, but as of now. I can do without all of them easily. Do not have this as ur criteria when selecting this phone.

I feel that too much has already been written about it. So I'll just share my pros and cons.
  

  PROS
  

  Very lightweight and snappy response most of the time
  

  Came with the Lollipop update
  

  AMOLED screen, so I use my Kindle and Bible app in night mode -white text on a black background as there is no backlight and black pixels take no power (to save power)
  

  Moto Voice works very well and Its good to be able to change OK Google to something else
  

  Untampered version of Android
  


  CONS
  

  The wave to silence/snooze works intermittently, rather mostly doesn't work so I've turned it off
  

  I found out that the Moto display turns on too many times when in close proximity, so I turned off that feature
  

  While the ambient display was a great feature on Kitkat, on the Moto X2 it is not as useful and lollipop ambient notifications are more informative and need less interaction, unfortunately lollipop wakes up the whole screen.
  

  Phone is very thin and slips very easily from the hand especially if you've got some cream or oil on your hands and I've been lucky that my screen is intact. I've ordered an Otterbox defender case from Otterbox. It slips off quite easily when using the double twist gesture to fire up the camera.
  

  On weekends when I use the phone a lot, I sometimes have to charge thrice in a day, however charging is fast
  

  Overall, most of what was special for this phone has been integrated into lollipop, so I have turned off all those sensors -which means I unnecessarily paid for that hardware. I still can't figure out how to stop the phone waking up when it senses movement.
  

  If I knew about all these things before I bought the phone, I would have waited for the next moto version from Motorola. I still love the phone.

  a) Moto Voice: Call your phone in a unique way to do common things. Isn't that the future of smartphones. Brilliant work.
  
  b) Moto display: I hardly ever push the power button now.
  
  c) Moto Actions: It's such a relief that  when I want to capture a moment, I don't have to press power button, unlock phone, find the camera app and find that I missed the moment.
  
  d) Moto Assist: I didn't know much about this before buying the phone, but it certainly helps when I don't get disturbed during meetings, or when I'm sleeping, or get messages read out while I'm driving.
  
  2. Design: I love the feel and ergonomics of the phone in my hand. Plus the metallic rim gives it a premium edge.

  # The battery backup is average as I was expecting that with just 2G/3G continuously on, the phone would survive at least 14-15 hours(even if you are NOT watching videos, NOT capturing pictures, NOT listening to music, NOT turned on your location or Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, NOT playing any games). But to my disappointment it lasts for 10 hours at max.   ####### UPDATE #######
  
  After updating my device to Android 5.0 Lollipop and using it rigorously for three months here is what I have to say:
  
  # Sometimes, the device gets hot(~42 C) even when its idle.
  
  # When used under direct sunlight, the display gets too hot to handle(~45 C) though it does not lag at all.
  
  # The camera performance has not been addressed in Android 5.0 update. Its still inconsistent and sometimes shuts down itself showing 'The device is stowed. Exiting Camera'. Moreover launching camera app by gesture & killing it from overview, does not respond to the gesture again
  
  # Sometimes, the phone starts lagging, like when Asphalt 8 screen is pinned
  
  # Sometimes, the battery drains like anything(from 100% to 85% in just 10 mins) in light usage

  # Moto Voice doesn't work properly(resets its volume, does not reply promptly to 'Open Whatsapp, Open Facebook, What's New commands)

After an intense research spanning two months or so, I ordered Moto X 2nd gen., my dream phone. I am using it from past 3 weeks and here is my review.
  
  I am in awe of Motorola's brilliant engineering. The design is slim and elegant. The curved metal frame gives it that premium look you are looking for. The indented Motorola 'M' logo looks and feels really cool. Performance is super fast, with almost no lag and multitaking (switches between applications) is super smooth.
  

  The display is spectacular. The phone is 5.2" inch, but fits perfectly in my hands. If you have long fingers, like me, it will be quite helpful to operate this phone with one hand. I am using Case Mate's Naked Tough Cover (bought from Flipkart) and it is a great fit. I recommend it.
  
  Storage: Only 10.06GB out of 16GB is available for use and out of ~10GB around 9.5GB is free. Since Moto X 2nd gen. supports OTG, you can easily transfer/store huge files to an OTG pen drive. I am using SanDisk Ultra Dual 16GB OTG pen drive and it works perfectly. I recommend it.
  
  Memory: Out of 2GB, ~1.8GB RAM is available. After updating and installing the most commonly used applications, nearly 1GB is usually free. And that's awesome!
  

  Camera: It is not that great, but it isn't bad either. The pictures taken in day light are pretty decent. In low light, no smartphone camera can take amazing pics anyway, so camera quality should not be judged under low light or night conditions. The full HD, 4K and SloMo video recording is amazing though. Double twist wrist to open camera is too good and works every time.
  

  Audio output from front speakers is really good and stunningly powerful; great for enjoying both music and videos. Disappointed with headphones output though as it lacks the clarity and punch.
  
  Moto Voice is awesome. However, I have not tested it really well and still getting used to it.
  

  Battery is average. In simple words, you will have to charge the phone at least once in 24 hours.
  

  I had an iPhone 3GS before this and one thing which hasn't changed moving from iOS to Android is getting Notifications on the lock screen.   Reasons to buy this phone: Display, 2.5GHz quad core processor, 2GB RAM, Notifications on lock screen, Speakers/Audio/Video, Moto voice and fast updates, just to mention a few.
  

  This phone is slim and delicate, and not for rough use, so make sure you get at least a back cover for it. Getting a screen guard would also be a good idea, just to ensure that the display stays scratch free.

I have been using Moto X2 for more than a month now. And I am really happy with my buy. This one is my first flagship product.
  

  The built is excellent. It is sleek, well rounded and cornered. Though it lacks the metal body, but still gives that premium finish. First thing you will notice about the phone  will be it's weight. It is so light. I have bought the basic version of the phone; wood / leather could give a better in-hand feel.
  

  Needless to say that the phone has got a seamless and smooth user interface. But what really impressed me is its Moto Voice and assist features. The phone always tries to interact with you and it is quite responsive. Voice command is really hand and you can control entire phone without never touching it. You can call, answer calls, text, Whatsapp, Facebook, click pics with the help of Moto voice.
  

  Camera is not so great, but it is neither that bad. Shots shot in low light are very grainy and noise-y. Though, pictures taken in day-light are good and have adequate details. Selfie camera is better relatively and clicks good enough pictures. The "shake-me-twice-to-open-camera" feature is really handy and useful.
  

  Coming to processor and other specs, it's 2GB RAM tag might not look so big. But, believe me, it is far more than enough. Motorola has done great job as far as optimization is concerned and the phone never lags even when you open multiple apps / tabs.
  

  The screen and display is fabulous. Touch is also equally good and flawless. I am a very rough mobile user and do not take care much when it comes to handling phone. But the Gorilla Glass has done its work perfectly and there is no scratch on phone screen till now. Phone is really, really water resistant (experimented).
  

  The battery is not so great. Juice will drain out quickly. But, still it could survive for almost a day for moderate uses. Battery would drain fast if you are on a 3G / data pack but would perform better while it is on WiFi. There is no problem of heating which I have faced.
  

  Sound quality is really great. My Sennheiser earphones works really well with the phone. I have not tried the earphones which comes with phone. Mics are not too loud but they are audible and at the same time are soothing to ears. Mobile lacks FM radio which I really miss at times.
  

  The phone has been priced 32k, which is little bit expensive for Indian market. Still it is way better than all other flagship products. Only thing which is missing is Moto Maker. Flipkart should make it available in more colors and textures.

Had been searching for a good smartphone in the price range of Rs 30000 now for the last 3 months . Am a bit of a tech geek so wanted top end hardware at a not so premium price . Am also someone who gives high priority to finish quality and external looks . My short list of phones was LG G3 ( available for approx Rs 30000 in Germany - was going there so i thought i could pick it up there ) , Sony experia Z3 mini and finally the Google Nexus 5 . Yes , the Motorola X (2nd Gen) , was not even on my list . After weighing the pros and cons of each phone i more or less resigned to getting the Nexus 5 . All logic told me it would be a safe good buy but my heart was not really there - the phone looks a little bland and whatever said and done it is still last years model and the hardware , though still very good , is a little behind cutting edge . Then i came across an ad for the Motorola Moto X . I did a little online research and the more i read the more my heart and my head started to veer towards it . I was a little apprehensive as its an online order only model so there was no way to go to a shop and take a look and feel of the real thing . I was scared that maybe it would be too big and heavy plus i was not too keen on a very large phone . Like the idea of having something which fits easily in my shirt or trouser pocket without looking obscene .
  
  So here goes , i know its been mentioned here by some other people , but really you will be literally wowed the first time you take the phone in your hand . Its a truly stunning piece of hardware . Built quality is top notch and the gentle curve at the back . Pure genius in terms of design asthetics . How does it compare to the others , i.e - LG G3 and Sony Experia Z3 . I would say , and this is a personal choice , but its truly the best amongst them . The LG G3 is good but i felt it was just a tad too large , the Moto X is just the right size . All my fears that it would be too large were put to rest as the design team of Motorola made sure almost the entire surface is taken up by the screen which makes it actually slightly smaller in overall dimensions to almost all 5 inch models .
  
  The screen , the user interface , touch responsiveness are all superb . A lot has been said about the screen , being an Amoled screen , but i can tell you text sharpness , colour saturation , edge detail are all top notch . The voice recognition feature of this phone is truly revolutionary ( and i have an Ipad Air ) and i would give it a couple of marks over the Siri from Apple . Plus the way its integrated into the system is absolutely fantastic . I am sure that with future software upgrades it will only get better . Using it i felt as though i was part of a science fiction movie !!!
  
  My only gripes with this phone - why oh why are they not offering the 32GB model in India ? Do they consider that for some reason we dont need extra storage ??? And the other - the Camera - let me put it this way . Its not a bad camera but for a phone costing Rs 30000 plus its - average . Hope Motorola will update the phone software soon to make it work better . The phone comes with a great inbuilt app called ' Migrate ' . It transferred all my stuff - pics , sms , photos , videos , contacts - literally everything from my HTC phone without any hiccups . Again great . Sound and call quality are again top notch . Processor is fantastic , no lag whatsoever , everything runs smooth as butter .
  
  Final verdict - i would give this phone 9 out of 10 - especially considering the price . It beats the pants off phones costing 40 thousand plus . I would have given it 10 out of 10 but for the camera being a slight let down . At the end - am super happy with this phone .

column6: no expandable memory,only 9.18 gb user available, good product otherwise , worth upgrading from  2013 model
column7:
After using the Moto X (2nd gen) (2014) for a couple of days, there is a lot to tell. Lets just shrink everything down under 2 sections, PROS and CONS.
  
  PROS
  
  1. Good Battery Life (NOT excellent)
  
  After removing from charge at 2 a.m. , i unlocked the phone at 10 a.m. in the morning and it was down to 97 percent. After heavy usage of wifi, mobile data, calling, browsing and texting, i was left with 22 percent at 11:45 p.m.
  

  2. Blazing fast and snappy performance
  
  No matter what they have put inside the device, it performs brilliant , and during this testing time, it never gave a lag (but the browser got stuck a few times)
  

  3. Handy Moto Apps
  
  The Moto assist, Moto actions, Moto voice and Moto display were the things i got this device for. They are very handy and help me a lot, surely it will help you if you buy one for yourself.
  

  4.Makes "Heads Turn"
  
  yeah, people were impressed (actually,fascinated) by seeing a phone made of ACTUAL WOOD and seeing the active display and touch less control in this phone which are exclusive to this phone.
  

  4.Price
  
  At the price which it offers hardware , it gives a neck to neck competition to the present flagships like the galaxy s5, htc one m8 , and even the experia z3... And the additional moto apps that come preloaded with the phone, makes the STOCK ANDROID experience even better for the price.
  

  5.Software
  
  It comes with android 4.4.4 kitkat and motorola has ensured an upgrade to android 5.0 lollipop as soon as possible, and as the phone is made by the support of google itself, we can expect the update to roll out with the nexus devices.
  

  6. Nice Speaker
  
  Well , a good upgrade as compared to last year's moto x. Moto x 2nd gen even made the htc's phone shy , the ones having boomsound. In short, its very loud and clear.
  
  CONS
  

  1. Camera
  
  The worst part of the phone is sadly, the camera. With a 13 megapixel camera, it is not able to produce as good photos as the other phones produce i mentioned above. Flash was not of big use to me though. The HDR mode photos were quite good, but not as good as that of the other phones it was compared above.
  
  while recording videos, you need a lot of light to make them look good.
  

  2. Slippery Design
  
  I decided not to put on a back cover as I wished to show off the wooden back, which resultantly caused the phone to slip from hand while i was calling or browsing. Thankfully, the dimple at the back help me to save it from falling, that too not to a huge extent.
  

  3. Storage
  
  We know that this phone doesn't comes with expandable storage, but the real problem comes is with internal storage. Flipkart says that user available space is 12 GB, but what the device actually had was 9.18GB , as approx. 720MB was occupied by the preinstalled Moto apps which shows the total memory in 10GB.
  

  Closing the review, i will like to tell the viewers that this phone is the phone you need for day to day usage. Last year's moto x was a good phone,it was snappy and fast, but what it lagged was raw power and on paper specs. The moto x 2nd gen takes care of both. Worth an upgrade even if you use use last year's moto x.
  

  P.S. - This phone has everything you need, no matter who you are (except if you are a photographer who uses phone camera for photography) .
  

  This phone , as I like to say to everyone is , "MADE FOR HUMANS"
  
  Go get it if you need a bang for the buck, its wroth it.

I got the regular black Moto X on the Big Billion day under exchange. Flipkart gave Rs. 8000/- for my old "Motorola defy plus" and extra 2000/- as cashback. so I got this for 22000/- only.
  

  Display - 5/5. Viewing angles are great and watching videos is a great experience. Color saturation is not a bother at all as some others are saying.

column6: You are looking on the right phone. Just buy it!
column7:
I have been using iPhone since 2009 till mid 2014. Bought HTC One M8 and used it for 4 months till I dropped it in water and it died. Being impatient and rebellious I dared to buy the Samsung Galaxy S5 but then silently sold it for 10K less in just 4 days. S5 had huge specs, the best in town but it was not "usable". Meaning I missed 7 out of 10 calls when the phone is place on a sofa or cushion or bed  due to its surprisingly low volume and this happened even if the place is quiet. Secondly the heat of the phone hurts if you use it continuously for just even 15 mins, not just the battery but the screen becomes horribly hot. Then the every irritating and gimmicky TouchWiz. I don't know what is worst on earth than this. Hence I was desperately searching for a "usable" phone with high-end specs. Moto X is what I was exactly looking for.
  

  Design: It has this metal frame which just feels premium but also helps your phone remain cool. The rubber back provides great grip and the Moto logo dimple is pretty helpful for increased grip while your on a call. The bulged metal speaker grills feel quite good too.
  

  Software: The OS is pure Android with non-intrusive modifications. This phone shall be one of first non-nexus phones to receive the much awaited Android L update. The phone has cute little animations that pop-up on the home screen itself that will pleasantly surprise you. I love the bed-bug.
  

  The specs are are fantastic and have been tweaked to use the power only when its required.
  

  The Moto X's Moto Display is absolutely useful. You won't believe how helpful it is until you have used it. And on an average it use less battery than when you repeatedly wake up the phone to check notifications.
  

  Audio: The frontal speaker is very loud and clear. It has a rich output but not as good as HTC One M8 tough. But having used to M8's sound I personally didn't find it to be that bad. Its more than average. The phone comes with very ergonomic earphone with reasonably deep bass but it feels cheap and lacks a remote to control music playback like "next", "forward", "back" etc. The Phone's earpiece is just a bit low in volume. That would mean you "might" struggle hearing in a loud place, but then it has a benefit that the other party's voice is not heard even in a quite room with people in it e.g. conference rooms etc.
  

  Camera: The camera is not as good as iPhone 5S's or Galaxy S5's but it can be best used in broad sunlight or in bright artificial lights because thats when you would have the least noise.
  
  The ring flash is just a design and it doesn't have any major impact on the overall picture quality when compared to normal led flash cameras on similar phones. The front camera is slow and not good for taking selfies but I don't use it for that. The good part of it is that it can offer better video chat quality on Skype or Hangouts when on low bandwidth networks like 3G due its low resolution which will consume less data.
  

  Storage: Before buying the phone, I was wishing hard that the phone to be have a MicroSD slot. But when I actually used it I found it has about 10.66 GB of user space on the device. I have installed all possible messaging and social networking apps, few 2D games, productivity apps  ~ 1GB , with about 100 songs ~ 500MB, migrated about 40 photos ~ 50MB and still I'm left with about 8GB of space remaining. Thats should work for an average user.
  

  Battery: Lasts for a day (10AM to 8PM) with WiFi, 3G, Location turned-on still left with 20%. With an average of checking Facebook, Twitter, WhatsApp updates in about 30 mins frequency.

column6: A Great Experience Spoiled by few important things
column7:
Bought this great phone on Flipkart's Diwali Sale on an exchange offer + cash back and the deal was just awesome. Phone came before promised date.
  

  Now below is my experience till now -
  

  Good Things  
  
  1) Design - Awesome is the word. It's not only sleek but unlike any other phone in the market. Feels good in hand because of curve back and matte finish. Overall nice ergonomics.
  
  2) Software - Pure Stock Android v4.4.4 OS with no stupid layers. Some of the add-on features like gesture phone silent and one tap notification read are awesome. If you have used/experienced Nexus 5 before you will know what I am talking about. It's fuss free and clean.
  
  3) Performance   Throw any application or game and it will play smoothly. Combination of 2GB RAM and 2.5 GHz Processor is awesome for power pack performance.
  

  Sadly don't have much good to write about beyond above. Here are the downsides  
  

  1)	Camera   Sadly for such price range, camera is just about okay. Day photos are good but low light photos are nothing to write about. Video quality is also just decent.
  
  2)	Accessories   Since Motorola is not the most popular brand in current scenario, finding accessories (Back cover, Screen Guards etc.) for this phone at local shops is a nightmare. Eventually had to buy the accessories from an online shopping site where you don't know the exact feel until you get the product on your hand. Also not much options are there in terms of customize covers.
  
  3)	Curved screen   Curve screen looks beautiful at first but you soon get to know the down side once you put a screen guard on it. It comes off too soon. It's only one month I have bought the phone and I have already bought my third screen guard (which also started to come off). This is highly irritating.
  
  4)	No storage expansion   though I knew this before buying the phone and I thought that it won't affect me much but I've started to feel that at least 32GB was necessary to last 2 years gadget life.
  
  5)	Battery   Battery just about lasts 13-14 hours on a heavy usage day (call/internet), if I play games and play video than it might die in 10 hours. Wish it had at least 3000 mAh battery.
  
  6)	Earphones   Moto has shipping highly uncomfortable earphones. They are made of hard plastic and your ear starts to hurt in few minutes of use.
  
  7)	Issue with microphone   This is the biggest spoiler. I don't know if this is particular to my handset but strangely in between the calls the person on opposite end complaints that they can't hear me at all. column6: Reviewing after two weeks of use
column7:
I have bought this phone as soon as it was available on the market. This is my third android phone. My two previous phone were Moto Defy+ and Nexus 5. I have to move out of nexus because of the unusual hardware fault. Defy+ ran 3 years without much of a problem. I am using this phone for more than two weeks now and writing a segment wise review of the phone.
  

  1) Looks :- To me this the best looking one till date. It is classy, slick and elegant. During the durga puja I was clicking pictures with this phone during Pandals visit, many people came to me and asked about the model. Everybody were just blown away with the looks. The metal frame gives the phone more sturdy feeling and also useful for grip. But it adds to the weight of the phone which would not feel the lightest.
  

  2) Display:- 1080 display with 441 ppi will give you the one of the best displays ever in phone. HD movies , Games looks too good on the phone. Touch is superb. Never experienced a single response glitch till date. The screen guard comes with the phone is pretty good and it still working fine with me. Anyway screen guard is not a must with Gorilla Glass 3. I can surely say this phone has a better touch response or video quality than nexus 5.
  
  The glitch with display is that the visibility is low under sunlight. Even with keeping the display settings as auto, I faced difficulties in reading the screen. Nexus 5, even the Moto x gen 1 would  win the race.
  

  3) Battery:- The battery capacity is low compare to the other flagship models. But believe me it easily last a day even with heavy use. I would still think the battery capacity should be at least 20% higher but when android L with better power management is round the corner then you can still dill with it. Do not expect too much with fast charging hype. There is not much significant difference in charging time.
  

  4) Camera:- If you are Nokia/Sony user you can not be totally satisfied with this 13 MP primary camera. Otherwise it is pretty decent camera to me. Comparing to nexus 5 I would say this one has the better camera. Motorola camera app would give you better customization than your Google camera. Daylight pictures are good and low light pictures are decent. the flash is very strong. But still If you are looking to buy a android phone with brilliant camera buy Gionee E7.
  
  The secondary camera is pretty Ok for Skype call. You can take decent Selfy with 2ndary cam but it is not the best Selfy Phone I guess.
  

  5) Performance: -  The performance is great. There is no lag what's so ever. I tested couple of games like Fifa 15 , Real racing etc. which ran very smooth. But I must admid I am really no addicted for mobile gaming. I have loaded many apps. Do use social n/w, office emails etc. from my phone. No issues observed in multitasking. 3g speed is very good. I have used it for tethering long time without much issue. I am not sure if this device is compatible with airtel 4g. Need to check that. Airtel 4g has his own limitation and it works with only a short list of device. I haven't observed any unnatural heating problem till date.
  

  6) Software:- The selling point of this phone is not the hardware but the smooth voice and gesture control which it offers. Dedicated h/w which is used just to respond to your voice and gestures. You can give your phone any pet name and start calling it in this name. You can get necessary updates you need without unlocking the phone. It can even read out message, can send sms, can call people, can take photos, selfy  for you just responding on your voice commands. The voice response is pretty accurate even with my petty Indian accent.
  

  7) Others: - The headphone quality is pretty good. The phone comes with just more than 12 GB of usable storage capacity. If you are not a pro gamer it should be good enough for you. But I still do not understand why Motorola is giving only 16 gb to a 32k phone. The speaker sound is pretty loud. Signal reception is satisfactory.
  

  Verdict:- If you buy this phone you will not regret it.

  As a true technology fan, I think there are still some scope for improvements in this device. Here are those -
  

  > 9.72gb usable space for a device that can record 4k video and play high end games? I know "No sd card slot" is a kind of monopoly business from Google but at least Motorola should have launched 32 gb model in India like nexus 5.
  

  >Ridiculously light weight device that has a plastic back which is slippery, there is chance of slipping out of hand. Textured back would have given more grip.
  

  >Notably warmer display than any other Amoled screen. Not all people like Yellowish display.
  

  >Nano sim. Why? Space management may be. That too in phone that is 5.2 inches tall. Cutting and inserting a nano sim is a tricky job.
  

  >What is the use of 13 mp sensor when you can not use it in wide screen mode? 10-12 mp should have been fine and sensor quality should have been improved for low light performance.
  

  >Touch less control can not control all the apps. Only few pre-selected apps can be opened. Motorola should update this in future.
  

  > 2300mAh. Well, Motorola missed that extra 300mAh.
  

  Rest of the features and specifications are just perfect.
  
  Just buy this phone, unbox it and hold it in your hand for the first time, you will not forget that feeling for a long time.
  

  Two major issues reported by some users -
  
  Over heating -  use only the charger provided with this phone. Don't use some other charger as they might have separate Amp rating.
  
  Battery Drain - For the first 2-3 charge cycle, let the device be idle for most of the time. Battery will get used to with the device. Then you can use it the way you want.
  

  Nano Sim tips - If you are changing you sim from mini or micro to nano rather than buying a nano sim then you may face problem while inserting the nano sim like I faced.
  
  # Cut the sim using a good quality cutter. Go to any reputed mobile shop, they have that cutter. Now even if you cut the sim to exact size of the sim tray you may see sim will not go all the way into the phone. That is because of the thickness. Take a piece of sand paper. Rub the non metalic side for few seconds. Eventually you will see your sim will be slimmer than before. Now you are ready to go.
  

  Another Issue - In Moto Voice, you will notice that "Good Morning", "Good Night" and "Talk to Me" commands are missing and even device is not accepting these command rather redirecting to google search when you say these commands. Go to play store, search "Moto", update all Moto apps and RESTART your device. After reboot these commands should work flawlessly.

column6: The best deal on arguably the best Android phone of 2014.
column7:
First of all addressing all the complaints of screen cracking: If you are buying a 20K phone then please use a tempered glass protector. It goes without saying!
  

  Looks: The perfect balance between form and function. However, the blue soft back looks different in real life from its pictures of Flipkart. So do google some images before buying.
  

  Ergonomics: A 5.2 inch phone that comfortably snuggles in your palm. If you have average sized hands you can just about use it single-handedly. Buyers with smaller hands beware! Also the curve at the back is functional too and allows for a nice comfortable grip.
  

  Screen: Brilliant Full HD AMOLED screen. No complaints at all. However the colours tend to be a bit warm.
  

  Software: Near stock Android means this is the next best thing to buying a Nexus. Also means no bloatware and a smooth running phone.
  

  Internals: The Snapdragon 801 may be last year's flagship but more than enough to ensure everything is zippy with zero lag. 2 GB ram is sufficient for all purposes but not enough to keep unnecessary apps always running in the background.
  

  Gaming: Not much of a gamer but whatever I tried ran at a smooth FPS with all visuals turned on. However, the slim phone can get quite hot in an extended session. This one is not really a heavy duty gaming phone. The smallish battery doesn't help either.
  

  Calls: Loud and clear! That's all that really matters.
  

  Camera: Not extensively tested but great daytime camera but really disappointing night time camera. Really simple & intuitive camera UI. However if you like more manual controls then look elsewhere or get a 3rd party app. Shutter speed is blisteringly quick though.
  

  Features:
  
  Active display that gives you time & notifications the moment you take your phone out of the pocket or approach it is a great touch.
  
  Moto voice means you can bark commands to Google Now without having to turn on the screen and is brilliant.
  
  Twist to launch camera is another great touch.
  

  Niggles:
  
  The screen tapers towards the edges and hence no tempered glass sticks perfectly to the screen and leaves annoying bubbles at the edges
  
  Moto voice can randomly get activated in conversation or while watching a movie. However this should be solved by tweaking the launch phrase.
  
  Battery life doesn't seem great but not really an issue for me personally as I tend to charge very frequently.
  

  Verdict: One hell of a phone that is way more than the sum of its parts. You've really got to own a Moto to know what it's all about!

  - Yes : The battery is a bummer. The battery graph curves very steeply both while charging and discharging. It is not unusual to see the battery drop from 100% to 57% in 35-40 minutes of texting and internet browsing on 3G. I keep a power bank handy.

  - IR Sensors are impressive and work every time! Some fancy yet useful features made me choose this phone over all others - like waving your hand 6 inches above the phone for silencing alarms and incoming calls, wrist twist for activating the camera and again for alternating between the rear and front cam.
  
  - Moto Voice is the soul of this phone. Not only useful for typical features like calling and texting, it is also very useful for navigating. Turning on Bluetooth, wifi, whatsapp is easier, without going through the various screens. column6: Probably the best Android experience yet!
column7:
Let me start this HUGE review by saying this - The Moto X 2nd Gen is a masterpiece.
  

  A good phone is not just about the best hardware. It should offer the best "experience". Everything, from how it feels in the hand to how smooth the apps run, matters. This phone manages to get almost every little thing right. It's one step closer to the "perfect" smartphone. Let's look at the individual elements : -
  

  Design : - This deserves to be mentioned first. Out of all the phones I've used or seen, this is one of the best in terms of design and aesthetics. I have the black model with the grey-ish polycarbonate back. There is a very prominent metal "dimple" in the back, just below the camera (which has a "ring flash"). This, added with the aluminium sides, gives this phone an extremely premium feel. The back is curved, which makes it a joy to hold in the hand. The phone is perfectly sized, and you won't have any problems with it being too big or too small. To summarise, you will absolutely not want to "ruin" this phone by putting it in a cheap case. (Please don't!) This is a work of art.
  

  Screen : - A 5.2-inch Full HD AMOLED screen. It's absolutely spectacular. Colours "pop out" and even incredibly tiny text is perfectly readable, The screen takes up most of the front of the device (compared to Apple and Samsung devices, which have big buttons below the screen), so the overall effect looks stunning. The upcoming Android Lollipop update (which focuses heavily on bright colours and pretty animations) is going to look spectacular on this screen for sure.
  

  Camera : - It's good. The 13mp back shooter takes cool photos, esp. in HDR mode (although it sometimes takes a while to focus). The 2mp front camera is good enough for selfies and video chats. Video recording is great, and the 4 noise cancelling microphones help in getting really good audio (I use it to record myself playing guitar). The camera can be accessed by "twisting" the wrist two times, a trick which every user of this phone will be using all the time. ;)
  

  Speaker : - It may look like two front speakers, but it's the bottom one which is the actual speaker. It's much better than Sony or Samsung speakers, but still far behind the unmatchable HTC Boomsound speakers. Still, bass is audible, and it's really loud.
  

  Software/Hardware : - Motorola takes the cake here. The software is smoother than butter. Hell, I found it to be smoother than my friend's Nexus 5, which is quite an achievement, It's stock Android 4.4.4 as of now. Moto hasn't changed anything from Google's version of Android except adding a few apps of it's own (compared to Samsung which changes EVERYTHING, from the UI to the features). Expect this to get the Lollipop update instantly (after the Nexus phones), which will improve the battery life and add many more features.
  

  Moto's own apps are helpful, and (again, unlike Samsung), not mere gimmicks. Moto Voice is always listening to you (Even when the screen is off), and it has a ton of functionality, which, added with Google Now, helps you control the device without even touching it. It's real helpful when you can check your phone notifications and even send Whatsapp messages while lying in bed, with your phone on your table! It doesn't drain the battery, as it runs on a separate low-power processor instead of the main one.
  

  The best feature, however, is the Moto Display. It activates when you hold your phone, or when you bring your hands near it. It shows the time, and your notifications in a beautiful, battery-saving interface, so that you don't have to even unlock your screen. I've gotten so used to this that I often expect other phones to light up as soon as I bring my hand near them!
  

  Performance is obviously outstanding, thanks to the Snapdragon 801 processor. High-end games run perfectly, and multitasking is perfect, with literally NO lag.
  

  Storage is 16GB and non-expandable, which is fine for most people, unless you store a lot of music and/or movies in your phone.
  

  Battery - 2300mah may look low, but it easily lasts the day with moderate to slightly heavy use. Those of you who are coming from devices with large batteries (like the Galaxy Note series) may find the lower battery slightly unsettling at first, but it's not a big deal. In the last few days, it has consistently lasted the entire day with all moto features + GPS staying on.
  

  At 32k, a phone like this is an absolute STEAL. I got it for around 24k thanks to the exchange offer (exchanged an old Galaxy S2), and I couldn't be any happier. column6: The Best phone money can buy!!
column7:
This is the best phone till date, even though the 3rd generation Moto X (Style) has been released. Its the perfect display size, perfect in the hand and the features like Moto Display and Moto Voice are the best.Given that its currently at a ridiculously low price of 15000 which decreases even further when you exchange your old phone for it, I'll recommend this phone to you in a heartbeat.
  

  I've read many reviews here on Flipkart that have said that the screen replacement cost is ridiculously high. Allow me to explain the reason.
  
  Most of the phones in the market have an LCD display. LCD displays are much cheaper to manufacture and hence cost less when you break your old display. This phone has an AMOLED display which cost much more to manufacture; just look at the TV market and you'll see that only a few OLED TV's are there (DO NOT confuse with LED TV's). THis kind of display uses less battery power, especially for Moto Display. An LCD Screen will hog battery when Moto Display is in use as the whole display lights up and not just the few pixels.

  Cons:
  
  Here's a complaint though. Motorola has gone and screwed their customers given the expensive repair costs that you'd incurr if you purchase any Motorola phone. Their after sales service is also utterly pathetic. All of this happened after Lenovo took over Motorola from Google so we all know whom to blame.
  
  Mentioning that the phone supports 4G is technically true but this isn't relevant to the Indian market. This is because the 4G bands that Indian telecom operators use (LTE band 40) is not supported by this variant and is only supported by the Chinese variant (XT1085). Releasing a non-supported 4G phone and calling it 4G is a blatant lie and they should be taken to court for mentioning the same. The least they can do is add LTE band 40 with the next firmware update so we can avail 4G services on Airtel and Aircel.
  
  Another bone I wanted to pick was that the moment you unlock the bootloader of any motorola device, you will void warranty. This is a bad move on part of Motorola given that most manufacturers will honour warranty if you bring it back to stock condition.

column6: The Amazing Moto X- android done right
column7:
I will keep this exhaustive so you can feel how I feel, fun fact- this is my 100th smartphone and my cure for incessant search for something better. Since last 5 years I have been down this road of mobile devices starting with a now humble blackberry Curve and a reason for my money going into a futile yet uncontrollable pursuit :) . The following review is for the phone entailing the following aspects-
  

  1) In hand feel- it is always better to know how it feels by giving the phone to users of other phones and knowing their reaction. I did the same with an iPhone purist who never acknowledges a rival product and hates Samsung the most. And you must see how delighted he was appreciating the aluminum frame and smooth feeling of the back and the fanatic Moto logo. And then I gave it to Galaxy S5 users and Sony. I even had a few hours with an iPhone 6 and feel really odd holding a behemoth of a device for 4.7 inch screen,  I mean apple sure could do better. So is this all euphoria and lies,  no sir. I am really and truly happy with the purchase and will keep it till iPhone 6s comes to apple's rescue with a far better camera and an updated processor.
  

  2) Performance- Even Virat has off days, not this beast. Give it any task,  give it to change apps as frequently as you can,  give it a slap or a thud, give it games that scream with demanding graphics and processing prowess. Give it some love cause it can. How does it do,  by keeping things simple and when Motorola gets itself out of Google way of Android. It is a sad affair how all other manufacturers just go on piling stuff after stuff and unnecessarily burden the underlying android for their. The main reason being profit and their own competing ecosystem. Users would not mind if things were to improve, alas we suffer the most in the form of frustrating lags and inordinate delays in getting future android.
  

  3) Hello future- You can almost feel like Iron man when your phone wakes up and tells you answers when you take a command (hello Shaktiman,  in my case: ). I demoed it to wife and she asked me to go to sabji purchase which showed how jealous she was   anyway,  on the use front this is a cool addition and is really helpful when you cannot reach your phone and need some information from Google Now. Moto display too is another my favorite when you can just wave your palm over it or just pick it up or just move the phone a little and it shows up the time and notifications. Just amazing. I think in 2014, every phone should have this cool stuff. Downside to this is a cluttered look on the white version of this owing to 4 IR sensors which make the phone unsightly, bad bad...
  

  4) Display,  Camera and battery life- Truth be told, this phone uses AMOLED from Samsung and they will not be giving Motorola their best, so on display front they are one generation behind Samsung. Still on a 1080p screen things are hardly noticed for the obvious lack of screen refinement. Still when you have a platform of 5.2 inch screen, things will always be interesting. Camera is a frustration  and I would urge everyone to install Google Camera, keep HDR on and problem solved. Better life contrary to everyone's quick judgement is as good as any flagship that launched in first half of the year. Don't forget this is 20k cheaper than iPhone 6 and you will learn to live with the one day battery life
  

  5) Lollipop - Guys, guys, guys,  Google  has a masterstroke in the form of Lollipop with the complete visual overhaul with Android L and they are already seen in apps like hangouts, drive, keep, fit etc to name a few and Motorola having kept it's traditional image will seed in the next as early as December and finally android will be as good looking as iOS. And thanks to Samsung's over the top feature list, you won't know if you got a new OS or just leafed out due to compromising overlaying touchwiz.
  

  And another fun fact, typed this entire review on my Moto X with a little help from SwiftKey :)
  

  Cheers,
  
  Jagan
