Dear all, after staying on BB OS 10 with Z 10 and Z 30 for more than 3 year I wanted to move on to Android. After a thorough research and going and various reviews on youtube, flipkart, amazon, techrader, gsmarena etc, I finally zeroed on two products Honor 7 and Moto X Force. And out of two I finally made it to Moto X Force. Following are few Pros and Cons that I found after 3 days of usage:
  

  Pros:
  
  1- Pretty good and fast camera (Front and back both, you can take 3 pictures in one sec)
  
  2- Exceptional brightness and display
  
  3- Fast browsing and data transfer
  
  4- Comfortable to hold ( though I don't have big hands)
  
  5- Amazing battery life (3760 MAH, expect close to 35 Hrs)
  
  6- Fast charging (40-100 in 40 Mins)
  
  7- Ergonomic design though it is 9.2 mm thick but in hand it feels 5-6 mm due to curved back
  
  8- Smart lock feature: Till it is in your hand or case it remains unlock, so no need to unlock it every time (so faster that any finger print sensor usage
  
  9- Stock android so you can use your own preferred launcher, I found Microsoft's Arrow launcher pretty cool
  

  Cons:
  
  1- Found volume rocker little sharp
  
  2- Speaker is just OK ( coming from BB Z30 which has marvelous speakers)
  
  3- Earphone is OK
  

  Infamous Heating Isssue:
  

  So far I have found it to be some gimmick, phone is all fine, handles all task pretty well, no heating during charging, video streaming, browsing etc ( used it continuously for more than 2 hours)  I don't know why lots of people are reporting heating issue.
  

  Internet is full of heating issues with S6, S7, HTC 10, iphone 6-7 etc.
  

  Final: Go ahead and buy it

Excellent product at 12999. Between 32GB(12999) and 64GB(15599) , the only difference being internal storage and for just around 25GB increment made no sense to pay 2600 INR. With that price you can buy a 128GB micro sd card and increase your storage space by a huge margin. Now coming to the pros and cons:
  

  1. Quad HD screen
  
  2. Shatter proof display
  
  3. Excellent photo quality and video quality at day time
  
  4. Wireless charging
  
  5. Fast charging
  
  6. Good Battery backup
  
  7. Android Nougat now available
  
  8. No overheating or network or screen issues faced as reported by other reviewers
  
  9. 2016 flagship at a lower mid range price in 2017. Sweet! Unless you require a dual sim this is the one to go for as compared to the likes of lenovo z2 plus, redmi note 4 etc
  
  10. Stock UI
  
  11. Moto gestures
  

  Cons:
  

  1. No Jio VOLTE support (not a con for me) even after Nougat update
  
  2. No dual sim even though the sim tray is that of a hybrid variety
  
  3. Stock camera app sucks big time. You cannot default video recording to 4k. The moment you restart the camera app, the default video setting is back to 1080p. No 1080p 60 frames option although the hardware is capable.
  
  4. Available total RAM is only 2.5 GB, although it hardly matters for this device. Overall RAM management is good.
  

  I would highly recommend this device if you are getting it at 12999 (32GB). Using a 2016 flagship than a 2017 lower mid range at the same price make so much sense and takes the experience to an all new level. Of course there are cons. No device is perfect. So if they really dont matter to you, just go for it!

column6: Best Phone I have used until now!!!!!!
column7:
Pre-ordered my Nexus on 18th Nov and Flipkart delivery was very fast as usual, got it the 2nd day the phone started selling in india. Kudos to flipkart on that.
  
  As far as the phone is concerned, its a beast. I owned a galaxy S4 before this one, so i was tired of the laggy, bloated sammy and its touchwiz UI. Galaxy Note4 even though crammed with same specs and better utilities and camera, meant nothing to me because i never used the gimmicks S4 offerd.
  
  Nexus 6 even though large is very comfortable to hold in hand (i have big hands by the way), because of its ergonomics and its not that heavy as well. It fits perfectly in my jeans as well. Got no complaints on that department. Once get used to the size, my 5" S4 looked like a dwarf and believe me you wont have problems getting used to the phone. :)
  
  6" screen is absolutly a beauty and when we lower the brightness to min in auto mode, slight pink coloring is there which i like by the way because i prefer it like that during night times in my room :D. Its bright @ outdoors in direct sunlight as well and Contents on the screen are readable too. Its good for reading and watching vidoes and movies as well.
  
  As far as Performance is concerned my Nexus handles everything smoothly and fastly. Games and apps open faster and transitions are smooth. While doing task switching you will notice teeny tiny lag because of all the pixels it have to push on the screen. But in no way it will hinder your daily usage and you wont notice that unless you are a geek :P. Also i havent noticed a lag because of the encryption. So 5 stars for performance.
  
  Next will be the Camera, 13Mp rear shooter takes some amazing shots in bright conditions and it handles well in low light conditions as well. Images are sharp and color reproduction is good as well. I am not a photoholic so am not comparing camera to that of iphones or galaxys or DSLR.  2mp front cam is good, but noise is visible and its not that sharp. It will good for posting to your social networking site, thats that. Am pretty happy with the camera of Nexus 6.
  
  Lollipop is great, had the Nexus 6 come with Kitkat. i would not have bought it. UI is clean and animations are great and i am in love with the material design :D. But it needs improvement, its very much buggy. For example in my Nexus 6, if i uncheck the automatic date and time option and then change the time manually, the recent apps button is rendered useless and i have to restart the phone to get it to work. Like this some bugs are there, but am sure bugs will be rectified very quickly and i will be getting updates before i know. Quoting my favourite reviwer MKBHD - "There is nothing that Software updates cant improve and Nexus 6 has one of the best hardware available in market to date".I got the 5.0.1 update as well. If this was sammy (samsung), i had to wait months to get the update. This is another reason i bought Nexus. :D :D
  
  Speakers are aaweesomee guys; I seldom heard music through loudspeakers on my S4, but speakers on Nexus 6 changed my attitude completly. But the headset provided with phone is not at all good and provide no noise insulation as well. So for music fans out there buy a good headset.
  
  Another most important thing as far as am concerned is Battery Life. I go to work at 6am in morning and get back home by 8pm and i will be left with atleast 10% of battery  and i dont need to carry charger any more. Am very very happy with that. Am getting 4.30-5.15hrs of screen on time what ever the usage is. If you turn on 2g/3g/LTE/wifi all the time then battery lasts for 18-24hrs, if you turn on the cellular/wifi connectivity occassionly then battery lasts fr more than a day. If you seldom use the data connectivity, then you can sctretch the usage upto 2 days :D. 3220MAH is adequate enough for me. Turbo charging is a good asset too but it kicks in only when the charge is less than 15% or 10% (am not sure if that). Gets from 4% to 30% in 15mins and there after charges normally-gets to 100% in under 1.5hrs.
  
  Call quality is good, its loud and clear unless your in a noisy environment like a travelling bus by the window side :P
  

  1 thing i absolutly loved in Nexus 6/Lollipop is the facial password. If you turn on facial password and when in lockscreen a small circle will be shown at the bottom of screen. if the face is recognized it will unlock or else it will show the lock in the circle, you can then swipe up the screen to type your alternate password and unlock device. facial recognition is very fast and a neat feature which i use all the time.
  
  Google Now works even when the screen is off and its pretty accurate too in recognizing our voice.
  

  Cons :
  

  Lollipop is buggy but it will improve eventually.
  
  No need of messenger app when you have hangouts.
  

  Am completely satisfied with the 44k i spent on my Nexus 6 unlike the 40Kk spent on S4 and i will recommend it to any1 looking for a decent phone and not some fancy gimmicks.

column6: Great all round Phone, this Nexus beast!
column7:
This phone is an absolute beast created by Google & Motorola! It's been around a month & a half since I have been using this phone & I would like to share my initial impressions about the same. I was using an iPhone 6 plus (16gb) before this, but handed the same over to my wife since I needed more storage space, so picked the 64gb Nexus 6. Also the price drop was a major factor in my purchase too!
  
  What's great:
  
  - The display in Quad HD is eye popping & beautiful! Everything looks rich & vivid, including movies & youtube videos
  
  - The processor functions like a beast! Completing tasks is a breeze & multitasking is superb
  
  - Android Lollipop (when purchased) was my best experience using Android (I returned to Android after a long gap after using IOS for almost 3 years). Marshmallow is even better with great battery saving & the same fluid interface as earlier
  
  - In-built Google Apps work seamlessly & take care of almost all my needs of using the phone
  
  - Power charging is top class & is such a convenience. Overall charge time is super quick & makes using the phone easy with no worries even if battery has drained; a quick charge ensures juice enough to use it longer
  
  What's good:
  
  - Battery life is decent & lasts me a little over a day. With minimal usage I can get through 2 days, however with heavy usage, it drains by the end of the day
  
  - The camera is good, I use a DSLR so my phone is used as a casual alternative & it does not disappoint for this kind of use
  
  - The phone design & finish is pretty good, however I do recommend using a back cover since it can be quite slippery even with a curved back
  
  - This phone supports wireless charging, although I haven't tried it (Great feature considering the new Nexus phones don't have this)
  
  - The front dual speakers are pretty decent too, although they do screech a bit at higher volumes
  
  - Audio performance with headphones is good. I use Senheiser CX 300 in-ears & the performance is quite good
  
  What could have been better:
  
  - The screen is curved at the edges & this is a big pain  when it comes to finding a screen guard or a tempered glass. This is more of a personal itch that I have, although the phone comes with a scratch resistant Gorilla glass display which is excellent, I still wanted a tempered glass screen guard. I must have searched the entire city & whatever I found left a big halo around the edges due to the curves. I finally found the best tempered glass online which was a US import; fits the screen only, not on the edges! (Yootech Tempered Glass for Nexus 6)
  
  - Audio quality of the supplied earphones is pretty ordinary, for a phone at this price, the headphones could have been better
  

  Overall:
  
  This is no doubt one of the best phones I have ever used & having used the iPhone 6 plus for a few  months before this, I can vouch for this statement. The 6 plus is a great phone with a super long lasting battery, but I feel the Nexus 6 has a better display & Android Marshmallow comes closest to the smooth IOS performance with the freedom of Android, making it a better alternative in my opinion. Although IOS I feel is still a safer eco system & Google can feel quite intrusive at times. Would recommend that you go through Google's privacy settings carefully to disable anything you feel can invade your privacy beyond your comfort zone! I don't find the Nexus 6 big, since I used the 6 plus before this & funnily the 6 plus feels smaller after the Nexus 6. I love big screen phones, so I don't mind the lack of one handed use ability.
  
  This phone is highly recommended, although critic reviews were quite mixed, my experience has been great. I think with Motorola build quality & a 5.96 inch screen with wireless charging feature, this phone contains some features even missing in the newly released 6PP. Phones that people choose are personal choices & IOS & Android are almost at a stage where they seem to be borrowing each other's  features. So I would not say that I recommend this phone over others, but I have listed what has worked well for me with the Nexus 6. If this is what you are looking in your phone too, then go for it, as its still available at a mouth watering price with a mind blowing screen & high end features.

column6: A sweet deal at this price
column7:
Nexus 6 was definitely overpriced when it was released, back in late 2014. Current price of 30k for the 32 GB version, however, is very compelling.
  

  Here's why you should go for this phone:
  

  - Stock Android, fast updates. I'm already running Marshmallow (Preview 3). You get a clean and smooth experience. Sure, Lollipop had many bugs initially, but 5.1.1 smoothed many things out. Also the ability to unlock the bootloader easily and install custom software is a must have for me.
  

  - Awesome performance: 5.1 improved performance and battery life, and it's flying more than ever in Marshmallow. It's a noticeable upgrade from my Nexus 4, which is still reasonably fast. Snapdragon 805 really flexes its muscles powering the QHD display, and 3 GB of RAM is aplenty.
  

  - Decent battery life: 1.5 to 2 days of usage under normal conditions. Doze in Marshmallow should be improving it even further.
  

  - Fast charging: It's a must have in present times.
  

  - Decent camera: Camera is reasonably snappy and takes good pictures. Definitely not the best one around, but still packs a punch. The camera module is the same as that of One Plus One. Dual LED flash. The flash ring is mostly a gimmick though.
  

  - Screen: I love looking at this QHD display. It's HUGE and beautiful. Sure, it's not the most accurate calibration, but looks a little punchy. I didn't find it too warm or too blue. Touchscreen is very responsive as expected. It's AMOLED panel is a generation behind the ones in latest Samsung flagships, so it's probably not as efficient as current generation. But no worries otherwise.
  

  - Front facing speakers: Combined with the screen, it makes an awesome media consumption experience. Loudness and clarity is more than decent.
  

  Now some cons:
  

  - No slow motion video: Though the hardware is more than capable of doing it, 60fps and 120fps video capture is not present. A quick Google/XDA search suggests that this is a limitation with the camera drivers used, so installing 3rd party apps probably won't help.
  

  - Front camera is only 2 MP: Though it takes decent pics, detail is limited due to this. Even in 2014, 5 MP front cameras were becoming a standard.
  

  - A bit on the heavier side: This may not be a problem for most. Also, the huge dimensions of the phone might take a little getting used to. But its totally worth it.
  

  - No finger-print scanner: Now it feels like I'm nit-picking, but Marshmallow is bringing native support for them, and new Nexus devices likely to be unveiled in September 2015 are also likely to have it. It would have been a nice addition to this phone.
  

  - I don't think the lack of removable storage is a problem anymore, with 32GB and 64GB versions available. Battery is also non-removable, which is a non-issue for me, but could be an issue for some. I think LG G4 is the decent choice available for such people.
  

  On the whole, it has been an awesome upgrade for me from my Nexus 4. Hopefully, slow-mo video support will come in the future. #Nexus4Life!

(Please Take the time to read the review, I'm sure it will help) So, The nexus 6 is a very very good phone and of course it is a fab device on paper (Google flagship.DUH!) but it lags behind in some aspects in day to day life. This review can be broken down into 2 segments. The SO good, The Not so good.
  

  Pro's: 1. The epic screen... Lately with the jump into the QHD world smartphones have been giving us wonderful screens. The nexus 6 with its 5.96 inch QHD screen is no exception. It's gorgeous and perfectly saturated with over 16M hues. But it's not the ABSOLUTE best large screen out there. I would give that to the Note 4 because I personally like that extra saturation.
  

  2. It's a nexus.... It would receive updates faster and give you a great materialistic software experience with Android L and so on.
  

  3.Camera.... It's easily the best camera by motorola so far...On par with the Moto Turbo.... It performs well in all lighting conditions and takes classy shots.
  

  4.Performance(multitasking and stuff....)... It's great with the general animations and scrolling and whatsoever you need to do with your device...
  

  5.Additional features.... Touchless control by motorola... Dual front facing speakers (which is the first time dual front facing speakers by motorola has been introduced( No. The Moto X had only a single driver on the bottom not dual speakers.) and water resistance makes it great for use.
  

  6.Of course.... It's built like a tank. It has a great soft touch feeling and the metal band makes it feel premium. Some people would find this a little big but it's overall a great feeling phone.
  

  Not so good category...
  

  1. Software experience.... It's great but android lollipop does very little to help with the single hand experience.
  

  2. Battery life.... Even though it has a 3220 mAh battery but we're in those 1st gen QHD phone section so it has a very slightly above average battery life in the real world mainly because it has all those extra pixels to push.
  

  3.Camera (sigh!) it has a great performing camera as we discussed earlier but due to its sensor it gives slightly grainy shots in extremely low light to low light conditions and the photo snapping process is a little slow compared to other flagships.
  

  4.Performance... As discussed earlier this device will perform great for day to day use and run all games like buttery smooth but the fact that it has all those extra pixels to push it very rarely to "less than often"ly drops frames in general animations in daily activities. But it may be fixed with more software update....
  

  Verdict: Great phone with a few general drawbacks but a must buy for a nexus lover.

Hello,
  
  For everyone who are looking forward to buy this device, a word of caution, this is a large phone with 5.96 inch. But that said, don't get intimidated with its size, you'll get used to it. Graduating from iPhone 4S after using for nearly 2 1/2 yrs, this was a big leap forward for me. I wanted to buy a premium phone with 1 day battery life, top of the line processor and hi-res display as I'm a pretty heavy user with my phone is loaded with graphic games like asphalt, nova 2 etc, WhatsApp, net browsing of all other things. This left me with very few options namely nexus 6, iPhone 6 plus, Note 4, LG G3.
  
  I tried my hands on G3 and Note 4 at Reliance Digital store, but I was unimpressed with its UI. It was lagging (might have been the issue with that piece). and second problem with these devices is the OS update schedule. Samsung and LG are very slow in updated their phones (Only recently they have upgraded to Android 5.0.1). So these two phones were cancelled from the list. This left me with Nexus 6 and iPhone 6 plus.
  
  iPhone 6 plus is really expensive device retailing at 62.5K for 16 GB model. Hence I decided to go with Nexus 6 which was steal of a buy at 33k for 32gb model with exchange. The main reason for going with nexus 6 was Lollipop out of box, otherwise android was a big no for me.
  
  Nexus 6 came with Lollipop 5.0 out of box. Was soon updated to 5.0.1 which fixed many issues from the initial OS release.
  
  After using it 2-3 weeks (bought it on 2nd January, 2015), I wanted to return the phone as it would frequently restart and would heat up as high as 42 deg with little use such as texting and web browsing. I called up Motorola customer care and they guided me to clear the cache memory and factory reset the phone, which I did and the issue was solved. A piece of advice to all, if you experience issues with restarting, heating or abnormal battery drain, kindly clear the cache memory and factory reset it, which should solve the problem.
  
  Talking about the phone, this is a beast of a device. with Snapdragon 805 processor coupled with 3 GB RAM, it just flies through the tasks thrown at it without breaking any sweat.
  
  The screen is a gem to look at with colour reproduction, crisp to read text and a healthy amount of pixel density (but is battery hogger, the screen on time is 4 hrs to 4 1/2 hrs) and the stereo speaker are loud enough and the output is clear enough.
  
  The quick charging feature is really handy as it charges the phone from 10% to 40% in 15 mins with phone kept on standby mode. The phone really heats up during this time, hence advised not to use the phone while charging. The phone cools down to ambient temp once the battery is fully recharged (which takes about an hr and half), so don't worry about the heating.
  
  The headphones provided are not very good, it gives decent output but I would suggest to use headphones from other brand to get better output.
  
  Coming to camera, I'm a bit disappointed with its low light. Taking photos in broad daylight or good light condition gives excellent detailed , sharp pictures using 13Mp, f 2.0 sensor.
  
  The latest flavour of android is really very eye pleasing and brings in a whole new lot of improvement and features compared to previous versions of android. This being the nexus device, you'll be the first to receive the latest OS from the Google and being a vanilla version this is free of any bloat-ware or OEM customisation, which is in a way good and bad depending on your personal preference.
  
  Coming from iOS, I still feel android lagging in few areas as the OS is not optimised for the big screen of Nexus 6 mainly easy of use. Though android allows customisation but lacks in ease of use.
  
  If you are comfortable with manually updating the OS using the factory image then the new version of lollipop i.e.. 5.1 (build LMY47I) is available on the android developer website. I would suggest go ahead and flash this new build as this brings a host of bug fixes and improvement. The battery life has significantly improved and the restart problem has been totally resolved. If you are a beginner or new to android like me search YouTube for detailed walk-through on installing the factory image.
  
  I would recommend this phone to everyone looking out for buying a premium android device which comparable performance with comparison of iPhone 6 plus at nearly 60% of its price.

column6: Could have been a great phone but the software lets it down.
column7:
********************** Edit after using for 6 months now*****************
  

  I am running the latest android 5.1 but it is totally buggy,
  
  phone crashes randomly,
  
  heats up,
  
  battery drains very quickly
  
  is frustratingly slow while executing normal commands (like taking ages to display names of the person calling you when the data is there in the contacts list!)
  

  Note: I do not play any games on this phone or listen to music/watch videos, I just have some 35 odd apps installed and some 8 GB of data on the phone. I believe all these issues stems from the memory leak problem that Google is yet to fix in Android 5.
  

  On paper the phone has great hardware but the software is a total letdown. I have been using android since v2 and was very happy with it but this phone is so bad, I am planning to get rid of this phone and buy an iphone 6 plus.
  

  **********************End of Edit*******************
  


  I have been using the phone for over two weeks now and the following are my observations:
  
  1. The phone is LARGE, very evident when you use it for the first few days but with time you will get accustomed to the size
  
  2. The back panel is smooth in texture so it tends to get slippery sometimes
  
  3. The new Android OS debuts a lot of new functionality and a refreshed design, which in most aspects is forward looking
  
  4. The biggest letdown is Android Lollipop power management, the phone simply runs out of battery! I dont play any games, nor am I watching HD video, neither is the GPS on all the time but the battery drains to 15% by early evening from 100% at 9AM. I updated to Android 5.0.1 but the problem persists..waiting for a new update from Google to fix this issue.
  
  Overall it is a great phone to have, with a very decent camera, call quality, speakers and display. If Google fixes the issues with Android Lollipop and the price rationalises further it will be an even better device to own!
